note: Evidence for flag eras. An era is listed only once someone has read its sources; every other era is unreviewed. Only positive evidence is written here, and what could not be confirmed is said in `open`, not left out.

classes.attested: Sources show this flag in use in this period. Needs one primary or reference source, or two compiled sources from different publishers.
classes.reconstructed: Described in sources but no image survives; the drawing is a reconstruction.
classes.symbolic: An emblem, banner or standard shown for a polity that had no flag of its own.
classes.none: No flag evidence exists; the image is a placeholder.
classes.unreviewed: Not yet checked against sources. The page text is the original compilation.
classes.placeholder: The image is a placeholder, as the page's own caption says. Whether a flag existed was not checked.

kinds.primary: The decree, document, image or object itself, or a museum record of it.
kinds.reference: A scholarly or institutional account that names its basis.
kinds.compiled: A general compilation (Wikipedia, Flags of the World); useful, but a copy of other writers.

fotw-cd-zr.note: Does not cover flags before 1971 or the 1997 replacement flag.

wp-flag-kh.title: Flag of Cambodia

fotw-li.title: Liechtenstein (Flags of the World)

fotw-uz.title: Flags of the World: Uzbekistan

wp-flag-tw.title: Flag of the Republic of China
wp-flag-tw.note: Does not cover the Japanese colonial period, the Qing period, the Kingdom of Tungning or Dutch Formosa; the final 38,693 characters were not read.

wp-history-of-flags.note: Mentions ancient Egypt only for pre-dynastic nome standards and the Narmer Palette; no dates and no royal emblems, crowns, uraeus or serekh; nothing on any dynasty or period.

wp-flag-gb-sct.title: Flag of Scotland
wp-flag-gb-sct.note: Says nothing of Alba, the Picts, Dal Riata or Strathclyde, the Norse, or the date of the lion rampant; the final 98,084 characters were not read.

fotw-gb-scotl.title: Flags of the World: Scotland

fotw-ly.title: Libya
fotw-ly.note: Does not cover the Ottoman, Italian or Allied periods, nor design details of the 1972 and 1977 flags.

fotw-ws.title: Western Samoa / Samoa

fotw-by.title: Belarus
fotw-by.note: Covers the 1995 and 2012 flag; older flags appear only as link labels; silent on Lithuania, the Russian Empire and the BSSR.

wp-aquila.title: Aquila (Roman)
wp-aquila.note: Covers legionary eagles from Marius (disputed) to Teutoburg and later; silent on SPQR and on the double-headed eagle origin.

wp-labarum.title: Labarum
wp-labarum.note: Covers Constantine, 312 and the labarum (from c. 317); silent on the Tetrarchy and the 395/476 divisions.

wp-flags-byzantine.title: Flags of the Byzantine Empire
wp-flags-byzantine.note: Covers Byzantine banners and the double-headed eagle; first 100,000 characters read; silent on Western Roman flags and 1453.

fotw-it-rmemp.title: Roman Empire

wp-flags-ottoman.title: Flags of the Ottoman Empire

fotw-tr-ottom.title: Ottoman Empire

fotw-lr.title: Liberia

fotw-ma.title: Morocco

wp-flag-ci-g4.title: Flag of Côte d'Ivoire

fotw-km.title: Comoros

wp-tug.title: Tug (banner)

fotw-ir-sass.note: Does not mention Qadisiyyah, any capture, or any Sasanian-era image.

fotw-af1901.note: Black flag with white royal arms, state and war flag; black as national colour under Abdul Rahman (1880-1901), citing Baert 2001.

fotw-af1881.title: Emirate of Afghanistan 1881-1901
fotw-af1881.note: Two-line note that the Emirate of Kabul flag became the flag of all Afghanistan from October 1881.

wp-durrani.title: Durrani Empire
wp-durrani.note: Infobox shows two flags with dated use 1747-1818 and a Herat flag; the text read does not describe their design.

wp-emirate-af.title: Emirate of Afghanistan
wp-emirate-af.note: Flags section: red and green triangular military flags with the shahada under Dost Mohammad and Sher Ali; first arms on a flag, a solid black banner with white emblem, under Abdur Rahman.

fotw-lv-cour.title: Courland (Latvia)
fotw-lv-cour.note: Duchy of Courland state, merchant and naval flags, citing Dzirkalis 1936, Bellin 1756, Norie and Hobbs 1848 and Steenbergen 1862.

fotw-lv-hist.title: Latvia: history of the flag
fotw-lv-hist.note: Flag history citing the Livlandische Reimchronik (1279) and The Flag Bulletin XXXI:6.

wp-duchy-courland.title: Duchy of Courland and Semigallia
wp-duchy-courland.note: Infobox shows the state flag of the duchy and a coat of arms, 1561-1795.

wp-swedish-livonia.title: Swedish Livonia
wp-swedish-livonia.note: Dominion 1629-1721 with conquest of Riga in 1621; infobox shows an 18th-century flag of Livonia, not the Swedish flag.

wp-duchy-livonia.title: Duchy of Livonia
wp-duchy-livonia.note: Vassal of Lithuania (1561-1629), then Poland-Lithuania; infobox carries a coat of arms and no flag.

wp-livonian-order.title: Livonian Order
wp-livonian-order.note: Branch of the Teutonic Order 1237-1561; the master's seal shows the Teutonic Knights' arms (marked citation needed).

wp-teutonic-order.title: Teutonic Order
wp-teutonic-order.note: Infobox attire is a white mantle with a black cross; its flag list pairs Terra Mariana with the flag file of the State of the Teutonic Order.

fotw-de-to.title: Teutonic Order (Germany)
fotw-de-to.note: Flag of the Teutonic Order: black Scandinavian cross on white, citing Smith 1975 and the Banderia Prutenorum.

wp-generalbezirk-lettland.title: Generalbezirk Lettland
wp-generalbezirk-lettland.note: German civil district 1941-1944 within Reichskommissariat Ostland; infobox flag is the flag of Nazi Germany.

lvportals-karogs.title: Latvijas karogs cauri okupācijas gadiem
lvportals-karogs.note: Popular article on the flag through the occupations; says the red-white-red flag did not disappear under the German occupation and that Latvian Legion uniforms carried its colours.

fotw-ly-1969.title: Libya, 1969-1972
fotw-ly-1969.note: Red-white-black flag adopted 7 November 1969; cites Whitney Smith 1980 and The Flag Bulletin XVI:6.

fotw-xo-far.title: Federation of Arab Republics (1 July 1972 - March 1977)
fotw-xo-far.note: Hawk-of-Quraish tricolour used by Egypt, Libya and Syria 1972-77; cites Smith 1975.

fotw-ly-1977.title: Libya, 1977-2011
fotw-ly-1977.note: Plain green flag adopted in 1977 after leaving the Federation; notes from Album des Pavillons.

fotw-ly-cyren.title: Cyrenaica, Libya
fotw-ly-cyren.note: Senussi black flag with white crescent and star; cites Franciae Vexilla (Corbic, March 1999).

fotw-ly-fez.title: Fezzan, Libya (spurious flag)
fotw-ly-fez.note: Shows that a red crescent flag reported for French-run Fezzan came from an alternate-history image, not photographs.

fotw-ly-trip.title: Tripoli, Libya
fotw-ly-trip.note: Reported historical flags of Tripoli and a debate on Ottoman-era flags, with contributors Stelter, Heimer and Ollé.

wp-bma-libya.title: British Military Administration (Libya)
wp-bma-libya.note: Infobox flag is the United Kingdom flag.

wp-italian-libya.title: Italian Libya
wp-italian-libya.note: Infobox flag is the crowned Italian tricolour (1861-1946 type), 1934-1943; lists a Fezzan-Ghadames flag file.

wp-ottoman-tripolitania.title: Ottoman Tripolitania
wp-ottoman-tripolitania.note: Infobox flag is an 18th-century maritime flag of the Regency of Tripoli.

fotw-es1701.title: Historical Flags 1701-1785 (Spain)
fotw-es1701.note: Charles II and Philip V replace the Burgundy cross ensign with royal arms on white; the cross continues as jack; cites El Buque en la Armada Española (1999).

fotw-es1785-w.title: War Ensign 1785-1931 (Spain)
fotw-es1785-w.note: Red-yellow-red war ensign by Royal Decree of 25 May 1785, state and war flag by Royal Decree of 13 October 1843; notes the 1899 depiction.

fotw-es1808-u4.title: Kingdom of Spain (1808-1813)
fotw-es1808-u4.note: White flag with arms under Joseph Bonaparte (Royal Decree of 12 July 1808), quoting a Spanish Navy page on red and yellow colours in the Peninsular War.

fotw-es-corte.title: Hernán Cortés' flags (Spain)
fotw-es-corte.note: Cortés' standard in Chapultepec (red with the Virgin Mary) after Calvo and Grávalos 1983.

fotw-mx-1521.title: Mexico - Discovering and Conquista (1517-ca. 1566)
fotw-mx-1521.note: Quotes Tapia, Mendieta, Gómara and others on Cortés' flag: red cross on white-and-blue with the motto 'In hoc signo'.

fotw-es-15thc-u4.title: 15th Century Flags (Spain)
fotw-es-15thc-u4.note: Royal standard of the Catholic Kings 1492-1506: white with their arms; quotes the Columbus logbook.

fotw-es-colum.title: Christopher Columbus' Flags, 1492 (Spain)
fotw-es-colum.note: Columbus' royal flag and captains' ensigns (white with green cross and crowned F and Y), citing Calvo and Grávalos 1983 and his logbook.

nps-spanish-flag.title: The Spanish Flag (Fort Matanzas)
nps-spanish-flag.note: Interpretive text: the red Burgundian saltire on white flown by Spanish ships from the early 1500s, carried to the New World and Philippines, replaced by the red-and-gold ensign in 1785 and regimental colours in 1843.

fotw-md-law.title: Moldova - Flag Laws
fotw-md-law.note: Flag laws of 1994, 2001 and 17 September 2010 with colour definitions.

fotw-su-md.title: Moldavia in the Soviet Union (1952-1991)
fotw-su-md.note: Flag approved 31 January 1952 with a green bar in the middle, one quarter of the width.

fotw-su-md-h.title: Moldavia in the Soviet Union (early flags)
fotw-su-md-h.note: Moldavian ASSR and SSR flags 1924-1952; the 1941-1952 flag is red with RSSM initials and hammer and sickle.

fotw-ro-mold.title: Principality of Moldavia
fotw-ro-mold.note: Moldavian flags from a 1533 Krakow document, the 1601 Dresden manuscript flag (via Enciclopedia Romaniei 1938-43) and 19th-century standards.

wp-flag-moldavian-ssr.title: Flag of the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic
wp-flag-moldavian-ssr.note: 1940-52 flag with RSSM initials; 1952 decree of a red cloth with a green middle stripe, red-green-red 3:2:3, hammer, sickle and star in the canton; 1990 tricolour.

wp-flag-coa-moldavia.title: Flag and coat of arms of Moldavia
wp-flag-coa-moldavia.note: Aurochs head arms; red silk princely flag with the arms in gold (1485); decline of flags under Ottoman control; red-and-blue standards from the early 19th century.

wp-principality-moldavia.title: Principality of Moldavia
wp-principality-moldavia.note: Infobox: flags 14th-15th century and 1831-1862; Bessarabia Governorate shown with the Russian flag as a successor.

fotw-er-1952.title: Historical flag of Eritrea (1952)
fotw-er-1952.note: Light blue flag with a green wreath, 1952 (Smith 1975; The Flag Bulletin May/June 1996); also used by the ELF.

fotw-er-plf.title: Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF)
fotw-er-plf.note: EPLF flag: green over light blue with a red triangle at the hoist and a yellow star; cites The Flag Bulletin 169.

wp-fed-eth-er.title: Federation of Ethiopia and Eritrea
wp-fed-eth-er.note: Infobox shows the Ethiopian flag (1897-1974) and the Eritrean flag (1952-1961); British Military Administration shown with the UK flag as predecessor.

wp-italian-eritrea.title: Italian Eritrea
wp-italian-eritrea.note: Infobox flag is the crowned Italian tricolour (1861-1946 type).

wp-bma-eritrea.title: British Military Administration (Eritrea)
wp-bma-eritrea.note: British control of Italian Eritrea 25 February 1941 to 15 September 1952; the article text read does not describe a flag.

fotw-gw.title: Guinea Bissau
fotw-gw.note: National flag, adoption by the National Assembly on 23 September 1973 (constitution article 2), photograph of the Madina do Boé assembly.

fotw-gw-paigc.title: P.A.I.G.C. party (Guinea-Bissau)
fotw-gw-paigc.note: PAIGC party flag: the national flag with the party initials under the star; notes the Cape Verdean flag derived from it.

wp-portuguese-guinea.title: Portuguese Guinea
wp-portuguese-guinea.note: Infobox flag is the Portuguese flag (1910-1974); colony from 1879 (before that a dependency of Cape Verde); the Liberated Zones appear as a successor with the PAIGC flag.

fotw-ws-hist.title: Samoa - Historical flags
fotw-ws-hist.note: 1948 four-star and 1949 five-star flag; New Zealand mandate defaced Red and Blue Ensigns with three palms (Admiralty warrants 1922-25, PRO documents); 1873-1879 kingdom flags.

fotw-de-colon.title: Former German colonies and overseas territories
fotw-de-colon.note: Flags used in the German colonies after Schurdel 1995 and Graudenz and Schindler 1988: the Reichsdienstflagge and the national flag.

wp-german-samoa.title: German Samoa
wp-german-samoa.note: Protectorate 1900-1914; imperial flag raised 1 March 1900; infobox shows the colonial office service flag.

fotw-zm-nr.title: Northern Rhodesia (Zambia pre-independence)
fotw-zm-nr.note: Northern Rhodesia flags 1910-1963: BSAC crest, arms granted 16 August 1939, Governor's flag, Federation blue ensign; cites PRO CO 323/1575/16.

fotw-cr-1821.title: Costa Rica - Historical Flag (1821-1822)
fotw-cr-1821.note: Blue-yellow-blue flag of the independence fighters 1821-22, against union with Mexico.

fotw-cr-1823.title: Costa Rica - Historical Flag (1823)
fotw-cr-1823.note: Flag hoisted 6 June 1823 after independence from Mexico (10 May 1823).

fotw-cr-1824.title: Costa Rica - Historical Flags (1824)
fotw-cr-1824.note: Flags of 4 March, 2 November and 22 November 1824.

fotw-cr-1840.title: Costa Rica - Historical Flags (1838-1848)
fotw-cr-1840.note: Flags of 1838, 1840, 1842 and the tricolour proclaimed 29 September 1848, by Jaume Ollé.

fotw-mr-1959.title: Mauritania - Former Flag
fotw-mr-1959.note: 1959 green flag with gold crescent and star adopted 1 April 1959; cites Carr 1961 (decree), Smith 1980, Znamierowski 1999.

wp-almoravid.title: Almoravid dynasty
wp-almoravid.note: Emblem section: the Almoravids adopted the Abbasid black standard from 1104; the Almohads adopted white against them.

fotw-pe-hist.title: Peru - Historical Flags
fotw-pe-hist.note: Index of Peruvian historical flags 1820-1825 after Fuentes 1975, with the Peruvian-Bolivian Confederation.

fotw-pe-1820o.title: History of the Peruvian Flag (October 1820)
fotw-pe-1820o.note: San Martín's decree of 21 October 1820 fixing a quartered flag with a laurel wreath and sun.

fotw-pe-1822.title: History of the Peruvian Flag (1822)
fotw-pe-1822.note: 1822 national, state, banner and merchant flags; notes a golden sun with a face on a flag at the Real Felipe fort museum.

fotw-pe-1823.title: History of the Peruvian Flag (1823)
fotw-pe-1823.note: Flag modified to horizontal form in 1823, decree of 25 February 1825.

fotw-sr-nl.title: Suriname - Colonial Flags
fotw-sr-nl.note: Colonial Suriname flags: unofficial flag with the three-master arms, 1959-1975 five-star flag with the decree of 8 December 1959, Governor's flags; contributors Sensen, Lutz, Southworth.

fotw-dz-regal.title: Regency of Algiers (Algeria, 1671-1847)
fotw-dz-regal.note: Regency of Algiers flags: the Ottoman flag in general use, deys' personal standards, a doubtful seven-stripe flag (MacMeekin) and white over black ship flags before 1830.

wp-list-algerian-flags.title: List of Algerian flags
wp-list-algerian-flags.note: Regency and French-period flags: a solid red flag of the Dey, red-and-yellow striped Odjak flags, a green flag with a yellow crescent reported in the 17th century, merchant stripe flags, the seven-stripe French Algeria ensign.

fotw-fj-his.title: Historical Flags (Fiji)
fotw-fj-his.note: Fijian flags 1865-1874 after Vexilla Nostra 164 and R.A. Derrick, with a 2015 Fiji Sun article; the 1871 flag of white and blue with a dove on a red shield.

fotw-fj-gb.title: British Fiji Islands 1874-1970 (Fiji)
fotw-fj-gb.note: Colonial badge sequence 1877-1924 with Admiralty and Colonial Office references (ADM 116/1847B, Admiralty Flag Book 1930).

fotw-ls-bas.title: Basutoland flags (Lesotho pre-independence)

fotw-su-ua.title: Ukraine in the Soviet Union (1949-1991)

fotw-su-ua-h.note: FOTW: Ukrainian SSR flags of 1919, 1923, 1927, 1930s, 1937 and the 1940s, each described.

fotw-ua-coss.title: Cossack Flags (Ukraine)
fotw-ua-coss.note: FOTW: Black Sea Cossack dark red banner with white Maltese cross, 1792.

wp-flag-ukrssr.title: Flag of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
wp-flag-ukrssr.note: Wikipedia: UkrSSR flags 1919, 1937 and 1949-50, with the UN prompt and the 21 Nov 1949 decree.

wp-rku.title: Reichskommissariat Ukraine
wp-rku.note: Wikipedia: text has no mention of flags or symbols.

ref-aeiou-fahnen.title: Fahnen Österreichs (AEIOU Österreich-Lexikon)

ref-goebl-adler.title: Auf der Suche nach einem Symbol: Das Staatswappen Österreichs 1934-1938 (M. Göbl, ADLER)

ref-goebl-adler.note: Named heraldry article: State Council fixed the colours 31 Oct 1918; Kruckenkreuz set in the red-white-red flag, 1934 arms.

ref-diem-symbole.title: Die Entwicklung der Symbole der Republik Österreich (P. Diem, Informationen zur Politischen Bildung 32, 2010)
ref-diem-symbole.note: Published civic-education booklet: history of Austria's flag and arms, 1233 to 1945, with citations to law gazettes.

ref-snl-norges-flagg.title: Norges flagg (L. Roede, Store norske leksikon)
ref-snl-norges-flagg.note: National encyclopedia entry by L. Roede: lion banner on the 1318 seal, Dannebrog, 1814, 1821, 1844 union mark, 1898 and 1905 changes.

wp-emblems-kalmar.note: Wikipedia: two 1430 letters of Eric of Pomerania describe the banner of the realms as a red cross in a yellow field; Three Crowns appear in the union arms.

fotw-yu-fy-mk.title: Flag of Socialist Macedonia
fotw-yu-fy-mk.note: FOTW: red flag with a yellow-outlined star in the canton, adopted 31 December 1946 (1963 constitution text quoted), earlier 1944-46 variants, superseded 1992.

fotw-mk-wwii.note: FOTW: one line that Macedonia was annexed by Bulgaria in 1941 and the Bulgarian flag used there; the 1944 Independent Macedonian State.

wp-krusevo.note: Wikipedia: IMRO insurgents flew Bulgarian flags in Krusevo; no mention of a red flag.

wp-serbian-empire.title: Serbian Empire
wp-serbian-empire.note: Wikipedia: Dusan crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks at Skopje on 16 April 1346; capital at Skopje; no flag text.

fotw-su-am.title: Armenia in the Soviet Union (1952-1991)
fotw-su-am.note: FOTW: dark blue bar in the middle, 1/4 width, approved 17 December 1952.

fotw-su-am-h.title: Armenia in the Soviet Union (early flags)
fotw-su-am-h.note: FOTW: Armenian SSR flags of 1922, 1937 and the 1940s; Transcaucasia 1922-36.

fotw-am-early.title: Early Armenian flags
fotw-am-early.note: FOTW: Iravan Khanate flag captured by Russian troops c.1827; Khachen principality flag of 1214; Mamikonian-era flag.

fotw-am-alish.title: Alishan's proposals (c.1885)
fotw-am-alish.note: FOTW: Alishan's c.1885 nationalist flags (red-green-blue and others).

wp-flag-armssr.title: Flag of the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic
wp-flag-armssr.note: Wikipedia: Armenian SSR flags of 1922, 1936-40, 1940-52 and the 17 December 1952 flag with a 1/4-width blue stripe in the middle.

wp-flag-bohemia.title: Flag of Bohemia
wp-flag-bohemia.note: Wikipedia: white-red Bohemian flag from the arms; Koebel 1545 and the 13th-century rhymed chronicle describe it; adopted by the Czech national movement in the 19th century.

wp-kingdom-bohemia.title: Kingdom of Bohemia
wp-kingdom-bohemia.note: Wikipedia: kingdom formally established in 1198 by Premysl Ottokar I; no flag text.

fotw-cz-bh.title: Bohemia (Czechia)
fotw-cz-bh.note: FOTW: Austrian crown lands had no flags of their own, only Landesfarben from the arms; white over red Bohemian flag used from the 19th century to 1918.

fotw-cz-bm39.title: Bohemia and Moravia Protectorate 1939-1945
fotw-cz-bm39.note: FOTW: timeline of 1938-39 annexations; Protectorate flag white-red-blue.

ct24-vlajka.title: Statni vlajka - jako jedina ze symbolu svoji podobu nemeni (Ceska televize, CT24)
ct24-vlajka.note: Public broadcaster explainer with vexillologist Ales Brozek: flag unchanged except in the war years until the dissolution of the state.

fotw-mm-73.title: Flags of Burma/Myanmar, 1974-2010

fotw-mm-48.title: Myanmar (Burma): 1948-1974
fotw-mm-48.note: FOTW: 1948 flag red with a blue canton, one large and five small white stars; adopted with the 1947 constitution, first hoisted 4 January 1948.

fotw-mm-old.title: Burma: flags of 1939-1948 (World War II era)
fotw-mm-old.note: FOTW: Blue Ensign with Burmese badge from 6/9 February 1939; Japanese rule 1940-45; puppet state flag 1 August 1943 - 1945.

fotw-mm-hist.title: Burma: historical flags before British colonial times
fotw-mm-hist.note: FOTW: Mon hintha flag c.1300-1500, Thu Ye Gyee flag, Konbaung peacock flag 1700-1885, mid-19th-century Mandalay flags, 1886-1939 British/Indian flag.

fotw-jp-hist.title: Historical flags of Japan (feudal / daimyo flags)
fotw-jp-hist.note: FOTW: in the period of war among the states (1467-1603) each of 68 kuni ruled by a daimyo had flags based on mon (hata-sashimono).

fotw-jp-e1945.title: Japan: civil ensign under occupation (E signal flag)
fotw-jp-e1945.note: FOTW: modified E signal flag used as Japanese merchant ensign 2 September 1945 - 31 March 1952.

wp-occupation-japan.title: Occupation of Japan

ref-saudipedia-first.note: Saudi national encyclopedia Q&A citing the Saudi Press Agency: first state flag green, silk and wool, shahada at centre, continued in the Second Saudi State; sword added under Abdulaziz.

fotw-sa-hist.title: The Evolution of the Flag of Saudi Arabia
fotw-sa-hist.note: FOTW: shahada on green linked to the Wahhabi movement of the late 18th century; sword added 1902 (one contributor); variants with a thuluth inscription from the 1927 Kingdom of Hijaz and Nejd.

fotw-sa-nejd.title: Emirate of Nejd and Hasa 1913-1921
fotw-sa-nejd.note: FOTW: flag of the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa unproven; a green flag with white hoist and inscription reported for 1902-1921.

fotw-sa-hail.title: Emirate of Ha'il 1835-1920
fotw-sa-hail.note: FOTW: Ha'il (Rashidi) flags, an Ottoman-like flag with golden crescent and star; no firm sources.

wp-red-ensign.title: Red Ensign
wp-red-ensign.note: Wikipedia: red ensign with St George canton from the 1620s; 1674 proclamation for merchant ships; flown by merchant ships since 1707; 1864 order in council allocated it to merchantmen.

wp-cnda-1865.title: Colonial Naval Defence Act 1865
wp-cnda-1865.note: Wikipedia: in 1866 the Admiralty told colonies owning vessels under the Act to fly the Royal Navy Blue Ensign with the colony's seal or badge.

fotw-gb-colon.title: British Empire and Overseas Territories (colonial flags)
fotw-gb-colon.note: FOTW: colonial flags (defaced Blue Ensigns with a badge) were introduced in 1869; badges based on the colony's public seal.

ref-dm-president.title: National Flag of the Commonwealth of Dominica (Office of the President)
ref-dm-president.publisher: Office of the President of the Commonwealth of Dominica (archived 2010)
ref-dm-president.note: Government description of the flag: red roundel with Sisserou parrot and ten lime-green stars over a triple cross of yellow, black and white on forest green; symbolism.

fotw-dm-col.title: Dominica: Colonial Badges and Flags
fotw-dm-col.note: FOTW: Blue Ensigns with Dominica badge 1955-65 and 1965-78 (full 1961 arms), earlier Leeward and Windward Islands badges; defaced Union Jacks for governors.

wp-history-dm.title: History of Dominica
wp-history-dm.note: Wikipedia: Dominica a French colony 1715-1763 and a British colony 1763-1978; independent 1978.

fotw-na-hist.title: Flag History of Namibia (German South West Africa, mandated territory)
fotw-na-hist.note: FOTW: German colonies had no flags of their own, imperial flags used; designs of c.1913 never used; SA Red Ensign flown until 31 May 1928, then the SA national flag.

fotw-na-flag.title: Namibia: national flag (1990 - )
fotw-na-flag.note: FOTW: flag adopted 21 March 1990 on independence, chosen by a committee; symbolism given by the committee chairman on 2 February 1990.

fotw-ph-hist.title: History of the Philippine Flag (M. L. Quezon III)
fotw-ph-hist.note: FOTW: article on the 1898 flag, the 1907 Sedition Act banning it and the 1919 repeal, and later colour changes.

fotw-ph-hist2.title: Philippines: explanation of the flag / history
fotw-ph-hist2.note: FOTW: flag first flown 1898; 1936 navy-blue flag restored on the return of American forces in 1944 and hoisted at independence on 4 July 1946.

fotw-ph-reint.note: FOTW reprint of a 1956 Philippines Free Press article: the flag was prohibited from 6 September 1907 and the ban lifted in 1919.

ref-snl-sverige.title: Sveriges flagg og våpen (L. Roede, Store norske leksikon)
ref-snl-sverige.note: National encyclopedia entry: union mark on the Swedish flag 1844-1905, removed 1 November 1905; flag law of 22 June 1906 lightened the blue.

fotw-se-fact.title: Sweden: facts and flag history
fotw-se-fact.note: FOTW: Swedish flag re-adopted 22 June 1906; flag age uncertain, 16th-century pictures; arms history.

fotw-bs-col.title: The Bahamas: colonial badge and flags (1869-1973)
fotw-bs-col.note: FOTW: Bahamas badge introduced 1869 and used on the Blue Ensign (white disc until 1923) until 1973; defaced Red Ensign unofficial.

fotw-br-col.title: Colonial Flags of Brazil
fotw-br-col.note: FOTW: Order of Christ banner, Iberian Union, Dutch West India Company flag in Dutch Brazil, Principality of Brazil flag, and the 1816 flag of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves with Brazil's armillary sphere ensign.

fotw-fi-duchy.title: Grand Duchy of Finland (1809-1918) flags
fotw-fi-duchy.note: FOTW: Finnish merchant flag 1809-21 prescribed then revoked; unofficial white arms-and-laurel flag of 1848; yacht club flags; 1902 pilot and customs flags.

wp-fi-swedish-rule.title: Finland under Swedish rule
wp-fi-swedish-rule.note: Wikipedia: Finland part of Sweden from the Middle Ages until 1809; no flag text.

wp-flag-sweden.title: Flag of Sweden
wp-flag-sweden.note: Wikipedia: oldest recorded pictures of the blue cloth with a yellow cross date from the early 16th century; legend of 1157 in Finland.

fotw-lt-hist.title: Lithuania: history of the flag
fotw-lt-hist.note: FOTW: Vytis on red official until 1795; independence 1918 after 200+ years of Russian rule; under German occupation 1941-44 the inter-war flag was flown in places and worn on sleeves, not officially sanctioned.

ref-vle-ostland.title: Lietuva Vokietijos okupacijos metais (1941-1944) (Visuotine lietuviu enciklopedija)
ref-vle-ostland.publisher: Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija (Mokslo ir enciklopedijų leidybos centras)
ref-vle-ostland.note: National encyclopedia: Lithuania became the Lithuanian General District within Reichskommissariat Ostland; no flag text.

fotw-ch-1798.title: Helvetic Republic (1798-1803)
fotw-ch-1798.note: FOTW: green-red-yellow horizontal flag adopted 14 April 1798; Directorate decree of 13 February 1799; Helvetic Legion flags.

ref-bs-helvetik.title: Freiheitsbaum und Trikoloren (Medienmitteilung des Regierungsrats Basel-Stadt, 1998)
ref-bs-helvetik.note: Cantonal government press release for the 200 years of the Helvetic Republic: green-red-yellow as the national flag of the Helvetic Republic.

ref-unifr-fahne.title: Warum ist die Schweizerfahne rot und weiss? (Universitas, Universitaet Freiburg)
ref-unifr-fahne.note: University explainer: the French chose a green-red-yellow tricolour as the first official Swiss flag, which disappeared after a few years.

ref-hls-helvetik.title: Helvetische Republik (Historisches Lexikon der Schweiz)
ref-hls-helvetik.note: National historical lexicon: Helvetic Republic 12 April 1798 - 10 March 1803, with a photograph of the 1798 flag in the Bundesbriefmuseum, Schwyz.

fotw-bw-hc.title: High Commissioner for Basutoland, the Bechuanaland Protectorate and Swaziland
fotw-bw-hc.note: FOTW: High Commissioner's flag 1931-68 (Union Flag with H.C. roundel); no distinctive badge or ensign for the Bechuanaland Protectorate.

wp-saint-louis.title: Saint-Louis, Senegal
wp-saint-louis.note: Wikipedia: the French moved their fort to the island of Ndar in 1659; nine chartered companies administered Saint-Louis 1659-1779.

fotw-bd-colon.title: British India (FOTW)
fotw-bd-colon.note: Contributor notes on British rule in India 1858-1947: the Union Jack with the Star of India insignia, Blue and Red Ensigns, and the Star of India badge; Admiralty warrant 1884 for the Indian marine ensign.

fotw-bd-benga.title: Bengal (British India)
fotw-bd-benga.note: Bengal flags from European flag charts of 1862 and 1868 (red scimitar between three red barrels on white) and an 1848/1862 chart showing a striped ensign with a Union Jack canton, similar to East India Company ensigns.

fotw-eic.title: East India Company (United Kingdom)
fotw-eic.note: Cites Wilson, Flags at Sea (1986/1999), Lens 1700, Rees 1820, Laurie, and Rowand, Naval and Maritime Flags of British India: striped ensign with a Union canton from 1707, the new Union flag from about 1801.

wp-flag-eic.title: Flag of the East India Company
wp-flag-eic.note: Infobox: horizontal red and white stripes with the Union Jack in the canton, adopted 1801, relinquished 1858.

fotw-bg-1878.title: Principality of Bulgaria, 1878-1908
fotw-bg-1878.note: Flags of the principality from Ivanov (1998) and Belov 1898; cites the 16 April 1879 constitution on the three-colour flag; naval ensign has a crowned lion in a red canton.

fotw-bg-1908.title: Kingdom of Bulgaria, 1908-1944: Royal Family
fotw-bg-1908.note: Royal standards of the kingdom from Bogoslovski 1912 and Ivanov (1998); says the kingdom flags were abandoned on 9 September 1944.

fotw-bg-1908n.title: Kingdom of Bulgaria, 1908-1944: Naval Flags
fotw-bg-1908n.note: Naval ensign of the kingdom described as the principality pattern with an established crown, per Bogoslovski 1912 and Flaggenbuch 1939.

fotw-bg-1944.title: Kingdom of Bulgaria, 1944-1946
fotw-bg-1944.note: Says the old flags became obsolete on 9 September 1944; reports a tricolour with the letters OF (Fatherland Front) used 1944-1947, from a 1955 atlas.

fotw-bg-18xx.title: Bulgaria: 19th-century flags
fotw-bg-18xx.note: Insurgent flags of the Ottoman period: the Freedom or Death flag in the Sofia War Museum and the 1876 April Uprising district flag.

fotw-bj-dah.title: Kingdom of Dahomey (FOTW)
fotw-bj-dah.note: Behanzin flag (light blue field, yellow shield with shark, egg and tusks, palm, snakes) captured at Abomey on 18 November 1892 and held in a Paris museum; engraving of King Ghezo with a different flag; Flag Bulletin 145 cited.

fotw-cm-hist.title: Historical flags of Cameroon (FOTW)
fotw-cm-hist.note: Solf's 1914 colonial flag proposals never implemented; German colonies used imperial flags; British Cameroons administered from Nigeria with only a proposed 1922 badge; 1919 division into French and British mandates.

fotw-de-col14-u6.title: Colonial Flags 1914 (Germany, FOTW)
fotw-de-col14-u6.note: Solf's 1914 drafts for colonial arms and flags, including Kamerun (elephant head), found in the Bundesarchiv in 2010 and never introduced; Kamerun 1884-February 1916.

fotw-de1867.title: North German Confederation 1867-1870 (FOTW)
fotw-de1867.note: Norman Martin's notes citing Article 55 of the constitution of 25 June 1867, the Imperial ordinance of 25 October 1867, the war ensign decree of 4 July 1867, Martin and Dreyhaupt (1999) and Znamierowski (1999).

fotw-de-roman.title: Holy Roman Empire 800-1806 (FOTW)
fotw-de-roman.note: Imperial banners: black eagle armed red on gold, double-headed from 1401; says the Empire had no national flag; cites Meyer's Lexikon 1897 and Norman Martin.

fotw-do-hist.title: Dominican Republic: Historical flags
fotw-do-hist.note: Trinitaria flag, the 1844 constitution article on the merchant flag, and the 1861-1865 Spanish rule with a red-white-yellow candidate flag; cites Corre (2001) and Estrade (1991) through contributors.

fotw-ht-hist.title: Haiti: Historical flags
fotw-ht-hist.note: Contributor history of Haitian flags: Petion's horizontal blue-red flag, Boyer's annexation of the Spanish part on 9 February 1822, Spanish Haiti 1821-22, the 1843 constitution confirming the horizontal flag.

wp-haitian-occupation.title: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo
wp-haitian-occupation.note: Narrative of the 1821 adoption of the Haitian flag by frontier towns and the unification of the island under the Haitian flag.

fotw-do-es.title: Santo Domingo Maritime Province 1863-1865 (Spain)
fotw-do-es.note: Single contributor note: province created 6 December 1862, blue-over-red swallow-tailed flag adopted 11 March 1863.

wp-roman-egypt.title: Roman Egypt
wp-roman-egypt.note: Egypt ruled as the imperial province of Aegyptus from the Roman conquest in 30 BC to AD 642.

whe-roman-egypt.title: Roman Egypt (World History Encyclopedia)
whe-roman-egypt.note: Article by Donald L. Wasson: Egypt became the property of Rome after the death of Cleopatra VII in 30 BCE, ending the Ptolemaic dynasty.

wp-ptolemaic.title: Ptolemaic Kingdom
wp-ptolemaic.note: Ruled by the Ptolemaic dynasty from Ptolemy I Soter until the death of Cleopatra VII in 30 BC, then conquered by Rome.

nml-ptolemy-tetradrachm.title: Currency/exchange; Coin; Tetradrachm (National Museums Liverpool)
nml-ptolemy-tetradrachm.note: Museum catalogue record of a coin of Ptolemy I Soter: diademed head with aegis on the obverse, an eagle with closed wings standing on a thunderbolt on the reverse; mint most likely Alexandria.

wp-serekh.title: Serekh
wp-serekh.note: Rectangular enclosure representing a palace facade, surmounted by the Horus falcon, setting apart the royal name; earliest such convention, dated back to the Gerzeh culture (c. 3400 BC), predating the cartouche by four dynasties.

livius-serekh.title: Serekh (Livius.org)
livius-serekh.note: Article by Jona Lendering (2017): the serekh as the first dynasties' main royal-name frame, topped by a falcon (probably Horus); Peribsen and Khasekhemwy varied it; Fourth Dynasty kings stressed cartouche names instead.

ees-crowns.title: The royal crowns of Egypt (Egypt Exploration Society)
ees-crowns.note: Learning resource of the learned society: Deshret, Hedjet, Pschent (double crown symbolising unification), Khepresh; Wadjet cobra on kings' foreheads; illustrated with named temple scenes of Ahmose and Seti I and museum numbers; notes no pharaoh's crown has been found.

carnegie-uraeus.title: Cobra Head from Decorative Panel (Uraeus), Carnegie Museum of Natural History
carnegie-uraeus.note: Museum catalogue entry, accession 7043-5, carved c. 1345-1347 BCE at Akhenaten's capital, bought from the Egypt Exploration Society in 1922: cobras represented Wadjet, a protective goddess connected to kingship, set into sun disk decorations.

wp-pschent.title: Pschent
wp-pschent.note: Double crown combining Hedjet and Deshret, representing the pharaoh's power over unified Egypt; attributed to Menes, first known on Djet; Palermo Stone gives it to First Dynasty and later pharaohs; no Pschent survives.

wp-fip.title: First Intermediate Period of Egypt
wp-fip.note: c. 2181-2055 BC, after the Old Kingdom; very little monumental evidence survives.

wp-sip.title: Second Intermediate Period of Egypt
wp-sip.note: Egypt divided into smaller dynasties between the Middle and New Kingdoms; Hyksos 15th Dynasty at Avaris.

wp-tip.title: Third Intermediate Period of Egypt
wp-tip.note: Begins with the death of Ramesses XI in 1077 BC; ends c. 664 BC with Psamtik I after the Kushite 25th Dynasty was driven out.

wp-late-period.title: Late Period of Egypt
wp-late-period.note: 664-332 BC: Saite 26th Dynasty and later native dynasties plus Achaemenid rule from 525 BC.

fotw-gq-1858.title: Spanish Guinea (1858-1959)
fotw-gq-1858.note: Colonial history from the Portuguese colonisation of 1474 and the 1778 cession; contributor statement (Candeias and Olle, 2001) that no flag existed for any Spanish colony; Governor General flag 1945-1968 and local pennants.

wp-spanish-guinea.title: Spanish Guinea
wp-spanish-guinea.note: Territories controlled by Spain from 1778 (Treaty of El Pardo with Portugal) to independence on 12 October 1968; province of the Gulf of Guinea from 1956.

fotw-su-kg.title: Kirgizian SSR (Soviet Union)
fotw-su-kg.note: Flag of the Kyrgyz SSR from 1952 with official proportions from the 1978 constitution; reverse side; coat of arms of 1937.

fotw-su-kg-h.title: Kyrgyzstan in the Soviet Union (early flags)
fotw-su-kg-h.note: No Kyrgyz flags in 1926-1936; a possible 1929 draft-constitution flag (vexillographia.ru says unknown if used); flags of 1937 and the 1940s with the name in Latin and Cyrillic letters.

fotw-su-cak.title: Central Asian Khanates and Turkestan
fotw-su-cak.note: Turkestan 1917-1924 flags from Flag Bulletin VIII:3 (1969) and contributor notes: Kokand autonomy, Basmachi, Soviet Republic of Turkestan 1918-1924.

fotw-ru-emp.title: Russian Empire (FOTW)
fotw-ru-emp.note: National and state flags of the Russian Empire: civil flag white-blue-red 1696-1917, black-orange-white 1858-1883, state flag 1883-1914.

fotw-mg-prot.title: Madagascar Protectorate (FOTW)
fotw-mg-prot.note: Protectorate flag 1885-1896 (blue-white-red with a red crescent) per W. Smith; the French protectorate ended on 29 September 1896 when Galliéni replaced the royal eagle on the palace with the French national flag (La Gazette de la Grande Ile, 2005).

fotw-mv-sul.title: Maldives: Sultanate until 1949
fotw-mv-sul.note: Quotes Crampton (1990) and Flaggenbuch for the old plain red flag, the red flag with a black-and-white hoist band and crescent, and the civil, state and festival flags.

fotw-mv-prot.title: Maldives: from protectorate to independence
fotw-mv-prot.note: Quotes Crampton (1990) on the 1953-54 republic, the 1954 restoration of the Sultan and the flags continuing to 1965; Sultan's flag 1954-1968; Harbour Master's ensign photographed in the 1950s.

fotw-ca-nf.title: History of the Flags of Newfoundland (FOTW)
fotw-ca-nf.note: David Prothero's notes citing Public Record Office documents (CO 60/38, CO 194/179, CO 854/7, DO 35/130/8) on governor's flags, the 1870 and 1904 badges, the 1918 Red Ensign, the 1931 National Flag Act, 1934 Commission, 1949 union and the 1952 statutes.

fotw-np-law.title: Nepal: law and construction details
fotw-np-law.note: Extracts of the Constitution of Nepal with the flag article and Schedule 1: Article 5 in the older constitution (labelled 1999 in the page), Article 8 of the 2015 constitution.

fotw-np-hist.title: Historical Nepalese flags (circa 1928)
fotw-np-hist.note: Flags from Perceval Landon, Nepal (1928): national flag of two red triangles with a green border and white faces on the crescent and sun; royal standard; Maharaja and army flags.

fotw-qa-his.title: Qatar: Historical Flags
fotw-qa-his.note: Overview by Jaume Olle (2000): plain red until about 1860, serrated white stripe from about 1860, c.1916 white flag, 1932/1936/1949/1971 versions; 1930s British letters in the Qatar Digital Library summarised by a contributor.

fotw-sb-1906.title: British Solomon Islands Protectorate c.1906-1947 (FOTW)
fotw-sb-1906.note: David Prothero's notes: Blue Ensign badge BRITISH SOLOMON ISLANDS around a crown, c.1906/1908-1947, first seen in a c.1909 amendment to the Admiralty Flag Book of 1907; Resident Commissioner's B.R. ensign c.1902-1947; sources Flags of Maritime Nations 1914 and Znamierowski 1999.

fotw-sb-1947.title: British Solomon Islands Protectorate 1947-1956 (FOTW)
fotw-sb-1947.note: Badge replaced in 1947 when arms were granted (10 March 1947): red shield with a turtle on a white circle, replaced in 1956 (arms of 24 September 1956); Gresham Carr 1953 and a district commissioner's memoir of 1954.

fotw-sb-1956.title: British Solomon Islands Protectorate 1956-1966 (FOTW)
fotw-sb-1956.note: Blue Ensign 1956-1966 after Znamierowski (1999); no description beyond the image.

fotw-gb-sc-rb.title: Royal Banner of Scotland (FOTW)
fotw-gb-sc-rb.note: Royal arms blazon and legal status; first known lion rampant on the 1222 seal of Alexander II, double tressure first certain on a seal of Alexander III; cites Fox-Davies and Innes of Learney through contributors.

wp-royal-banner-sct.title: Royal Banner of Scotland
wp-royal-banner-sct.note: Earliest recorded use of the lion rampant as a royal emblem by Alexander II in 1222; double border added under Alexander III (1249-1286); use restricted by Act of the Parliament of Scotland.

fotw-gb-s-ori.title: Legendary Origin of the Scottish flag (FOTW)
fotw-gb-s-ori.note: Athelstaneford legend with quotations from Fordun, Boece (Bellenden 1531), Leslie, Spottiswoode and Bower; Nick Groom's account dating the story to a lost source of c.1165 and the battle to 832.

wp-athelstaneford.title: Athelstaneford
wp-athelstaneford.note: Village article: the legend of the 832 battle, Saint Andrew's vision to Pictish King Oengus II and the white cross in the sky.

fotw-th-his.title: Historical Flags of Thailand (FOTW)
fotw-th-his.note: Chronological overview citing Crampton 1991-1992 and Poels 1990, and a contributor's summary of The History of Thai Flags (Fine Arts Department of Thailand, 1977): plain red 1680, chakra 1782, elephant 1817, 1855, 1916, 1917.

fotw-tt-col.title: Colonial and Pre-republican Flags (Trinidad and Tobago)
fotw-tt-col.note: Notes by David Prothero and others: Blue Ensign badge introduced 1875 for Trinidad, extended to Trinidad and Tobago in 1889, replaced by a shield version in 1958; no official Red Ensign.

fotw-tt-tob.title: Tobago (FOTW)
fotw-tt-tob.note: Tobago's ownership 1632-1814, separate colony until 1888/89, blue ensign with its own badge from 1876/1877; contributor notes (Olle, Prothero).

wp-hist-tt.title: History of Trinidad and Tobago
wp-hist-tt.note: Columbus 1498; Trinidad Spanish until the 1797 British capture; Tobago British after the 1814 Treaty of Paris; the islands united in 1889; independence 1962.

fotw-ye-north.title: North Yemen
fotw-ye-north.note: Flag hoisted 1 November 1962 (UAR flag with one star removed); notes the 22 May 1990 union removing the star; royalist forces 1962-1970.

fotw-ye-south.title: South Yemen
fotw-ye-south.note: Flag introduced about 30 November 1967: tricolour with a light blue hoist triangle bearing a red star; history of the Federation of South Arabia.

fotw-ye-kingd.title: Kingdom of Yemen (1918-1962)
fotw-ye-kingd.note: Flag adopted 1927 (red with white sabre and five stars) from National Geographic 1951 and 1961; in use until 1962, royalists to 1970; imam's flag red with the shahada.

fotw-ye-brit.title: Yemen under British Rule
fotw-ye-brit.note: Colony and Protectorate of Aden before 1959; Aden a dependency of British India until 1937; Federation of South Arabia 1959-67.

fotw-ye-caden.title: Colony of Aden
fotw-ye-caden.note: Aden Colony flag in use until 18 January 1963; 1 April 1937 change from Indian Empire settlement to Crown colony; dhow badge by George Kruger-Gray.

fotw-bt-his.title: Bhutan: History of the national flag
fotw-bt-his.note: Quotes the on-line book "The Origin and Description of the National Flag and Anthem of the Kingdom of Bhutan" and Sonam Kinga, Polity, Kingship and Democracy: the 1949 treaty flag and the 1956 white-dragon version.

fotw-bt-2flag.title: Bhutan: change to the second version of the flag
fotw-bt-2flag.note: Timeline of the 1949, 1956, late 1950s and 1968/1969 versions, with printed flag-book evidence (Observer's Book 1966 and 1971, Kannik 1956, Pedersen 1970).

fotw-kh-hstry.title: Cambodian Flag History
fotw-kh-hstry.note: Based on a Flag Bulletin article (no. 133) and Flaggenbuch: flags from c.1863 to 1993 with dates; text by M. Schmoger, 2001, plus later contributor additions.

fotw-cl-hist.title: Chile: Historical flags
fotw-cl-hist.note: Patria Vieja (1812-1814), the Spanish flags of the Reconquista (1814-1816), the 1817 Transition flag and the Patria Nueva flag of 18 October 1817; quotes Gobierno de Chile Emblemas Patrios.

fotw-ee-histo.title: Estonia: History of the Flag
fotw-ee-histo.note: Contributor texts: the blue-black-white flag from 1881-1884 student societies, the 1918 and 1922 decisions, the 1940 ban; nothing on the pre-1881 periods.

fotw-gr-evna2.title: Greece: History of the national flag, part 2 (1828-1970)
fotw-gr-evna2.note: Citing the book Hellenic flags: two national flags (cross-and-stripes at sea, plain cross on land) used unchanged 1832-1970; crown flags of the Kingdom 1832-1924 and 1935-1970, all abolished in 1970.

fotw-gr-evna3.title: Greece: History of the national flag, part 3 (1970 until today)
fotw-gr-evna3.note: Dates 18 August 1970 (7:12 cross-and-stripes becomes national flag), June 1975 (plain cross sole flag), 22 December 1978.

fotw-gr-wwii.title: Greece during the Second World War
fotw-gr-wwii.note: Koukidis and the Acropolis flag, 27 April 1941; occupation-zone ship pennants flown under the Greek flag (order of 10 April 1943, citing Herzfeld).

fotw-gr-ottom.title: Greece under Ottoman rule
fotw-gr-ottom.note: Ottoman national and merchant flags; the Greek merchant ensign (red with blue central stripe); Rigas flag of 1797.

fotw-gt-hist.title: Guatemala: Historical Flags
fotw-gt-hist.note: Contributor posts citing Crampton (1990), Flagmaster, Le Gras (1858) and deguate.com: flags of 1823-1825, 1825, 1843, 1851, 1858 and 1871 with decree dates.

fotw-cam-us.title: Central America: Historical Unions and Federations
fotw-cam-us.note: Contributor posts quoting Crampton (1990) on the 1823 federal flag and a vdiest.nl timeline: incorporation into Mexico 5 January 1822, independence again 1 July 1823, federation to 1841.

fotw-gy-hist.title: Guyana: Historical Flags
fotw-gy-hist.note: Contributor posts (Prothero, Grieve, Sensen) on British Guiana: Blue Ensign with a ship badge from 1875, badge changes 1906 and 1954; red ensign unofficial and doubtful; the three Dutch colonies became British in 1814 and one colony later.

wp-berbice.title: Berbice
wp-berbice.note: Infobox shows the Dutch West India Company flag (1627-1792) and the Union Jack (1803-); no tricolour.

wp-demerara.title: Demerara
wp-demerara.note: Infobox shows the Dutch West India Company flag and the Union Jack for the colony.

fotw-hi-hi.title: Historical flags of Hawaii
fotw-hi-hi.note: Contributor posts: a chronology 1794-1959 summarising Quaife et al. (1961), a quoted Polynesian newspaper of 31 May 1845, and a list of variant versions in older flag charts.

wp-republic-hi.title: Republic of Hawaii
wp-republic-hi.note: Notes the ceremony of 12 August 1898 when the Flag of Hawaii was lowered over Iolani Palace and the US flag raised.

fotw-lr-1827.title: Liberian flag in 1827-1847
fotw-lr-1827.note: Contributor quotes the American Colonization Society resolution of 9 April 1827 (flag for the colony) and Smith (1980) on the cross flag used until 26 July 1847.

fotw-lr-pr.title: Liberia: Governmental flags
fotw-lr-pr.note: Presidential flags; a 2003 contributor note that German TV showed the national flag beside the presidential flag behind Charles Taylor.

fotw-mx-his.title: Mexico: Historic Evolution of the National Flag
fotw-mx-his.note: Chart and text by Villascan citing Mexican government and museum sources; New Spain used Spain's flags and arms.

fotw-mx-1821.title: Mexico: Flag from 1821-1823 (Mexican Empire)
fotw-mx-1821.note: Decrees of 2 November 1821 and 7 January 1822 (quoted), abolished 14 April 1823; crowned eagle on the white stripe; coronation 21 July 1822.

fotw-mx-1823.title: Mexico: Flag from 1823-1880
fotw-mx-1823.note: Decree of 14 April 1823 removing the crown; in force until 1968; Juarez government used it during the Second Empire and restored it on 15 July 1867.

fotw-mx-1863.title: Mexico: Flag from 1863-1867 (Second Mexican Empire)
fotw-mx-1863.note: Imperial flag adopted 18 June 1864, confirmed 1 November 1865 at 1:2, abolished 15 July 1867; quotes the 1 November 1865 decree on the imperial arms.

fotw-mx-1880.title: Mexico: Flag from 1880-1916
fotw-mx-1880.note: Revisions of the 1823 flag and arms in 1880 and 1899.

fotw-mx-1916.title: Mexico: Venustiano Carranza's flag (1916-1934)
fotw-mx-1916.note: Decree of 20 September 1916, in effect 1 October 1916; arms approved 22 August 1918; in use until 5 February 1934.

fotw-es-1506.title: Spain: Historical Flags 1506-1700
fotw-es-1506.note: Burgundy Cross flag as Spain's main ship symbol from Charles I (1518) to Charles II (1665) and its naval ensign 1506-1701.

fotw-nz-hist2.title: Historical flags of New Zealand: United Tribes flag choice (1834)
fotw-nz-hist2.note: Quotes Busby's despatch of 26 March 1834 on the vote of 25 chiefs on 20 March 1834 between three flags (votes 3, 10 and 12).

fotw-nz-hist3.title: Historical flags of New Zealand: Flag of the United Tribes (1835-1840)
fotw-nz-hist3.note: Gazetted version of 1835; original 1834 drawing with eight-pointed stars and black fimbriation; replaced by the Union Jack on 6 February 1840 (quoting Cayley 1966).

fotw-nz-hist4.title: Historical flags of New Zealand: Origins of the New Zealand Flag (1840-1898)
fotw-nz-hist4.note: David Prothero's outline 1840-1903 from Admiralty and Gazette sources: Union Jack 1840, NZ blue ensign 1867, Southern Cross ensign gazetted 23 October 1869, Ensign Act assent March 1902.

fotw-nz-hist5.title: Historical flags of New Zealand: Origins of the New Zealand Flag (1898-1903)
fotw-nz-hist5.note: Prothero on the signalling ensigns of 1899-1900 and the New Zealand Ensign Act 1901: assent 24 March 1902, proclamation gazetted 12 June 1902.

fotw-pl-ug.title: Polish underground state (WWII)
fotw-pl-ug.note: Contributor text: the legal symbols of the government in exile and its Delegation were those of the Second Republic; the Home Army anchor flag was used in the 1944 Warsaw Uprising.

fotw-pl-gg.title: General Government (German occupation 1939-1944)
fotw-pl-gg.note: Contributor text: the General Government had no flag of its own; German swastika flags flew in Warsaw, Cracow and Lwow and the Polish flag was forbidden on pain of death.

fotw-pl-xx.title: Poland: 20th century flags
fotw-pl-xx.note: Contributor text: the eagle was crowned from 1295 or slightly earlier, and the government in exile and its troops in WWII kept the crowned eagle.

fotw-pl-xix.title: Poland: 19th century flags
fotw-pl-xix.note: Contributor posts on the Duchy of Warsaw, the Congress Kingdom flag of 1815-1831 and the white-red bicolour of the 1831 Sejm; no basis cited beyond the posters.

fotw-pl-royal.title: Polish royal banners
fotw-pl-royal.note: Banners from Wladyslaw Lokietek to Stanislaw August Poniatowski, drawn by Adam Kromer; little text, and the 1553 court banner of Zygmunt August is the oldest kept in Poland.

fotw-ru-h.title: Soviet Russia (1917-1923) and early flags of Russia in the Soviet Union (1923-1954)
fotw-ru-h.note: Contributor posts citing Order No 320 of April 1918, the flag approved on 20 May 1918, the constitution of July 1918 and later decrees; initials in yellow Cyrillic in the canton.

fotw-ru-su.title: Russia in the Soviet Union (later flags)
fotw-ru-su.note: RSFSR flag revised in 1954 with a light-blue hoist bar of one eighth the flag length (constitution of 1978 quoted); two 1954-1955 patterns.

fotw-su.title: Soviet Union
fotw-su.note: Contributor note that the hammer, sickle and star flag was adopted in 1923, with a red star bordered yellow, not in 1918.

fotw-ru-tzar.title: Tsar's Personal Flags

era-1945.says: A royal decree of 19 February 1937, no. 93, fixed the colours of the flag of the Kingdom as red, white and blue; FOTW and Wikipedia both quote it that way. The Royal House says the colours were bright vermilion and cobalt blue.
era-1945.open: The sources disagree on the shade: FOTW dates 'bright vermilion and cobalt blue' to 1958, while the Royal House page gives that wording as the decree's own. The decree text itself has not been read. The hex swatches on this page are approximations, not a specification.

era-1940.says: FOTW, citing Poels in Vexilla Nostra 198 (1995), says the tricolour stayed the national flag but its use was restricted by the occupiers. NOS reports that from 1940 any demonstrative act for the House of Orange was punishable. Wikipedia (Reichskommissariat Niederlande): 1940-1945, the Reichskommissariat's infobox flag is the German Reich flag. Neerlandia (1957): during the occupation friends of the occupier often used the orange-white-blue as the Dutch flag, devaluing the old Prince's flag.
era-1940.open: The Reich flag as the occupier's flag and the tricolour remaining nominally the national flag under restriction are both stated, but no ordinance was found, so which restrictions fell on the tricolour and when is not established; no source supports a ban in 1943. The page's drawing is the occupier's flag, schematically.

era-1830.says: FOTW (nl.html): the red-white-blue tricolour was the flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands 1813-1940; the flag was adopted formally only by Order in Council of 19 February 1937 (no earlier law). Wikipedia (Flag of the Netherlands): the 1937 decree states 'The colours of the flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands are red, white and blue' and was prompted by orange-white-blue flags promoted by the NSB. Wikipedia (United Kingdom of the Netherlands): the Belgian Revolution broke out 25 August 1830, Belgium declared independence 4 October 1830 and the Dutch recognised it on 19 April 1839; the article says nothing about the flag.
era-1830.open: No source states that the flag was unchanged through the 1830 secession or describes its status 1830-1937; the continuity rests on FOTW's one-line statement that the tricolour was the kingdom's flag from 1813 to 1940.

era-1813.says: Wikipedia reports 1813 newspapers describing red-white-blue flags with orange pennants and solid orange flags, and says the question of the national flag was left undecided; its statement that William preferred red-white-blue is marked 'citation needed' there. The Royal House confirms independence returned in 1813 but says nothing about the flag. FOTW: the red-white-blue tricolour was the flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (1813-1940 and 1945-now) and the southern Netherlands were united with it 1815-1830. Wikipedia (United Kingdom of the Netherlands): kingdom 1815-1839 with the Flag of the Netherlands as infobox flag. Neerlandia (1957): in 1813 both red-white-blue and orange-white-blue flew from the gables.
era-1813.open: The tricolour's use is attested by several sources, but the formal national status was undecided in 1813 per Wikipedia and no source describes an 1815 decree; FOTW notes there is no law before the 1937 decree. The page's 'treaty-built union of three countries' is not examined.

era-1810.says: The Royal House says the Netherlands was annexed by France in 1810 and the national flag was replaced by the French imperial standard. Wikipedia says the national flag was replaced by imperial emblems in 1810, without a citation there.
era-1810.open: Which French flag flew on Dutch buildings is not established; 'imperial standard' may not be the plain tricolour drawn here. Wikipedia's own Kingdom of Holland page gives the annexation date inconsistently.

era-1806.says: The tricolour continued under Louis Bonaparte. Wikipedia dates the flag without the Maiden to 5 June 1806 (no citation there), records naval crews rioting over the flag in August 1806 and a royal decree of 1 December 1807 affirming the Statenvlag for the navy (both citing de Jonge, 1831). FOTW says Louis proposed adding quartered arms to the navy's flag and withdrew the proposal when the navy would not accept it.
era-1806.open: The 5 June 1806 date has no primary source behind it in either reference. The motive this page used to state ('a deliberate choice to present continuity') had no source and was removed.

era-1795.says: Dirk Langendijk's design in the Rijksmuseum shows the Dutch Maiden and the Lion holding a spear topped with a liberty cap, in the upper-left corner of the existing flag, for the Batavian navy, effective 1 March 1796. FOTW, citing Wilson (1986, p. 60), puts the decree altering the navy's flags (not the merchant flags) on 14 February 1796; the States General publication Wikipedia cites carries the same date.
era-1795.open: The emblem was on the navy's flag only. Its removal in 1806 is Wikipedia's, without a citation. FOTW also describes a tricolour 'with a small white canton' (credited to Roy Stilling, 1996), which we have not reconciled with the Maiden emblem. This page used to describe a 'canton with a liberty cap used briefly 1795-96'; that is not what the sources show.

era-1650.says: Red replaced orange gradually. Wikipedia places the transition between about 1630 and 1660, with red appearing as early as 1596-97 (its infobox and text differ), the name Statenvlag in 1664 (de Jonge, 1833, p. 75) and the navy always flying it after 1663 (de Waard, 1900). The Royal House says red gradually replaced orange during the 17th century because orange is less visible at sea. Wikipedia gives the Republic's distance from the House of Orange as the reason.
era-1650.open: No decree for the change was found, so 'c. 1650' is the midpoint of a transition, not an event. This page used to say the flag flew over the VOC and WIC fleets, New Amsterdam and Batavia; no source for that was found and it was removed.

era-1581.says: Orange-white-blue is attested from the 1570s. Wikipedia cites Rey (1837) for use by the Prince of Orange then, Jacob Duym for officers' brassards at the siege of Leiden in 1574, an order of the Admiralty of Zeeland of 1587 for naval flags in these colours, and de Waard (1900) for the navy flying it from 1588 to 1630. The Royal House dates the first reference to 1572; FOTW says it was used from the second half of the 16th century and named for William of Orange.
era-1581.open: Wikipedia calls it uncertain whether the Sea Beggars carried the colours at Den Briel in 1572, so this page no longer says it flew from the Sea Beggars onward. The era starts at the Act of Abjuration (1581), not at the flag's first appearance. The earliest colour image, of 1575 in Jan van Hout's album, is on Wikipedia without a reference we could read.

era-1433.says: The Cross of Burgundy was the emblem of the Burgundian dukes (Hutchinson, 2007, as cited on Wikipedia). It is drawn here as the emblem, not as a flag of the northern provinces.
era-1433.open: Its use as a flag across the Habsburg Netherlands after 1477 is stated on Wikipedia without a citation and has not been confirmed.

era-1000.says: No single polity existed, so there is no flag to attest; the maroon field is a placeholder.

era-50bce.says: Tacitus (Histories 4.22) describes the force under Civilis following images of wild beasts brought out of woods and sacred groves, and names the Batavian elite and 'German allies'. He describes no flag.
era-50bce.open: This page used to say Tacitus records Batavian and Frisian war-standards; the passage names the Batavians and unnamed German allies, not the Frisii.

era-15.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Afghanistan): the Islamic Emirate flag, a white field with the black shahada, was reinstated on 15 August 2021 after the Taliban victory; a variant carries 'Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan' in Pashto beneath. FOTW: the Taliban flag flew at the Kunduz border crossing on 8 August 2021 with the shahada much larger than the 1996-2001 flag and an extra inscription below; its historical index lists 'Since August 2021' as a separate period.
era-15.open: Neither source says the 2021 flag is identical to the 1997-2001 one: FOTW notes a larger shahada and added inscription, so 'readopted unchanged' is not supported. Wikipedia's adoption dates are 27 October 1997 and 15 August 2021; FOTW's own date for the current flag (4 January 2004) is the tricolour's. The 15 August 2021 date is Wikipedia's; FOTW shows the flag in use from 8 August.

era-550bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — two millennia of successive outside empires».
era-550bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-2001.says: Both: a black-red-green tricolour with the national emblem, 2004. Wikipedia: restored 28 January 2002, 2004 version used from 9 October 2004 to 15 August 2021 (2013 latest version). FOTW: 4 January 2004 tricolour, 2:3, bearing 1298 AH.
era-2001.open: The mosque-and-wheat emblem content and the shahada placement on this page are not covered; the two sources differ on the 2004 day (4 January vs 9 October).

era-27.says: Wikipedia: plain white banner 27 September 1996 to 26 October 1997; black shahada on white 26 October 1997 to 13 November 2001. FOTW 'Afghanistan 1996-2001': after the Taliban took Kabul in 1996 the flag was 'at least initially' a plain white banner; the black-on-white shahada flag was adopted 27 October 1997 (Reuters, 26 October 1997, on the change of name to Islamic Emirate; a Taliban source says 25 October) and abolished in 2001; FOTW's historical index lists 'September 1996 - November 2001: white flag, at times with the Shahada in black'.
era-27.open: The black shahada date differs by a day or two (25, 26 or 27 October 1997 across the sources). A Flag Bulletin report of a green shahada is called probably mistaken. The symbolism stated earlier on the page is not covered by either source.

era-28.says: Wikipedia: a provisional flag 27 April to 6 December 1992, then the Rabbani government's flag with the shahada and the year 1298 on the emblem, 7 December 1992 to 27 January 2002, in Northern Alliance areas after 1996. FOTW: a provisional green-white-black flag with white lettering on the green stripe and black on the white (April-December 1992, citing Baert 2001), then from 2 December 1992 'three horizontal stripes of green, white, black with the coat of arms over all in the centre' in gold, used by the Northern Alliance to 2001.
era-28.open: The adoption date of the emblem flag is 2 December 1992 in FOTW and 7 December in Wikipedia; FOTW's note that the emblem carries the date 1371 differs from Wikipedia's mention of 1298 on the later emblem. Neither source says this design is the ancestor of the 2004 flag, and the page's colour symbolism is not covered.

era-27-1.says: Wikipedia: tricolour without seal 27 April to 18 October 1978; a red flag with a yellow seal 19 October 1978 to 21 April 1980; the tricolour returned 22 April 1980 under Babrak Karmal until 29 November 1987. FOTW: the republican flag without emblem after April 1978 (Baert 2001); a red flag with a gold emblem of script, wreath and star, 'October 1978 - April 1980' (decree of 18 October 1978); a black-red-green flag with an emblem released 21 April 1980; the same stripes with a new emblem from 30 November 1987 to 1992.
era-27-1.open: The red flag with the gold emblem drawn on the page was in use only from October 1978 to April 1980; from 1980 to 1992 both sources show a black-red-green tricolour. The official colour meanings and the end date in April 1992 are given by FOTW only in passing.

era-17.says: Wikipedia: the republic's flag was identical to the monarchy flag except for the removed year, 17 July 1973 to 8 May 1974; from 9 May 1974 to 26 April 1978 a new seal with a golden eagle, minbar, wheat and sun rays. FOTW (citing Baert 2001): the 1973 flag was the 1930-73 flag without the date; a Republican flag was introduced on 9 May 1974, three horizontal black-red-green stripes with a yellow eagle-and-wheat arms on the canton.
era-17.open: FOTW describes the 1973 flag as probably still carrying the monarchy emblem minus the date, so the eagle emblem of the page's drawing belongs only to 9 May 1974 to April 1978. The 'continuity of national colours' rationale is not covered.

era-1919.says: Wikipedia: the 1919 flag had no tricolour; the tricolour came about 1928 and the final monarchy flag, with a wheat emblem and the year 1348, is dated 27 March 1931 to 16 July 1973. FOTW: Amanullah's 1919 flag was a black field with the new arms (eight-pointed rays, an oval in 1921); a vertical black-red-green flag followed in 1928; the flag adopted on 31 October 1931 (three stripes, mosque and wheat arms, date 1348) served until 1973.
era-1919.open: The tricolour with the mosque-and-wheat emblem that the page draws belongs to 1931-1973; from 1919 to 1928 the flag was black, and the years 1928-1931 saw several changes. Wikipedia dates the 1931 flag to 27 March, FOTW to 31 October (the constitution). The page's colour meanings are not supported by either source.

era-1747.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Afghanistan): a black field is attributed to the Hotak dynasty, the last solid black flag was under Abdur Rahman Khan. Wikipedia (Emirate of Afghanistan): the first arms on a flag, a solid black banner with a white emblem in the centre, came under Abdur Rahman Khan; under Dost Mohammad and Sher Ali the state flags are described as triangular, red and green, with the shahada in white. Wikipedia (Durrani Empire): its infobox shows two Durrani flags dated 1747-1801/1803-1809/1839-1842 and 1801-1803/1809-1818, but the text read gives no design. FOTW: black became the national colour under Abdul Rahman (1880-1901); the 1901-1919 flag was a black field with the royal arms in white.
era-1747.open: The plain black field with a white emblem is documented only from Abdur Rahman's reign (1880-1901) and the 1901-1919 flag, not for the Durrani period of 1747-1818 or for the red-and-green flags described for the mid-19th century. No source read describes the Durrani flag's design, so the page's Durrani-era black standard is unsupported.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia: the Assembly voted on 7 April 1992 to remove the communist emblem and golden star, and the flag is the black double-headed eagle on red. Flags of the World (main page) also dates the removal to 7 April 1992. FOTW's communist-period page (1946-1992) describes no 1991 or 1992 change.
era-1991.open: All three readings give 1992, not 1991, for the plain eagle flag; the page's era start of 1991 and the caption 'unchanged since 1912' are not supported (Wikipedia and FOTW show different designs in 1912-1914, 1928-1943 and 1946-1992). Not checked: any source dating a 1991 change, and the NATO and EU dates.

era-1190.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — fragmented medieval principalities, no unified banner».
era-1190.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-400bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — Illyrian tribal kingdoms and Roman/Byzantine provincial rule, no unified banner».
era-400bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: in early 1946 a gold star was placed above the eagle; Law 5506 of 28 December 1976 describes a red five-pointed star embroidered in gold, designed by Sadik Kaceli. FOTW: in 1946 a red five-pointed star with gold border was placed above the eagle's heads. Both give removal on 7 April 1992.
era-1946.open: Page said the star went 'the moment the single-party state ended'; sources date removal to 1992.

era-1944.says: Flags of the World's partisan page: a provisional autonomous government (September 1943) used the pre-occupation flag with a yellow star in the canton; the Democratic Government was proclaimed 10 October 1944, flags with the yellow star stayed in use while others had a hammer and sickle; at the 29 November 1944 liberation festivities in Tirana the plain eagle flag was used with no star. Wikipedia: the Democratic Government's flag was first published in War Bulletin no. 51 of 28 November 1944 and used at public events and military courts until 1946; its section describes no star (a golden star above the eagle appears only in early 1946).
era-1944.open: Only Flags of the World describes the star (yellow, in the canton); Wikipedia's section is silent on a star, so the main claim 'eagle flag with a star added' rests on one publisher. The flag Wikipedia shows for 1944-46 is not described in its text. FOTW and the page's black-outlined star above the eagle disagree: that is the 7 March 1946 constitutional flag, not the 1944 one.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: in October 1943 the union with Italy was dissolved, the country reverted to the decrees of September 1928, and pre-Italian flags and symbols were used. Flags of the World's German-occupation page: after the German occupation (26 September 1943) the National Assembly re-established the 1928 monarchical constitution on 20 October 1943; the flags of the earlier regime were readopted and the Savoy crown and the Lieutenant's flag were abolished; the emblem is a black double-headed eagle (Fachinger: shifted toward the hoist). Both are Wikipedia and FOTW, two publishers.
era-1943.open: Neither source gives an exact design: whether the Zog-era crown or Skanderbeg helmet was restored is not stated (FOTW says 'flags of 1939' readopted, which contradicts the Savoy-crown abolition); the page's 'no crown or party symbol' is an inference. FOTW's account rests on Ollé (1996) and an observer.

era-1939.says: Wikipedia: a fascist flag replaced Zog's on 4 December 1939; the 1940 yearbook says the flag is red with the black double-headed eagle and the sign of the lictor's fasces at the centre. Flags of the World: the Italian-union kingdom's flag was adopted 13 April 1939 (constitution of 3 June 1939: red with the double-headed eagle in the centre); Royal Decrees 141-142 of 28 September 1939 added the Skanderbeg helmet, fasces and Savoy ribbons; the state flag was used 3 June 1939 to 25 July 1943.
era-1939.open: The sources put the fasces in the arms or at the centre of the eagle, not a small fasces beneath it as the page's caption says; the two sources also differ on the start date (13 April / 3 June vs 4 December 1939). FOTW notes a May 1942 'flag unrest' that brought back the Zog-era flag in part.

era-1928.says: Wikipedia: the 1928 Fundamental Statute (art. III) describes a red flag with a black double-headed eagle in the centre; versions shown for 1928-1934 and 1934-1939. Flags of the World's Kingdom page: Zogu proclaimed King on 1 September 1928, constitution 22 November 1928, flags approved 3 August 1929 and made official by Royal Legislative Decree no. 178 of 8 August 1929 (a state flag with a black eagle, 1:1 eagle, 2:3 flag; royal standard square with two golden branches below the eagle).
era-1928.open: Crown versus helmet is unresolved: the FOTW main page says the eagle was surmounted by Skanderbeg's gold helmet as a royal crown, Wikipedia mentions a crown only in its introduction, and FOTW's Kingdom sub-pages describe neither (only tagging a helmet). The caption's helmet is therefore not established; the red field with black eagle under Zog is.

era-1925.says: Flags of the World's republic page: 'On 25 January 1925 a national assembly proclaimed a republic and the national flag was not modified'; the flag of the republic dates from a 20 January 1920 statute, a black double-headed eagle on red; a 1926 presidential standard has Skanderbeg's golden helmet on the eagle. Wikipedia: the republic's flag was always shown square and first appears in Teki Selenica's 1927 guidebook; images are labelled 1925-1928.
era-1925.open: FOTW dates the flag's design to 1920 and the republic's proclamation to 25 January 1925; Wikipedia gives no design text for 1925-28 beyond the square shape. The caption's 'without a royal crest' is consistent, but the 1926 presidential standard carried a helmet.

era-1914.says: Flags of the World's Principality page: the 1914 flag is the former flag with the eagle's beak and claws yellow and a yellow thunderbolt; the Prince's standard is square with a crown in place of the star and a peacock escutcheon; Wied landed at Durres on 7 March 1914 and left on 3 September 1914; Essad Pasha's rebels sought reincorporation into Turkey; the page does not cover 1915-1925. Wikipedia: Essad Pasha's flag was light red with a white star polygon (letter of 7 May 1915); a 1915 flag from Durres is in a museum; Korce flag 1916-1920; the surviving 1920 Lushnje flag is dark red with a black eagle.
era-1914.open: The two publishers describe different flags and details (FOTW: yellow-clawed eagle, white star, thunderbolt; Wikipedia: unsourced principality section, star variants, gold star on the surviving flag). The caption's 'same eagle flag claimed by rival governments' is contradicted for Essad Pasha's star flag; 1915-1925 is covered only by Wikipedia.

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: the flag raised at Vlore on 28 November 1912 left no surviving trace and there is 'no definitive proof' of its appearance; a 1913 postcard model and Kristo Floqi's 1937 letter (thin red cloth, black double-headed eagle) are cited and the accounts conflict; a 17 December 1912 New York weekly cover shows the Provisional Government's flag, resembling a March 1914 cover. Flags of the World: Flag Day is 28 November; its Principality page says the 1914 flag is 'based on the former Albanian flag' but describes no 1912 flag.
era-1912.open: The design of the 1912 flag is supported only by Wikipedia (a model and later memoirs); FOTW does not describe it and does not link it to Skanderbeg. Not read: any scholarly source on the Vlore flag.

era-1479.says: Wikipedia: the Ottoman Latin merchant flag (1453-1793) appears as an image only; a red eagle flag was raised for the first time in possibly 400 years at Deciq on 6 April 1911 by Ded Gjo Luli. Flags of the World's Albania page: the Ottomans took Kruje on 16 June 1478; it describes no Ottoman-era Albanian flag. Wikipedia's article on the Ottoman flag (read) says the red crescent-and-star flag was official from 1844 and shows a Rumelia Eyalet flag, but does not discuss Albania.
era-1479.open: No source read states that the Ottoman state flag was the flag of the Albanian vilayets or that they had none of their own; the red-with-crescent state flag dates (1793 navy, 1844 national) cover only the later part of the era. Not found: a source on pashalik or vilayet flags.

era-1444.says: Flags of the World: on 28 November 1443 Skanderbeg 'raised the red flag with the black double-headed eagle'; Marin Barleti (c. 1508-1510) described the family emblem as a double-headed eagle on red; the modern flag 'is said to have been the flag of Skanderbeg'; the helmet with a goat's head is tied to Durand-Monti's Albanie (1990). Wikipedia: Skanderbeg adopted a flag like the Eastern Roman flag, a double-headed eagle on red, cited to Mucha, Crampton and Louda (1985); the League of Lezhe used it; Elsie (2010) hedges 'also said to have been'; a 1556 Veronese painting is read as showing him with the flag.
era-1444.open: Both publishers hedge: the attribution rests on tradition, one cited book on Wikipedia, and Barleti's later description; no contemporary banner survives. The date differs (FOTW 28 November 1443 with Free Principality; Wikipedia 1443 after Nis), and the goat-horned helmet crest is FOTW-only, from a 1990 book.

era-1962.says: Both sources give 1962, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 3 July 1962; Flags of the World dates it 3 July 1962.
era-1962.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-900.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — successive Berber and Arab dynasties».
era-900.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-202bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — Numidia, Roman/Vandal/Byzantine rule, and the Arab conquest».
era-202bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Algeria): the official flag was the French flag (the invasion began under the white Bourbon flag, then the tricolour was adopted); a striped merchant ensign was used 1848-1910 and green-and-white star-and-crescent nationalist flags from the 1930s and in 1945. FOTW (French Colonial Empire): Algeria was considered integrated French territory, depending on the Minister of the Interior, and the French flag 'seems to have been the only national flag flying there'. Wikipedia (List of Algerian flags): a seven-stripe ensign of French Algeria with the French colours whose exact rules and years of use are unknown.
era-1830.open: FOTW qualifies its statement with 'seems', and both sources show subsidiary flags (the striped ensign, the ensign prescribed in 1875, nationalist flags from the 1920s-30s), so the French flag was the national flag but not literally the only flag.

era-1516.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Algeria), citing al-Jilali: plain red flags, 'devoid of any symbol', were the Regency's main emblem, unlike Ottoman flags with a crescent and star; a green-yellow-red tricolour is reported for 1516 and a red-yellow-green striped flag in a 1551 atlas. Wikipedia (List of Algerian flags): a solid red flag for the Dey (18th century) and red-and-yellow striped Odjak flags captured by the French. FOTW (Regency of Algiers): apart from the deys' elaborate personal standards 'the flag in use in the country was the Ottoman flag'; before 1830 ship flags were white over black; a red flag with a white head is reported as the Dey's standard; a French writer's green standard with a gold crescent may be an error.
era-1516.open: The sources disagree: Wikipedia says the Regency used plain red flags unlike the Ottoman crescent-and-star flag, while FOTW's contributor says the Ottoman flag flew in the Regency, and neither dates any flag to 1516 with certainty. The red field with white crescent and star drawn on the page is supported only by FOTW's general reference to the Ottoman flag.

era-1866.says: Wikipedia: the civil vertical tricolour dates from 1866 (reforms adopted 22 April 1866 by Bishop Caixal), arms added to the vertical flag around 1939, standardised by the 1993 Constitution. Flags of the World (historical flags): 'In 1866 Napoleon III obtained the inclusion of the blue'; talocci (1993) says the tricolour replaced the yellow-red flag in 1866; a horizontal blue-yellow-red flag with a coronet in the centre is described in 1898 (Spender) and 1917 (National Geographic) and abolished c. 1934/5; a vertical blue-yellow-red flag with the arms (coronet, no motto) is shown in Flaggenbuch 1939. Wikipedia (Andorra): the New Reform of 1866 is linked to the national symbols such as the tricolour flag.
era-1866.open: The page's arms in 1866 are contradicted: Flags of the World shows a coronet, not arms, on a horizontal tricolour between 1866 and about 1934/5, and vertical stripes with arms only from c. 1939; sources differ on the 1993 constitution date (28 April versus 4 May) and the 1866 date is marked uncertain by Flags of the World.
