era-1806.says: Flags of the World (historical flags): 1806-1866 a vertical yellow-red bicolour, adopted c. 1806 and replaced by the tricolour in 1866 (Pedersen 1971, linking the colours to the Counts of Foix, and Herzog & Hannes 1990 agree; Talocci 1993; image from the 1932 Grand Larousse Illustre); its main page says that when Napoleon gave Andorra a constitution in 1806 the flag, in vertical French pattern, used the local traditional Catalan colours. Wikipedia (Andorra) does not mention 1806 and says Napoleon I re-established the Co-Principate in 1809 and an imperial decree restored independence in 1814.
era-1806.open: Wikipedia gives no independent flag for 1806-1866 and no source supports this page's plain blue-yellow-red tricolour; the 1806 date for the flag rests on Flags of the World alone and Wikipedia gives 1809/1814 for the Napoleonic restoration.

era-1278.says: Wikipedia (Andorra): the polity was formed by a charter in 1278 (the first paréage, mediated by Peter III of Aragon, splitting sovereignty between the Count of Foix and the Bishop of Urgell), as a lordship within the Principality of Catalonia until 1715. Flags of the World (historical flags): before 1806 Andorra used the Catalan Quatre Barres, since 'no other flag was known' before the 19th century (Olle), with no colours or design given on the page.
era-1278.open: The Catalan flag is Ollé's inference rather than a documented Andorran flag; neither source describes episcopal or comital heraldry used as a flag; the page's schematic drawing is not documented.

era-1975.says: Both sources give 1975, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 11 November 1975; Flags of the World dates it 11 November 1975.
era-1975.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1575.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Angola says Angola flew Portugal's national flag in the colonial period, lowered in Luanda at noon on 10 November 1975; its Portuguese Angola article (1575-1975) shows the Portuguese flag as the infobox flag and a 1932 proposed Angolan flag. FOTW's Portuguese colonies page says that since the 1940s the government saw the colonies as parts of the country and made no flags for them other than the national flag (only flags for officials and military units, and unadopted proposals).
era-1575.open: The sources support the Portuguese national flag, but the drawing shows a green-white-red horizontal flag with a red canton and a yellow disc, not Portugal's flag; it needs redrawing. The 1575 start, pre-1900 Portuguese flags and the earlier kingdom ensigns are not covered by FOTW, which speaks only of the 1940s onward.

era-1967.says: Wikipedia: the current flag was adopted 27 February 1967, 11 days after royal assent to the West Indies Act 1967, to mark self-government; over 600 people entered the competition, won by Reginald Samuel; full independence 1 November 1981 with the 1967 flag kept. FOTW: flag adopted 27 February 1967 on associated statehood, competition of over 600 entries won by Reginald Samuel, independence 1 November 1981.
era-1967.open: FOTW says a 1994 decision gave the sun seven full points and the page does not confirm that the 1967 flag was identical to today's; FOTW says the flag was apparently adopted for land use at first.

era-1632.says: Flags of the World (Antigua colonial flags): before 1 July 1956 government boats flew the Leeward Islands Blue Ensign; from 1956/57 a Blue Ensign with a shield badge from the 1909 Leeward Islands arms on a white disc (a beach, hills, a grey building and a prominent agave plant, not a pineapple), and from 1967 a badge of the granted arms; the pineapple was the crest of the Leeward Islands arms and of the later Antigua crest; the plain red ensign was the civil ensign. Wikipedia's list: a Blue Ensign with the colonial arms of Antigua on a white disc 1956-1962 and without it 1962-1967; Leeward Islands Blue Ensigns 1871-1958; Wikipedia's flag article: the first flag for the territory was a Blue Ensign defaced with the arms in the late 1950s.
era-1632.open: Both publishers support a Blue Ensign with an Antigua badge only for 1956/57-1967 and a Leeward Islands ensign for 1871-1956; nothing read gives a flag for 1632-1871. The 'simplified pineapple' badge is not what FOTW describes for 1956-67 (agave shield); the pineapple was the crest.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia says the flag was officially recognised on 20 July 1816 at Tucumán, that Pueyrredón established the sun flag on 25 January 1818, that on unification in 1861 the national flag replaced Buenos Aires State's flag, that Roca's decree of 25 April 1884 limited the sun flag to government institutions, that decrees of 1943 and Decree 10,302/1944 regulated it, that Law 23,208 of 1985 let individuals use it, and that Decree 1650/2010 standardised colours and proportions. FOTW (Gregoric) says Congress at Tucumán passed the plain triband in 1816, that the Congress, then in Buenos Aires, created the war flag by adding the sun on 25 February 1818, and that the 1884 decree defined the 1:2 ratio and restricted the sun flag to military and government agencies.
era-1861.open: The sources differ on the sun flag's date (25 January or 25 February 1818). FOTW gives only the year for Tucumán, and does not cover 1861. This page used to say the sun flag became the sole civil and state flag.

era-1816.says: Wikipedia says independence was declared on 9 July 1816 and the flag officially recognised on 20 July 1816, and that Pueyrredón established the flag with the Sun of May on 25 January 1818 (a 1944 decree says 25 February). FOTW (Gregoric) says the Tucumán Congress passed the plain triband in 1816 and that the Congress in Buenos Aires added the sun on 25 February 1818.
era-1816.open: The date of the sun differs between sources.

era-1810.says: Wikipedia says Belgrano wrote on 26 February 1812 proposing a national flag, that it was first raised at Rosario on 27 February 1812, that the First Triumvirate ordered him in early March 1812 to stop using it, that he had it blessed at Jujuy on 25 May 1812 and called it the national flag, and that the origin of the colours cannot be accurately established. FOTW (Gregoric) says there are several theories about the design raised on 27 February 1812 and that triband flags were in use by 1814 without the sun.
era-1810.open: This page's «adopted informally as the flag of the patriot army» is close to Wikipedia's account, which also says the government told him to stop.

era-1776.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Argentina): the last formal Spanish flag, set by Charles III in 1785, was red and yellow. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy Flag): the Burgundy flag remained in use in Spain's overseas empire (Bandera de Ultramar) and was reportedly a jack until Charles III's red-yellow-red naval ensign of 1785. FOTW: the Burgundy saltire was an ensign 1506-1670s and a jack until 1785, and remained the Spanish military flag on land up to 1843.
era-1776.open: Neither publisher mentions the Rio de la Plata, so use of the Burgundy cross there is inferred; as a naval ensign it was superseded by the red-yellow flag in 1785, so the 'military and naval ensign' caption fits only 1776-1785 for ships.

era-1820.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Argentina): Rosas made the official shade turquoise blue in 1829, unofficial Rosas-era variants had four Phrygian caps and a red sun, Federalist units used dark blue and red-and-white flags, and the State of Buenos Aires flew its own flag from 1852 to 1861. Wikipedia (Argentine Confederation): infobox flag captioned 1836-1852, State of Buenos Aires secession 11 September 1852, no flag descriptions. FOTW's historical page lists Quiroga flags of 1826-1833 and links to external Olle pages for 1829-1862, but does not describe a Confederation state flag.
era-1820.open: The Wikipedia flag article contradicts the page's 'one law-fixed flag flown by both sides'; the second publisher does not describe Confederation or Buenos Aires state flags.

era-1516.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy Flag): earliest use in Spain 1506 and later overseas as the Bandera de Ultramar. FOTW (Spain 1506-1700): the main Spanish symbol from Charles I (1518) to Charles II (1665) was the red Burgundy cross on varying fields, 'a military banner' possibly carried by the conquistadors, with separate ensigns for American waters and for expeditions to the Indies.
era-1516.open: Neither publisher mentions Peru or the Rio de la Plata, and the Burgundy cross is described as a military banner with varying field colours, not an administrative flag; no flag specific to the territory is documented.

era-1991.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1990, before this era begins in 1991, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1 August 1918 (re-adopted on 24 August 1990); Flags of the World dates it 1995.
era-1991.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Armenian SSR): the flag was adopted on 17 December 1952 - like the Soviet flag but with a quarter-width horizontal blue stripe in the middle; the 1922 flag was red with the Cyrillic letters ССРА in the upper left corner and lasted a month before the Transcaucasian SFSR; between 1936 and 1940 red with a gold hammer and sickle and the Armenian letters ՀԽՍՀ beneath; between 1940 and 1952 the letters changed to ՀՍՍՌ. FOTW agrees: Soviet Armenia was proclaimed 29 November 1920; 1922 red with yellow initials; 1937 yellow Armenian initials with a yellow hammer and sickle above; 1952 flag with a dark blue bar in the middle, 1/4 of the width, approved 17 December 1952.
era-1920.open: The drawing on the page is the 1952 flag only; the earlier flags (1922, 1937, 1940s) and the TSFSR years 1922-36 are not drawn. Neither source says the stripe was near the bottom edge.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: on 1 August 1918 the National Assembly voted a horizontal tricolour of red, blue and orange (a 19 September 1918 instruction asked for yellow in place of orange cloth); parliament reaffirmed it in June 1919; Soviet troops entered Yerevan 29 November 1920. FOTW: the flag was used 1918-1921 and the red-blue-orange tricolour was readopted on 24 August 1990.
era-1918.open: Neither source read gives the meanings of the colours (blood, sky, courage) stated on the page; the end date differs slightly (Wikipedia late 1920, FOTW 1921).

era-1828.says: Wikipedia mentions Armenian militia battle flags of 1826-1828 (double-headed eagle, Noah's Ark, Christ) and an 1885 tricolour by Ghevont Alishan; FOTW's Early Armenian flags describes the flag of the Iravan Khanate captured by Russian troops c.1827 (diagonally divided dark red and white with a yellow device, held in a museum in Baku), and FOTW's Alishan page gives his c.1885 flags (red-green-blue, derived from the church calendar).
era-1828.open: No source read describes the flag flown by the Russian administration over the Armenian provinces; the black-gold-white tricolour on the page is not found. Wikipedia's Armenian Oblast article has no flag text. Next: a source on Russian imperial flag usage in the Caucasus.

era-1375.says: Wikipedia says that after division between Persian and Ottoman empires 'the idea of an Armenian flag ceased to exist for some time'. FOTW (Early Armenian flags): the Iravan Khanate (1747-1827), nominally Persian, had a flag diagonally divided dark red and white with a yellow device, captured by Russian troops c.1827 and kept in a museum in Baku.
era-1375.open: No source read describes an Ottoman or Safavid flag over these lands, or dates the partition; the khanate flag is from the end of the era only, so the page's split drawing remains undocumented.

era-1045.says: Wikipedia notes Cilician Armenian flags on maps of 1325, 1339 and 1375 and, in the Book of Knowledge, a flag of Cilician Armenia with white over grey and red crosses. FOTW (Early Armenian flags): the medieval Principality of Khachen (c. 820 to the 16th century) is shown with a golden cross on an apricot field on a flag dated 1214.
era-1045.open: No source read describes flags under Byzantine, Seljuk or Mongol overlordship, or the generic field drawn; Cilician flags are known only from maps (Wikipedia) and the Khachen flag is a regional case, not the kingdom's.

era-885.says: Wikipedia says that when Armenia gained independence in 885 the flag was a dark red canvas with a white leopard and a Christian cross, and that the 'Ani leopard' remains in the arms of Gyumri. FOTW (Early Armenian flags) reports only a Mamikonian-era (4th-8th century) red-white-green flag with a cross captured at Awarair in 451, from one author, and nothing for the Bagratid kingdom.
era-885.open: The leopard-and-cross flag is in Wikipedia alone and cites no medieval source in the extract read; the blue field with gold cross and disc drawn on the page is in no source read.

era-1901.says: Wikipedia says a federal flag competition of April 1901 drew 32,823 entries, the winning design first flew over the Royal Exhibition Building in Melbourne on 3 September 1901 with five near-identical entries sharing the prize, Edward VII's approval was announced on 11 February 1903, the Southern Cross stars were standardised to seven points on 23 February 1903, the Commonwealth Star gained a seventh point on 8 December 1908, and the Flags Act 1953 received royal assent on 14 February 1954. FOTW (Morris) says the competition was announced in the Gazette of 29 April 1901, the flag first flew on 3 September 1901, the King's approval was given in 1902 and confirmed by a proclamation of 20 February 1903, a seventh point was added by the Gazette of 19 December 1908, and the Flags Act 1953 was confirmed in a Gazette of 14 April 1954.
era-1901.open: The sources differ on the 1908 date (8 or 19 December), the 1903 dates, and the 1954 date (14 February assent or 14 April gazette). This page used to say the star was seven-pointed from the start.

era-1788.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Australia (citing the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet) says Phillip raised the Union Jack on 7 February 1788 when he proclaimed New South Wales, that the Union Jack of that date was the 1606 version without St Patrick's cross, that each colony had a flag based on the Blue Ensign with a state badge, and that the National Colonial Flag dates from 1823-24. FOTW's Victoria page dates the colony's blue ensign with the Southern Cross to 1870 (shield and crown 1877) and its New South Wales page shows flags of 1867 and 1870.
era-1788.open: Nothing read says the Union Jack was the formal ensign of all six colonies throughout; the drawn Union Jack with St Patrick's cross is the post-1801 form, not the 1788 flag. The Department's own timeline (pmc.gov.au) could not be read: one page returned an Incapsula bot-gate and two were empty without scripts, so no workaround was tried.

era-1955.says: FOTW says the Flag Act passed by the Austrian parliament on 28 March 1984 put into effect the state flag (red-white-red with the arms) and its 2:3 ratio, and that the plain triband is the national flag and civil ensign. Wikipedia's infobox gives 1 May 1945 for the formal adoption and 28 March 1984 for the state flag, and 1230 for the origin of the design.
era-1955.open: The date a plain red-white-red became Austria's flag again depends on which event is meant: 1945 (restoration), 1955 (this era's start) or 1984 (the Flag Act); the sources read do not give 1955. FOTW also notes the law does not specify the shade of red.

era-1156.says: FOTW quotes Peter Diem: Duke Frederick II (1210–1246), the last Babenberg, adopted the red-white-red arms in 1230, and the first colour document bearing them dates from 1232. Wikipedia says it is first documented in a seal on a deed of 30 November 1230 for Lilienfeld Abbey, and that the Leopold V story (Siege of Acre, 1191) is a legend.
era-1156.open: This is evidence for 1230, not for the whole era from 1156: nothing was found for a red-white-red banner before 1230. Both sources describe arms and colours; whether a banner of this design was flown in the 13th century is not established. Wikipedia's 1230 and 1232 statements carry citation-needed tags.

era-1867.says: Wikipedia says black-yellow was the Habsburg monarchy's national flag, later the Austrian Empire's, until 1918 (citing Preuß, Flaggenlexikon). FOTW says the red-white-red ensign with a shield was adopted as merchant ensign on 20 March 1786, that a dual-monarchy merchant flag was created in 1869 (18 February 1869 decree, in use from 1 August 1869), and that a red-white-red war ensign was used from 1880 until 10 October 1915.
era-1867.open: The image shows an eagle on gold, which is the imperial standard rather than the black-yellow flag the sources describe. This page's statement that red-white-red was «used for the Austrian lands since medieval times» is stronger than the sources: Diem puts the arms in 1230 and FOTW the ensign in 1786.

era-1918.says: Göbl (ADLER, via Austria-Forum): on 31 October 1918, before the First Republic was proclaimed, the State Council, then running the government provisionally, fixed the new state colours on the proposal of the Christian Social deputy Wilhelm Miklas, bypassing Habsburg black-yellow for the older Babenberg red-white-red; when the new flag was to be hoisted (12 November 1918), Red Guards tore the white stripes out so that only red cloth rose. AEIOU: the colours were taken over in 1918 by the Republic from the old Babenberg flag. Wikipedia: German Austria adopted the red-white-red triband after Austria-Hungary dissolved in 1918.
era-1918.open: Neither source calls it 'the first government in centuries to fly it without an eagle or crown' (AEIOU says red-white-red survived as the navy flag); the page's text on seeking union with Germany is not covered here.

era-1938.says: FOTW (Steven Shea, 1996): the Austrian flag was not used after the Anschluss of 1938 and was restored in 1945. Diem (2010): red-white-red was largely uncontested until 1938, and red-white-red flags appeared in Vienna again only in early April 1945 on the Rathaus and the Palais Auersperg. Göbl: after the Anschluss in March 1938 the 1934 eagle was at once shelved. Wikipedia (Flag of Germany): from 15 September 1935 the Nazi flag was Germany's exclusive national flag.
era-1938.open: No page read says in so many words that the Reich's swastika flag was the flag flown in Austria 1938-45 (an inference from the 1935 German flag law and the annexation); Wikipedia's Anschluss article records only Nazi flags greeting the troops. Sought: an Austrian or German source on flag orders for the Ostmark.

era-1945.says: FOTW (Steven Shea, 1996) says the flag was restored with independence in 1945; Wikipedia's infobox gives 1 May 1945 as the formal adoption, with no law or citation named.
era-1945.open: The Allied occupation (1945–1955) is not described by either source; the page's statements about the four zones were not checked.

era-1934.says: Göbl (ADLER): the Fatherland Front's Kruckenkreuz, taken over from a 1924 decoration, was placed in the middle of the red-white-red flag and from 1936 equated domestically with the state flag; the 1934 arms were a double-headed, haloed black eagle with the red-white-red shield. Diem (2010): the Kruckenkreuz, introduced in September 1933, was soon built into the red-white-red flag; the Kruckenkreuz flag counted as equal to the state flag and could be flown beside it domestically; the 1 May 1934 constitution (art. 3) restored the double-headed eagle with haloes in place of the single-headed eagle.
era-1934.open: The page's caption and drawing ('single-headed eagle and mural crown') describe the 1919 arms, not the 1934 ones; neither source says the state flag itself carried the eagle (page text corrected).

era-1919.says: Göbl: the State Council set the red-white-red colours on 31 October 1918, bypassing the Habsburg black-yellow for the older Babenberg colours, which also appear in the Habsburg-Lorraine house arms but were less identified with the dynasty. Diem (2010): despite the First Republic's bitter political camps, red-white-red remained largely uncontested until 1938; the 8 May 1919 arms law gave the eagle with mural crown, sickle and hammer. Wikipedia: German Austria adopted the triband in 1918 and it was formally adopted 1 May 1945.
era-1919.open: No source gives a separate 1919 act for the flag, and the page's claim that it was a political break with the Habsburgs is only partly supported (Göbl: they avoided black-yellow but red-white-red is also in the Habsburg-Lorraine house arms).

era-1804.says: AEIOU Österreich-Lexikon: in 1804 the Austrian imperial state took over, with the arms, the black-yellow flag (black double eagle on a gold ground) of the Holy Roman Empire; red-white-red survived only as the flag of the war and merchant navy and as the house colours of Habsburg-Lothringen. Wikipedia: the black-yellow flag was the national flag of the Habsburg monarchy and the Austrian Empire, with a caption dating the Empire's flag c.1804-1867.
era-1804.open: The Congress of Vienna and the 'Holy Roman title' passages of the page are not covered by these sources; the black-yellow flag's end date (1867 per Wikipedia caption) is not confirmed by AEIOU.

era-1453.says: Diem (2010): the red-white-red flag symbolised belonging to the Duchy of Austria, played a relatively small part once mercenary armies replaced knightly ones, and was displaced by the black-yellow imperial banner in the centuries when Austrian archdukes were emperors; red-white-red appeared at homage ceremonies, processions and triumphal arches, and Joseph II introduced a red-white-red sea flag on 20 March 1786. AEIOU: the Bindenschild stayed the arms image of the lands, with the imperial eagle added from 1433. Wikipedia: Habsburgs took the colours after 1278 (Rheinfelden 1283).
era-1453.open: The page's 'war banner' and the 1453 start are not in the sources; red-white-red here was largely ceremonial and the imperial banner prevailed, so 'continues as the lands' own flag' is too strong (page text corrected).

era-1282.says: Wikipedia: the red-white-red arms are first documented on a deed of 30 November 1230, were adopted by Ottokar II after 1246, and by the Habsburgs after 1278 (Rheinfelden 1283); FOTW: Friedrich II adopted the arms in 1230, first document 1232. AEIOU Österreich-Lexikon: the Bindenschild replaced the imperial eagle on Austrian flags about 1230, the first picture of an Austrian army flag dates from 1254, and for the whole of the lands the Bindenschild soon became the only valid flag image, with the eagle added again from 1433. Diem (2010): the red-white-red colours are the creation of Duke Friedrich II, who gave the duchy a new seal image c.1230.
era-1282.open: Sources differ on the first document (Wikipedia 1230, FOTW 1232). None says the Habsburgs chose these colours over their own ancestral ones; Wikipedia records only that they took them over.

era-1991.says: Flags of the World: the flag was 'readopted 5 February 1991' (the 27 February 1993 date it gives is for the national emblem) and its design was set in Article 23 of the 1995 Constitution, and the page links it to the 1918-1920 flag. Wikipedia: the 1918 flag was banned under Soviet rule from April 1920 and reinstated on 5 February 1991 (Nakhchivan adopted it on 17 November 1990), with slight variations in colours and size; infobox dates 9 November 1918, 5 February 1991 and 22 October 2013 (colours standardised).
era-1991.open: Wikipedia is internally inconsistent on whether reinstatement was 17 November 1990 or 5 February 1991; the exact colour match to 1918 is not stated and the colours were standardised in 2013. The earlier summary that the sources disagreed on the year came from misreading the infobox's 1918 and FOTW's emblem dates.

era-4bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia: the 1918 flags were banned from April 1920 and the Soviet republic used eight flags, the last issued 7 October 1952: red with a horizontal dark blue band on the bottom fourth (the Caspian), a golden hammer and sickle and a gold-bordered red star in the canton, specified 5 May 1956 and discarded on 5 February 1991. Flags of the World (Azerbaijan SSR): the 1952 flag adopted 7 October 1952, dark blue bar in the base one quarter wide, emblem placement unknown.
era-1920.open: Both sources call the band dark blue, not the 'light blue' of the page's caption (the infobox gives #00309A); the star and hammer and sickle are not in FOTW's text, and the drawing shows only the 1952 design while eight flags were used in 1920-1991 (the first, 19 May 1921).

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: the republic declared independence 28 May 1918 and adopted a first flag (red, white crescent and eight-pointed star) on 21 June 1918; a blue-red-green tricolor with crescent and star on the red band was approved in draft 9 Nov 1918 and raised over parliament 7 Dec 1918; banned after April 1920. FOTW: the flag was used 1918-1920 in a slightly different version from today's, and the star was already on it.
era-1918.open: FOTW does not give the exact 1918 adoption date; the page's colour-meaning gloss is attributed by FOTW to Ali Bey Hussein Zade rather than stated as an official meaning.

era-1813.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Russia article: white-blue-red was the merchant maritime flag from 1705; Alexander II decreed black-yellow-white as the official heraldic state flag in 1858 (used on government buildings); white-blue-red was authorised for festive use on land in 1883 and formally made the sole national flag by an imperial order of 29 April 1896. Neither the Azerbaijan flag pages of Wikipedia and Flags of the World nor the Russia article say what flew over the Azerbaijani provinces after the 1813 Treaty of Gulistan.
era-1813.open: The card's black-gold-white tricolour fits only 1858-1896 of the 1813-1918 span; white-blue-red was the sole national flag from 1896, and no source read states which flag was used in Azerbaijan or that any flag was specific to the region. Flags of the World's Russian history page (ru_his.html) returned 404.

era-1747.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Azerbaijan flag page describes a flag of the khanates. A web search for Karabakh and Baku khanate flags returned no usable source.
era-1747.open: The generic field shown is not documented by any source read; a source on individual khanate banners (Karabakh, Baku, Quba, Shaki) is still missing.

era-1538.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Azerbaijan flag page describes a Safavid flag. A web search found only general statements that the lion and sun appears on Safavid-period state flags (c. 1576-1732) and a Persian-language journal article on Safavid flags; the Encyclopaedia Iranica article on flags returned 403 and was not read.
era-1538.open: The teal field with a gold roundel is not described by any source read; the Iranica article on flags (blocked, 403) and the journal article on Safavid flags were not read.

era-861.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Azerbaijan flag page describes a Shirvanshah flag. A web search snippet from a Baku Old City site mentioned a 'goldish' Shirvanshah flag in a court poet's divan and a lions-and-bull's-head heraldic image, but the page returned 404 when fetched, so nothing from it is used.
era-861.open: The green field and white crescent are not supported by any source read; the one hint found (a gold flag in a court poet's divan) points to a different colour and could not be verified.

era-1973.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 10 July 1973 and names Hervis Bain as designer; FOTW gives 'Flag adopted: 10 July 1973', designer Hervis Bain, and the coat of arms 7 December 1971. Wikipedia reads the two aquamarine bands as the surrounding water, the gold band as the sun and land-based resources, and the black triangle as the strength and determination of the people; FOTW quotes Smith (1975) giving the gold as the sands of the islands and the black triangle as unity and the resolve to develop land and sea, and doubts the 'embroidered' meanings.
era-1973.open: The two sources agree on the date and designer; the meanings of the colours are later explanations, differing between them (sun/resources vs sands), not official.

FOTW (colonial badge and flags): the Bahamas badge was introduced in 1869 and changed little until discontinued in 1973, on a white disc on the Blue Ensign until 1923; officially there was no Red Ensign, though many defaced ones were flown unofficially.
era-1718.open: Both sources document the badged Blue Ensign only from 1869; nothing read covers a flag in 1718-1869 and the 'Pirate Republic' framing is not in either. The badge shows a ship, not the rising sun described earlier on the page.

era-1971.says: Wikipedia: the serration originally had 28 white points, reduced to eight in 1972, and to five on 14 February 2002 under Decree-Law 4. FOTW historical page: the 1933 serration had 28 triangles; a 5 October 1950 proclamation specifies eight teeth; the flag was adopted 19 August 1972 per Album des Pavillons, with eight teeth until 2002.
era-1971.open: FOTW's contributor argues the eight-point version dates from 1950, not 1972; neither source mentions 1971 independence or points varying print to print.

era-1783.says: Wikipedia: earliest flags plain red; after the 1820 maritime treaty with Britain a white stripe was added (to signify the treaty and distinguish the flag from pirates'); serrations came in 1932. FOTW historical page: plain red before 1820; a vertical white stripe at the hoist was added in 1820 to symbolise a truce; plain red stayed in de facto use until 1910; serration introduced in 1932/33 to distinguish from Ajman, Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
era-1783.open: Both give the white band after the 1820 treaty and the serration in the 1930s, not gradually over a century; the reason given for the band differs between sources (pirates vs truce), and neither mentions 1783.

era-899.says: Wikipedia (History of Bahrain): the Qarmatian revolution began around 900 and the Qarmatians were defeated by the Abbasids in 976; Sheikh Abdullah bin Ali Al Uyuni seized the country in 1076-1077 (the Uyunids ruling 163 years); the Usfurids took control in 1253; the islands became tributary to Hormuz in 1330; the Jabrids rose in the mid-15th century; a Portuguese-Hormuz force conquered Bahrain in 1521; it links a Jarwanid page but gives no dates. Flags of the World's Bahrain history page has no medieval material and says only that the pre-1820 flag 'may well have been solid red'.
era-899.open: Neither publisher mentions any flag, seal or banner of these dynasties; the card's four-dynasty succession is only partly dated by Wikipedia (the Jarwanids are undated there), and the claim that they used banners rather than fixed flags is not found in the sources read.

era-1971.says: WP: 'Swadheen Bangla' flag first made 6 June 1970 at Dhaka University; raised there 2 March 1971 (or stitched 1 March, map added 2 March); Mujib hoisted it 23 March 1971; wartime flag green with red disc and yellow map; map removed 13 Jan 1972. FOTW: red disc with gold map on bottle-green, first flag hoisted at Dhaka University 3 March 1971, Mujib 23 March 1971, design attributed to Quamrul Hasan.
era-1971.open: Sources differ on 2 vs 3 March 1971. Provisional-government adoption is not stated by either.

era-1947.says: Wikipedia's list for Bangladesh gives Pakistan's flag (green, white crescent and star, white strip) for 1947-1971. Wikipedia's Pakistan article says the Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947, that it became the flag of the Dominion and from 1956 of the Republic, and that the design is unchanged; FOTW's Pakistan page gives the flag as adopted in August 1947 (14 August there). FOTW's Bangladesh page notes that the first independent Bangladesh flag omitted Pakistan's crescent and star.
era-1947.open: Neither Pakistan source mentions East Pakistan or East Bengal; that Pakistan's flag flew over the eastern wing is inferred from it being the national flag of the whole state. The colour symbolism given earlier on this page is not covered here.

era-1858.says: Wikipedia lists the Union Flag, a Viceroy's flag (1885-1947), a Red Ensign-based British Raj flag (1880-1947) and a Bengal Presidency blue ensign for British India. FOTW's page on British India says India's flag was the Union Jack bearing the insignia of the Order of the Star of India (with Blue and Red Ensigns too), that the Company's territories passed to the Crown in 1858 and that the Empire of India was created in 1876; its Bengal page shows flags of Bengal from 1862 and 1868 charts.
era-1858.open: FOTW's Star of India Union Jack is a contributor description (Roy Stilling, 1996) that does not name the year it began; the page's schematic composite is a drawing of that description. FOTW's Bengal flags (a scimitar between three barrels) are a different, local flag and are not on this page.

era-1757.says: Wikipedia's article on the East India Company's flag gives horizontal red and white stripes with the Union Jack in the canton, adopted 1801 and relinquished 1858; FOTW's East India Company page, citing Wilson's Flags at Sea, gives the ensign with a Union canton from 1707 and the new Union flag from about 1801, with varying stripe counts. FOTW's Bengal page shows a striped ensign with a Union Jack canton from an 1848/1862 chart 'similar to the ensigns of the British East India Company'. Wikipedia's Bangladesh list gives a Bengal Presidency blue ensign.
era-1757.open: Both sources describe the Company's ensign and jack but neither says it was a territorial flag of Bengal as opposed to a Company and shipping flag; the number of stripes varies between sources (9, 11, 13), so the page's schematic stripe count is a choice. The 1757 start (Plassey) is not stated by these sources.

era-1576.says: Wikipedia's Bangladesh list gives a moss-green alam flag for the Bengal Subah under the Mughals (1576-1717), tagged as failing verification, and a Nawab of Bengal flag (white with three red barrels and a red sword) for 1717-1757. Wikipedia's article on the flags of the Mughal Empire says the imperial alam was primarily moss green with a lion and sun (citing the Ain-i-Akbari and Padshahnama paintings); FOTW's Mughal page shows an imperial standard carrying a lion with the sun behind it. FOTW's Bengal page confirms a white flag with a red scimitar between three red barrels from an 1862 chart (barrels and sword yellow in an 1868 source).
era-1576.open: No source read gives a flag for Bengal in particular under the Mughals except the Wikipedia list entry that is tagged as failing verification; the lion-and-sun imperial alam supports a green Mughal standard but not the gold sun alone shown here. The Nawab flag (white, three barrels, sword) is from 1862-1868 charts, not a contemporary source.

era-1204.says: Wikipedia's Bangladesh list names the Bengal Sultanate only as a link and describes no flag; its article on the Bengal Sultanate has no flag description in the text read. FOTW's pages on Bangladesh, India's early history and Bengal do not cover the Sultanate.
era-1204.open: No source read describes a Bengal Sultanate flag; the maroon-and-crescent drawing is the page's own reconstruction.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia lists the white-red-white flag for the Republic of Belarus 1991-1995 (also the BNR 1918 and the BSSR 1990-91). FOTW lists 'Historical Flag (1918, 1991-1995)' by link label.

era-1922.says: Wikipedia: BSSR flag red with gold ССРБ (1919-1927) then БССР (1927-1937), with hammer, sickle and star from 1937; on 25 December 1951 a flag by Nikolai Gusev, red with a green lower band and a hoist ornament designed in 1917 by Matrona Markevich. Flags of the World: red with yellow initials in 1919 and yellow BSSR lettering with a star, hammer and sickle in 1937 and the 1940s; the decree of 25 December 1951 gives a red upper stripe (two thirds) and green lower stripe (one third), a gold hammer and sickle with a gold-bordered red star in the hoist canton, and a white ornament on red along the hoist; the SSR emblem was used until 10 December 1991.
era-1922.open: The page starts the era in 1922 while both sources date BSSR flags from 1919; FOTW gives no description for the 1927 flag beyond the constitution reference; the card shows the 1951 design only.

era-1919.says: Wikipedia: plain red flag of the Lithuanian-Byelorussian SSR (1919-1920); BSSR flag with gold ССРБ letters 1919-1927. Flags of the World (early flags): Byelorussia merged into the Lithuanian-Byelorussian SSR on 27 February 1919 and was re-established in August 1919; a pure red flag was used in early 1919; the 1919 Byelorussian SSR flag was red with yellow SSRB initials in the upper hoist (Dunin-Borkovsky, 1923).
era-1919.open: The Lithuanian-Byelorussian SSR is dated 1919-1920 on Wikipedia and February to August 1919 on FOTW; neither source mentions a hammer-and-sickle emblem on the 1919-1922 flag; the war-split framing is not covered.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia lists the white-red-white flag as that of the Belarusian People's Republic, 1918. FOTW labels it 'Historical Flag (1918, 1991-1995)' and lists the BNR in exile 1919-1925 by label.
era-1918.open: FOTW gives only link labels; the origin of the colours (Grand Duchy heraldry) is not covered.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Russia): Peter the Great decreed the white-blue-red tricolour as the commercial maritime flag in 1705; the black-yellow-white tricolour became the official state flag in 1858, government buildings flying it while merchant ships and citizens kept white-blue-red; white-blue-red was allowed on land for festivities in 1883 and named the sole national flag in 1896. Flags of the World (Russia): the white-blue-red tricolour was the civil ensign since 1799 and was recognised for use on land in 1883, and the black-orange-white flag was never formally abolished, so Russia had two civil flags from 1883 to 1914.
era-1795.open: Neither source speaks of Belarus or a flag flown over the Northwest Region; the black-yellow-white state flag of 1858-1896 is not shown on the card; the page's 'no regional variant' remark is not covered.

era-1392.says: Wikipedia (Vytis): Vytautas made the horseman a state emblem; at Grunwald in 1410 his regiments carried red banners, thirty with an armoured horseman; in 1578 Guagnini described a red silk state flag with a white mounted knight; the arms remained the principal emblem of the Grand Duchy until 1795, and the Belarusian lands, part of the Duchy since the Middle Ages, took it into local heraldry. Flags of the World (Belarus arms): Pahonia on the seal of Grand Duke Vytautas in 1407, frequently used as a state symbol in the 14th-15th centuries, and on the covers of the Statutes published in Old Belarusian in 1529, 1566 and 1588.
era-1392.open: The 1392 start is tied to Vytautas's rule, not stated as a flag date; FOTW describes no banner; the colour red and white knight rest on Wikipedia's 1410 and 1578 accounts.

era-1944.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1831, before this era begins in 1944, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 23 January 1831; Flags of the World dates it 23 January 1831.
era-1944.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia says insurgents replaced the French flag on Brussels city hall on 27 August 1830 with a horizontal red-yellow-black tricolour, and that on 23 January 1831 the National Congress enshrined the tricolour without setting the stripe order, the stripes changing from horizontal to vertical that day, with the modern form (black at the hoist) reached on 12 October 1831. FOTW says the first true national flag in 1830 was horizontal red-yellow-black, that the Provisional Government decreed on 23 January 1831 that the colours be placed vertically, that the Navy set black at the hoist on 15 September 1831 and the Interior Department on 12 October 1831, that horizontal and vertical flags coexisted until 24 September 1838, and that the colours come from the arms of Brabant.
era-1830.open: The sources differ on who acted on 23 January 1831 (the National Congress or the Provisional Government). This page used to say vertical black-yellow-red was adopted within days of the uprising and as a homage to revolutionary France; neither source says either. The drawing shows the later vertical form.

era-1384.says: Flags of the World (Belgium plate) says the Cross of Burgundy was 'adopted by most of the provinces of the Lower Countries in the 15th century', most sources crediting John the Fearless, first confirmed use 1411 as a livery element. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): the banner dates to the early 15th century; the Habsburgs inherited the Burgundian Low Countries in 1477 'and adopted the flag'; a similar flag was used by the Seventeen Provinces in the 15th and 16th centuries. Wikipedia (Burgundian Netherlands) places the Burgundian state at 1384-1482 and links its infobox flag to the Cross of Burgundy.
era-1384.open: Both sources date the cross to the early 15th century (1411), not 1384; the page's 'common banner of their whole domain' with provincial arms kept beneath it is not stated by either. Flags of the World calls its plate 'alleged' in places.

era-1581.says: Wikipedia (Spanish Netherlands) gives the Cross of Burgundy as the flag of the territory (infobox, 1556-1714) with a civil ensign; Wikipedia (List of Belgian flags, tagged citation needed) lists a white flag with the Cross of Burgundy and a red-white-yellow civil ensign with the cross. Flags of the World (Belgium plate) captions a simplified Cross of Burgundy '15th-18th centuries' and a yellow-white-red flag of the Spanish Netherlands '16th-18th centuries', with the cross in the white stripe in a variant.
era-1581.open: Sources differ on the span (Wikipedia 1556-1714 or 1482-1714); the red-white-yellow stripes, which both sources also show, are not on this page's drawing. Wikipedia's list entry is uncited and Flags of the World calls its own plate 'alleged'.

era-1714.says: Flags of the World (Austrian Netherlands page, citing Flag Bulletin 32, 1993) describes a red-white-yellow civil ensign for 24 September 1781 - 31 December 1786 with the imperial Austrian eagle and the Cross of Burgundy behind it; its Belgium plate shows a red-white-red flag with Austrian arms for 1787 and yellow-white-red until 1786. Wikipedia's List of Belgian flags describes a red-white-gold tricolour with the arms of Austria for 1781-1786 (tagged citation needed); Wikipedia's Austrian Netherlands article gives only an unexplained infobox flag for 1714-1797. Flags of the World's United Belgian States page covers only the 1789-1790 revolution (Hainaut volunteers' colour, deposition of Joseph II proclaimed 24 October 1789; Austrian rule restored November-December 1790) and says nothing of Habsburg or Austrian flags.
era-1714.open: The sources support an eagle or Austrian arms only on the 1781-1786 civil ensign, not a Habsburg eagle flag for the whole 1714-1795 period; no source read describes a flag for 1714-1781 or 1787-1795, and the cross is attested for the Spanish period rather than this one.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia (Military Administration in Belgium and Northern France) shows a German war ensign (1938-1945) as the infobox flag for 1940-1944 and says nothing in its text on Belgian flags. Flags of the World's occupation page describes only the square black-white-red flag with eagle of the Militaerbefehlshaber (Falkenhausen, 28 May 1940 - 20 Jul 1944), not a civil flag order.
era-1940.open: The two sources use different German flags (a war ensign versus the commander's flag) and neither says the Belgian tricolour was suppressed or that no Belgian symbol was tolerated.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: the National Congress enshrined the red, yellow and black tricolour in January 1831 and the modern form (black at the hoist) was reached on 12 October. FOTW: 23 January 1831 decree, vertical stripes with black at the hoist (navy decree 15 September 1831), national flag confirmed 28 January 1936. Two publishers therefore give the same design in force through 1918-1940, with an explicit confirmation in 1936.
era-1918.open: Neither source describes the interwar years in detail or says the flag was 'restored' after 1918; the page's 'restored' wording is unconfirmed.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia (German occupation of Belgium in WWI) names the Governor-General and the General Government (1915 Flamenpolitik), says patriotic badges showing the royal family or national colours were banned and replaced by ivy leaves, and that mutineers flew the red flag over the Brussels Kommandantur in November 1918. It does not mention an Imperial German flag. Flags of the World's Belgium pages do not cover 1914-1918.
era-1914.open: The Imperial German flag over the Generalgouvernement is not stated by any source read; a ban on Belgian national colours is reported only for badges. The 1914-1918 government-in-exile at Sainte-Adresse is listed on the FOTW index (fr-76-sa.html) but was not read.

era-1815.says: Flags of the World (Belgium plate) captions the red-white-blue flag '1814-1830' as the flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, which then ruled Belgium; Wikipedia (United Kingdom of the Netherlands) shows the Dutch tricolour as the infobox flag for 1815-1839 and says Belgium was declared independent on 4 October 1830. Flags of the World (1830 Revolution) adds that before 26 August 1830 Brussels displayed the orange Dutch cockade or the French flag.
era-1815.open: Neither source says in words that no distinct Belgian flag existed in 1815-1830; the page's 'erasure of separate identity' reading is interpretation.

era-1795.says: Flags of the World (1830 Revolution) says that before 26 August 1830 Brussels displayed the orange Dutch cockade or the French flag; the Belgium plate (be!hist) shows no flag for 1794-1814 and its author remarks the French flag was omitted. Wikipedia and FOTW's main pages do not cover French rule.
era-1795.open: No source read states that the French tricolour was the flag of the annexed Belgian departments in 1795-1815; the Flags of the World France pages and a source on the 1795 annexation were not read.

era-1981.says: Wikipedia: adopted 21 September 1981, independence day (standardised 28 August 2019): a royal blue field with red stripes at top and bottom and a white disc holding the 1907 coat of arms, which recalls the logging industry with tools and mahogany trees, with the motto Sub Umbra Floreo and 50 leaves recalling 1950. FOTW: adopted 21 September 1981; blue field with red stripes added in 1981, a white disc with 50 olive leaves and the coat of arms (oar, sledgehammer, saw, axe, ship, tree), the motto glossed 'I flourish in the shadow'; standardised in 2019 at 3:5.
era-1981.open: The sources agree on date and design. They differ on the leaves (Wikipedia: for 1950 and the PUP; FOTW: the year 1950) and FOTW does not call the tree a mahogany; the page's 'laurel ring' simplifies the 50-leaf wreath.

era-1950.says: Wikipedia: from 1950 onward an unofficial national flag was in use, blue with the coat of arms on a white disc, tied to the PUP (50 leaves recalling 1950), and the 1981 flag added red stripes top and bottom. FOTW: the blue flag with a white disk, without stripes, was adopted on 2 February 1950, the PUP proposed a blue flag with the coat of arms in a white circle, and the two red stripes were added on 21 September 1981.
era-1950.open: Neither source mentions a 1964 self-government flag; Wikipedia notes the UDP, founded 1973, objected to the blue-and-white design.

era-1862.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Belize): a British Honduras flag 1870-1919, a flag 1919-1981, a governor's standard 1884-1981; the 1907 arms formed the basis of the badge. Wikipedia (British Honduras): declared a colony in 1862, crown colony 1871. FOTW (bz-bhond): the badge was approved in 1870 and used until 1981, apparently shown on a white disc until about 1920, with the disc ordered removed in 1919; the Blue Ensign continued probably until 1981; the badge has a Union Jack, mahogany-logging tools and a ship flying a red ensign; Lieutenant Governors served 1862-1884.
era-1862.open: Both sources give 1870, not 1862, as the start of the badge ensign, and no flag is dated 1862-1870; the era's start and its end at 1950 are the page's. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 125,584 characters.

era-1638.says: Wikipedia (British Honduras): the first English logging settlement is generally attributed to Peter Wallace's 1638 landing at Haulover Creek; the 1786 Convention of London affirmed Spanish sovereignty and Spain never attempted to reclaim the area after 1798; Guatemala's 1945 constitution called it its twenty-third department; the territory was declared a British colony in 1862. FOTW (bz-bhond): before 1862 the territory was governed by Superintendents.
era-1638.open: No source describes a flag flown by the settlers; the British ensign claim, and the page's stated Spanish and Guatemalan disputes after 1821, remain unconfirmed. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 125,584 characters.

era-1990.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia: after the 1972 coup brought a Marxist-Leninist government, a green flag with a red five-pointed star in the top-left canton was introduced in 1975 and the old flag was reinstated on 1 Aug 1990. FOTW: 1975-1990 the flag was green with a red star in the canton under the People's Republic of Benin; the 1959 flag was re-established at the National Conference of 19-28 Feb 1990 and reintroduced 1 Aug 1990 (the page also says 1991 elsewhere, unresolved).
era-1975.open: Wikipedia says the green flag was never adopted by law (de facto only); the page's claim of deliberate alignment with other Marxist-Leninist states' iconography is not covered by either source.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: Dahomey became independent on 1 Aug 1960 with the 1959 flag unchanged. FOTW: the flag was first hoisted 1 Aug 1960 and was the same as the current one up to 1975.
era-1960.open: The page's phrase 'a decade of coups' is not covered by either source.

era-1958.says: Wikipedia: Dahomey got limited self-government in the French Community on 4 Dec 1958 and chose its flag (a yellow and red flag with a green hoist band) on 16 Nov 1959 to replace the French tricolour. FOTW: adopted 16 Nov 1959, first hoisted 1 Aug 1960.
era-1958.open: Neither source says the territorial assembly made the choice; the 1959 flag is the same as the one the page labels the 'tricolor'.

era-1894.says: Wikipedia's list of historical flags gives the French tricolour as the official flag of French Dahomey, 1894-1959. FOTW's page on the French colonial empire says the French Tricolore was the common and specific flag of French West Africa, a federation that lists Dahomey among its colonies, and that only some territories hoisted flags of their own in 1958-59 (Dahomey is not named among them); the use of the French flag was the rule and local flags the exception.
era-1894.open: FOTW does not name Dahomey as flying the tricolour; it says so for the federation. Wikipedia ends the period in 1959 and the page in 1958; the 1894 start (French conquest and protectorate) is not dated by FOTW's colonial page.

era-1625.says: No single national flag is established. Wikipedia's list: King Ghezo's flag (1818-1859) white with a red border and a war elephant, King Glele (1859-c.1890) not known to have used a banner, King Behanzin's banner (c.1890-1894) light blue with a coat of arms. FOTW's Dahomey page agrees on Behanzin (light blue field, yellow shield with a dark grey shark, egg and tusks, green palm, snakes; the flag captured at Abomey on 18 November 1892 and held in a Paris museum) and, citing an engraving of King Ghezo receiving a French mission under a different flag, suggests 'each king may have had his own flag'.
era-1625.open: The appliqué praise-symbol banners (ship for Agaja, buffalo for Ghezo) and the c.1625 start are not covered: Wikipedia's Ghezo flag shows an elephant, not a buffalo, and FOTW does not describe Ghezo's design in the text read. The red-field drawing remains an informed reconstruction, not a transcription of an attested flag.

era-1969.says: Both sources give 1969, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1969; Flags of the World dates it 1969.
era-1969.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1949.says: Wikipedia: a first flag credited to Mayum Choying Wangmo Dorji in 1947 and introduced in 1949 at the Indo-Bhutan Treaty signing, square, yellow above and red below the diagonal with a green Druk per an official document, though photographs suggest about 4:5 and a pale green; a 1956 version made the dragon white; the red changed to orange in 1968 or 1969. Flags of the World (two history pages, drawing on the on-line book 'The Origin and Description of the National Flag and Anthem of the Kingdom of Bhutan' and Kinga's Polity, Kingship and Democracy): the first flag appeared at the 1949 treaty, square, yellow over red on the rising diagonal with a green dragon; a 1956 royal tour flag with a white dragon; a late-1950s 2:3 redesign; and in 1968 or 1969 the red recoloured orange.
era-1949.open: The two sources differ on who designed the 1949 flag (Wikipedia credits Mayum Choying Wangmo Dorji, FOTW's sources the king, embroidered by Lharip Taw Taw) and on proportions; the dragon's colour changed from green to white during the span, so the drawing's approximate colours fit only part of it. FOTW says the orange-with-green-dragon image once shown 'doesn't seem to have existed'.

era-1616.says: Wikipedia covers no flag or banner from 1616 to 1907 and no use of the Druk before 1907 apart from the traditional 'turquoise druk' explaining the green; 1907 appears only as Ugyen Wangchuck's crowning. FOTW says a monastery named Druk was set up c. 1200 and links the dragon emblem to Bhutan from then, without describing any flag.
era-1616.open: The Druk as the state's emblem from 1616 and any banner of the Druk Desi state are not covered.

era-1825.says: Wikipedia: 31 October 1851 tricolor adopted under Belzu; 1888 decree on the colors' meaning; 19 July 2004 Decree 27630 proportions 15:22; 5 August 2009 Decree 241 and wiphala. FOTW: late 1851 decree under Belzu; 14 July 1888 decree; 2004 decree with 7.5:11 ratio; 2009 constitution.
era-1825.open: The proportions are from 2004, not 1888 as the page said.

era-1776.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Bolivia): the gallery captions the colonial flag as the Spanish Empire flag (1506-1825 in Peru and Bolivia, 1821 in Peru; 1506-1785 or 1701 in other colonies), with the image file named Cross of Burgundy. FOTW (Burgundy Cross Flag): the red saltire raguly on white was Spain's ensign from 1506 and its military flag to 1843. U.S. National Park Service: this white flag with the red Burgundian saltire was carried by Spanish ships and flown over the fortresses guarding Spain's New World possessions until the red-and-gold ensign of 1785.
era-1776.open: No source names the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata or Upper Peru's own use of the cross; the Wikipedia caption gives the Spanish flag in Bolivia to 1825 but is not discussed in its text, and from 1785 the red-yellow-red flag replaced the cross at sea. The 1776 start comes from none of the sources read.

era-1559.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Bolivia): the colonial Spanish Empire flag in Bolivia is captioned 1506-1825, with the image file named Cross of Burgundy. FOTW (Burgundy Cross Flag): the cross was Spain's ensign from 1506 and military flag to 1843. U.S. National Park Service: it was the flag flown by ships and over fortresses in Spain's New World possessions.
era-1559.open: No source mentions the Audiencia of Charcas or its 1559 founding; the Spanish flag is attested for the empire and for Bolivia in general, not for the Audiencia, and the schematic simplified saltire on the page is a drawing, not a surveyed flag.

era-1998.says: FOTW (Engene, quoting Bullivant, 5 February 1998) says that on 4 February 1998, parliament not having agreed, the High Representative chose among three designs offered by an expert commission, that the colours were changed to match the Council of Europe's, and that the triangle represents the three constituent peoples. Wikipedia says High Representative Carlos Westendorp proclaimed the flag on 4 February 1998 and that the triangle approximates the country's shape.
era-1998.open: FOTW says it was not chosen through a public competition. Wikipedia names Mladen Kolobarić as designer but tags it citation-needed. This page's reason for the colours («neither side claimed them») was not found in either source; FOTW gives the yellow as a sun and symbol of hope and the blue and stars as Europe.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia: the white flag with the Kotromanic lily arms was adopted 20 May 1992 and used until 3 February 1998. FOTW: adopted provisionally 6 April 1992 and permanently 20 May 1992, a white field with a blue shield, white bend and six golden fleurs-de-lis, described as the medieval Kotromanic arms; white chosen in May 1992 because the earlier blue was too close to the UN flag. Radio Slobodna Evropa: it was the official flag of the Republic from recognition in 1992 until 1998 and Republika Srpska authorities regard it as a Bosniak war flag.
era-1992.open: How the flag was chosen is given only by FOTW; Serb and Croat objections as described on this page are reported in general terms only by RSE (RS view of it as a Bosniak war flag); FOTW does not mention objections.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: red flag with the federal Yugoslav tricolour in the canton, officially adopted 31 December 1946, lasting until 6 April 1992. FOTW: adopted 31 December 1946, red with the Yugoslav tricolour and a yellow-edged red star in the canton, retained in the 1974 Constitution; people favoured red because the national tricolours of Serbs and Croats were seen as later imports.
era-1945.open: The era is dated from 1945 but both sources date the flag from 31 December 1946; FOTW gives no end date (Wikipedia: 1992); the page's explanation of why Bosnia had no historic flag to revive is not in either source.

era-1878.says: FOTW: after the occupation Austria-Hungary adopted a horizontal red-yellow flag with the arms in the middle for Bosnia (1878-1908), and a red-yellow horizontal bicolour after the 1908 annexation; the arms were based on those of Stjepan Vukcic Hrvatinic. Wikipedia (flag article): Bosnia a red-and-yellow horizontal bicolour and Herzegovina the reversed colours, changed after 1908 (citation needed). Wikipedia's coat-of-arms article says both lands received arms in 1878 inspired by those of Hrvoje Vukcic Hrvatinic.
era-1878.open: Which Hrvatinic (Stjepan or Hrvoje) the arms derive from differs between FOTW and Wikipedia; the Herzegovina reversed bicolour rests on Wikipedia alone (FOTW says Herzegovina had no provincial colours in 1897, citing Meyers); which colour was on top is not spelled out beyond 'red-yellow'.

era-1463.says: Wikipedia: Gradascevic's 1831-32 revolt used a green flag with a yellow crescent and star (citation needed); a green flag with a white crescent and eight-pointed star was used in Herzegovina and at the second siege of Hotin. FOTW's Ottoman-era page confirms a swallow-tailed West Herzegovina war flag at Hotin and a flag of the 1831-32 uprising, but gives no colours in its text and says the exact date of use is unknown.
era-1463.open: The colours rest on Wikipedia alone (citation needed); FOTW does not state them and its text does not mention a plain red general Ottoman flag, so the page's 'general Ottoman flag was plain red' is unsourced.

era-1377.says: Wikipedia's flag article and its Kingdom of Bosnia article both give the kings' arms as a blue shield with six golden lilies around a white bend (kingdom 1377-1463; Tvrtko crowned autumn 1377). The Kingdom article shows a 'royal banner of King Tvrtko I' without describing it.
era-1377.open: Both are Wikipedia. FOTW's medieval page covers only the 1350 Book of All Kingdoms 'Boxina' flag (yellow-red with a white star), not the Kotromanic arms; the Hrvatska enciklopedija entry on the Kotromanici gives the 1377-91 and 1463 dates but says nothing of arms. No second publisher states the arms or that a white-field flag bore them.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia (NDH article): the Independent State of Croatia encompassed all of Bosnia and Herzegovina; its flag is shown for 1941-1945. FOTW: the NDH state flag (red-white-blue with the state arms and the Ustasa U) was fixed by law-decree of 28 April 1941 and used everywhere except by naval forces; the state ended 8 May 1945.
era-1941.open: Neither source says the NDH flag was flown in Bosnia by name (FOTW does not mention Bosnia); the 'Greater Croatia' intent is not covered.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia): the Kingdom's flag was a blue-white-red horizontal tricolour, officially adopted 1922. It does not mention Bosnia in this period. Neither the Bosnia flag articles nor FOTW's Bosnia page cover 1918-1941.
era-1918.open: No source read states that Bosnia had no distinct flag of its own in 1918-1941 or that the tricolour flew there; FOTW's Yugoslav history page was not found (404).

era-1154.says: Wikipedia's Kingdom of Bosnia article says the Banate lasted from at least 1154 to 1377 and gives the Kotromanic arms (blue shield, six golden lilies, white bend); it does not date the arms to the Banate. FOTW's medieval page shows only the 1350 'Boxina' yellow-red flag with a white star, attributing Bosnia then to the Frankopan family.
era-1154.open: No second publisher states the lilies for the Banate period; the Angevin homage and wildflower tradition are not covered; FOTW's 1350 Boxina flag is a different design.

era-1885.says: Wikipedia: the Bechuanaland Protectorate was formed in 1885; before independence the territory had no distinctive national emblems and flew the Union Jack; the national flag was adopted 30 September 1966. FOTW (High Commissioner): the High Commissioner for Basutoland, Bechuanaland and Swaziland (1931-68) flew a Union Flag with a crowned H.C. roundel in a laurel garland, and 'no mention is made of distinctive badges or ensigns for Swaziland or the Bechuanaland Protectorate' (only Basutoland, a Crown Colony, had a badge, in 1951).
era-1885.open: The page's Blue Ensign with a Bechuanaland badge is contradicted: the sources show no territorial flag, only the Union Flag and the High Commissioner's flag. The drawing needs replacing.

era-1889.says: Wikipedia says a provisional flag inspired by the US flag flew from 15 to 19 November 1889 until Deodoro da Fonseca vetoed it, that Decree No. 4 of 19 November 1889 legally replaced the monarchy's flag, that Raimundo Teixeira Mendes, Miguel Lemos, Manuel Pereira Reis and Décio Villares designed the new one, that the 1889 flag had 21 stars, that stars were added on 21 April 1960 (Guanabara), 30 May 1968 (Acre) and under Law No. 8,421 of 11 May 1992, and that Law No. 5,700 of 1 September 1971 sets the construction. FOTW says Decree No. 4 of 19 November 1889 established the basic design, that Benjamin Constant prepared the decree, that the sphere depicts Rio's sky on 15 November 1889, that the original had 21 stars, and that Law 5443 of 28 May 1968 modified the flag.
era-1889.open: The sources disagree about Law 8421: FOTW dates it 1972 in one place and 1992 in another, and Wikipedia's body says it added four stars in one section and six in another. FOTW does not cover the 1960 change.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia says Pedro I's decree of 18 September 1822 marks the independent Kingdom's flag, that Debret designed the royal standard that became the imperial flag (citation needed), that green stood for the House of Braganza and yellow for the House of Habsburg, that the first imperial flag is captioned as having 19 stars, and that Law No. 704 of 29 August 1853 added a 20th star for Paraná. FOTW says Brazilian flag historians attribute the lozenge design to Debret, that Pedro signed three decrees on 18 September 1822 including one creating the green-and-yellow cockade, and that the imperial flag carried an armillary sphere as its central charge.
era-1822.open: The star count changed within this era (19 stars, then 20 in 1853, and more later), so the single drawing cannot be right for all of 1822–1889.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia: Brazil was raised to a kingdom united with Portugal and the Algarves in 1815, and a charter of 1816 gave Brazil arms of a gold armillary sphere on a blue field. FOTW (Colonial Flags of Brazil): the flag of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves was used 1816-1822; the 1816 law quoted gives the Brazilian Kingdom 'a like ensign, a gold armillary sphere in a blue field', which FOTW calls the Brazilian flag from then, while the united kingdom's flag was a 'union jack' of the Portuguese empire.
era-1815.open: Neither source describes the united kingdom's flag in words here; the page's claim that Brazil had no flag of its own is contradicted - an armillary-sphere ensign for Brazil was decreed in 1816.

era-1500.says: Wikipedia: Portuguese merchant ships to Brazil before 1692 used a green-and-white maritime flag linked to the House of Braganza (citing the Cruzeiros National Association), and a new merchant flag of 1692 had a white field and a golden armillary sphere (citation needed). FOTW (Colonial Flags of Brazil): the Order of Christ banner (a cross, usually red) was the banner hoisted in the Portuguese territories from the first landing; the Iberian Union 1580-1640; the Dutch West India Company's flag used as the local flag of Dutch Brazil (1630-54, ended 1661); the Principality of Brazil's flag after 1645, which a contributor says was the heir's personal flag and probably never flew there.
era-1500.open: Neither source gives one colonial banner for the whole 1500-1815 span; the page's statement that none exists is consistent with them, but 'variants of the Portuguese royal arms' is not what they list (Order of Christ cross, a green-and-white maritime flag, the 1692 armillary flag, and the Dutch company flag).

era-1984.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1959, before this era begins in 1984, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 29 September 1959; Flags of the World dates it September 1959.
era-1984.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1959.says: Both: flag adopted 29 September 1959 with the constitution, the crest added to the striped flag (Wikipedia: designer Pengiran Muhammad Yusuf; FOTW: crest superimposed after the 1959 constitution).
era-1959.open: FOTW also gives 1932 for the coat of arms, unreconciled; the self-government framing is uncovered.

era-1945.says: Both: the yellow flag with white and black diagonals dates from 1906 and was used to 1959 (Wikipedia caption 1906-1959; FOTW 1906-1959 flag, 17:15 per Crampton).
era-1945.open: Neither source treats 1945 as a boundary; the colour meanings differ between sources.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia (Japanese occupation of British Borneo, first 100,000 of 240,500 characters): the infobox flag, captioned 'Flag of Japanese-occupied British Borneo', is the Japanese flag, and schoolchildren bowed to the Japanese flag each morning; Brunei's own 1906-1959 flag appears only as a predecessor entry. Flags of the World (historical flags) dates the Japanese occupation from 1941 and gives no end date or occupation-era flag.
era-1942.open: The Japanese flag in occupied Brunei rests on Wikipedia alone; a Japanese military administration ensign and the statement that no Bruneian flag flew are not covered by either source; Flags of the World gives no end date for the occupation.

era-1888.says: Wikipedia: solid yellow until 1906, then white and black diagonals added; a caption labels a flag 'from 1888 to 1906' without describing it. Flags of the World (historical flags): the plain yellow flag before 1906 (Kariyasu 2000; Sache asks which flag was used from 1886 to 1906 and gets no firm answer); the 1906-1959 flag has white and black diagonal stripes on yellow (Flaggenbuch 1939; Dorling-Kindersley 1997: 'a similar version without the coat of arms was first used in 1906'), stripe proportions 17:15 (Kariyasu, queried); Brunei became a protectorate in 1886 per that page, 1888 per this one.
era-1888.open: Two publishers agree on plain yellow before 1906 and the striped flag after it, so this page's plain yellow for the whole 1888-1942 era is contradicted for 1906-1942; whether the stripes were flown continuously to 1942 is not stated.

era-15.says: Wikipedia: before 1906 the sultans and officials such as the wazirs used personal standards as Brunei's only flags, and yellow is traditionally the royal colour in Southeast Asia. Flags of the World (Brunei historical flags): 'Yellow was the royal colour of Borneo' (W. J. Chater, Sarawak Long Ago, 1969, quoted by C. C. Teo 1998) and 'the plain yellow flag was used in Brunei which represents Brunei's Sultan' before 1906 (Kariyasu 2000).
era-15.open: Both publishers support yellow as the sultan's colour, but neither describes any 15th-century flag, and the plain yellow flag is attested only for the years before 1906 by a single contributor; the drawing is a representative colour, not a documented banner.

era-1989.says: Wikipedia says the Zhivkov Constitution was amended so the pre-communist flag could return, readopted on 27 November 1990, and that the 1991 Constitution (Art. 166) describes a horizontal white, green and red tricolour. FOTW says the 27 November 1990 amendment removed the coat of arms from the description, that the fourth Constitution took effect on 13 July 1991 with no coat of arms, and that the current coat of arms was adopted on 21 July 1997.
era-1989.open: Neither source says the 1991 text 'keeps the coat of arms as a separate state symbol'; the 1997 arms law is FOTW's.

era-632.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia says the Dimitrov Constitution kept the colours and put the People's Republic emblem at the hoist of the white stripe; a version valid from 27 January 1948, a slightly redesigned emblem from 5 January 1967, and a ribbon split into 681 and 1944 first hoisted on 21 May 1971. FOTW dates the second Constitution to 6 December 1947 and the third to 18 May 1971.
era-1946.open: The emblem's parts (wheat wreath, star, dam and factory) are not described in either source; the 1946 date of the republic is not in them.

era-1878.says: Wikipedia says the flag was first adopted in 1879 after the 1877–78 war, in Article 23 of the Tarnovo Constitution, as three horizontal colours white, green and red. FOTW gives 16 April 1879 and notes a white-green-red banner with a lion and 'BULGARIA' presented at Braila in 1877, and a view that a 1878 constitution confirmed the tricolour without a lion.
era-1878.open: No flag for Eastern Rumelia in either source; the earlier 'almost immediately' and green flag claims were not found.

era-1885.says: Wikipedia and the FOTW main page give the white-green-red tricolour from 1879. FOTW's page on the principality (1878-1908) quotes the first constitution of 16 April 1879 (article 23: three horizontal colours, white, green, red), shows the merchant ensign as the plain tricolour and the naval ensign as the tricolour with a red canton bearing a golden crowned lion, and gives a prince's standard with a crowned lion.
era-1885.open: The lion is on the naval ensign's canton and the prince's standard, not on the national flag as these sources describe it, so the lion drawn on this page's flag is not shown by them to belong to the national flag. The union with Eastern Rumelia (1885) is not covered by FOTW's page or the flag articles.

era-1908.says: Wikipedia and FOTW's main page give the same tricolour from 1879 to 1947. FOTW's pages on the kingdom (1908-1944) describe the royal standards and a naval ensign that keeps the principality's pattern, a tricolour with a red canton bearing a crowned lion, 'the shape of the crown ... established' (Bogoslovski 1912, Flaggenbuch 1939).
era-1908.open: A crown appears on the lion of the naval ensign's canton and on the royal standards in FOTW; neither source puts a crown on the plain national flag, so the crown drawn on this page's flag is not shown to belong to it. The 1908 independence date is not stated by Wikipedia's flag article or by FOTW's main page.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia dates the coup to 9 September 1944 and gives the national flag with no crown and no lion until the emblem of 1947. FOTW's page on 1944-1946 says the kingdom's flags became obsolete on 9 September 1944, that navy commanders chose designs at will, and (from a 1955 atlas, contributor note) that a tricolour with the letters 'OF' (Fatherland Front) on the green stripe was used 1944-1947.
era-1944.open: The OF-lettered tricolour rests on a single FOTW contributor's report from a 1955 atlas and is not on this page; the page's plain tricolour is what Wikipedia and FOTW's main page give. The page's 1946 end date and the 'Soviet-occupied transition' wording are not stated by these sources, which put the next change at the 1947 constitution.

era-1941.says: FOTW treats 1908 to 9 September 1944 as one period of kingdom flags, all abandoned on that date, and its section on changes in 1937-1944 lists only a division commander's flag (1937) and colours given to naval units (December 1937). Wikipedia and FOTW's main page give the plain tricolour as the national flag from 1879 until the 1947 constitution.
era-1941.open: Neither the flag articles nor FOTW's pages discuss the Axis alliance or 1941 as such, so the row rests on the tricolour being in force throughout the kingdom's period, not on a source describing 1941-1944 flags specifically.

era-1396.says: Neither flag article describes Ottoman-period flags in Bulgaria. FOTW's page on 19th-century Bulgarian flags shows insurgent banners from the Ottoman period (the 'Freedom or Death' flag in the Sofia War Museum; the April Uprising 1876 district flag, captured and probably burnt), and FOTW's Ottoman index lists a Bulgaria page; Wikipedia's article on Ottoman Bulgaria labels its infobox flag as the Ottoman Empire's.
era-1396.open: No source read states that the Ottoman red flag with crescent and star was the flag flown in Bulgarian lands, or that no Bulgarian flag existed; the insurgent banners are not state flags but show the claim 'no distinct Bulgarian flag' is too absolute. Ottoman flag changes across 1396-1878 were not checked.

era-1185.says: Wikipedia's flag article: 14th-15th century portolan maps show Second Empire flags with white or golden grounds and red Shishman insignia or unidentified symbols, no lion. Wikipedia's article on the Second Bulgarian Empire captions two flags 'according to Dulcert's portolan (c. 1325)' and 'according to Soler's portolan (c. 1380)'. FOTW: only the 1997 coat of arms (crowned lion) uses crowns modelled on Second Bulgarian State rulers; FOTW's page on the principality adds that the lion was known from the late 14th century on coins of Tsar Ivan Shishman (citing Smith 1975).
era-1185.open: No second publisher describes the portolan flags, and none ties a gold lion on dark red to the Asen dynasty; the drawing remains an unverified heraldic reconstruction. A Bulgarian museum or academic source for the medieval banners was not found in the pages read.

era-1018.says: Wikipedia's flag article mentions red banners for Krum and Simeon of the First Empire that cannot be verified, and notes the Byzantine flags on the maps look consistent; Wikipedia's article on the First Bulgarian Empire captions a 'war flag of Krum's army' from the Manasses Chronicle (before 1018). Neither it nor FOTW (main, 1878-1908, 1908-1944 and 19th-century pages) describes a flag for Bulgarian lands under Byzantine rule in 1018-1185.
era-1018.open: No source read gives a flag for Bulgarian lands under Byzantine rule, 1018-1185; the schematic imperial device is not established, and its Byzantine imperial basis was not checked in a Byzantine flag source.

era-1984.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 4 August 1984. FOTW's Burkina Faso page says the flag was adopted 4 August 1984 after the August coup, in the pan-African colours with a yellow star over the red and green stripes (red for the revolution, green for abundance, the star as the revolution's guiding light).
era-1984.open: Design and swatch colours not checked against a specification.

era-1500.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: the Upper Volta flag was introduced on independence, 5 August 1960, listed for 1960-1984, its bands standing for the Black, White and Red Volta. FOTW's Upper Volta page: the flag was horizontal black-white-red for the same three rivers and was in use until the 1984 change.
era-1960.open: The adoption date differs: FOTW says 9 December 1959 (citing Smith 1975), Wikipedia 5 August 1960.

era-1958.says: FOTW's Upper Volta page says the black-white-red flag was adopted on 9 December 1959 (citing Smith 1975), within the 1958-60 autonomous republic; Wikipedia lists the Republic of Upper Volta for 1958-1960 with no separate flag and dates the black-white-red flag to independence on 5 August 1960.
era-1958.open: The sources disagree by eight months on adoption (December 1959 against August 1960), so the tricolour for the whole of 1958-60 is not established; nothing read says which flag flew from 1958 to late 1959 (presumably the French tricolour).

era-1904.says: Wikipedia says the French tricolour was the official flag of French Upper Volta and lists its periods 1904-1919, 1919-1932, 1932-1947 and 1947-1958; its French Upper Volta infobox shows the French flag. FOTW's French colonial empire page says that use of the French flag was the rule in all French colonies, local flags the exception, and lists Upper Volta among the French West Africa colonies.
era-1904.open: FOTW also notes governors' flags; whether a distinct local ensign existed for Upper Volta is not addressed by either source.

era-1967.says: Wikipedia: the flag that became the current design was adopted 28 June 1967 (ratio 2:3 changed to 3:5 on 27 September 1982); white saltire for peace, green for hope, red for the nation's suffering in the freedom struggle; three red six-pointed stars for Hutu, Twa and Tutsi and for Unity, Work, Progress. FOTW: current flag adopted 28 June 1967; ratio 3:5 set 27 September 1982; red the independence struggle, green hope, white peace; stars for the motto and said to represent Hutu, Tutsi and Twa.
era-1967.open: The page's era label gives 1966 for the republic, which neither source dates; the 1967 date shown for the flag is 28 June 1967.
