era-1600.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1962.says: Wikipedia: the first national flag was adopted 1 July 1962 and included a karyenda drum as a symbol of the monarchy; in November 1966 the drum was replaced with a sorghum plant. FOTW (historical page): the independence flag consisted of a white saltire dividing the field into alternating red and green areas with a central disc; the drum was removed after the monarchy fell in 1966 (28 November 1966 republic), leaving the sorghum plant; the king reportedly ordered a red-drum variant changed.
era-1962.open: Both sources confirm 1 July 1962 and the drum in the flag, but FOTW describes a white saltire over red and green quarters with a central disc, not the plain white field with a gold drum drawn here; the exact 1966 dates conflict within FOTW.

era-1916.says: FOTW (historical page): Ruanda-Urundi became a Belgian League of Nations mandate (20 July 1922 in one passage, 24 October 1924 in another) and a UN trust territory 1946-1961; it describes no Ruanda-Urundi flag. Wikipedia and FOTW on Burundi do not cover the period.
era-1916.open: No source read describes the flag used in Ruanda-Urundi; the Belgian tricolour with a badge is not established, and the mandate start dates in FOTW conflict (1916 occupation versus 1922/1924).

era-1897.says: FOTW (Burundi historical page): the area came under German control in 1903 and became part of German East Africa. FOTW (German East Africa page, read for Tanzania): the governors' flag from 1898 was the black-white-red national flag with the uncrowned imperial eagle in the white stripe; a 1914 colonial flag was never adopted. No source describes a flag flown over Burundi itself.
era-1897.open: The black field with a black-white-red canton drawn here is not described by any source read, and the German date differs from this page's c. 1897 start (FOTW says 1903).

era-1993.says: Wikipedia says the present flag was first adopted in 1948 and readopted on 24 September 1993 after the Constituent Assembly election and the restoration of the monarchy. Flags of the World's history page says the 1948-1970 flag, a blue-red-blue triband with a white Angkor Wat, was reestablished on 30 June 1993 (the main page gives 29 October 1948, the history page 20 October 1948, for the original adoption); in 1993 the temple is usually outlined black rather than red.
era-1993.open: The sources differ on the 1993 day (24 September per Wikipedia, 30 June per FOTW) and on the October 1948 day. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-802.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1970.says: Wikipedia gives adoption on 9 October 1970 and relinquishment on 17 April 1975, and describes the flag as a blue field with a red canton bearing a white Angkor Wat and three white stars in the upper fly corner. Flags of the World's history page gives the same design and dates (introduced 9 October 1970, used until April 1975).
era-1970.open: The two sources agree with each other but not with this page: the drawing and text show a blue field with a red border and no stars, where both sources have a red canton with Angkor Wat and three white stars. Left unreviewed until the drawing is checked.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia gives adoption in 1976 and relinquishment in 1979. Flags of the World's history page says the January 1976 constitution of Democratic Kampuchea set a red field with a three-towered yellow stylised temple (called only a 'monument' in the constitution), used until January 1979 and afterwards by Khmer Rouge forces and at the UN.
era-1975.open: The era starts in 1975, but FOTW says that from April 1975 to January 1976 plain red flags seem to have been used inside the country and the 1948-1970 flag stood at the UN; the page's 'plain red field' fits 1975 only if that is meant. A contributor adds that a plain red flag may have flown beside the national flag.

era-1979.says: Wikipedia: in 1979 the PRK was established after the Vietnamese invasion and the FUNSK revived the Khmer Issarak flag, with the colour pattern of the Democratic Kampuchea flag but a yellow five-towered Angkor Wat silhouette; the infobox dates the PRK flag 1979-1989; in 1989 the State of Cambodia flag's lower half became blue; UNTAC flag used 1992-1993. Flags of the World's history page agrees: a flag based on the 1976-1979 one with five towers instead of three, used 1979-1989; on 1 May 1989 a red over blue bicolour with a yellow five-towered Angkor Wat for the State of Cambodia; a UN blue flag with a white map under UNTAC.
era-1979.open: The drawing (plain red with the emblem) fits only 1979-1989; the State of Cambodia flag of 1989-1991 and the UNTAC flag are different designs that fall within this page's 1979-1993 span. The sources call the emblem yellow, not gold.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: the blue-red-blue design with Angkor Wat was adopted in 1948 and used 1948-1953 under the protectorate and 1953-1970 after independence; the Khmer Republic flag replaced it on 9 October 1970. FOTW: the present horizontal-band flag was officially adopted on 29 October 1948 and used until October 1970; the present flag returned on 24 September 1993.
era-1953.open: Neither source mentions a separate 1953 flag; the colour of the silhouette (white) and the number of towers are not described in the sources read.

era-1863.says: Wikipedia lists Cambodian protectorate flags for 1863-1940 and 1940-1948 (colour labels blue, red and white) and says Angkor Wat has appeared in the centre of the flag since around 1875. Flags of the World's history page says the first Cambodian flag probably dates from about 1863 and was used, with variations, until 1948: a red field with a blue border and a white Angkor Wat, on the evidence of Flaggenbuch, with a different variant in the Flag Bulletin.
era-1863.open: Neither source says the plain French tricolour was the protectorate's flag, and FOTW and Wikipedia both end the period's Cambodian flag in 1948, not 1953. Whether the tricolour flew beside the Cambodian flag is not covered.

era-1975.says: Both sources give 1975, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 26 October 1957; Flags of the World dates it 20 May 1975.
era-1975.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1394.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1961.says: WP: 1961-1975 Federal Republic flag had two gold stars in the upper half of the green band for East and West Cameroon. FOTW: in 1961, when Southern Cameroon joined, two yellow stars were added to the upper green stripe (citing Cannon).
era-1961.open: Both sources read are compiled; WP's stars paragraph is uncited.

era-1957.says: WP: tricolour (green, red, yellow) adopted 26 Oct 1957 by Law 46, confirmed by the 21 Feb 1960 constitution; pan-African colours, Cameroon 'second state to adopt'. FOTW: first flag adopted 29 Oct 1957 (law 57/46), vertical green-red-yellow.
era-1957.open: Sources differ on 26 vs 29 October. Whether the 1957 flag had no star, and any Ethiopian link, are not stated.

era-1916.says: Wikipedia's page shows a French Cameroon flag (1916-1960) and a British Cameroons flag (1922-1961). FOTW's French colonial page lists Cameroon as a mandate of French Equatorial Africa whose common flag was the French Tricolore; its Cameroon history page says the territory was divided on 28 June 1919 between a French mandate (Cameroun) and British mandates (Northern and Southern Cameroons) administered from Nigeria, that the British territories 'did not have distinctive flags or badges' (a 1922 badge was proposed and probably never used) and that the Union Flag was lowered over Buea in 1961.
era-1916.open: Neither publisher gives the design of the Wikipedia captions, and FOTW does not explicitly say the Tricolore flew in Cameroun itself or the Union Jack in the British Cameroons before 1961; the page's 'no unified flag existed' is the only part left unsupported. FOTW dates the split to 1919, Wikipedia's French flag to 1916.

era-1884.says: FOTW's Cameroon history page says German colonies and protectorates had no flags of their own and used Imperial German arms and flags throughout the Empire, and that Wilhelm Solf's 1914 colonial arms and flags (for Kamerun, an elephant head) were never implemented because of the war; FOTW's colonial flags page lists Kamerun 1884-February 1916. Wikipedia's page shows a German Colonial Office flag and a 'proposed flag of German Cameroon' that was never adopted.
era-1884.open: The page's black-white-red ensign with a Kamerun badge is contradicted by both: the badge flag was only a 1914 proposal. Which German flag (the black-white-red national flag or the imperial naval ensign) flew over Kamerun is not stated, so the row's claim holds only as 'imperial German flags, no colony flag'.

era-1965.says: Wikipedia says the House of Commons passed the design 163 to 78 on 15 December 1964, the Senate approved it two days later, Queen Elizabeth II signed the royal proclamation on 28 January 1965, and the flag was inaugurated on Parliament Hill on 15 February 1965; its all-party committee voted 15 to 0 for George Stanley's single-leaf design. FOTW says Parliament adopted the National Flag on 22 October 1964, certified it on 28 January 1965, and that it was proclaimed by the Queen and took effect on 15 February 1965, after a «33-day debate».
era-1965.open: The sources disagree on the parliamentary date (15 December or 22 October 1964). Wikipedia credits Stanley's design.

era-1000.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner recorded for this brief Norse outpost».
era-1000.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1921.says: Wikipedia says the Royal Arms proclaimed in 1921 made red and white the official colours, that the coat of arms replaced the composite shield on the Red Ensign, that an Order in Council of 1924 approved it for government buildings abroad, and that a 1945 Order in Council approved it wherever a distinctive Canadian flag was desirable. FOTW says the Red Ensign was used from 1870 and authorised by the British Admiralty for use at sea in 1892, that red and white are the official colours King George V designated in 1921, and that the 1921 arms showed three maple leaves.
era-1921.open: This page used to call it «semi-official»; both sources describe formal approvals. A 1946 parliamentary committee recommended a red ensign with a golden maple leaf and the prime minister declined to act (Wikipedia).

era-1957.says: Flags of the World (Canada, Prothero): the maple leaves in the arms were green in 1921 and not changed to red until 1957; (the 1957 Red Ensign page) on 8 October 1957 the government announced that the maple leaves would be red, with the Irish harp changed. Wikipedia (Canadian Red Ensign): the 1957 version has red and gold leaves where the 1922-1957 version had green leaves. The Canadian Heraldic Authority's register blazons the ensign as the Royal Union Flag in the canton with the shield of the Dominion's arms in the fly, in use until the national flag of 1965.
era-1957.open: The register entry does not mention the leaf colour; the ensign's date is given as 1957-1965 by FOTW and Wikipedia treats 1957 as a revision of the 1922 design.

era-1867.says: Wikipedia says the first Canadian flag after Confederation was the governor general's flag, a Union Flag with a shield (1867); that no official national flag was adopted in 1867–1965 and the Union Flag was the de facto flag in Canada; and that the Red Ensign with a Canadian composite shield was used unofficially from 1870 and approved by the British Admiralty in 1892. FOTW (Palac) says the Red Ensign, created in 1707 as the Merchant Navy ensign, was used on sea and land from 1870 and authorised at sea as the Red Canadian Ensign in 1892.
era-1867.open: FOTW describes a parliamentary resolution of 18 December 1964 approving continued use of the Union flag as a Commonwealth symbol. This page's «only fully official flag» is stronger than Wikipedia's «de facto».

era-1534.says: Wikipedia: Cartier planted a cross bearing French royal arms at Gaspe in 1534; the Royal Banner of France was a blue flag with three gold fleurs-de-lis flown over early fortifications, and the completely white flag of the French Royal Navy was flown from ships and forts. Flags of the World (French Canada before 1763): from 1534 to 1763 the royal banner of France, azure with three gold fleurs-de-lis, was the most commonly used flag in New France, and French military flags including the white flag of the royal navy were also flown; it does not mention Cartier.
era-1534.open: Both sources make the blue Royal Banner the main flag and the white naval flag a secondary one; the card shows only the white flag and no source dates it for 1534-1763 or calls it the standard royal banner.

era-1763.says: Flags of the World (Canada 1763-1865): after the Treaty of Paris the Royal Union Flag was flown over British North America, the 1606 version until the 1801 version with the Irish cross. Wikipedia: the Union Flag was the de facto British national flag in Canada from British settlement in Nova Scotia after 1621, the Red Ensign in unofficial use from the 1860s, and a United Empire Loyalist flag used by Loyalists (undated).
era-1763.open: Neither source says the Union Flag was the sole flag or gives it a legal status in the separate colonies; the colonies' own flags and the Loyalist flag are not described.

era-1992.says: Both sources give 1992, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 25 September 1992; Flags of the World dates it 22 Sep 1992.
era-1992.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia: first national flag hoisted 5 July 1975, official by law on 19 April 1976; yellow and green horizontal bands with a red hoist band bearing a black star framed by corn and a shell; based on the PAIGC flag like Guinea-Bissau's; replaced 25 September 1992. FOTW (cv_1975): very similar to Guinea-Bissau's flag but 2:3 instead of 1:2, with a black star, maize wreath and golden scallop shell; both flags derive from the PAIGC flag; Cape Verde changed it in 1992 (22 September per cv.html) after the 1980 coup in Guinea-Bissau ended the planned union.
era-1975.open: FOTW gives no adoption dates for 1975-76 and does not state the band order in the text read; Wikipedia and FOTW differ by three days on the 1992 change (25 vs 22 September). The page's 'PAICV' attribution: Wikipedia says the PAICV succeeded the PAIGC in 1980.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia (Portuguese Cape Verde): the infobox flag is the official Portuguese flag dated 1910-1975, the colony's arms are dated 1951-1975, and proposed flags of 1932 and 1965 appear as proposals only. Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): the republican green (hoist, 2/5) and red (fly, 3/5) flag with the arms and armillary sphere was presented 1 December 1910 and made official by decree of 19 June 1911. FOTW (pt-hist): the republican vertical green-red flag with armillary sphere dates from 1910; FOTW does not clearly describe colonial use, and its Cape Verde history page lists only a 1967 colonial flag proposal.
era-1910.open: Portugal's own flag is established by two publishers, but its use over Cape Verde 1910-75 rests on Wikipedia's infobox only; neither FOTW page confirms it, and the page's 'without change' is unproven (the 1932 and 1965/1967 proposals were not adopted as far as read).

era-1830.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): in 1830 the liberal government on Terceira decreed a flag of equal blue (hoist) and white (fly) with the arms centred on the boundary, in use from Maria II's return in 1834 until 1910. FOTW (pt-hist): 1830-1910 a vertical blue-white bicolour with the arms, approved 1830 and hoisted in Lisbon only in 1833. Wikipedia (Portuguese Cape Verde) shows no flag for this period, only anthems (Hino da Carta 1826-1910).
era-1830.open: Portugal's flag is established by two publishers; its use in Cape Verde 1830-1910 is not stated by any source read. Wikipedia and FOTW differ on the hoisting date (1834 use vs 1833).

era-1495.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): in 1495 Manuel I changed the national flag to a white 2:3 rectangle with the coat of arms (the earlier square banner of arms was last used by John II in 1485); the arms became seven castles round-shield in 1521. FOTW (pt-hist): 1495-1830 a white field charged with the national arms, with a green Order of Christ flag in 1640-56. Wikipedia (Portuguese Cape Verde) dates the colony from 1462 and shows no flag for the period.
era-1495.open: Portugal's flag is established by two publishers; use over Cape Verde 1495-1830 is not stated by any source read, and the page's 'five small blue shields' quinas-only banner is a simplification of the arms described.

era-1460.says: Wikipedia (Portuguese Cape Verde): the Portuguese founded Ribeira Grande in 1462 and the colony's span is 1462-1975. Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): before 1495 the national flag was a banner of arms with the royal shield filling the field, John II's 1485 square banner being the last such flag.
era-1460.open: No source states the flag carried by Cape Verde's first settlers; the founding is dated 1462, not 1460. Before 1495 the royal banner was a square banner of arms per Wikipedia, not a white rectangle.

era-1958.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1894.says: Wikipedia: the flag of France was used during colonial Ubangi-Shari from 1903 until 1960 (it does not date 1894). FOTW: there was 'no distinctive colonial flag' and the French tricolour was used before independence; French Equatorial Africa ran 1910-1958 and no AEF flag is described.
era-1894.open: Start date differs: Wikipedia 1903, the page 1894, FOTW gives none; whether the tricolour was used until 1958 or 1960 is not settled.

era-1959.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1900.says: FOTW's page on the French colonial empire says the French Tricolore was the common flag of French Equatorial Africa and that Chad adopted its current flag on 6 November 1959 and 'had previously no other flag than the French Tricolore', while a special governor's flag (ochre with a red circle and a blue bird?) was reported but seems older (Second World War?). Wikipedia captions the French flag as used in French Equatorial Africa (1900-1959) and shows a Free French government of Chad flag and a personal flag of Pierre-Olivier Lapie (both 1940-1942); FOTW's Chad page dates the protectorate 1900, the colony 1920 and the province of French Equatorial Africa 1946.
era-1900.open: The Free French government of Chad flag (1940-1942) and the governor's flag are exceptions to 'no distinct territorial flag'; the governor's flag description in FOTW is a query ('blue bird?') and may belong to the Second World War period.

era-1990.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1817, before this era begins in 1990, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 18 October 1817; Flags of the World dates it 17 October 1817.
era-1990.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1818.says: Wikipedia: 18 October 1817 official by decree; 1854 square canton and 2:3 ratio; 1912 star diameter; 1967 Decree 1534. FOTW: 17–18 October 1817 decree by O'Higgins; the original carried a coat of arms; 1854 legislation; 1912 Law 2597; 1967 Decree 1534.
era-1818.open: The decree day differs (17 vs 18 October); the designer is disputed.

era-1817.says: Wikipedia: Patria Vieja flag reportedly raised 4 July 1812, formally adopted 1813; Reconquista 1814–17; a transitional blue-white-red flag in 1817 dropped within months; current flag 18 October 1817. FOTW: independence declared 1810 with the blue-white-yellow Patria Vieja; 1817 transitional blue-white-red horizontal tricolour; decree 17–18 October 1817.
era-1817.open: The sources date the Patria Vieja flag differently (1810 vs 1812).

era-1541.says: Wikipedia: colonial Chile used Spanish royal symbols including the Cross of Burgundy; 1785 flag for Spanish Armada ships. Flags of the World's Chile pages (history, variants) start with the Patria Vieja of 1812 and, for 1814-1816, say only that the relevant Spanish flags were used during the Reconquista.
era-1541.open: Only Wikipedia ties the Cross of Burgundy to colonial Chile; FOTW's Chile pages say nothing of 1541-1810. A general Spanish source for the cross (FOTW's Spain pages) does not mention Chile. The drawing is still a simplified approximation.

era-1973.says: Wikipedia: the construction of the flag is defined, at present, by Supreme Decree No. 1,534 of the Ministry of the Interior of 1967 (adopted 18 October 1817); it mentions Decree No. 890 of 1975 making public mistreatment of the flag a felony and the 1980 theft of the 1818 original flag by MIR members. Flags of the World quotes an official publication, 'About our Flag': the layout was fixed by legislation of 4 July 1854, the star size in 1912, and 'the flag was last regulated in a law of 18 October 1967'; a contributor adds that subsequent legislation has only specified the design without altering anything.
era-1973.open: No source describes the flag in use under the military government as such: the unchanged flag for 1973-1990 follows from both sources giving the 1967 decree as the current definition, and from neither recording a change. Wikipedia's note on the 1975 decree and the 1980 theft is not about design.

era-1949.says: Both sources give 1949, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1 October 1949; Flags of the World dates it 27 Sep 1949.
era-1949.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-2070bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner from either dynasty; Shang known through oracle bones, not flags».
era-2070bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1928.says: Wikipedia: Lu Haodong's design 21 February 1895; red field added by Sun in winter 1906; 17 December 1928 act; the 12 rays mean the twelve months and traditional hours. FOTW: twelve points mean the twelve traditional Chinese hours; Decree No. 47 dated 19 December 1928 cited by a contributor.
era-1928.open: The adoption day differs (9, 17 or 19 December 1928); the 'Wholly Red Earth' motto is not in either source.

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: the provisional Senate chose the Five-color flag in 1912; red Han, yellow Manchu, blue Mongol, white Hui, black Tibetan. FOTW (reader comment): five horizontal stripes red, yellow, blue, white and black for the Han and four other groups.
era-1912.open: FOTW is only a reader comment; the exact 1912 date is not given.

era-1644.says: Wikipedia: yellow dragon flag adopted 1862 (originally triangular), used as a makeshift national flag in 1868, rectangular version adopted 1889, used until the 1911 Revolution; azure dragon on yellow with a flaming red pearl; not originally meant as a national flag, used on official occasions and on official vessels. FOTW: dragon flag was state flag and naval ensign from 1872, Zhang Yinhuan proposed it as a national flag in May 1889 and the court adopted it; yellow stands for the Manchu and the dragon for the emperor; five claws for the emperor.
era-1644.open: The page's claim that the dragon was an imperial emblem used for centuries before the flag is not covered by the sources read; neither gives a day-level adoption date.

era-1368.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China; Wikipedia (Flag of the Qing dynasty) says yellow has been the royal colour of Chinese emperors since the Ming. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags) shows modern 'Ming flags' with a black character on a white disc at Nanjing's Zhonghua Gate, unsure whether they are replicas, and cites Todorović for historical variants in yellow, green, red or black and five-colour sets.
era-1368.open: No source describes a Ming state flag or documents red and gold banners; the sources point to yellow as the imperial colour and to varied colours for banners. The page's dragon-embroidered banners are uncovered.

era-1271.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags) mentions the Yuan only as the Mongol dynasty overthrown in 1356 and gives no Yuan flag; its main flag pages do not either.
era-1271.open: No source read describes a Yuan state flag, banner or colour, or says whether one existed; the black Mongol banner on the card is not covered. Mongol banners belong to the Mongol Empire page.

era-960.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags) describes twelfth-century Song paintings of the Cai Wenji story that show five plain flags in cardinal colours (green east, red south, white west, black north, yellow centre) plus a multicoloured one, which the author suggests may be a Song flag shown anachronistically.
era-960.open: Red appears only as one of five direction colours in later paintings, not as a dynastic colour; no source states that red was the Song's colour or that the Song had a state flag.

era-618.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags): a Dunhuang mural (Cave 156) shows yellow sun-and-moon flags and dark rectangular flags with four or seven tails, likely commemorating an 851 victory; paintings in Princess Changle's tomb (621-643) at the Zhao Mausoleum show plain red flags with very long tails.
era-618.open: These are flags in murals, not a Tang state flag; no source calls gold the Tang colour or describes a Buddhist palette. Both the red tomb flags and the yellow mural flags are cited, so the page's single gold swatch is not established.

era-206bce.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags) attributes a set of five cardinal-colour flags to the Han-era story of Cai Wenji (captured 194-195, returned 207) but doubts that the set was used jointly that early, and cites Willetts for the colour and direction system being completed in the Han period.
era-206bce.open: No source read gives the Han a state flag or says red was its colour; Wikipedia's Han dynasty article, read to 100,000 of 248,791 characters, does not mention dynastic colours or banners.

era-221bce.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China. Wikipedia (Wuxing) says Zou Yan paired ritual colours with elements, black with water, and that from the Qin onward most dynasties invoked the theory, but names no element or colour for the Qin. Wikipedia (Qin dynasty), read to 100,000 of 171,942 characters, says nothing on a dynastic colour or flags. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags) has no Qin flag.
era-221bce.open: The Qin's black or water association and any Qin banner are not stated by any source read.

era-1046bce.says: Wikipedia (Flag of China) calls the Qing dragon flag the first national flag of China. Flags of the World (early Chinese flags) cites Mencius that ordinary men were called with a plain red silk standard, scholars with a two-dragon standard and administrators with a five-coloured feather standard, and gives a reconstruction c.1500 BC in which twelve red ribbons marked the emperor. Wikipedia (Wuxing) names no Zhou colour.
era-1046bce.open: These are rank standards, not a Zhou state flag; no source states that red was the Zhou's dynastic colour or that cosmologists assigned it later.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia: current arrangement adopted 26 November 1861; Decree 861 of 17 May 1924 and Decree 62 of 11 January 1934. FOTW: 26 November 1861 as the flag-adoption date.
era-1861.open: The double-width yellow is from Wikipedia's description only; the 'unique among Gran Colombian states' claim is unsourced and dropped.

era-100bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — known through monumental stone statuary, not any banner».
era-100bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1819.says: Wikipedia: Miranda's flag first raised 12 March 1806; Gran Colombia's Congress adopted the colours on 17 December 1819. FOTW: Angostura Congress of 15 February 1819 adopted Venezuela's flag; Cúcuta constitution promulgated 3 October 1821 ratified the symbols.
era-1819.open: Neither source says whether the flag had a star.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia: the Republic of New Granada adopted the Gran Colombian colours on 9 May 1834, and its Flag of Colombia lists New Granada flags for 1831-1834 and 1834-1858; the New Granada article says the 1834 flag ran to 26 November 1861 and used the colours in a different arrangement. FOTW's historical page (citing a 1986 atlas) says Colombia kept the horizontal yellow-blue-red flag in the ratio 3:2:1 until 1834, then changed to equal vertical stripes red-blue-yellow, and to the present 2:1:1 flag on 26 November 1861.
era-1830.open: Neither the 1831-34 flag (unequal horizontal bands per FOTW) nor the 1834-61 flag (vertical stripes per FOTW) is the equal horizontal bands drawn here; FOTW's account rests on a single contributor citation. The drawing needs redrawing.

era-1550.says: FOTW's historical page says only Spanish flags were used in New Granada until 1810, that the Kingdom of New Granada had arms granted by Charles V in 1548, and (a contributor's remark) that the Cross of Burgundy was the Spanish flag from 1506 until 1785. Wikipedia's Viceroyalty of New Granada infobox shows the Cross of Burgundy flag.
era-1550.open: The Cross of Burgundy over New Granada rests on the Wikipedia infobox image and a general remark; after 1785 Spanish flags changed (red-yellow-red), and the viceregal seal's gold sun is not described by any source read.

era-1450.says: Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Colombia nor FOTW's Colombia pages (main, historical flags, indigenous peoples) mention the Muisca or any pre-Spanish flag; FOTW says only Spanish flags were used in New Granada until 1810, and Wikipedia's Muisca Confederation title redirects to a political-units article.
era-1450.open: Silence in these sources is not evidence that no Muisca banner existed; an archaeological or ethnohistorical source would be needed.

era-2001.says: Flags of the World: 'On 23 December 2001, a new Constitution was adopted, which prescribed a new flag, which was hoisted on 31 December 2001'; four horizontal stripes for the four islands (Ngazidja blue, Mwali yellow, Nzwani red, Maore white), a green triangle, and a crescent with four stars. Wikipedia: officially adopted on 23 December 2001, replacing the 1996 flag; stripes yellow, white, red, blue for Moheli, Mayotte, Anjouan and Grande Comore, crescent and four stars for the same islands, green for Islam.
era-2001.open: The sources differ slightly on the adoption route (FOTW: constitution of 23 December 2001, hoisted 31 December; Wikipedia: a referendum) and on the meaning of the green triangle (federation and possibly Islam in FOTW, Islam in Wikipedia); the caption's '2001-02' is not needed.

era-1975.says: Both publishers give the same sequence. Flags of the World: the 1963 flag continued after independence; the Soilih flag was used 12 November 1975 to 13 May 1978, red over green (top two thirds red) with the crescent and four stars in a diamond; after the 13 May 1978 coup the flag was officially changed on 23 May 1978 to a green field with a larger crescent and four stars between its horns; the 7 June 1992 constitution had the crescent point upward with the stars on a horizontal line. Wikipedia: the 1963 design continued in 1975; 12 November 1975 Soilih's two-thirds red; 1 October 1978 all green; 1992 rotated upward; 1996 added the Arabic words 'Muhammed' and 'Allah'.
era-1975.open: The card's 'in use with only minor variation 1975-2001' is not supported: the 1975-78 flag was two-thirds red, and the 1992 and 1996 flags changed the layout and added inscriptions (the 1996 flag is only on a FOTW link and Wikipedia). The 1978 date differs (FOTW 23 May, Wikipedia 1 October).

era-1841.says: Wikipedia lists the French flag for the Comoros as a former flag for 1887-1963 and the 1963 local flag designed by Suzanne Gauthier. Flags of the World: Ngazidja became a French protectorate on 24 June 1886 and was annexed in 1911 (ratified 23 February 1914); an 1889 coin shows a French tricolour with 'R.F' beside the sultan's white flag; the Comoros were incorporated into Madagascar in 1896 and became a Territory on 1 January 1947; the local flag dates from 13 July 1963.
era-1841.open: The French tricolour is attested as the flag of the Comoros only for about 1887-1963 (and shown beside the sultan's flag in 1889), not for 1841 (the Mayotte cession is not covered by any page read); the card's end date of 1975 ignores the 1963 local flag that both publishers record.

era-1991.says: Both sources give 1991, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 15 September 1959; Flags of the World dates it 18 August 1959.
era-1991.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1970.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Republic of the Congo): the 1970-1991 flag had a red field with the new arms in the canton, a gold star with a hammer and hoe over it in a wreath of two palm branches, inspired by the Soviet flag, used 2 January 1970 to 9 June 1991. FOTW (cg_prc): the new flag was adopted 30 December 1969 with the constitution and in force from 1 January 1970, red (for the blood of anti-colonial fighters) with a yellow star for the party's leading role and a hammer and hoe as a variation of the hammer and sickle; the original flag was restored in 1991 (10 June 1991 on cg.html).
era-1970.open: Both sources agree on the design in outline and on 1970 to June 1991. FOTW does not mention the palm branches or the canton position, and its adoption date (30 December 1969) differs by days from Wikipedia's (2 January 1970).

era-1959.says: Wikipedia: adopted 15 September 1959, a yellow diagonal band with a green upper and red lower triangle, unchanged at independence on 15 August 1960, the only Pan-Africanist flag with a diagonal. FOTW: adopted 18 August 1959 (Loi constitutionnelle no. 8), green, yellow and red diagonal, kept at independence 15 August 1960 and the fifth national flag to use those colours.
era-1959.open: Adoption day differs (15 September vs 18 August); the page's attribution of the colours to Ethiopia and Ghana is not in either source.

era-1880.says: FOTW (fr-colon): 'the common and specific flag for all of these possessions [French West and Equatorial Africa] was of course the French Tricolore'; a green-over-yellow Middle Congo flag with the tricolour in the canton was proposed but rejected in Parliament. Wikipedia (French Equatorial Africa): the federation ran 15 January 1910 to September 1958 and its infobox flag links to the Flag of France. Wikipedia (Flag of the Republic of the Congo): the French authorities reportedly forbade the colony its own distinctive colonial flag. FOTW (cg.html): the territory came under French sovereignty in the 1880s and was part of French Equatorial Africa 1910-1958.
era-1880.open: The tricolour is stated for the possessions generally by FOTW and for the federation by Wikipedia's infobox; neither pins the 1880 start (FOTW says 'the 1880s') and the 1959 end of the era is the page's. The Middle Congo flag proposal was not adopted and the dates of that proposal are not given.

era-1848.says: Wikipedia: current design 29 September 1848 at Pacífica Fernández's suggestion; 27 November 1906 state flag with arms; 21 October 1964 arms altered; colours linked to the ideals of 1848. FOTW: current design 1848; 27 November 1906; 21 October 1964 law.
era-1848.open: FOTW does not give the day or credit in 1848 beyond naming two candidates.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Central America» gives adoption in 1823, 2000 and relinquishment in 1839, within a year of this era's 1823 and 1838. The Flags of the World page that article links also carries 1838, and has 1823 next to a word about adopting.
era-1823.open: Only the dates were compared. The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1838.says: Wikipedia (list of Costa Rican flags): a flag from 22 November 1824 to 15 November 1840 and a white-blue-white flag from 21 April 1840 to 20 April 1842. FOTW (1838-1848): a flag 'in use 1838-1840 (unofficial)'; the flag of 21 April 1840 with a state version bearing the shield and a civil version without it, abolished 20 April 1842; the 22 November 1824 flag 're-established' and in use until 12 November 1848 though out of use after September 1842; a 1842 flag in use after September 1842; and the tricolour with a shield proclaimed on 29 September 1848 (first hoisted 12 November 1848).
era-1838.open: Both sources show several flags in 1838-1848 rather than one plain blue-white-blue flag, and FOTW's colour descriptions for 1838 and 1842 are given only in images; the page's claim is contradicted but not replaced by a documented single flag. The 1840 end date of the 1824 flag (Wikipedia) differs from FOTW's note that it was restored and used to 1848.

era-1821.says: FOTW (1821-1822): a blue (pale) over yellow over blue tricolour was used between 1821 and 1822, the flag of the independence fighters who opposed union with Mexico, used September 1821-May 1822 and from 10 May to 6 June 1823; FOTW (1823): the flag hoisted on 6 June 1823 after independence from Mexico (proclaimed 10 May 1823). Wikipedia's list of historical flags includes the First Mexican Empire flag for 1821-1823 and a Costa Rica flag from September 1821 to 6 June 1823.
era-1821.open: FOTW describes a Costa Rican blue-yellow-blue flag opposed to union with Mexico and says only that it 'perhaps' stayed in use during the Mexican domination of 1822-23; no source read shows the green-white-red Mexican Empire tricolour flown over Costa Rica.

era-1564.says: Wikipedia (list of historical flags of Costa Rica): the Cross of Burgundy for 1541-1821 and the Spanish flag of 1785 for 1785-1821, various Spanish Empire flags covering the land until 1821. FOTW (Burgundy Cross Flag): the red saltire raguly on white was the Spanish ensign from 1506 and the Spanish military flag from the 16th century to 1843. U.S. National Park Service: this flag was carried by ships and flown over the fortresses that guarded Spain's New World possessions until the red-and-gold ensign of 1785.
era-1564.open: Only Wikipedia's list ties the cross to Costa Rica, and it gives 1541 rather than 1564; FOTW and the Park Service describe Spanish use generally, and from 1785 the red-yellow-red flag replaced it at sea. No source read says which Spanish flag flew in the Captaincy General of Guatemala specifically.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: tricolour adopted 3 December 1959 (law no. 59-240); kept in the constitution of 3 November 1960; Loubao's proposal to replace orange with red not adopted. FOTW: Law No. 240 of 3 December 1959; independence 7 August 1960; Constitution of 2000 Article 29 restates the design.
era-1960.open: Meanings differ: official (Delafosse) vs savanna/forest readings, which Wikipedia calls unofficial.

era-1958.says: Wikipedia: 4 December 1958 autonomous state in the French Community, free to adopt its own flag; tricolour adopted 3 December 1959. Flags of the World (main page): the flag was prescribed by Law No. 240 of 3 December 1959, and independence was achieved on 7 August 1960; its page on the French colonial empire says that some possessions hoisted a flag of their own during French rule, shown on the pages of the countries concerned.
era-1958.open: No source says what flag flew from December 1958 to December 1959; the 1958 start of autonomy rests on Wikipedia alone, and FOTW's French colonial page does not list Cote d'Ivoire's status in the Community.

era-1848.says: FOTW (credited to Željko Heimer) says the red-white-blue tricolour was first used as a flag in 1848, a drawing of a Slavic barricade in Vienna being the first documented use, and that a tricolour in the Varaždin Town Museum dates from 1848 or a few years later. Wikipedia's «Flag of Croatia» has the tricolour in use in 1848, without a citation.
era-1848.open: The pan-Slavic colours «formally adopted that same year at the Prague Slavic Congress», stated on this page, were not checked. FOTW says the tricolour was banned from 1852 (imperial decree of 10 September 1852) and reintroduced about 1860; the page's single year does not show that.

era-1868.says: FOTW says the state flag with the arms was in use from 1867 and adopted in 1868 under the Nagodba, with the Crown of St Stephen; an edict of 16 September 1876 specified the crown; a viceroy's decree of 21 November 1914 (no. 8378) named the red-white-blue tricolour the civil flag of Croatia and Slavonia; and the official arms stayed in use until 29 October 1918. Wikipedia says the civil flag was in use, citing Boršak-Marijanović (1996) for the arms variant.
era-1868.open: FOTW notes that Dalmatia was in the Austrian half and that unofficial variants existed (other crowns, none, other shields). The page's remark that the flag asserted «a unity the empire never actually granted» is interpretation and was not sourced.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia dates the Illyrian Provinces to 1809-1814/1815 (Treaty of Schonbrunn, 14 October 1809) and shows the French flag in its infobox but describes no distinct provincial flag. Flags of the World's Croatia and Slovenia pages, and its Habsburg-era Croatia page (which starts in 1848), do not mention the Illyrian Provinces or any flag for them.
era-1809.open: That the French tricolour flew over the provinces rests on Wikipedia's infobox image alone; no second source was found. The page ends the era in 1813 while Wikipedia has Austria recovering the area in 1813-1814.

era-1527.says: Wikipedia (Coat of arms of Croatia): the checkerboard is first attested as a decorative symbol of the Kingdom of Croatia in 1495 and appears officially on the seal of the Cetingrad Charter of 1527; historically the first field was mostly white and there was no official standard until the 19th century. Flags of the World (Croatia: coat of arms): the oldest preserved red-and-white arms are on the Cetina seal of 1 January 1527, when the Croatian Parliament accepted the Habsburgs as kings, with the arms dated about 1525 under unclear circumstances; the order of squares did not matter in historical arms and red-first became common in the 20th century.
era-1527.open: Whether the checkerboard was flown as a flag in this period, rather than carried as arms, is not established by either source; FOTW does not mention 1495; the first-square-red swatch follows today's flag.

era-1918.says: FOTW (credited to Željko Heimer) describes the flag as blue-white-red, used before the law and formally introduced with the 1921 constitution, and prescribed as the civil and state ensign by Article 2 of the 1922 law. Wikipedia gives the 1922 law as the first official adoption (Službene Novine Kraljevine SHS no. 89, 28 February 1922) and a 1918 start in its infobox.
era-1918.open: Wikipedia's infobox (1918) and its text (1922) disagree on adoption. This page used to say the regional tricolours «kept their own orderings»; neither source says that, and FOTW reports the 1929 dictatorship reportedly banned them, unclear whether enforced.

era-1929.says: FOTW says there was apparently no change in the flag law when the kingdom was proclaimed in 1929, and that the 1937 law did not change it. Wikipedia dates the renaming to 3 October 1929 and shows the same blue-white-red flag.
era-1929.open: FOTW adds that the 1929 dictatorship reportedly banned national tricolours such as the Croatian one in favour of the Yugoslav one, and that it is unclear whether this was enforced (Heimer, 2009). This page used to say Croatian politicians resisted through the 1930s; no source for that was found.

era-1939.says: FOTW says all sources seem to agree that the Croatian tricolour was used after 1939, that its use was governed by natural law and not by any written regulation, that a version with the coat of arms in the centre was reportedly for state use, and that the crownless arms seem not to have been official though crownless versions were used on flags. Wikipedia's «Flag of Croatia» has a similar flag without the crown above the checkerboard, uncited.
era-1939.open: No decree for the flag was found, which agrees with the page's «by custom». Wikipedia's Banovina article describes no flag and dates the Cvetković–Maček Agreement to 24 August 1939 and the Banovina's de jure existence to 1945.

era-1941.says: FOTW quotes the law-decree signed by Ante Pavelić on 28 April 1941 and published in Narodne novine no. 15 on 30 April: three horizontal fields red, white, blue, with the state arms (25 fields, the first white) in the middle of the white field and, on the red field near the hoist, a curl enclosing a white field with a dark blue letter U. Wikipedia describes the crown removed, a U added at the top left and the first field white, without a citation.
era-1941.open: The older red-white-blue civil flag stayed in use everywhere except on state or local administration buildings until further regulation (FOTW). The decree text was read only as quoted by FOTW.

era-1943.says: FOTW says the state was Democratic Federal Yugoslavia from 29 November 1943, that before 1946 the red star usually sat in the white field without a yellow edge, and dates the red-star flag to 1941 (July, Heimer; September, Smith 1975). Wikipedia describes the red star added to the white band and the ratio changed from 2:3 to 1:2, with a citation-needed tag.
era-1943.open: Wikipedia's account of this period has no citation. The page's phrase that communism was «laid directly over the old kingdom's flag» is interpretation and was not sourced.

era-1946.says: Both give 31 January 1946 and the new constitution for the yellow-edged red-star flag. FOTW credits Đorđe Andrejević-Kun with the design (Wikipedia has a citation-needed tag on this) and says the state was renamed the Socialist Federal Republic on 7 April 1963 with the flag unchanged.
era-1946.open: The end differs: FOTW says the flag was abandoned in spring 1991 and the federation's name ended on 15 January 1992; Wikipedia's infobox gives 27 April 1992 with a citation-needed tag. This page ends the era in 1992.

era-1947.says: FOTW says the red-white-blue flag with a yellow-bordered red star was officially adopted on 18 January 1947 and officially abandoned on 25 June 1990, and quotes Article 7 of the 1974 constitution for a red five-pointed star in the centre. Wikipedia has the star with a yellow border replacing the arms in 1947, and the arms returning in May 1990.
era-1947.open: The end is June 1990 in FOTW and May 1990 in Wikipedia; this page says 1990. Wikipedia names no adopter for the 1947 flag.

era-1991.says: Flags of the World (Heimer, 2013) quotes Article 6 of the constitution (published 2 January 1992 in the Službeni glasnik) prescribing the Serb tricolour, red, blue, white from top to bottom, and says the flag was never formally changed. Wikipedia (Flag of Serbian Krajina) lists the Republic's flag for 1991-1995 as a historical flag and describes the Serb ethnic flag as a horizontal tricolour of red, blue and white; Wikipedia's article on the Republic gives the same constitution date and shows a flag but no description.
era-1991.open: Wikipedia does not itself state the colour order of the Republic's flag, so the order rests on FOTW's quotation of the constitution; left unreviewed until a second source states it.

era-1420.says: Wikipedia (Venetian Dalmatia): the Republic of Venice ruled parts of Dalmatia between 1409 and 1797, with Dalmatia incorporated in the Stato da Mar in 1420 and annexed by the Habsburgs in 1797. Wikipedia (Flag of Venice): the Lion of St Mark with an open book in peacetime and an upright sword in war, relinquished in 1797. Flags of the World (Serenissima): the lion holds a book, the sword variant was the war flag, used until May 1797.
era-1420.open: No source read says that the Venetian lion flag was flown in Dalmatia from 1420; Wikipedia's Venetian Dalmatia article does not mention the lion or a flag, and FOTW's Venice pages do not mention Dalmatia. The page's carved lions on fortress walls are not covered.

era-1358.says: FOTW, quoting Josip Luetić (1967), says the 1272 Statutes made the flag official as «VIXILLUM S. BLASIJ» and that it flew on Dubrovnik ships until 27 December 1807, when General Lauriston ordered it replaced; a white flag inscribed Libertas is described as a secondary ensign. Wikipedia describes St Blaise's flag as white with gold edging, the patron saint of the Republic, and a surviving flag over 200 years old, citing Britannica.
era-1358.open: The end differs by a year: FOTW gives 27 December 1807 for the flag, this page and the era's title say 1808. FOTW says a Libertas flag on a Croatian stamp was never used in Dubrovnik. The page's statement that Libertas was among the earliest civic mottoes flown as a flag in Europe was not sourced.

era-925.says: Wikipedia's Coat of arms of Croatia describes the central Croatian shield as a golden six-pointed star (the morning star) over a silver crescent on blue, finds its oldest example on frizatik coins of Andrew II as Duke of Croatia, says it 'did not have any Croatian CoA state relevancy and significance in the medieval period' and calls it a common misconception that it is the first and oldest known Croatian arms, naming the three leopard heads instead.
era-925.open: An emblem, not a flag: the drawing shows the later star-and-crescent shield for reference only. Neither flag source describes any flag or banner for 925–1102, and the page does not date the Andrew II coins.

era-1902.says: Wikipedia: designed 1849 by López and Teurbe Tolón; first raised 19 May 1850; adopted 20 May 1902; decree 21 April 1906; meaning of the stripes. FOTW: López credited 1849; adopted 20 May 1902; official explanation of the stripes and triangle.
era-1902.open: Wikipedia's own references differ on the 1906 date.

era-1868.says: Wikipedia: Guáimaro chose López's flag over Céspedes's Demajagua; April 1869 Congress designated it national. FOTW: Céspedes's flag is the official flag of Bayamo.
era-1868.open: FOTW gives no date for the Céspedes flag.

era-1898.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Cuba): the United States flag flew from 1 January 1899 until independence; Wikipedia (Military Government of Cuba): the infobox flag is the US flag (45-star file) for 1898-1902, with the military government installed on 1 January and the Republic born on 20 May. The Daily Concord Standard of 10 January 1899 prints a soldier's letter from Camp Columbia near Havana: American flags were raised over Morro Castle and Fort Cabanas and 'the flags of the two nations were exchanged' at the salute.
era-1898.open: The 20 May 1902 end of the US flag rests on Wikipedia alone; Flags of the World's Cuba pages do not cover the occupation; the newspaper is a soldier's letter (OCR text), not an official record, and the page's 1898 start is the war, not the flag.

era-1515.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): the flag was introduced in the Spanish Empire after 1506 and 'remained in use in Spain's overseas empire' (the Burgundian flag was reportedly a secondary naval jack until 1785); the 1843 date in that article refers to the Spanish army, not overseas use; Wikipedia's Cuba flag captions give the Cross of Burgundy for 1521-1843. The US National Park Service page calls it the Spanish Colonial Flag carried by ships and flown over fortresses, replaced as the naval ensign by the red-and-gold striped flag under Charles III (1785), adopted by forts in 1793 and by regiments in 1843. Flags of the World (Maritime Provinces of Spain) shows provincial flags for Havana, Santiago de Cuba, Trinidad and others dated 1845-1885; Wikipedia's Captaincy General of Cuba infobox shows a Spanish flag, not the cross.
era-1515.open: Two publishers support the Cross of Burgundy as the Spanish colonial flag, but both indicate it gave way to the red-and-gold flag from 1785-1793 on ships and forts, so a Cross of Burgundy flag over Cuba until 1868 is contradicted or unconfirmed; no source describes Cuban use specifically, and the 1515 start (Wikipedia: 1521) is not given.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: flag in use from 16 August 1960, designed by Ismet Guney (Turkish Cypriot), neutral design excluding blue, red, crosses and crescents (Article 4); copper map, two olive branches for peace; slight alteration 24 April 2006. FOTW: Constitution 6 April 1960 Article 4 'neutral design and colour'; adopted 16 August 1960; Guney designer; white = peace, copper map, green olive branches; 20 April 2006 ratio 3:5 to 2:3.
era-1960.open: Wikipedia and FOTW differ on the 2006 date (24 vs 20 April) and the colour specifications.

era-330.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1925.says: FOTW's British rule page: Cyprus became a Crown Colony in 1925 (annexed 1914); a Blue Ensign with a 'CHC' badge on a white disc was approved in 1881, the two-lion badge of 1905 went on the Union Jack and from 1922 on the Blue Ensign, and a Cyprus Red Ensign was authorised in 1922. Wikipedia lists British-period flags 1881-1922 and 1922-1960, and its British Cyprus infobox shows the 1922-1960 flag.
era-1925.open: The Blue Ensign with a Cyprus badge is supported, but the badge was two lions (CHC letters before 1922), not the gold disc with island arms drawn here, and the drawing shows a Union Jack with a disc rather than a Blue Ensign. The flag dates from 1922, not 1925, which is only the Crown Colony date. The drawing needs redrawing.

era-1878.says: FOTW: 1878 Cyprus put under British administration but remained part of the Ottoman Empire; annexed 1914; Crown Colony 1925. A Blue Ensign with a CHC badge was approved in 1881 (and a High Commissioner's Union Jack with the badge). A 1937 traveller cited by FOTW saw the Union Jack over police stations. Wikipedia dates the first British-period flag 1881-1922.
era-1878.open: The page's statement that the Union Flag was the island's only flag and that no badge existed before 1925 is contradicted by the 1881 CHC badge and 1905 two-lion badge; the Ottoman flag's nominal use to 1914 is not described by either source. The drawing shows a plain Union Flag.

era-1571.says: Wikipedia's Ottoman Cyprus infobox shows the Ottoman crescent-and-star flag (after 1844). Wikipedia's Flags of the Ottoman Empire and FOTW's Ottoman page agree that the red flag with white crescent and star dates from 1793 (naval decree) and was made the national flag in 1844; earlier Ottoman flags varied (Wikipedia notes 1613 naval flags in green and white with crescents).
era-1571.open: The red crescent-and-star flag drawn is established only for roughly 1793/1844-1878, not 1571-1793; no source read describes a flag flown on Cyprus itself.

era-1489.says: FOTW's Kingdom of Cyprus page ends with Catherine Cornaro's abdication and the sale of her rights to Venice in 1489, and describes no Venetian-period flag. Wikipedia's Venetian Cyprus article has a coat of arms of Venetian Cyprus and a commented-out Venice flag image, but no flag text.
era-1489.open: The Lion of St Mark as the flag flown over Cyprus is not stated by any source read; not looked for: a Venetian-flag reference page.

era-1192.says: FOTW's Kingdom of Cyprus page says the first flag (1192-1268) was the banner of arms of Guy and Aimery of Lusignan: barry of eight argent and azure with a red lion rampant, armed, langued and crowned gold, the lion being an augmentation granted by Richard I; it says no contemporary depictions of the flag are known and presents it as a reconstruction. It gives later flags from 1268 (quartered Jerusalem and Lusignan) and 1393. Wikipedia's House of Lusignan agrees on the lion as an augmentation granted by Richard I and shows a royal banner of Janus of Cyprus.
era-1192.open: The drawing's blazon matches FOTW's, but FOTW itself says it cannot be confirmed by contemporary depictions; the 1268-1489 flags differed. Kept unreviewed because the drawing is a reconstruction of the earliest, not the 15th-century, banner.

era-1993.says: Wikipedia says the Czech Republic kept the flag in 1992–1993 and that Act No. 3/1993 defined it (the cited version dated 17 December 1992); FOTW (Heimer) says the blue-triangle flag was adopted on 17 December 1992. FOTW also quotes Joe McMillan that neither successor state was to use federal symbols, and Hugh Agnew that the Czech National Council ignored a federal resolution to that effect.
era-1993.open: FOTW's own sources disagree on whether the adoption was 1992 or 1993. This page used to say Slovakia's negotiators objected and that the asset-division law left the flag unsettled; neither source says that.

era-1989.says: Wikipedia says the Czech part of the federation reverted to the red-and-white flag under Law 67/1990 of 13 March 1990; FOTW (Heimer) gives 13 March 1990 to 17 December 1992 for the official white-over-red flag and Jan Kravcík that it was never actually used, the Czechoslovak flag remaining the familiar one. FOTW gives 1 March 1990 as the approval date in another note.
era-1989.open: This page used to say the flag never changed through these years; the Czech lands had their own white-over-red flag in law.

era-1939.says: FOTW (Blanc, 1996) says the Protectorate flag had three horizontal stripes: white, red, blue. Wikipedia says Nazi authorities banned the wedge flag and that a horizontal white-red-blue tricolour replaced it during the war (citation needed).
era-1939.open: This page used to show a plain white-over-red bicolour; neither source supports it, and the drawing and swatches were corrected. Neither source says who ordered the change or on what date.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sache) says the white-red flag was first officially hoisted in Washington on 18 October 1918, at Masaryk's residence, and was identical to Poland's. Wikipedia says the National Assembly approved the flag with a blue hoist triangle on 30 March 1920 to distinguish it from Poland's, after Jaroslav Kursa's 1919 proposal.
era-1918.open: Explanations of the blue differ (the third Slavic colour in use since 1848; a nod to Slovaks; Slovak mountains called «late mythology»). Wikipedia marks the rationale citation-needed. This page used to say the blue represented Slovakia and Ruthenia.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: the 1920-1939 flag (white over red with a blue wedge) was restored in 1945 (citation needed) and used until 1992; the Nazis banned it in 1939 and a white-red-blue horizontal tricolour was used in the war. Czech Television (CT24): the state flag lasted, apart from the war years, until the dissolution of the common state. FOTW: the Protectorate's flag was a white-red-blue triband, and the Czechoslovak coat of arms of 1920 stayed unchanged 1945-1960.
era-1945.open: No page read states in so many words the date or act of restoration in 1945; 'legal continuity' reasoning on the page is not covered.

era-1198.says: Wikipedia: Bohemia became a kingdom formally in 1198 under Přemysl Ottokar I; from 1253 a two-tailed silver lion on red was the arms of the Kingdom of Bohemia, with the oldest surviving full-colour depiction in the early 1270s fresco at Krems and in the 1310s Passional of Abbess Kunigunde; Wikipedia (Flag of Bohemia): white-red banners were carried into battle by the Bohemian kings' armies and the 13th-century rhymed chronicle of Ottokar of Styria describes the flag. FOTW (Bohemia): the arms are a white double-tailed lion on red.
era-1198.open: Only Wikipedia dates the two-tailed lion (from 1253) and says the kings used a black eagle in a silver shield in the first half of the 13th century, so the lion cannot be carried back to 1198; FOTW names the arms but gives no dates. Dalimil's legend of the second tail is a legend, not evidence.

era-1158.says: Wikipedia (Coat of arms of Bohemia) says the lion was first shown with one tail and that Emperor Frederick granted Vladislaus II a silver lion on red (no year, citation needed); Wikipedia (Flag of the Czech Republic) says the traditional colours derive from an 1192 coat of arms showing a rampant lion with a double silver tail on red; Wikipedia (Flag of Bohemia) says the silver lion on red was granted in the 12th century; the same coat-of-arms article says the Bohemian kings used a black eagle in a silver shield in the first half of the 13th century, with red gonfanons earlier.
era-1158.open: The Wikipedia articles contradict each other on the 12th-century lion (one tail, two tails, black eagle), and none names a ducal seal; the page's 'first attested on a duke's own seal' and the single-tail form rest on no source read. Next: a Czech heraldic or archival source (e.g. on the seals of Vladislaus II and Přemysl Ottokar I).

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: the 1920 flag (approved 30 March 1920) was restored in 1945 and, as listed for 1945-1992, was one of only three socialist-country flags in Europe without the coat of arms at the centre; captions give separate naval ensigns and a war flag (1960-1990). FOTW records no emblem or flag change in the communist period and says the Czechoslovak flag remained in use; a 1968 idea of separate Czech symbols was dropped after the Warsaw Pact invasion.
era-1948.open: Neither source mentions a 1948 event, the comparison with Hungary or Poland, or a presidential flag in the communist period; Wikipedia gives no dates for this period.

era-1938.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Czech Republic): the flag approved on 30 March 1920 has been in continuous use except during the German occupation (1939-45), and the 1920-1939 flag is labelled as the state flag of the republic. CT24: the flag lasted, apart from the war years, until the dissolution of the state. FOTW (Bohemia and Moravia 1939-1945): the Second Republic's loss of Sudetenland on 1 October 1938, Slovak and Subcarpathian autonomy on 6 and 8 October 1938 and the annexations of March 1939; the former Czechoslovak state flag was used in the first months of the Protectorate (FOTW, cz_bh).
era-1938.open: No source states the flag specifically for the Second Republic; the sources imply it by saying the 1920 flag was in use until 1939 and the war years were the exception (read as 1939-45). The page's wording about lost population and fortifications is not covered.

era-1526.says: FOTW (Bohemia): the Austrian crown lands had no flags in their own right but Landesfarben derived from their arms; Bohemia's were white over red from the silver double-tailed lion on red, and a white-over-red flag was used in Bohemia from the 19th century to 1918 and became the first flag of Czechoslovakia. Wikipedia (Flag of Bohemia): white-red banners derived from the royal arms were carried into battle by the Bohemian kings' armies; the heraldic flag is described and drawn in Koebel's 1545 work; the Czech national movement adopted the colours in the 19th century. Wikipedia (Flag of the Czech Republic): the traditional colours derive from an 1192 coat of arms.
era-1526.open: A two-tailed lion banner as a distinct flag of the crown land is not documented for the Habsburg centuries beyond Koebel's 1545 description; the sources describe Landesfarben and, in the 19th century, a white-red bicolour rather than the lion banner drawn on the page.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia says a regulation of 1748 (11 June in its infobox, 11 July in the Danish title it cites) set the merchant-ship flag and its proportions, that private use was outlawed by a circular of 7 January 1834 and the ban repealed by a regulation of 7 July 1854 (the swallow-tailed Splitflag excluded), and that the Guinness record for the oldest continuously used national flag dates from 1625. FOTW says regulations of 11 July 1748 set the proportions (28:34 per Southworth) and that regulations of 1 May 1893 allowed up to 28:37.
era-1814.open: The 1748 date differs by a month between Wikipedia's own sources. The German occupation of 1940–45 is not covered by either source.

era-1219.says: Wikipedia says the legend ties the flag to the Battle of Lyndanisse on 15 June 1219 (earliest source: Christiern Pedersen's Danske Krønike of the 1520s) and that the Gelre Armorial of about 1340–1370 is the earliest known undisputed colour rendering. FOTW (Andersen) dates the Gelre Armorial's red banner with a white cross to about 1370–1386, and says a Danish text of 1478 is the first to use the name Dannebrog, a Dutch text having used it about 100 years earlier.
era-1219.open: Neither source supports a flag of 1219 itself. This page used to say the design was unchanged for eight centuries.

era-1397.says: FOTW (Kalmar Union Flag): the only evidence is two letters of 1430 in which Erik of Pomerania orders priests to wear the 'banner of the realms', described as a red cross on a yellow field; there is no pictorial evidence or surviving flag, a museum flag is a recreation, and contributors dispute whether the references mean the union banner or the Dannebrog. Wikipedia (Kalmar Union): the gallery calls it 'the unofficial flag of the Kalmar Union as described by Erik of Pomerania' with no design in the text; Wikipedia (Dannebrog): a 1398 seal of Eric with a small Dannebrog.
era-1397.open: The gold field and red cross are supported only as a disputed 1430 description; the three crowns on this page's drawing are not described by either source, and the union's end date varies (1521 FOTW, 1523 this page).

era-1523.says: Wikipedia (Denmark-Norway): Norway had its own royal standard until 1748, after which the Dannebrog became the only official merchant flag in the union; the union is dated 1536/1537-1814. Wikipedia (Flag of Norway): from 1537 to 1814 Norway used the same flag as Denmark, though a red banner with the golden lion and silver halberd is shown as Norway's flag in 1669-70, flew over Akershus until at least 1698, and entered all Norwegian regiments' colours in 1641; after 1814 Norway used the Danish flag with the royal-flag canton.
era-1523.open: Both are Wikipedia articles, and they are not fully aligned (a shared Dannebrog versus a separate Norwegian lion banner); FOTW's Denmark page does not cover the period. The page's 'Norway had no flag of its own' is contradicted by the lion banner.

era-1977.says: Both sources give 1977, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 27 June 1977; Flags of the World dates it 27 June 1977.
era-1977.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1896.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Djibouti): the flag of France was used between 1896 and 1977 and the only ensign used was the tricolour. Wikipedia (French Somaliland, 1884-1967 in the infobox and formally established 1896 in the text) and (French Territory of the Afars and the Issas, 5 July 1967 to 27 June 1977): both infobox flags are the French tricolour, with a governor's flag also shown and no local flag. FOTW (dj-fs): the colony was formed in 1896; prior to independence the French tricolore 'would have been used' as the national flag; the colonial governor's flag was a blue square with the tricolour in the canton and a swallow tail; independence flag adopted 27 June 1977 (dj.html).
era-1896.open: FOTW's statement is hedged ('would have been used') and gives no dates; the start varies between 1884, 1894 (FOTW dj.html) and 1896. The 'T.F.A.I.' marking is not supported by any source.

era-1978.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives adoption on 3 November 1978. FOTW gives 'Flag adopted: 3 November 1978 (modified 1988)' and the coat of arms 21 July 1961 (the 1961 date belongs to the arms, not the flag), and quotes the description in Act No. 18 of 1978, the National Emblems of Dominica Act, gazetted 1 November 1978 and effective 3 November 1978; a Flag Bulletin report says a revised form was introduced on 3 November 1981. The Office of the President describes the flag as a red roundel with a Sisserou parrot on a twig within ten lime-green stars for the ten parishes, on a triple cross of yellow, black and white over forest green.
era-1978.open: The parrot and stars were modified in 1981, 1988 and 1990 per Wikipedia and FOTW, so the drawing is simplified; the government page does not give the Kalinago/soil/water meanings of the three bands stated on the page (it reads the cross as the Trinity).
