era-1783.says: Wikipedia's table: Union Jack 1763-78 and 1784-1801; UK flag 1801-75; Leeward Islands flags 1875-1940; Windward Islands flags 1940-58; a Dominica flag 1955-65 and another 1965-78. FOTW (Colonial Badges and Flags): Blue Ensign with the Leeward Islands' badge 1875-1940, none recorded 1940-55, the Dominica badge (a ship at the Cabrits on a shield) 1955-65, and the full 1961 arms 1965-78, all without a white disc; defaced Union Jacks for governors (full 1961 arms from 1967).
era-1783.open: A Dominica-badge Blue Ensign is documented only from 1955; before 1875 the sources show the Union Jack, and the page's 1783/1805 start dates are not supported. The 1961 arms are described but whether the badge on the page is the parrot is not stated.

era-1763.says: Wikipedia's historical table: French royal standard 1715-63 and 1778-84; Union Jack 1763-78. Wikipedia's History of Dominica: Dominica a French colony from 1715 until the end of the Seven Years' War in 1763, then a British colony from 1763 to 1978.
era-1763.open: Neither Wikipedia article gives the 1783/1805 end dates or says which flag flew in 1805 (Wikipedia's table implies the Union Jack from 1784); FOTW's Dominica pages begin in 1875. A reference on the 1778 French capture and 1783 return is not found.

era-1865.says: Wikipedia: at the restoration in 1865 the flag was reintroduced with some changes, the coat of arms placed in the centre and the fly-side blue and red quarters flipped. FOTW's main page: quartered blue and red with a white cross and arms, with origin from the Haitian flag and adoption on 6 November 1844; its history page gives the second Spanish rule as ending 11 July 1865 and an 1844 constitution article describing a merchant flag of blue and 'rosados' quarters with a white cross.
era-1865.open: The two publishers date the flag differently (Wikipedia: changed and reintroduced 1865, infobox date 1863; FOTW: adopted 1844) and FOTW does not say what changed in 1865, so 'unchanged in core design since 1844' is contradicted only by Wikipedia; the 1913 decree's content is not described.

era-600.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no woven banners; caciques used carved wooden/stone duhos, ceremonial regalia, and body paint as marks of authority».
era-600.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia: Spain annexed the territory in 1861 at Santana's request and the Dominican flag was replaced by the Spanish flag until 1865. FOTW's Dominican history dates the second Spanish rule 18 March 1861 to 11 July 1865 and has contributors inferring (not documenting) that the Spanish flag was re-hoisted; it also mentions a red-white-yellow flag that one source links to 1861-1865 and a single contributor's note of a blue-over-red swallow-tailed flag of the 'Santo Domingo Maritime Province', adopted 11 March 1863.
era-1861.open: The two publishers agree on the annexation and dates, but FOTW offers no source for which flag flew and lists candidates (Spanish red-yellow-red, red-white-yellow, a 1863 provincial flag); the red-yellow-red drawing, and its 1785 origin, are not established by a source that states the flag.

era-1844.says: Wikipedia: Duarte's flag first hoisted 28 February 1844; colours blue, red, white with meanings; arms added in 1865. Flags of the World: colours derive from Haiti's flag; national flag adopted 6 November 1844.
era-1844.open: Dates differ (28 February vs 6 November 1844: hoisting versus adoption); Wikipedia's 1838 Trinitaria flag date conflicts with its own table; arms-at-crossing in 1844 not confirmed.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia's flag article: Haiti ruled the eastern part 1822-1844 and used the Haitian flag there; its article on the Haitian occupation says frontier towns adopted the Haitian flag in November 1821 and that Boyer unified the island under the Haitian flag. FOTW's Haiti history: Boyer annexed the Spanish part on 9 February 1822 (after the Republic of Spanish Haiti of 30 November 1821); Petion changed the blue-red flag to horizontal in 1807, Boyer kept it from 1820, and the 1843 constitution confirmed the horizontal blue and red flag. FOTW's Dominican history says the Dominican flag derived from the Haitian bicolour.
era-1822.open: FOTW does not say in terms which flag flew in the eastern part in 1822-1844; it follows from the unification and the Haitian flag being horizontal blue and red throughout. The short-lived Spanish Haiti flag (1821-22) is a separate matter and not shown on this page.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia ends the Cross of Burgundy in 1795, mentions French occupation, and gives a Spanish flag for 1809-1821. FOTW's Haiti history: Toussaint Louverture adopted the French tricolour in 1798 and occupied the Spanish part of the island in January 1801; the French occupied the island in 1802; the Republic of Spanish Haiti was proclaimed 30 November 1821.
era-1795.open: No source read describes the 1795 cession or states which flag flew over Santo Domingo in 1795-1809; the French tricolour is the page's stand-in, and FOTW supports a French tricolour only for Toussaint's 1801 occupation.

era-1492.says: Wikipedia: the Cross of Burgundy was the flag of the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo for 1492-1795 and Spanish military units used it from the 15th to 18th centuries. FOTW's Spanish pages: the Burgundy cross was Spain's ensign from 1506 to the 1670s and a jack until 1785, was used as a land war flag up to 1843, and 'was never the official flag of the Spanish Empire, but rather a military banner'; Charles II and Philip V dropped the cross for royal arms on white as the ensign from the 1670s-1701, and the red-gold-red ensign came in 1785.
era-1492.open: FOTW does not mention Santo Domingo and contradicts the 'standard colonial and maritime banner' wording and the 1492 start (its dated use begins 1506); the claim that the cross was the Captaincy General's flag for 1492-1795 rests on Wikipedia alone.

era-1997.says: Wikipedia: the current flag was adopted 18 February 2006 under the new constitution, a design like the 1966-1971 flag with a sky blue background; the 1997 flag used immediately before it resembled the 1960-1963 flag (a large star with six smaller stars). Flags of the World (history page): 'Democratic Republic of Congo (1997 - Feb 2006)' is a blue field with yellow stars (construction details 9 December 1997), and the 2006 draft constitution restores the sky-blue flag with a red, yellow-fimbriated diagonal and a star; its main page says the 'new' flag matches the 1963-1971 design with a lighter blue.
era-1997.open: Both sources put the drawn red-diagonal flag at 2006, not 1997: the 1997-2006 flag was a different design, so the card's 'readopted 1997' caption and 1997 start are not supported. Wikipedia's meanings (blue peace, red martyrs' blood, yellow wealth, star the future) are its own reading and are not dated.

era-1971.says: Wikipedia: light green field with a yellow circle holding an arm with a red torch, the Popular Movement of the Revolution (MPR) emblem, part of Mobutu's re-Africanisation; in use until Mobutu's overthrow in the First Congo War. FOTW: adopted 19 November 1971 (Loi 71-007), light green field, yellow disc, right arm holding a torch with red flame; green for hope, the disc for natural resources, flames for martyrs.
era-1971.open: Neither source states the colour of the arm; the page's 'black arm' is unsupported.

era-1960.says: Both: the 1960-63 flag was the Free State design with six smaller stars added for the six provinces (Wikipedia; FOTW: six yellow stars in a vertical line on the hoist, a larger star at the centre, used until 1963). FOTW: the 1963 flag was adopted 30 June 1963, light blue with a red diagonal stripe edged yellow and a large yellow star in the canton; Wikipedia: 1963 flag with a smaller star in the top hoist corner and a red yellow-lined diagonal band, slightly modified in 1966 and changed in 1971.
era-1960.open: The red stripe's meaning as blood shed in the Congo Crisis is not stated: Wikipedia gives 'blood of the country's martyrs' for the current flag, and FOTW quotes a contributor's symbolism for the 1966-71 flag. FOTW's start date for the 1963 flag is inconsistent (1963 vs 1964).

era-1908.says: Flags of the World (pre-independence page): the Free State's blue flag with a gold star was unchanged when the state became Belgian in 1908 ('No change was made to the flag'); the Belgian Congo flag is 'the well known big yellow star on blue', and the history page says the flag was adapted at independence by adding six gold stars in the hoist. Wikipedia: the 1877 yellow-star flag remained in use through the Belgian Congo period until 1960, and the 1960-1963 flag added six smaller stars for the provinces.
era-1908.open: The card's ring of six small stars is contradicted by both publishers, which put the six stars at the 1960 independence flag; the Belgian Congo flag was the single-star Free State flag. Whether a separate Belgian colonial or governor's flag existed is only linked (FOTW), not read.

era-1885.says: Wikipedia: the 1877 flag of Leopold II's International African Association, a yellow star on blue, continued as the Congo Free State flag. Flags of the World: the Association hoisted the flag since 1877 (per a 1914 booklet by Roland and Duchesne); the Free State 'adopted a blue flag with a golden star in its center', reputedly designed by H. M. Stanley (a claim Bakker says the sources do not confirm), and one commenter cites Pakenham that the design was borrowed from the old kingdom of Congo.
era-1885.open: Neither source calls it Leopold's personal flag; its design origin (Stanley, Kongo) is unverified.

era-1390.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Kongo): founded around 1390, independent until 1857/1862, titular monarchy abolished 1914; Afonso I 'subsequently designed a coat of arms for Kongo' after his victory, used by later kings on official documents until 1860; the infobox flag is captioned 'Flag according to Giovanni Cavazzi da Montecuccolo, 1650s' and another image is a banner of King Afonso I. Wikipedia (Afonso I): the coat of arms was issued to him (c. 1528-1541) and used until at least 1860. FOTW's Congo pages do not cover the kingdom.
era-1390.open: Wikipedia does not say the arms were granted by Portugal in 1512 (it says Afonso designed them), and it shows a flag, so the card's 'no separate flag survives' and '1512 Portuguese-granted' are not supported. A single publisher covers the kingdom; a museum entry for the arms (Met Museum) returned HTTP 429 and was not read.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia: 19 November 1830 provisional flag; 1835 yellow-blue-red first adopted by law; 1845 Marcista flag; 26 September 1860 restoration; 5 December 1900 arms decree. FOTW: 26 September 1860 decree; 5 December 1900 arms; yellow stripe double width.
era-1830.open: The sources differ on whether the Gran Colombia flag lasted until 1845 or 1830.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Gran Colombia» gives adoption in 1821 and relinquishment in 1830, within a year of this era's 1822 and 1830. The Flags of the World page that article links also carries 1830, and has 1822 next to a word about adopting.
era-1822.open: Only the dates were compared. The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Quito) and the Quito outlet Primicias, quoting the Spanish officer Samano's inventory after the Battle of Ibarra in December 1812 ('una bandera de tafetan encarnado con aspa blanca'), describe the Quito rebels' flag of 1809-1812 as a red field with a white saltire; Wikipedia says a transcription error long made it plain red. Wikipedia (Flag of Ecuador): the Guayaquil flag of 9 October 1820 had blue and white stripes with three stars, and a decree of 2 June 1822 set a white flag with a blue first quarter and a star. Flags of the World does not cover 1809, 1820 or 1822.
era-1809.open: The sources document a red flag with a white saltire for Quito, not the teal field with three dots drawn on the card, which is an invented device; Wikipedia's Flag of Ecuador says plain red in one place and an inverted Cross of Burgundy in another, and the Primicias article is a newspaper, not a scholarly source.

era-1563.says: Wikipedia (Ecuador) says the Cross of Burgundy flag of the Spanish empire flew over Ecuador for many years (1534-1820); Wikipedia (Real Audiencia of Quito) dates the Audiencia 1563-1822 (created by Royal Decree on 29 August 1563) and carries an unlabelled Cross of Burgundy image in its infobox but describes no flag. Flags of the World's Ecuador page does not cover the colonial period.
era-1563.open: No source says the Audiencia had no flag of its own or flew a banner in 'Spanish royal colours'; the red and white bands drawn on the card are not the Cross of Burgundy.

era-1984.says: Wikipedia: Free Officers introduced the red-white-black flag with the Eagle of Saladin in 1952; current flag since 4 October 1984. FOTW: flag and coat of arms dated 4 October 1984; 1985 laws cited by a comment.
era-1984.open: The sources differ by a year on the laws (1984 vs 1985).

era-642.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: UAR 1958–71 with two green stars; Federation of Arab Republics 1972–84 with a golden Hawk of Quraish, kept until 1984. FOTW: 1958 Presidential Decree, flag red, white with two green stars, black; 1972 law amended, stars replaced with a golden hawk.
era-1953.open: FOTW notes its source list omits the 1952–58 flag.

era-1922.says: Wikipedia: after 1922 recognition King Fuad I adopted a green flag with a white crescent and three stars. FOTW: Royal Decree of 1923 set the first national flag of modern Egypt, green with a white crescent and three stars.
era-1922.open: The year differs (1922 vs 1923); star meanings are not covered.

era-1805.says: Wikipedia: the Muhammad Ali dynasty used a red flag with stars and crescents, similar to the Ottoman flag, kept after 1914. FOTW's Ottoman-period page, quoting Whitney Smith, says Muhammad Ali set three white crescents and three stars on a red field, which became the first real Egyptian national flag in the mid-19th century (the personal flag of the khedives); its British Protectorate page says the khedive's flag was made the national flag after 1914. The flag was used 1867-1881 under Isma'il and Tewfik.
era-1805.open: Both sources support the red flag with crescents and stars, but FOTW has three crescents each with a star (six-pointed at first, later five-pointed) while the drawing shows a single crescent with three stars; the drawing needs redrawing. The 1881 formalisation is not covered.

era-1517.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Egypt has a caption dating the Ottoman flag over the Egyptian Eyalet to 1793-1844. Wikipedia's Flags of the Ottoman Empire and FOTW's Ottoman page date the red flag with white crescent and star to 1793 (naval) and 1844 (national); FOTW's Egypt page shows a green-yellow-green 'Mamelik' flag for Egypt in an 1711 Dutch chart grouped with Ottoman flags.
era-1517.open: The red crescent-and-star flag is established for 1793 onwards only; for 1517-1793 the evidence is the 1711 chart's green-yellow-green flag (a secondary source citing a chart) and 16th-17th century Ottoman war flags in other designs.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Mexico): the First Mexican Empire's flag was a green, white and red tricolour with the national arms and a crown on the eagle, decreed by Iturbide in November 1821 and first used in July 1822, used 1821-23. Wikipedia (First Mexican Empire; History of El Salvador): the former Guatemalan lands, including El Salvador, were annexed shortly after the empire's establishment, El Salvador feared incorporation into Mexico, and the empire ended in 1823 when Iturbide was ousted. Wikipedia (Flag of El Salvador): on 20 February 1822 Arce unveiled a blue-white-blue flag in San Salvador amid a war against the empire's annexation efforts, used until 1865; Flags of the World: the flag was first adopted in 1822 by Arce leading militia against Mexico, and its pages do not discuss the annexation.
era-1821.open: The Mexican tricolour over El Salvador is supported only by combining Wikipedia articles (one publisher); no source read says the imperial flag flew in San Salvador, and the annexation sources describe El Salvador as resisting. A Salvadoran government page on historical flags could not be fetched (web.archive.org blocked).

era-1525.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy flag): the saw-toothed red saltire on white served the New World viceroyalties; Flags of the World (Spain): the red Burgundy saltire on a usually white field was the Spanish military flag from the 16th century and an ensign to the 1670s; neither El Salvador page describes a flag before 1822. Wikipedia's History of El Salvador gives independence in 1821 as part of the First Mexican Empire and says nothing of colonial flags.
era-1525.open: No source read connects the Cross of Burgundy to El Salvador or the Captaincy General of Guatemala, or dates a colonial flag to 1525.

era-1968.says: Wikipedia and Flags of the World both say the flag was raised at independence from Spain on 12 October 1968: a green-white-red tricolour with a blue triangle at the hoist and the coat of arms (a silk-cotton tree under six stars) on the white band. Both say the arms on the flag were changed under Francisco Macias Nguema (Wikipedia: 1978 to 21 August 1979; FOTW: 1972-79) and the 1968 arms restored in August 1979.
era-1968.open: Wikipedia says the coat of arms was added to the flag sometime after independence, while FOTW says the flag with arms was adopted at independence; the dates of the Nguema-era change differ (1978 vs 1972). The 1979 date in both sources is the restoration, not the adoption; the colour symbolism on this page was not compared.

era-1778.says: Wikipedia's flag article captions the Spanish flag as 'flag used in Equatorial Guinea during Spanish colonisation (1785-1931)'; Wikipedia's Spanish Guinea article dates Spanish control from the Treaty of El Pardo in 1778 to independence on 12 October 1968. FOTW's Spanish Guinea page says no flag existed for any Spanish colony in the area (only maritime registration flags and a Governor General's standard, 1945-1968).
era-1778.open: The sources agree on Spanish control from 1778 and on no Guinea-specific flag, but state which national flag flew only for 1785-1931 in a Wikipedia caption; Spain's pre-1785 ensign, the Second Republic tricolour and the Franco-era arms 1938-1968 are not described in the pages read.

era-1471.says: FOTW's Spanish Guinea page says Fernando Po and Annobon were colonised by Portugal in 1474 and the Portuguese kept control until the 1778 cession to Spain (Treaty of El Pardo); Wikipedia's Spanish Guinea article places the 1778 Treaty of El Pardo between the Spanish and Portuguese empires. Neither names a flag.
era-1471.open: Two publishers support Portuguese control of the islands until 1778 (from 1474 in FOTW, not 1471), but no source read describes a flag flown over them, nor whether Portugal's national flag of the time (not a modern one) is what the drawing shows.

era-1993.says: Wikipedia: after independence the flag was modified and first hoisted officially on 24 May 1993, the gold olive wreath (14 leaves each side, from the 1952 flag) replacing the gold star of the EPLF flag in the red triangle; the wreath was standardised at 30 leaves and the ratio changed from 2:3 to 1:2 on 5 December 1995. FOTW: the flag has a red triangle at the hoist with a yellow wreath, green over blue in the fly; flag adopted 5 December 1995, coat of arms adopted 24 May 1993; the EPLF flag it derives from had a red triangle and a yellow star.
era-1993.open: The page's date of 'adopted in 1995' is for the standard version; the 1993 version (2:3, 14 leaves) is documented by Wikipedia only. The UN-emblem reading of the wreath is a hearsay remark on FOTW, which says no official meaning is recorded; FOTW and Wikipedia agree green is agriculture, red the independence struggle, blue the sea.

era-1952.says: Wikipedia (Eritrea; Federation article): the blue flag with olive branches was chosen on 15 September 1952, banned at the 1962 annexation; its federation article shows the Ethiopian flag (1897-1974) and an Eritrean flag (1952-1961). FOTW (Eritrea 1952): a light blue flag with a green wreath, adopted 1952 and used 'until absorbed into Ethiopia in 1959', continuing as a flag of liberation to 1993 (The Flag Bulletin 1996). FOTW (Imperial Ethiopia): the Ethiopian flag was a green-yellow-red tricolour; the version with the Lion of Judah was the state flag and the plain tricolour the national flag; FOTW (1987-91) says the Derg continued with the plain tricolour.
era-1952.open: Both sources show Eritrea with its own blue flag in the federation (1952-1959 or 1962, dates differ), so the Ethiopian tricolour with the lion is supported only as the state flag of Ethiopia and for the annexed years from 1962 to 1974; after 1974 the plain tricolour (1974-87) and a modified state flag (1987-91) are described, and the EPLF flag from 1991 to 1993 is not on the page. The drawing is therefore too narrow for 1952-1993.

era-1941.says: FOTW: the British expelled the Italians after the Battle of Keren in 1941 and administered the country under a UN mandate until 1951, when it was federated with Ethiopia. Wikipedia (British Military Administration (Eritrea)): British control from 25 February 1941 to 15 September 1952; its Federation article lists the British Military Administration with the Union Flag in the infobox.
era-1941.open: The Union Flag is shown only in a Wikipedia infobox; no text read says it was flown over Eritrea, or whether the markings 'B.M.A.' were used. FOTW has no page for the British administration of Eritrea. The end date differs (1951 FOTW, 1952 Wikipedia).

era-1890.says: FOTW: Eritrea became an Italian colony on 1 January 1890 and a province of Italian East Africa in 1936. Wikipedia (Italian Eritrea): the colony's infobox shows the crowned Italian tricolour (the 1861-1946 type), for 1882-1936.
era-1890.open: The Italian flag appears only in a Wikipedia infobox; no text read describes a flag flown in the colony or the gold colonial badge on the white field, and the page's drawing is described as schematic.

era-1270.open: The change to green on top is 1914 on Wikipedia and 1941 on FOTW; neither source says Haile Selassie formalised the lion flag.

era-1874.says: Wikipedia: the plain Union Flag was Fiji's only flag from first raising on 10 October 1874 to 1877; from 1877 a blue ensign with a white-disc badge (foliage, war clubs and a shield with a mermaid), from 1883 a disc with a crowned lion and FIJI, and from 1908 the colony's arms, with the full arms in the fly from 1924. FOTW (British Fiji Islands): the same badge sequence (1877 circular foliage badge with a mermaid shield; 1883 white disc with the lion crest and FIJI approved by the Admiralty; 1908 arms granted on 4 July on a white disc; 1924 the white circle removed on a governor's instruction, noted in the Admiralty Flag Book 1930).
era-1874.open: Both sources date the Blue Ensign from 1877, not 1874, and show that the badge changed four times and the white disc was dropped in 1924; the page's 'roundel with a local landscape motif' matches none of these.

era-1871.says: Wikipedia: the Kingdom of Fiji's flag was a vertical bicolour of white and light blue with a red shield bearing a white dove with an olive branch under a crown, with no Union Jack. FOTW (Historical Flags): on 5 June 1871 Cakobau proclaimed the United Kingdom of Fiji, which used a white and blue flag with the dove on a red shield until 10 October 1874 (after R.A. Derrick in Vexilla Nostra 164); a 2015 Fiji Sun article notes the flag 'didn't last very long' and was to be replaced by a red flag quartered by a blue cross, unsourced.
era-1871.open: Two sources agree on a white and blue flag with a dove on a red shield for 1871-1874 but the page's drawing, a blue field with a Union Jack canton, does not match and should be replaced; the arrangement of the stripes (vertical or horizontal) is shown only in images.

era-1917.says: Wikipedia says a design competition followed the declaration of independence in late 1917, Eero Snellman and Bruno Tuukkanen set the final form, a temporary de facto flag was used from December 1917 to May 1918, the cross flag was adopted in May 1918 (28 May in the infobox), the blue was darkened and the arms made rectangular in 1920, and Law 380/1978 defined the rectangular state flag and swallow-tailed national flag. FOTW says the swallow-tailed state flag is listed as adopted on 26 May 1978 (citing Album des pavillons, 2000) and gives the proportions and the blue as PMS 294.
era-1917.open: The 1918 date is Wikipedia's alone and differs from this page's 29 May by a day; FOTW's page covers only the current flags. Neither source mentions the colours' origin in the 19th century beyond Wikipedia's Topelius tradition (citing Inglefield, 1978).

era-1809.says: Wikipedia: the first known 'Flag of Finland', presented in 1848, showed the coat of arms in laurel on white; captured Finnish merchant ships flew the St George flag in 1853-56; a blue-cross flag was made official in 1861 for private vessels; in 1910 the Russian authorities decreed a Russian flag in the canton, which Finns resisted. FOTW (Grand Duchy of Finland): a Finnish merchant flag of 1809-21 (blue ensign with the Russian tricolour in the canton) was prescribed but soon revoked in favour of the Russian merchant ensign; the unofficial flag of the Grand Duchy raised by students on 13 May 1848 was white with the Duchy's arms and a laurel wreath; yacht club flags from 1861/1882 are the root of the national flag.
era-1809.open: 'Never adopted its own official flag' is too absolute: a merchant flag was prescribed in 1809 and a blue-cross flag made official for private vessels in 1861; the dark-field arms flag drawn on the page is not what the sources describe (white).

era-1150.says: Wikipedia (Finland under Swedish rule): Finland was a part of Sweden from the Middle Ages until 1809, with Swedish rule over most of Finland ending on 17 September 1809 under the Treaty of Hamina. Wikipedia (Flag of Sweden): the oldest recorded pictures of the blue cloth with a yellow cross date from the early 16th century, and a legend places the origin of the golden cross on blue in 1157 during the First Swedish Crusade in Finland. Wikipedia's Flag of Finland dates the first known Finnish flag to 1848; FOTW (Finland) covers no flag before 1978.
era-1150.open: No source read says that Finland flew the Swedish flag, or describes any flag in Finland before the 16th century; the c.1150 start is the traditional crusade date, which Wikipedia calls uncertain and controversial, and the blue-yellow cross flag is documented only from the early 16th century.

era-1970.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted on 18 February 1965, first hoisted at midnight on independence day; three bands of red, blue and green separated by thin white stripes (designer Louis Thomasi); it remained unchanged throughout the 1982-89 Senegambia confederation; blue is the river, red the sun and savanna, green forests and agricultural goods, the white stripes unity and peace. FOTW: adopted 18 February 1965 (Dorling Kindersley; Smith says 'officially hoisted' then), stripes red, white, blue, white, green in 6:1:4:1:6; the page records no change when the republic was proclaimed in 1970 and says the flag and arms were not modified during the Senegambia federation (given as 1981-1989 by FOTW).
era-1970.open: The flag dates from 1965, not 1970; 1970 is the republic. Neither source mentions a change in 1970 (a silence, not an explicit statement of continuity), and the sources date Senegambia differently (1981 vs 1982). White-stripe meaning varies in FOTW (unity and peace, or rice fields).

Wikipedia notes it was the only Union Republic flag whose hammer and sickle was not gold.
era-1921.open: The drawing and caption show a gold hammer and sickle and a blue-white-blue stripe; neither source gives gold or a white-edged stripe, so the drawing needs redrawing against the sources. The 1921-22 flag is not described by either source, and the 1922-36 Transcaucasian federation years are not Georgian-republic flags.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: dark red field with black and white bands in the canton, designed by Iakob Nikoladze, abolished after the 1921 incorporation into the USSR. FOTW's First Republic page agrees: the flag designed by Jakob Nikoladze (contest winner) was flown from 1918 until the Red Army's conquest in March 1921; it is the 1990 flag with a 1:2 ratio and slightly larger canton.
era-1918.open: Contributors on FOTW date the flag's first acceptance differently (1917, 22 April 1918, 26 May 1918, 22 April 1921). A black-white-red variant was also reported.

era-1801.says: Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Georgia nor FOTW's Georgia pages (main, historical flags, 1990-2004, First Republic) describe flags flown in Georgia under Russian rule; FOTW's Russian Empire page documents the empire's black-yellow-white flag of 1858-83 and later flags without reference to Georgia.
era-1801.open: That the Russian imperial flags were the flags flown over Georgian territory 1801-1918 is not stated by anything read; the Georgian Governorate and Georgia within the Russian Empire articles on Wikipedia carry no flag text.

era-1490.says: Wikipedia shows flags for Mingrelia (1550s, 1560s, 18th century) and Kakheti (18th century) and none dated for Imereti or Samtskhe-Saatabago; FOTW, reporting the Georgian Parliament's website, gives a plain white flag for the Imereti Kingdom (15th-18th centuries) and a black flag with a white cross for West Georgia (13th-14th centuries).
era-1490.open: Neither source gives a maroon field with a gold cross for these kingdoms, so the drawing is unconfirmed; FOTW passes on the Parliament captions without their basis, and Wikipedia gives no dates for Kartli or Imereti.

era-1243.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Georgia shows a 1339 Dulcert chart with Georgia's flag and a 1367 Pizzigano chart showing a five-cross flag over Tbilisi, which fall in this era; FOTW's historical page gives a black flag with a white cross for West Georgia (13th-14th centuries) from the Parliament's website.
era-1243.open: No source says Georgia flew a distinct state flag under Mongol overlordship in so many words, and the generic field drawn here is not a documented banner.

era-1008.says: Wikipedia: single red cross on white attributed to Vakhtang I, a dark red cross and a star on white attributed to Queen Tamar, the five-cross banner dated to the 12th century, a coin of David IV, and the 1367 Pizzigano chart's Jerusalem-cross flag over Tbilisi. FOTW: the Parliament website shows a white flag with a red disc of St George for the 5th-15th centuries and a white five-cross and a white red-cross flag for the 12th-15th centuries; the five-cross flag is first described in the Book of All Kingdoms (1345-1350).
era-1008.open: Every source read gives a red cross on white; none gives the maroon field and gold cross drawn here, so the drawing needs redrawing. The Parliament-site flags are given without basis.

era-1990.says: Wikipedia says the German Unity Flag was raised in front of the Reichstag on 3 October 1990 and that the current flag was adopted on reunification. FOTW says the tricolour was re-adopted in 1949 and extended to civil use on 14 August 1950.
era-1990.open: The flag itself is the one adopted in 1949 (Basic Law, Article 22); 1990 is when it became the flag of the reunified country.

era-1945.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no German national flag was allowed to fly».
era-1945.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1806.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no shared confederal flag, only individual client-kingdom colors».
era-1806.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-100bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no unified banner; each tribal confederation had its own standards, mostly unrecorded».
era-100bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1949.says: Wikipedia says Article 22 of the Basic Law of 23 May 1949 reads «The federal flag shall be black, red and gold», and that East Germany also used black-red-gold in 1949–59. FOTW (Sensen) says the GDR's tricolour had no coat of arms in 1949–1959 and carried one in 1959–1989.
era-1949.open: The sources differ on the West German date: FOTW gives 8 or 9 May 1949 (about two weeks before the Federal Republic existed), Wikipedia 23 May 1949. The 1 October 1959 GDR emblem law was not found in the part of Wikipedia that was read.

era-1933.says: Wikipedia says a ruling of 12 March 1933 made two flags legal, black-white-red and the Nazi Party flag, and banned black-red-gold, and that on 15 September 1935 the dual arrangement ended with the Nazi flag the sole national flag. FOTW says the Third Reich replaced the tricolour with its own flag on 12 March 1933.
era-1933.open: The image is a stylised abstraction, not a reproduction.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sensen) says the tricolour was re-adopted as the Weimar Republic's flag on 11 August 1919. Wikipedia says the Weimar constitution designated black-red-gold in 1919, that black-white-red was kept as a civil ensign with the new flag in the canton and as a merchant flag in 1919–1933, and that black-white-red was reintroduced for diplomatic missions abroad in 1922.
era-1918.open: This page used to say black-red-gold became a national flag «for the first time»; Wikipedia says the Frankfurt Parliament declared it official in 1848–49. «11 August» is FOTW's; Wikipedia gives only «August 1919».

era-1871.says: Wikipedia says the North German Confederation's 1867 constitution declared black-white-red the civil and war ensign and that the 1871 constitution kept it. FOTW says the Empire chose a flag based on north German traditions, Bismarck favouring a Kleindeutschland solution, and gives no separate date for the 1871 decision.
era-1871.open: This page's explanation of the colours (Prussian black-white plus Hanseatic red-white) was not found in either source.

era-1866.says: Wikipedia: black-white-red appeared for the first time in 1867 in the constitution of the North German Confederation, which declared it a civil and war ensign. FOTW's North German Confederation page: the flag was adopted on 25 June 1867 (Article 55: 'the flag of the navy and merchant fleet is black-white-red'), was made the merchant flag by ordinance of 25 October 1867, and was extended to the whole of Germany on 16 April 1871; the most common theory is a combination of Prussia's black-white and the white and red of the Hanseatic League.
era-1866.open: FOTW says the significance of the colours is 'not completely clear' (other guesses: Prussia and Hamburg, or Brandenburg) and notes that the same colours were long used by the city of Allenstein, so 'deliberately engineered' is a theory; the sources date the flag to 1867, not 1866, and it was only a civil ensign in 1867-1870 (the war ensign was a different flag).

era-1815.says: Wikipedia says the Bundestag adopted the black-red-gold tricolour on 9 March 1848, that the Frankfurt Parliament declared it the official colours in 1848–49, and that the German Confederation was restored in 1850; its origins are in Jena's Urburschenschaft (1815) and the Lützow Free Corps. FOTW says the Frankfurt Parliament adopted it in 1848 for a proposed united German Empire and that it was abolished in 1852.
era-1815.open: Wikipedia contradicts itself on whether the Confederation had a flag of its own. This page used to say the tricolour «was never the Confederation's official flag»; that is not what the sources say for 1848–52. Prussia's black eagle on white, shown beside it, was not covered by either source.

era-962.says: Wikipedia: the Holy Roman Empire (800/962-1806) had no national flag, black and gold were the emperor's colours and the imperial banner was a black eagle on gold, its claws and beak red after the late 13th or early 14th century and a double-headed eagle from the early 15th century. FOTW's Holy Roman Empire page: the flag was an imperial banner used by the Emperor, not a national flag; the banner was a black eagle armed red, generally on gold (sometimes on white), and in 1401 a double-headed eagle replaced the single-headed one; the Empire's territories increasingly acquired their own flags.
era-962.open: Both sources date the double-headed eagle to about 1401-early 15th century, so the double-headed eagle drawn for 962 onward is correct only for the later period; FOTW starts the Empire at 800 (Charlemagne) while Wikipedia gives 800/962. The red 'armed' detail and the white-field variant differ in dating between the sources.

era-1966.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted 6 March 1957, flown until 1962 and reinstated in 1966 after Nkrumah was overthrown in February 1966; its text describes a red-gold-green triband with a black five-pointed star in the gold stripe. FOTW's 1964-66 page says the white-stripe flag ran from 1 January 1964 to 28 February 1966, after which the older flag was restored.
era-1966.open: Wikipedia's text says the original flag flew until 1962, FOTW and the page's other sources give the white-stripe variant 1964-66; the 1962-64 years are not explained. Design and swatch colours not checked against a specification.

era-1295.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — earliest Akan states, no flag or war banner survives».
era-1295.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: January 1964 variant with white replacing yellow (CPP colours). FOTW: a white middle stripe 1 January 1964 - 28 February 1966, described in Smith 1975, and the white stripe was a feature of the Convention Peoples' Party flag.
era-1964.open: Both sources agree on a white middle stripe and the period, but the drawing shows a gold middle stripe with a star and an arc that neither source describes; the drawing needs redrawing with a white stripe. Whether the star was kept is not stated.

era-1957.says: Both: red-gold-green with a black star adopted at independence March 1957, designed by Theodosia Okoh; colour meanings red blood, gold minerals, green forest; star tied to Black Star Line (Wikipedia 6 March 1957; FOTW 'lone star of African freedom').
era-1957.open: Wikipedia says this flag ran to 1962 (Union of African States flags in between), the page says 1964; unresolved.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia: the Gold Coast flag 1877-1957 was a defaced Blue Ensign, replaced by the national flag; its Gold Coast colony infobox gives 1821-1957 and shows that flag. FOTW's Gold Coast page (after Carr 1961) says the badge was a brown elephant before a palm tree among green mountains, with the initials 'G.C.', on the Union Flag (with a garland) and on the Blue Ensign (without), used 1877-1957.
era-1821.open: The Union Flag alone, as drawn, is not the colony's own flag; nothing read covers 1821-1877. A Red Ensign is not mentioned.

era-1670.says: FOTW's Ashanti page (after McMeekin and the Fachinger collection at Bremerhaven) shows several Ashanti flags: a yellow-over-black-over-green tricolour with a yellow device, a fimbriated version with a throne emblem, and uprising flags of yellow with a striped canton; a reader's 2022 article gives a design with a 'hat' emblem. Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Ghana nor FOTW's Ghana page mentions frankaa war banners.
era-1670.open: FOTW's flags are undated and may belong to the 19th-20th centuries; the page's statement that no fixed national flag existed, and the appliqued war banners and Golden Stool remarks, are not confirmed. Asante Empire on Wikipedia has no flag text.

era-1974.says: Wikipedia says Law 48/1975 and Presidential Decree 515/1975 took effect on 7 June 1975 making the former land flag the sole flag, that in 1978 the sea flag returned as the sole flag, that its adoption date is 22 December 1978, and that Law 851/1978 describes it as cyan and white with five cyan and four white stripes (the exact blue left to flagmakers). FOTW (Adams) says the plain cross flag was the only national flag from June 1975 until December 1978, that the striped flag was adopted by law on 22 December 1978, and gives Pantone 286 C as a reference blue.
era-1974.open: The shade of blue is unspecified in law; Pilalis says the lighter blue belongs to the defunct kingdom's arms and the flags use dark blue. This page used to say the nine-stripe flag was unchanged since the 19th century.

era-1204.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — a fractured patchwork of Crusader lordships, each with its own banner».
era-1204.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-2700bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — nearly four millennia, no single banner ever unified this span».
era-2700bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1967.says: Wikipedia says a decree of 18 August 1969 made the sea flag the sole national flag, the ratio changed from 2:3 to 7:12 on 18 August 1970, and the monarchy was abolished on 1 June 1973. Flags of the World (history, parts 2 and 3) says the two national flags, plain cross on land and cross-and-stripes at sea, stayed in use unchanged from 1832 to 1970, that all crown flags were abolished in 1970, and that on 18 August 1970 the 7:12 cross-and-stripes flag became the national flag and ensign.
era-1967.open: The sources differ on whether the sole-flag decree is 1969 (Wikipedia) or 1970 (FOTW). Dark blue becoming common from the late 1960s is 'citation needed' in Wikipedia. The phoenix emblem on seals was not checked.

era-1924.says: Wikipedia says the Second Hellenic Republic removed the crowns from all flags on 25 March 1924, after crowns had replaced the arms in a decree of 28 December 1863, and that the 2:3 ratio was set on 20 February 1930. Flags of the World (part 2), counting the republic of 1924-1935 as the First Republic, says the crown flags were most probably not used in that period, while the two plain national flags continued.
era-1924.open: This page used to say the flag had no crown to remove; both sources show that the royal flags did carry one. FOTW says the adoption date of the crown flags is unknown.

era-1832.says: Wikipedia says the first official naval ensign specifications under Otto were published in 1833, with the royal arms on the cross, that crowns replaced the arms by a decree of 28 December 1863, and that a decree of 26 September 1867 set the shape and use of flags. Flags of the World says the striped flag was approved in 1832, and its part 2 says the cross-and-stripes sea flag and plain cross land flag were used unchanged 1832-1970, with a naval ensign prescribed in 1858 carrying the Wittelsbach arms.
era-1832.open: The sources differ by a year (1832 FOTW, 1833 Wikipedia) and on the date of the arms-bearing naval ensign (1858 FOTW), and neither says the plain striped flag was the Kingdom's state flag throughout, as the page used to say; crown flags were used for official purposes.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia says the First National Assembly at Epidaurus officially adopted the flag on 13 January 1822 and that Provisional Government Decree 540 of 15 March 1822 set the land flag, naval ensign and civil ensign. FOTW (Adams) says the striped flag and the plain white cross on blue both date from 1822, the nine stripes said to stand for the nine syllables of the motto «Freedom or Death».
era-1821.open: The meaning of the colours (blue for sea and sky, white for purity), stated on this page, was not found in either source. The syllable explanation is the one given.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia says the Axis occupation of 1941-1944 forbade the Greek flag, which became a symbol of resistance. Flags of the World (WWII page) tells of the evzone Koukidis, ordered on 27 April 1941 to replace the Greek flag on the Acropolis with the Nazi flag, and says that under an order of 10 April 1943 Greek ships with Greek crews flew an occupation-zone pennant directly under the Greek national flag.
era-1941.open: Neither source describes the flag of the government in exile, which is what the page's caption claims. The two sources also pull in different directions on whether the Greek flag was banned or flown on ships; not resolved.

era-1944.says: Flags of the World (part 2) says the use of the two national flags, and the crown flags of the Kingdom (1935-1970), remained unchanged until 1970. Wikipedia captions the 1863 flag pattern as used 1944-1969 and notes the 1967 Compulsory Law 198 on regional flag days did not change the flag.
era-1944.open: Neither source covers the restoration of the monarchy, the civil war or the 'unbroken legal continuity' wording. The flag of the Democratic Army of Greece (FOTW gr^dse.html) was not read.

era-1935.says: Wikipedia says Kondylis declared the monarchy restored on 10 October 1935 and a decree of 7 November 1935 reinstated the 31 May 1914 decree on crown flags; a caption dates the 1863 pattern to 1935-1941. Flags of the World (part 2) says the Kingdom's flags, with crown flags, were in use 1935-1970 and the two national flags were unchanged.
era-1935.open: Neither source names Metaxas or describes propaganda symbolism, and neither was read for the claim that the flag was never altered under his regime.

era-1913.says: Wikipedia gives a decree of 31 May 1914 making the crown flag the state flag for ministries and civil services. Flags of the World (part 2) says the two national flags were used unchanged from 1832 to 1970 and lists the Kingdom's crown flags for 1832-1924.
era-1913.open: Neither source covers the Balkan Wars, the wartime split between Athens and Thessaloniki or the 1922 catastrophe as flag history; those parts of the page text rest on no flag source.

era-1460.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Greece) says unofficial flags were used under Ottoman rule, often with the double-headed eagle or crosses. Flags of the World (Greece under Ottoman rule) says Greek ships had to fly a red flag with a blue central stripe, gives a Smyrna variant, notes that from 1774 Greek merchant ships flew the Russian naval ensign, and shows the 1797 flag of Rigas Velestinlis. Wikipedia (Flag of the Ottoman Empire) dates a plain crescent flag c.1480-1780, a naval decree for the crescent and star in 1793 and the official crescent-and-star flag to 1844.
era-1460.open: The page's 'red field with crescent and star' is not supported for 1460-1821: Wikipedia puts the star and crescent flag in 1793 (navy) and 1844 (national), and both sources show distinct Greek flags, so 'no distinct Greek flag' is contradicted. The red-crescent banner over mainland Greece is not described by either Greek page.

era-1261.says: Wikipedia cites a 14th-century Palaiologan flag as the only attested Byzantine flag and says the double-headed eagle was the Palaiologoi's symbol. Flags of the World (Byzantine page) calls the imperial flag yellow with a black crowned double-headed eagle, the dynasty's symbol after 1261, on contributor commentary without a cited basis, and also reports that the Book of All Kingdoms (1350) shows the Emperor of Constantinople with a quartered flag of red crosses on white and gold crosses on red.
era-1261.open: Two compiled sources agree the eagle was the dynasty's symbol, but the black-on-yellow flag drawn here is not evidenced for 1261-1460: the one dated illustration (1350) shows a different flag, and the Despotate of the Morea is not mentioned in either.

era-1974.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted on 7 February 1974, independence day, replacing a temporary Associated State design (green, yellow, blue bands with a nutmeg); green for vegetation, yellow for the sun, red for harmony and courage, six stars for the parishes, a central star for Carriacou and Petite Martinique, and a nutmeg. Flags of the World: the flag was 'assigned on December 6, 1973, the same day as the Coat of Arms'; its history page says the present flag replaced the associated-state flag at independence.
era-1974.open: The sources differ on the adoption date (6 December 1973 assignment vs 7 February 1974 in force at independence); the caption's 'unchanged since 1974' was not checked against later amendments.

era-1498.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder field — pre-colonial era, no flag survives».
era-1498.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-300bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder field — Grenada's earliest known settlers, no flag survives».
era-300bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1783.says: Flags of the World (history page): a Blue Ensign with a sugar-mill badge (a trapiche with the motto HAE TIBI ERUNT ARTES) for 1875-1903, then a Blue Ensign with a ship badge (possibly Columbus's ship, motto 'clarior e tenebris') for 1903-1967 or 1974 depending on source, with the sea shown green or blue; associated-state flag 1967-1974. Wikipedia: Blue Ensign with a colonial badge 1875-1903, a second badge 1903-1967; the 1783 Peace of Paris gave Britain the island permanently.
era-1783.open: Both publishers support a badged Blue Ensign only from 1875; nothing read gives a flag for 1783-1875. The card's 'harbor badge' does not match FOTW's sugar mill (1875-1903) or ship (1903-) badges.

era-1763.says: Wikipedia: sovereignty alternated between France and Britain through the 18th century and the 1783 Peace of Paris left Britain with the island; no flags named. Flags of the World's Grenada pages (main and history) cover no flag before the 1875 Blue Ensign.
era-1763.open: A British Red Ensign for 1763-1783 is not documented by any source read; also not read: a source on British merchant or naval ensigns in the West Indies in this period.

era-1650.says: Neither Wikipedia nor Flags of the World names a flag for French Grenada. The Canadian Military Heritage page says Louis XIV's 1661 decree made the plain white flag the French Royal Navy's flag, that it was the only flag on the forts of New France, and that a white flag with fleurs-de-lis was flown only in the king's presence.
era-1650.open: The source on the French white ensign concerns New France, not Grenada, and describes it without fleurs-de-lis, so the card's gold fleur-de-lis is not supported; no source read says what flew over Grenada in 1650-1763.

era-1968.says: Wikipedia: scroll dated 15 September 1821; 1968–97 a similar state flag; 1997 current design. FOTW: regulation 12 September 1968 (5:8, ISCC-NBS colours, quetzal 'supreme symbol of liberty'); Decree 104-97 current flag.
era-1968.open: The 1997 date is 26 December or 26 September.

era-1871.says: Wikipedia: 17 August 1871 blue and white restored as vertical stripes with a new coat of arms. FOTW: August 1871 decree (12, 13 or 17); 18 November 1871 decree defines the arms.
era-1871.open: The sources differ on the day.

era-1851.says: Wikipedia: a pro-Spanish faction took over in 1851 and added red and yellow to the flag; the table dates a Guatemala flag to 1843-1851 and the 1871 flag restored blue and white as vertical stripes (17 August 1871). Flags of the World (historical flags page, citing Crampton 1990 and Flagmaster): a flag introduced on 14 March 1851 under President Mariano Paredes, with red and yellow recalling Spanish rule, replaced on 21 May 1858 by another with a central stripe, until the vertical blue-white-blue was introduced in 1871 (17 or 18 August, 12 August in another FOTW page).
era-1851.open: The placement of the red and yellow is not settled: FOTW quotes an 1865 French description of a flag cut into a red-white-yellow part and a blue-white-blue part, and its contributors disagree on the 2:3 and 1:2 proportions; the page's 'hoist side of the top and bottom bands' is not confirmed. The 1858 flag falls inside this page's span and is not drawn.

era-1841.says: Wikipedia: Guatemala flag dated 1838-1843 and 1843-1851 (designs not described); the federation flag was used in Guatemala until 1851. Flags of the World (historical flags page, a contributor): from about 1838 to 1843 the 1825 flag was used with the 1825 arms in the central white stripe, and flags were adopted on 26 October 1843 (ratio 2:3) and abolished on 14 March 1851.
era-1841.open: The two sources show that Guatemala had flags of its own dated 1838/1843-1851, which contradicts the page's plain blue-white-blue carried on informally; their designs are not described in the text read. The 1841 start is not covered.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia: United Provinces of Central America flag 1823-1824; Federal Republic flag 1824-1838 in the table; used in Guatemala until 1851. Flags of the World (Central America and Guatemala pages, contributor posts quoting Crampton 1990): the first flag, made by Colonel Arce in 1822, was adopted for the United Provinces on 21 August 1823, the Central American flags derive from the blue-white-blue tricolour, and Guatemala's flags are shown as a member of the United Provinces (1823-1825) and of the Federal Republic (adopted 22 November 1824, a federal flag from 1 January 1825); its timeline gives Guatemala's exit from the federation in 1839 and the federation's end in 1841.
era-1823.open: The emblem details (five volcanoes, cap of liberty, rainbow) are in FOTW images only, not in the text read. The sources differ on the years (Wikipedia 1823-1824 and 1824-1838; FOTW 1823-1825 and 1825 to about 1838), and Guatemala left the federation in 1839, before this page's 1841.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia: flag of the First Mexican Empire listed for 1821-1823, no annexation event described; the Federal Republic of Central America article lists the Mexican Empire flag as its predecessor in its infobox. Flags of the World (Central America page, quoting a vdiest.nl timeline): independence of the Kingdom of Guatemala on 15 September 1821, incorporation into Mexico on 5 January 1822, independence again on 1 July 1823.
era-1821.open: The annexation is now sourced by FOTW, but only Wikipedia (a table and an infobox, no text) ties the Mexican Empire flag to Guatemala; no source describes the flag over Guatemala or its eagle. Guatemala's own flag before the annexation (15 September 1821 to January 1822) is not covered.

era-1524.says: Wikipedia (Guatemala): a flag of the Kingdom of Guatemala is listed for 1524-1821 without design. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): the saw-toothed red saltire on white served as flag of the New World viceroyalties. Flags of the World (Spain 1506-1700 page): the red Burgundy cross, most often on white, was the main symbol of Spanish ships from 1518 to 1665 and the naval ensign 1506-1701, and a land war flag to 1843; the page does not mention Guatemala.
era-1524.open: Use of the Cross of Burgundy in the Captaincy General of Guatemala specifically, and the royal arms alongside it, are not covered by any source read; Wikipedia's Captaincy General of Guatemala article shows no flag text. After 1701 and 1785 Spain changed its ensigns, so the 1524-1821 span is not covered either.

era-1973.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted on 24 September 1973, the day of the proclamation of independence; it is almost identical to the flag of the PAIGC, which has the party initials under the star; the black star symbolises the party's leadership. FOTW: the National Assembly proclaimed independence and the first constitution on 23 September 1973, whose article 2 describes the flag; the party flag is the national flag with the party sigla beneath the star; the flag follows Ghana's pan-African colours with the black star.
era-1973.open: The national flag is the PAIGC flag without the initials, not 'unchanged'. The independence date differs by a day (23 or 24 September 1973). FOTW calls the Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde link a short-lived confederacy that broke apart over conflicts between the two peoples; Wikipedia does not mention it.

era-1230.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder field — no surviving territorial banner attributed to Kaabu».
era-1230.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1963.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Guinea-Bissau): the PAIGC adopted its flag in 1961, with the Pan-African colours of Ghana and Guinea-Conakry and a Black Star on a red bar at the hoist, the party initials beneath. Wikipedia (Portuguese Guinea): the Liberated Zones appear as a successor state with the PAIGC flag. FOTW: the party flag is the national flag with the sigla below the star; a 1974 PAIGC book photographs the independence assembly at Madina do Boé 'in the bush' with many small flags and a large one, and a photograph from the independence war showing the flag with Cabral's image was reported.
era-1963.open: Neither source dates the first use of the flag in the liberated areas to 1963 (Wikipedia gives 1961 for the adoption); the page's earlier black hoist band with a red star is contradicted by both. The liberated zones are named only in Wikipedia's infobox.

era-1911.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): the green-and-red republican flag was decreed on 30 June 1911. Wikipedia (Portuguese Guinea): the colony's infobox shows the Portuguese flag for 1910-1974. FOTW (Portuguese colonies): the Portuguese government's position, held 'almost since the 40ies', was that colonies had no flags other than the national flag, apart from officials' and military flags; distinctive colonial flag proposals (1965-67) were never adopted.
era-1911.open: FOTW's statement covers the 1940s to 1974; for 1911 to the 1940s no source read describes colonial flag practice. Wikipedia gives 1910 as the start of the republican flag in the infobox and 30 June 1911 for the decree. The page's end date of 1963 is the start of the PAIGC war, not a change of flag.

era-1867.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): Portugal's flag took a blue-and-white field in 1830 and the republic replaced it in 1910-11. Wikipedia (Portuguese Guinea): a dependency of Cape Verde until 1879, a colony of the Portuguese Empire from 1879, with the Portuguese flag in the infobox for 1910-1974 only.
era-1867.open: No source read shows the blue-and-white flag over Portuguese Guinea, and the page's 1867 start is contradicted by Wikipedia's 1879 date for the colony (a separate colony from Cape Verde); FOTW has no page on the kingdom-era flag in the colony.

era-1958.says: Both sources give 1958, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 10 November 1958; Flags of the World dates it 10 November 1958.
era-1958.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1891.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1727.says: Wikipedia shows a Futa Jallon flag captioned pre-1896 and used under the French protectorate 1896-1912, with no design described, and a reconstructed flag for Samory Toure (1898). Flags of the World (Futa Djalon Kingdom): the state existed ca. 1700 to post-1934, created by the Fulani c.1725 under Karamoko with its capital at Timbo from 1780; two flag images are shown, one for the state and one for the French protectorate with the French flag in a canton, the state flag bearing an Arabic inscription read as the tahmid 'Alhamdu liLlah'.
era-1727.open: Both sources show a flag for the Imamate, so the card's claim that none is documented is wrong, but neither describes its colours or dates it to 1727-1891; the green field with crescent and star drawn on the card is not described by either.

era-1966.says: Both sources give 1966, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 26 May 1966; Flags of the World dates it 1966.
era-1966.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia: Blue Ensign with colonial badge in the fly; unofficial red version at sea; first flag introduced 1875, changed 1906 and 1955; colonial flags 1:2. Flags of the World (historical flags page, David Prothero and others): the three Dutch colonies became British in 1814 and were united into British Guiana some years later; the colonial Blue Ensign carried a circular badge with a three-masted ship from 1875, an oval badge in a yellow garter from 1906, and the badge from the 1954 arms; the red ensign was unofficial and 'dubious', commercial vessels flying the plain Red Ensign.
era-1814.open: Both sources date the colonial Blue Ensign with badge from 1875, so the 1814/1831 start is not supported and nothing is said of flags before 1875. The two sources differ on whether an unofficial defaced red ensign existed (Wikipedia yes, FOTW doubts it).

era-1616.says: Wikipedia's Berbice and Demerara articles show in their infoboxes the flag of the Dutch West India Company (dated 1627-1792 for Berbice) and then the Union Jack, not a plain tricolour. Flags of the World's historical page says only that Dutch Guiana had four colonies of which three became British in 1814; its Suriname colonial-flags page mentions the West India Company arms, a three-master on a sea, possibly on tricolour flags there.
era-1616.open: A Dutch tricolour for Essequibo, Demerara and Berbice is not stated by any source read; the infobox company flag is a Wikipedia editors' choice, not a cited description. What flew over the colonies in 1616-1814, and how it varied between the Company's and the States' periods, is not established.

era-1820.says: Wikipedia: 1806 present design under Pétion; 1820–49 plain blue-and-red; 1964–86 Duvalier black-and-red; 26 February 1986 current design. FOTW: 1964 Duvalier black version; 17 February 1986 restoration; constitution of 29 March 1987 defines blue over red with arms on a white panel.
era-1820.open: The sources differ on the 1986 day; neither describes the 1849 empire.

era-1803.says: Wikipedia: 18 May 1803 Arcahaie flag; 20 May 1805 black and red; 1806 blue-and-red under Pétion; 1808 arms. FOTW: 18 May 1803 Arcahaie, made by removing the white stripe from the French tricolour.

era-1697.says: Wikipedia (Saint-Domingue): the colony is dated 1659-1803 (infobox 1697-1803), Spain recognised French control of the western third at Ryswick in 1697, and the infobox flag is captioned 'Flag before the French Revolution' without a description. Wikipedia (Flag of France): the royal white flag and the navy's white ensign were pre-revolutionary, a white field strewn with gold fleurs-de-lis was sometimes seen, and the tricolour dates from 1790. FOTW (ht-hist) covers Saint-Domingue only from 1790 and describes no French royal or colonial flag before 1803.
era-1697.open: Wikipedia gives a pre-Revolution flag image for the colony without describing it, and a general account of the royal white flag; no source states that this white ensign with fleurs-de-lis was flown in Saint-Domingue. The page's colony start of 1697 vs 1659 is a source disagreement.

era-1492.says: Wikipedia (Captaincy General of Santo Domingo): the infobox shows the flags of Spain and the Cross of Burgundy (the latter a military flag); the whole island was Spanish until 1605, from the 17th century French, English and Spanish forces contested the western third, and Spain ceded it to France at Ryswick in 1697. FOTW (ht-hist) gives no Spanish flag before 1803.
era-1492.open: The Cross of Burgundy over Hispaniola is shown only in Wikipedia's infobox for the captaincy (1492-1821), not specifically for the western part or dated within it; the page's 'same flag throughout' is not established. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 197,786 characters.

era-1949.says: Wikipedia: Decree 29 of 18 January 1949 (26 January per infobox) with turquoise; January 2022 turquoise; 27 January 2026 navy again. FOTW: 1949 decree sets the stars farther apart in an X; 2022 turquoise.
era-1949.open: The January 1949 day differs inside Wikipedia.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Central America» gives adoption in 1823, 2000 and relinquishment in 1839, within a year of this era's 1823 and 1838. The Flags of the World page that article links also carries 1838, and has 1823 next to a word about adopting.
era-1823.open: Only the dates were compared. The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1866.says: Wikipedia: Medina, Decree 7, 16 February 1866 (or 7 March) adds five stars. FOTW: 1866 stars added (9 January, 16 February or 19 January); 1933 regulation 194 of 27 September closer stars.
era-1866.open: The 1866 day is uncertain and the X pattern dates from 1949.

era-1838.says: Wikipedia: 1823 flag adopted in the United Provinces, based on Argentina's. FOTW: stars added in 1866.
era-1838.open: FOTW does not cover the 1823 flag.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia (First Mexican Empire): lands of the former Captaincy General of Guatemala were annexed to the empire in 1822-1823 (map caption includes modern Honduras); Wikipedia (Captaincy General of Guatemala): the elite 'joined the First Mexican Empire by annexation' after the 15 September 1821 independence. Flags of the World (Central America unions): incorporation into Mexico on 5 January 1822 (vdiest.nl timeline), and the federal blue-white-blue flag adopted 21 August 1823; it names no flag flown under Mexican rule. Flags of the World (Honduras historical flags): Honduras used the federal flag from 1823.
era-1821.open: The Mexican annexation of 1822-23 is attested by two publishers, but no source says the Mexican Empire's green-white-red flag with an eagle flew over Honduras; Wikipedia's First Mexican Empire page is captioned only 'Flag of Mexico' and the eagle is not described.

era-1524.says: Wikipedia (Captaincy General of Guatemala): the infobox shows the Cross of Burgundy for 1527-1821 and the captaincy included present-day Honduras. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): it served as the flag of the Viceroyalties of the New World, with a footnote that a viceregal banner lasted as a symbol of New Spain to 24 August 1821. The National Park Service calls it the Spanish Colonial Flag flown by ships and over fortresses, with the striped red-and-gold flag replacing it as the naval ensign in 1785 and at forts in 1793. Flags of the World's Honduras pages do not cover the colonial period.
era-1524.open: No source says the Cross of Burgundy was flown in Honduras itself or flown alongside the royal arms; the sources disagree on whether it persisted to 1821 (Wikipedia captaincy and viceroyalty claims) or gave way to the striped flag from 1785-1793 (National Park Service); the 1524 start is not given (Wikipedia: 1527).

era-1989.says: Wikipedia says no change to the flag was needed after communism fell in 1989 and that it was reaffirmed on 19 June 1990 (Act XL of 1990); it gives 1848 for the design and 23 May 1957 for its adoption as the state flag. FOTW says the 1949 constitution was modified by Law XL of 1990 and the coat of arms adopted in 1990, and dates the flag to 1957.
era-1989.open: This page starts the era in 1989; the legal acts in the sources are 1957 and 1990. The sources agree that the plain tricolour was the flag throughout 1957–1990.

era-1949.says: FOTW (Molnár, 2001) says the flag bore the Rákosi coat of arms in 1949–1956 and that the tricolour was in use again from 1956. Wikipedia says the Rákosi arms became the badge in 1949, that revolutionaries cut the emblem out in 1956, and that on 23 May 1957 the pure tricolour became the official state flag, the new arms never officially placed on it (Act II of 1957).
era-1949.open: The image shows the 1949–1956 flag, so it is evidence for those years only; for 1957–1989 both sources say the plain tricolour was official. This page used to describe the arms as a «1957 redesign»; that was wrong.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Hungary): in 1946-1949 the badge arms lost the crown and a flag with the Kossuth arms was used, again in 1956-1957; communist arms with a red star were added in 1949. FOTW (hu.html): the tricolour was used 1919-1949 and the Rakosi arms 1949-1956. FOTW (hu_hist) and Wikipedia (Second Hungarian Republic) list the Republic of Hungary from 1 February 1946 to 20 August 1949 and describe no flag; Wikipedia's infobox shows the Hungarian tricolour-type flag without describing it.
era-1946.open: Attested only as the red-white-green tricolour through 1946-49. Whether it carried the Kossuth arms (Wikipedia) or was plain (the page's drawing) is not settled: FOTW is silent and the infobox is not a description. Treat the plain drawing as unconfirmed.

era-1920.says: FOTW says the tricolour was in use again in 1919–1949 and, quoting the DK book (Phil Nelson, 1999), that until 1945 the royal crown appeared in the centre of the national flag. Wikipedia says the tricolour appears with minor arms in 1920–1944/45, hedging («it seems») and noting a version without arms was also used.
era-1920.open: Both sources are hedged or second-hand on whether the arms were on the flag; the page's description of the shield is not confirmed.

era-1919.says: FOTW (Molnár, 2001) gives 21 March–31 July 1919 for the Hungarian Soviet Republic's red flag. Wikipedia says it used a solid red banner for about four and a half months.
era-1919.open: Neither source says the republic rejected the tricolour as a bourgeois relic, as this page does.

era-1918.says: FOTW says the tricolour was in use in 1867–1919. Wikipedia captions the Károlyi-era flag of the short-lived Hungarian People's Republic in 1918–1919.
era-1918.open: The page's claim that this was the first time the tricolour was stripped of royal emblems «in Hungary's history» was not checked; Wikipedia says the tricolour was used without arms at other times.

era-1867.says: FOTW says the tricolour was in use in 1867–1919 and that after 1848 it represented the Hungarian state within the Empire (Heimer, 2000). Wikipedia says that after the Compromise of 1867 the tricolour became official again, with the Kossuth minor arms as a badge, until 1918.
era-1867.open: The caption describes a crest; the sources describe the tricolour with a badge.

era-1699.says: Wikipedia says red-white-green colours were visible at Leopold II's coronation in 1790, were formally described in 1806, and were mandated by Act XXI of 1848. FOTW records the official colours of the Kingdom as red, white and green in 1806 and Law XXI of 1848 restoring the national colour and arms; it says Hungary was under Austrian occupation from 1849 to 1867.
era-1699.open: This supports the tricolour from 1790 or 1806 to 1867, not for 1699–1790. Both sources give earlier dates that conflict (1608, with Wikipedia saying there is no evidence).

era-1000.says: Wikipedia: the Árpád stripes are the flag of the royal House of Árpád and became increasingly common in the later medieval period; silk cords in red, white and green appear on document seals from the 15th century. FOTW: the red, white and green colours are said to date to the 9th century and to have been first used in 1608 under Matthias II (a DK book quoted by a contributor), and does not mention the Árpád stripes. Wikipedia (Arpad stripes): constant use in Hungarian heraldry since the early 13th century, the first depiction on a 1202 seal of King Emeric; a debated striped banner on coins of Stephen I is marked citation needed; a striped banner appears in the Chronicon Pictum (c.1360); after the Middle Ages the stripes survived only in heraldry. FOTW (hu_hist) lists a red-white Arpad Dynasty flag in a modern church flag collection.
era-1000.open: The 1202 seal gives a dated first heraldic depiction; no source read shows the stripes as the kingdom's flag between 1000 and 1200, and FOTW's list is a modern collection, not medieval evidence. The earlier 15th-century seal-cord statement from Wikipedia's flag article remains separate.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia (Government of National Unity): 16 October 1944 to 7 May 1945; the infobox shows the Hungarian tricolour as the national flag and the Arrow Cross flag as the party flag. Wikipedia (Flag of Hungary): the tricolour carried the minor arms 1920 to 1944-45, a version without arms also being used. FOTW (hu_hist) names Szalasi as head of state from 16 October 1944 and describes no Arrow Cross flag.
era-1944.open: The sources support a tricolour as the state flag and a separate Arrow Cross party flag; a stylized cross as the government's flag is not supported. The page text was corrected and the drawing/caption no longer match the sources.

era-1541.says: Wikipedia (Eyalet of Budin): 1541-1686 (sanjak list referring to before 1699); the infobox shows a map, not a flag, and the page mentions no flag or banner. FOTW (hu_hist) does not mention Ottoman Buda; Wikipedia (Flag of Hungary) and FOTW (hu.html) give Ottoman Hungary only as a sidebar link or not at all.
era-1541.open: No flag of Ottoman Buda is described in any source read; the 'standard Ottoman provincial banner' is unsupported. The end date is 1686 in the infobox and 1699 on this page.

era-1526.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Hungary 1526-1867): after Mohacs (29 August 1526) the country was ruled by two crowned kings, John I and Ferdinand I, and the Treaty of Nagyvarad was 24 February 1538; the infobox shows arms only. Wikipedia (Arpad stripes): the stripes appear in seals of later rulers including Janos Szapolyai. FOTW (hu_hist) has no flags or dates for either claimant.
era-1526.open: Szapolyai's seal use of the stripes is mentioned but no source describes a flag used by both rivals; the page's claim that both claimed the same striped flag is not established. Wikipedia Kingdom text read to 100,000 of 122,169 characters.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: infobox adoption 17 June 1944. Flags of the World (Iceland historical flags): the blue-white-red cross design was approved by royal decree on 19 June 1915 and adopted by law on 30 November 1918; in 1944 legislation dropped the 'ultramarine' specification and the blue became darker. The design itself therefore continued unchanged into the republic, with only the shade of blue altered.
era-1944.open: The page says nothing changed in 1944; Flags of the World says the blue was darkened by the 1944 law, so 'unchanged' holds for the design only. The two sources do not describe how the 1944 republic law treated the flag beyond the shade.

era-930.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: Iceland was granted sovereignty by Denmark in 1918 and the flag was adopted as the national flag; the state flag was first flown 1 December 1918. Flags of the World (historical flags): the king accepted the flag on 30 November 1918 and it was adopted by law that day; first hoisted as state ensign on 1 December 1918 when Iceland became a separate kingdom united with Denmark under one king; the 1915 decree had permitted land use and local waters only.
era-1918.open: The page's claim about merchant and international use is not in either source; Flags of the World dates the first state use to the same day as Wikipedia.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia: the Danish flag was required in Icelandic territorial waters until the decree of 19 June 1915 approved Iceland's flag; a blue-and-white flag was used unofficially from the late 19th century and first displayed publicly in 1897. Flags of the World (historical flags, J. O. Engene): the Danish flag was used by ships and in Iceland through the union; unofficial blue-and-white flags appeared in 1897; the 1915 decree approved the present design.
era-1814.open: The page's 'oldest continuously used national flag', the Greece comparison and 'first time a flag of its own flew' are not supported (Flags of the World says an unofficial 1897 flag was rejected as too like the Greek flag); the Dannebrog claim rests on a contributor note without dates.

era-1523.says: Wikipedia (Denmark-Norway): infobox flag is the Dannebrog (official since 1625); Iceland was a dependency, excluded from the 1814 Kiel cession, and a colony of the Kingdom of Denmark; the Dannebrog became the union's only official merchant flag after 1748, Norway having kept its own royal standard until then. Wikipedia (Iceland): the Danish flag was required in Icelandic waters until 1915. Flags of the World (historical flags): Iceland's arms (crowned stockfish) were part of the Danish arms, ships used the Danish flag, and Iceland's union with Norway and Denmark meant the Danish flag was used there.
era-1523.open: Neither source dates the Dannebrog in Iceland before the 17th century; the Wikipedia infobox date is 1625, and the pre-1748 Norwegian royal standard is not tied to Iceland. The page's governance claims are not covered.

era-1397.says: Wikipedia (Kalmar Union): infobox gives 1397-1523 and the lead lists Norway's maritime colonies 'then including Iceland'; a gallery captions 'the unofficial flag of the Kalmar Union as described by Erik of Pomerania' and a flag captured in 1427 shows the arms of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Pomerania. Flags of the World's Iceland pages do not mention the union banner.
era-1397.open: The three-crowns banner as a flag flown over Iceland is not described in any source read; the unofficial union flag is not described in the text read (first 100,000 of 134,275 characters); the Danish-led 1523 end is dated, not the flag.

era-1262.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Norway 872-1397): the infobox shows a banner captioned 'Likely royal banner used since the 13th century', and the text says 'Iceland, Faroe Islands and Greenland remained under Norwegian administration until 1814'; it does not mention the 1262-1264 Old Covenant or describe the banner's charge.
era-1262.open: The crowned lion with an axe is not described in the text read; the 1262 date of submission to the Norwegian crown and the dates of Norwegian rule over Iceland are not covered; Flags of the World's Iceland pages are silent.
