era-1561-1.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Courland): the state flag of the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia (1561-1795) was divided red over white, 1:2; the civil ensign had a red and white chequer square at the hoist; under Duke Jacob (1642-82) the colonial naval ensign was raspberry red with a crab, with a black-eagle variant, and red-with-white-eagle and white-with-black-eagle flags also existed. FOTW (Courland): the same three ducal flags from Dzirkalis 1936, a red-over-white flag as 'Pavillon de Curlande' on Bellin's 1756 chart, and eagle flags on 19th-century flag charts.
era-1561-1.open: The sources describe a red-over-white state flag and eagle and crab naval flags; none mentions a stag, so the page's dark red field with a stag is not supported. The 1561 and 1795 dates are Wikipedia's.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: the final Soviet Latvian flag was adopted in 1953 and includes blue wavy bands at the bottom; during Soviet rule the national flag was unusable and its display treated as a crime.
era-1953.open: Neither source mentions a star or white in the bands.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: the first Soviet Latvian flag was red with a gold hammer and sickle and 'LPSR' above them.
era-1944.open: The page's claim of a star is not in the source; the dates of use are not given.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia (Generalbezirk Lettland): the German civil district of 1941-1944 shows the flag of Nazi Germany in its infobox. Wikipedia (Flag of Latvia): the red-white-red flag was unusable 1940-41 and 1944-91, 'and briefly during occupation by Nazi Germany'. A Latvian article (lvportals.lv) says the red-white-red flag did not disappear during the German occupation and that Latvian Legion uniforms carried a patch in its colours.
era-1941.open: The German flag as the occupation authority's flag is shown by one Wikipedia infobox only; no source read says what the occupation administration permitted for Latvian civil use, and Wikipedia's wording on the Latvian flag during the occupation is ambiguous. FOTW's Latvia pages are silent on 1941-44.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia: the first Soviet Latvian flag was red with a gold hammer and sickle and 'LPSR' above them; Soviet rule 1940–41 made the national flag unusable.
era-1940.open: The sources read give no date of adoption in 1940.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: c. 1279 the Rhymed Chronicle of Livonia has Latgalian tribes from Cēsis under a 'red flag with a white stripe'; a design by Ansis Cīrulis was accepted in May 1917; the Constitutional Assembly affirmed the red-white-red flag on 15 June 1921. FOTW: Republic proclaimed 18 November 1918; the flag was used 1921–39.
era-1918.open: FOTW does not cover the chronicle or 1921 law; 'oldest flag in the world' was dropped as unsourced.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Russia): the white-blue-red tricolour was introduced by Peter the Great and adopted as a civil ensign in 1705; in 1858 Alexander II declared the black-yellow-white tricolour the national flag, and in 1896 Nicholas II replaced it with the white-blue-red tricolour. Wikipedia (Flag of Courland): the flag of the Courland Governorate (1795-1918) was a green-blue-white striped rectangle.
era-1795.open: Russian flag history is attested but is not tied to the governorates: the white-blue-red civil ensign was not the national flag from 1858 to 1896, and Wikipedia gives the Courland Governorate its own green-blue-white flag. No source read gives a flag for the Livland governorate, so 'the imperial tricolour over the two governorates' is not confirmed.

era-1721.says: Wikipedia (Swedish Livonia): Livonia was a Swedish dominion until 1721 (Treaty of Nystad), after the Capitulation of Estonia and Livonia in 1710. Wikipedia (Flag of Russia): the white-blue-red tricolour was adopted as a civil ensign of the Tsardom in 1705 and continued as the civil ensign of the Russian Empire.
era-1721.open: Which flag stood for Russian Livonia between 1721 and 1795 is not stated by any source read; the tricolour is attested only as a civil and naval ensign of Russia, not as a provincial flag, and the page's 'imperial tricolour' is not confirmed.

era-1621.says: Wikipedia (Swedish Livonia): Sweden took Riga in 1621, the Truce of Altmark of 1629 left it with Livonia, and the Treaty of Oliva of 1660 confirmed it until 1721; its infobox shows an 18th-century flag of Livonia rather than the Swedish flag. Wikipedia (Duchy of Courland and Semigallia) shows Courland as a separate vassal duchy through this period.
era-1621.open: No source read says the Swedish state flag flew over Riga or Livonia; the infobox shows a provincial flag instead. The Courland contrast is supported by the Courland articles, but the Swedish cross is not tied to Livonia by any page read.

era-1561.says: Wikipedia (Duchy of Livonia): a vassal state of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (1561-1629) and then of Poland-Lithuania, its infobox carrying a coat of arms and no flag. Wikipedia (Duchy of Courland and Semigallia): Courland was a separate vassal duchy from 1561 under its own dukes.
era-1561.open: No source read shows a joint Polish-Lithuanian banner over Livonia; Wikipedia's Duchy of Livonia has a coat of arms and no flag. Wikipedia gives the duchy to 1629 (Sweden took Riga in 1621), not 1621.

era-1201.says: Wikipedia (Livonian Order): a branch of the Teutonic Order 1237-1561; the master's seal shows the Teutonic Knights' arms (flagged 'citation needed'). Wikipedia (Teutonic Order): attire a white mantle with a black cross, and its flag list pairs Terra Mariana with the State of the Teutonic Order flag. FOTW (Teutonic Order): flag a black Scandinavian cross on white, citing Smith 1975 and the Banderia Prutenorum. FOTW (Latvia history) quotes the Livonian Rhymed Chronicle on a Latvian unit from Wenden that carried a red banner crossed by white in 1279, which is not an Order banner.
era-1201.open: These sources attest the Teutonic Order's black cross on white, not a banner specific to the Livonian Order or to Terra Mariana; the link is inferred from the Order's being a branch. The page's 1201 start predates the Order (1237) and falls in the Brothers of the Sword period, whose banner is not described here; the page's 'plain cross' is therefore unconfirmed for the Livonian state.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: the flag was introduced into the Constitution on 7 December 1943 (first raised 21 November 1943 at Bechamoun), three horizontal stripes with a double-width white stripe and a cedar occupying one third of it. Flags of the World: adopted 07 Dec 1943; the 1926 constitution's blue-white-red with cedar article was changed on 7 December 1943 to red, white and red horizontal stripes with a green cedar.
era-1943.open: 'Unchanged since 1943' is not exact: Wikipedia says the cedar was usually drawn with a brown trunk until a 21 September 1990 amendment made the whole tree green. FOTW says the cedar was officially green from the start; the two differ on that.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia: demonstrators raised a cedar-bearing tricolour at Baabda on 22 March 1920; it captions the State of Greater Lebanon flag as used 1920-1943 and quotes the constitution of 23 May 1926 (blue, white, red vertical bands, cedar on the white). FOTW (citing Heimer): the French tricolour with a cedar in the middle was used under the French mandate; it quotes the same 23 May 1926 article.
era-1920.open: Neither page describes the plain French tricolour as the mandatory power's own flag in Lebanon, or the two flying side by side.

era-1861.says: Flags of the World (Ollé, 2003, on the Ottoman page): 'The flag of the Mutaserif (governor) and Mutasaferiat (land under his rule) was the Ottoman state flag', a red cloth with a white crescent and star (Nehmé 1995). Wikipedia dates the Mutasarrifate 9 June 1861 to September 1918 and records a 1907 proposal to add a cedar branch to the Ottoman flag and a white cedar flag at Baabda from 2 November 1918; FOTW's cedar page says the Maronite cedar flag had its first attested use in October 1848 and was in use in 1918-1919.
era-1861.open: The mutasarrifate's flag is stated only by Flags of the World (Ollé); Wikipedia implies the Ottoman flag by the 1907 proposal but does not say it. The crescent-and-star design for 1861-1918 is not tied to a decree in the sources read.

era-1517.says: Flags of the World lists the Ottoman flag for 1516-1918 as a red cloth with a white crescent and star (Nehmé 1995) and, on its Lebanon history page, separate flags of local houses: the Maanid emirate (c. 1119-c. 1697), the Chehab emirate (c. 1697-1842, blue with a white crescent), Jumblattians, Nakadites, and others. Wikipedia and FOTW date Maronite use of a white cedar flag to 1848 and the 17th/18th century. Wikipedia's article on the Ottoman flag  puts the crescent-and-star as late 18th-century and the five-pointed star flag as 1844.
era-1517.open: The page's claim that the red crescent-and-star flag was the empire-wide flag from 1517 is not supported: the Ottoman flag article says the star and crescent came into use in the second half of the 18th century and was officially adopted in 1844. Local emirs' flags are documented only on FOTW's page.

era-1289.says: Flags of the World (Nehmé 1995): the Mamluk flag in Lebanon was 'a cloth embroidered with golden threads' (tagged plain yellow), listed 1282-1516. Wikipedia (Mamluk Sultanate): the sultans followed the Ayyubids in using yellow as the colour associated with the sultan, on sultanic banners; sultans and emirs also had personal blazons (about forty-five symbols such as a cup, sword or animal) that stayed on their banners; Tripoli fell to the Mamluks in 1289 and Ottoman conquest followed in 1517.
era-1289.open: A gold field is stated by both publishers; the simplified eagle blazon on the card is not, since blazons were personal and the sources name no eagle. The card is a reconstruction, not a surviving banner.

era-1109.says: Wikipedia (County of Tripoli, 1102-1289): its infobox flag is captioned as a banner of arms of the House of Toulouse-Tripoli, derived from the arms, and a separate image gives the 'attributed arms'; the article mentions no Jerusalem cross for the county. Flags of the World's Lebanon history page lists only the Kingdom of Jerusalem (1099-1291) as a crusader entry and links to a general page for it.
era-1109.open: The card's Jerusalem-cross banner is not supported: the one source naming a county banner points to Toulouse-Tripoli arms, whose design the article text does not describe. Not read: any source on the Toulouse cross banner or on Tripoli's crusader-era flags.

era-1109-1.says: Flags of the World's Lebanon history page lists a 'Phoenician (?)' flag, blue for the sea with red added later (Nehmé 1995), a 'Tanukh (?)' flag supposed to date from the 4th century, and the Umayyad (660-750) and Abbasid (750-1258) caliphates; its Phoenician page questions how old the Phoenician and Tanukh flags are and how reliable their existence is. Wikipedia describes no flag for antiquity and mentions the cedar only as a tree.
era-1109-1.open: The card's 'no flag documented' is consistent with FOTW's own doubts, but FOTW does list the questioned Phoenician and Tanukh flags; no source states that the cedar was a defining symbol in antiquity (FOTW's Phoenician page does not mention cedars).

era-1966.says: Wikipedia: the flag adopted on 4 October 2006, the 40th anniversary of independence, is a horizontal blue, white and green tricolour with a black mokorotlo (Basotho hat) in the centre; blue is the sky or rain, white peace, green prosperity; it replaced the military-emblem flag. FOTW (Lesotho): parliament voted 84 to 18 in September 2006 for the new flag, with the hat and the colours of peace, rain and prosperity; the black symbolises Africa; the flag was introduced at midnight on 3 October 2006. FOTW (previous flags): the 1966 independence flag was replaced on 17 or 20 January 1987 by a flag with a shield and spears, which lasted until 2006.
era-1966.open: The black hat flag dates from 2006, not 1966: Lesotho had a different flag from 1966 to 1987 and from 1987 to 2006, so the era title 1966-present covers three flags. Wikipedia and FOTW give the meaning of blue as the sky or rain and the black as Africa (FOTW).

era-1824.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — Basotho Kingdom under Moshoeshoe I, no flag documented».
era-1824.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1824-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — scattered Sotho-Tswana clans before unification, no flag survives».
era-1824-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-san.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — San hunter-gatherer society, no flag of any kind, ever».
era-san.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1868.says: Wikipedia: the Union Jack served as the flag of Basutoland from 1884 to 1966, with an unofficial Basutoland flag, a Resident Commissioner's flag and a coat of arms used 1951-1966. FOTW (Basutoland flags): Basutoland 'did not have a distinctive colonial flag of its own and flew only the Union Jack as a national flag' until independence in October 1966; the Resident Commissioner's flag was a Union Jack with the 1951 arms on a white roundel; Basutoland's protection was requested by Moshoeshoe in 1868, and the territory returned to the Crown in 1884; a contributor suggests the arms in a white circle may have been used unofficially on a blue ensign after 1951.
era-1868.open: Both sources contradict the page's Blue Ensign with a Basutoland badge for the colonial period (only an unofficial ensign after 1951 is suggested); the 1868 start is the year protection was requested, not the start of a flag.

era-2003.says: Wikipedia: the April 1961 law specifies eleven alternating red and white stripes and a blue canton with a white star; the Deshield Commission (1974-1978) recommended no changes. Flags of the World (last modified 2026) describes the current flag as eleven red and white stripes with a blue canton bearing a white five-pointed star under the Flag Law of 11 April 1961, introduced on 26 July 1847.
era-2003.open: Neither source discusses the postwar years; that the flag was unchanged since 2003 rests on both describing the same design as the present flag. The meaning of the stripes as eleven signatories is a FOTW contributor's.

era-1000.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — fragmented pre-colonial era, no unifying flag».
era-1000.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1980.says: Wikipedia: Deshield Commission reported 24 January 1978 that no flag changes were recommended. Flags of the World's governmental-flags page carries a contributor note that German television in 2003 showed Charles Taylor with the presidential flag and the national flag, and its military-flags page mentions the 1997 disbanding of the armed forces and the ECOMOG force.
era-1980.open: No source states what the national flag was in 1980-2003 beyond that one 2003 report, and neither says no faction replaced it. The 1961 law stayed the flag law, but the silence of the sources is not evidence of no change.

era-1847.says: Wikipedia: 26 July 1847 independence declared; flag adopted and unfurled in Monrovia 24 August 1847; seven US-born women stitched it; eleven stripes for the signers of the Declaration of Independence; star for the first independent African republic. FOTW: 16 June 1847 Annex established six red and five white stripes, blue canton and white star; Susanna Waring-Lewis chaired the committee; eleven stripes for signers (or convention delegates).
era-1847.open: Adoption date differs (16 June vs 24 August 1847); 'modelled deliberately on the US flag' is not stated by either source.

era-1839.says: Wikipedia: 9 April 1827 resolution set a US-pattern flag with a white cross in place of the stars; US flag used by the Commonwealth's first government until 26 April 1845. Flags of the World (page on the 1827-1847 flag, citing Smith 1980): Liberia had had a flag since 1827, the US flag with a white cross for the stars, which was altered to eleven stripes and a single white star on 26 July 1847; a Liberian ship flying it was seized by the British in 1845.
era-1839.open: The two sources differ: FOTW has the cross flag in use through 1847, Wikipedia has the Commonwealth's government using the US flag until April 1845. Neither describes a Commonwealth flag as such for 1839-1847, so the page's 'through the entire period' is only supported by FOTW's citation of Smith.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia: the 9 April 1827 resolution created the first colonial flag (US pattern, white cross in the canton); African Americans began arriving in 1822. Flags of the World (page on the 1827-1847 flag) quotes the resolution of the American Colonization Society board of 9 April 1827: a flag was requested for the colony at Liberia, to be as like the US flag as possible yet distinct, 'omitting the stars and substituting therefore a white cross in the center of the azure field'; its main page says the colony's flag had a cross in the upper-left corner.
era-1822.open: That the US flag itself flew at Cape Mesurado from 1822 until 1827 is not stated by either source. The FOTW quote is a contributor's transcription of part of the resolution, with no addressee.

era-2011.says: Wikipedia: the 1951 red-black-green flag with a white crescent and star was readopted by the National Transitional Council (infobox 23 August 2011, text 3 August 2011) after the fall of Gaddafi. FOTW (Libya): the 1951-1969 flag was used by most flag-bearing protesters as an opposition symbol from the uprising of February 2011, and the NTC's Constitutional Declaration of August 2011 defines the flag.
era-2011.open: Wikipedia's two dates for the readoption conflict (23 August and 3 August 2011); FOTW calls the introduction date uncertain and says no earlier decree regulated its use. The page's claim that it was used from 'the earliest days' is supported by FOTW's reports from 21 February 2011.

era-630bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no flag in the modern sense existed in the ancient Mediterranean».
era-630bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1977.says: Wikipedia: plain green flag adopted 19 November 1977, used until 2011, described as Gaddafi's symbol for his political philosophy. FOTW 'Libya, 1977-2011': the flag was adopted in 1977 after Libya left the Federation of Arab Republics; green is the national colour and a symbol of devotion to Islam; the page also reports unconfirmed variants (a naval ensign with crossed anchors, a late takbir version).
era-1977.open: Neither source mentions the Green Book for the flag, and neither says it was the only national flag without a design. FOTW gives only the year 1977, and the end in 2011 is shown by its 1977-2011 heading.

era-1969.says: Wikipedia: the Libyan Arab Republic used the red, white and black Arab Liberation Flag from the 1969 coup until 1972, and the Federation of Arab Republics flag with a golden hawk from 1972 to 1977. FOTW: a red-white-black horizontal tricolour (1:2) adopted on 7 November 1969, with green stars to be added for any union; from 1972 the Federation's red-white-black flag with the hawk of Quraish in gold, which Libya gave up in 1977.
era-1969.open: The two sources do not explain the pan-Arab symbolism of the 1977-era change beyond the Federation; Wikipedia also mentions a flag for a planned 1974 merger with Tunisia that FOTW does not cover. Wikipedia gives a 3:2 ratio for the Federation flag where FOTW does not give one.

era-1951.says: Wikipedia: flag officially adopted 24 Dec 1951 at independence, constitution Article 7 of 7 Oct 1951; attributed to Shennib; star and crescent linked to the Senussi flag. FOTW: Kingdom flag 1951-1969 from independence, and the NTC used it as its symbol from 27 Feb 2011.
era-1951.open: Only the adoption date and 2011 revival are shared by both; the designer attribution is flagged by Wikipedia as needing a citation; first UN-created state claim not covered.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: Union Flag in the British-administered areas and the French flag in Fezzan-Ghadames, 1947-1951, with the Emirate of Cyrenaica's black flag with white crescent and star from 1949; the British Military Administration article shows the UK flag in its infobox. FOTW (Cyrenaica): after the Italian defeat of 1943 and the British-French occupation, Italy gave up Libya by the Treaty of Paris (10 February 1947); a black flag with a white crescent and star, the Senussi flag, was recognised for Cyrenaica under British administration after 1945. FOTW (Fezzan): a red crescent flag reported for French-run Fezzan is shown to be spurious.
era-1943.open: No second source states the French flag over Fezzan-Ghadames; FOTW instead shows that a red crescent flag attributed to it was a false image, and Wikipedia's Italian Libya infobox still carries a Fezzan-Ghadames flag file. No source read describes flags for Tripolitania before 1947 or for 1943-47 in general.

era-1911.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Libya): the colonies of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, merged as Italian Libya in 1934, used the flag of Italy, listed 1911 to 1947. Wikipedia (Italian Libya): the infobox for 1934-1943 shows the crowned Italian tricolour, with the arms of Savoy.
era-1911.open: Both are Wikipedia articles, and no second publisher or reference source was found for the Italian flag in Libya; FOTW's pages on Libya and Italy did not cover colonial flags. The sources do not say it was the sole official flag, and the Libyan resistance and the short-lived Tripolitanian republic of 1918-1923 are not covered.

era-900.says: Wikipedia (Ottoman Tripolitania): the vilayet existed 1864-1911 and its infobox shows an 18th-century maritime flag of the Regency of Tripoli. FOTW (Tripoli): in the Turkish period various flags were reported, including red with yellow or white crescents; a contributor states that the only official flag in Ottoman possessions was the Turkish red flag with crescent and star, private ships flying many red and red-green variants.
era-900.open: The red field with a white crescent and star is stated for Ottoman possessions generally by one FOTW contributor, and that flag's crescent-and-star form is dated only from the late 18th century; no source read gives flags for Tripolitania, Cyrenaica or Fezzan before 1864 or under the Karamanlis, and nothing supports the page's start date of c. 900.

era-1937.says: Wikipedia's text says the crown was added on 24 June 1937; its infobox gives 30 June 1982 for the current version. FOTW's history page (after Baert) says a yellow prince's bonnet was added in the blue stripe near the hoist on 24 June 1937 after the confusion with the Haitian flag at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, with the crown modified in 1957 and again in 1982, and its law page quotes Joseph Hoop's 1937 presentation of the flag.
era-1937.open: The crown's shape changed in 1957 and 1982, so 'unchanged since 1937' holds for the blue-over-red bicolour with a crown, not the crown itself. Design and swatch colours not checked against a specification.

era-1719.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — newly formed principality under Empire suzerainty».
era-1719.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-15bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — Roman province, then medieval lordships, no attested banner».
era-15bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1866.says: Wikipedia: blue and red livery colours date from Prince Joseph Wenzel I in 1764, blue and red replaced gold and red on the national flag in 1852, and the October 1921 constitution gave the blue-red banner official status before the crown was added in 1937. FOTW's history page agrees: blue and red have been national colours since 1852, in vertical or horizontal stripes, and the fundamental law of 5 October 1921 prescribed blue over red horizontally; it also says yellow over red is said to have been used until 1921.
era-1866.open: Both sources leave the orientation (vertical or horizontal) before 1921 unsettled, and FOTW's 'yellow over red until 1921' sits awkwardly with blue-red since 1852. The drawn horizontal blue-over-red is firm only for 1921-37.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia describes a flag of two horizontal gold and red bands (3:5) for 1719-1852, taken from the coat of arms. FOTW's history page says the flag was yellow over red until 1852 or 1921 (it says 'until 1921'), still used locally at festivities, and that blue and red became the national colours in 1852; it also notes Liechtenstein's German Confederation membership 1815-1866 on the main page.
era-1815.open: Both sources contradict the page's statement that no fixed flag existed; the drawing (an arms-like roundel on cream) is not a flag and needs redrawing as gold over red, with blue and red from 1852. The two sources differ on when the gold-red flag ended (1852 against 1921).

era-1990.says: Wikipedia says the Supreme Soviet readopted the tricolour on 18 November 1988, the Provisional Constitution of 11 March 1990 confirmed it, the 1992 constitution wrote it in without an aspect ratio, and Law IX-2331 of 8 July 2004 changed the ratio from 1:2 to 3:5 and adopted the historical state flag. FOTW adds 7 October 1988 on Gediminas Tower, 25 January 1989 standard and proportions, and the state flag law of 26 June 1991.
era-1990.open: FOTW's header gives 20 March 1989 as an adoption date; the two sources differ on the 1989 act.

era-1150.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — pre-heraldic era, no flag survives».
era-1150.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-100.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — known only through outside Roman-era sources».
era-100.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: 1945 SSR flag red with hammer and sickle and 'LIETUVOS TSR'; in 1953 changed to red with a white and green bar at the bottom. FOTW: 15 July 1953 red-white-green flag confirmed, used until 1988.
era-1944.open: Neither source mentions a star on the flag.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia says the Lithuanian national flag was prohibited and prosecuted under the Nazi German occupation of 1941-44. FOTW (history of the flag) says that when the Germans invaded the pre-war Lithuanian flag flew wherever possible, that the Germans were intolerant of Lithuanian aspirations but 'had no major objections' to using the inter-war flag for their own ends, and that Lithuanian troops conscripted by the Germans wore small yellow-green-red shields on their sleeves, unofficially. The Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija confirms Lithuania became the Lithuanian General District within the Reichskommissariat Ostland under Generalkommissar Renteln at Kaunas, with no word on flags.
era-1941.open: Wikipedia and FOTW disagree about whether the Lithuanian flag was banned or tolerated, and neither describes an occupation flag; the page's stylised occupation drawing is unsupported. A Lithuanian archive or museum source on flag orders in 1941-44 is needed.

era-1940.says: FOTW: Soviet occupation banned national symbols in June 1940; on 27 September 1940 the Presidium of the Lithuanian SSR replaced the tricolour with a red flag with a golden hammer and sickle. Wikipedia: Soviet occupation began in 1940 and a push by Smetona to change the flag was halted.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: a commission submitted a protocol for the yellow-green-red tricolour on 19 April 1918 and the Council accepted it; the 1922 constitution adopted the tricolour. FOTW: 19 April 1918 approval by the commission; December 1905 the red flag with a white knight was proposed by Basanavičius and rejected because red suggested revolution.
era-1918.open: Neither source says the tricolour was chosen because it lacked a heraldic precedent; that motive was dropped.

era-1569.says: Wikipedia: the Vytis red banner with a mounted knight was used at the 1410 Battle of Grunwald and was the Grand Duchy's flag until the late 18th century. FOTW: Guagnini in 1578 describes a red silk flag with a white mounted knight under the ducal crown.
era-1569.open: Wikipedia does not say the rider was white; the Polish Eagle contrast is not in either source.

era-1253.says: FOTW: a 1337 chronicle mentions a Lithuanian flag burned at Bajerburg without describing it; Długosz has Vytautas bring 40 regiments with red banners, 30 bearing a mounted knight, to Tannenberg; Guagnini (1578) gives a white knight on red. Wikipedia: Vytis used at Grunwald in 1410.
era-1253.open: The page's earlier claim of attestation from the 14th century is not in the sources; the first description of the knight is 1410.

era-1795.says: FOTW (history of the flag): from the 15th century until 1795, when the remnants of the Grand Duchy were absorbed by Russia, the white Vytis on red was the official Lithuanian state flag; Lithuania regained independence in 1918 after '200 plus years' of Russian occupation, and in 1918 Basanavičius proposed a return to the Vytis on red, set aside because red recalled Lenin's communism. Wikipedia: the Vytis was the Grand Duchy's flag until annexation by Russia, nothing on 1795-1904, and the 1905 Great Seimas favoured the tricolour over the Vytis. FOTW's other pages: Lithuania Minor's green-white-red flag known from the 17th century and Lithuanian-American association flags.
era-1795.open: No source read says which flag the Russian administration flew over the Lithuanian governorates (the Russian tricolour is the page's assertion) or describes bans; the claim that no Lithuanian flag existed for 123 years is not supported, since sources record the Lithuania Minor flag and 1905 proposals.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Luxembourg): the horizontal red-white-light-blue tricolour was fixed on 12 June 1845, defined in 1848, and regulated by the law of 27 July 1993 (a 1972 emblems law was amended). Flags of the World (Luxembourg): flag law of 23 June 1972 and a 1993 regulation fixing the shades and proportions. Wikipedia (German occupation of Luxembourg): a photo caption shows civilians in Wiltz 'flying the flag of Luxembourg' at the liberation by US forces (liberation of the capital 10 September 1944).
era-1944.open: No source describes a formal 'restoration' in 1944/45; the 1944 start rests on the liberation dates and the photo caption. The sources differ on the de jure date (1993) and the 1972 law, and proportions were not checked.

era-963.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — pre-heraldic era, no flag survives».
era-963.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-53bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — no unified banner; Roman provincial and Frankish rule, no independent Luxembourgish state».
era-53bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia (German occupation of Luxembourg, first 100,000 of 173,833 characters) says that from August 1940 Luxembourgers wore pin-badges in the national colours, which drew attacks from the Volksdeutsche Bewegung, and that German became the only official language on 6 August 1940. It mentions no German or Gau Moselland flag. Flags of the World's Luxembourg pages do not cover the occupation.
era-1940.open: The Reich flag flown over Luxembourg as stated on this page is not described in any source read; the remaining 73,833 characters of the Wikipedia article were not read, and the 1942 annexation into Gau Moselland is not dated there.

era-1890.says: Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg): the grand duchy passed to the House of Nassau-Weilburg in 1890, and its timeline marks 'Full independence' at 1890. Flags of the World: full independence in 1890 under Nassau-Weilburg after William III left no male heir. Wikipedia (Flag of Luxembourg): the tricolour was fixed on 12 June 1845 and defined in 1848, so it was already the flag in 1890; Flags of the World also dates the tricolour to 1845.
era-1890.open: The page's 'first full independence since 1443' and '450 years' are in no source read; no source describes the flag specifically in use 1890-1940.

era-1839.says: FOTW: 1839 agreement made the western part of Luxembourg Belgian, the eastern part stayed under the Dutch crown. WP and FOTW both give 12 June 1845 for fixing the horizontal red-white-blue tricolor, derived from the arms.
era-1839.open: Purpose of distinguishing from Belgian/Dutch flags is not stated; WP calls its origin claims uncited.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg): the 1815 Congress of Vienna made Luxembourg a Grand Duchy in personal union with the Netherlands. Wikipedia (Flag of Luxembourg): 'Luxembourg had no flag until 1830' (uncited), when patriots were urged to display the national colours during the Belgian Revolution. Flags of the World: flags in the arms colours first used around the 1830 revolt.
era-1815.open: The Wikipedia statement is uncited and the drawing on the page shows the later design; no source describes how the Grand Duchy was marked 1815-1830. The 1839 end of the era (partition) was not checked.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg) says the country became part of the departement of the Forets in 1795 and labels 1795-1815 'French rule'; Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) uses the Flag of France icon for the French First Republic (1795-1804) and First French Empire (1804-1815). Flags are not discussed in either text.
era-1795.open: Annexation is attested, but no source read states in text that the French tricolour was flown over Luxembourg; only navigation icons show it, and Flags of the World is silent.

era-1714.says: Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) places Luxembourg in the Austrian Netherlands (1714-1795) and illustrates it with an 'Austrian Low Countries Flag' icon; Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg) dates Habsburg rule to 1714-95. Neither describes a flag in text.
era-1714.open: Neither Wikipedia page nor Flags of the World says what flag, if any, flew over the Duchy of Luxembourg; the double-headed eagle on this page is not described by any source read.

era-1581.says: Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) places Luxembourg in the Spanish Netherlands (1581-1714) with a generic 'Flag of the Low Countries' icon; Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg) dates Spanish rule 1556-1714. Wikipedia's Spanish Netherlands article (read for Belgium) gives the Cross of Burgundy as that territory's flag.
era-1581.open: No source read ties the Cross of Burgundy to the Duchy of Luxembourg itself; the start year (Wikipedia gives 1556) differs from this page's 1581.

era-1443.says: Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) shows a 'Banner of the Burgundian Cross of Burgundy' file as the Burgundian entry for 1443-1482; Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg) says the country passed to the Habsburgs in 1477 after brief Burgundian rule and lists the duchy 1352-1482. Flags of the World (Belgium plate) says the Cross of Burgundy was adopted by most Low Countries provinces in the 15th century.
era-1443.open: No source states in text that the Cross of Burgundy flew over Luxembourg specifically; the Burgundian period ends in 1482 or 1477 in Wikipedia, not 1581, and 1443 is the Burgundian conquest date used by Wikipedia's infobox.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia: Kutlesh flag with the Vergina Sun adopted 11 August 1992; Greece objected, imposed a blockade from February 1994 and sought trademark protection in 1995; current flag adopted 5 October 1995. FOTW: August 1992 flag of 16 rays, a 1992 competition of over 100 designs, current flag adopted 5 October 1995.
era-1992.open: Neither source gives the 30% GDP figure.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: ASNOM proclaimed the state on 2 August 1944; the first flag was a gold-edged red star on red, December 1944; an amended version adopted 31 December 1946 stayed in use until 1992. FOTW (Flag of Socialist Macedonia): red flag with a yellow-outlined star in the canton, adopted 31 December 1946 and superseded by the Vergina sun flag in 1992; the 1963 constitution text describes a red star with a gold edge, the star's centre at the intersection of the diagonals of the top hoist quarter; earlier variants were used from 1944 (photos of ASNOM); FOTW's contributors add that the red field was chosen in memory of the Ilinden uprising and Kruševo Republic.
era-1944.open: The Ilinden link is a statement by one FOTW contributor (Todorović), not a document; the page's 'only republic flag that skipped the pan-Slavic tricolor' is in neither source and is not true of the other republics' red flags with stars.

era-13.says: FOTW (Ilinden Uprising and the Republic of Kruševo): in August 1903 a plain red flag was hoisted in liberated Kruševo at the initiative of Nikola Karev, a socialist activist and leader of the provisional administration. Wikipedia (Ilinden Uprising): after the victory the insurgents raised the IMARO flag, with a cross on one side and the slogan 'Freedom or Death', and flew Bulgarian flags; its Kruševo Republic and Nikola Karev articles say IMRO insurgents flew Bulgarian flags and do not mention a red flag.
era-13.open: The two publishers disagree: FOTW names a plain red flag, Wikipedia an IMARO flag and Bulgarian flags. Neither names a primary source for the red flag.

era-1941.says: FOTW (Macedonia during the Second World War, Z. Heimer 1995): Macedonia was annexed in 1941 by Bulgaria and the Bulgarian flag was used there. Wikipedia's Flag of North Macedonia and its article on Bulgarian rule of Macedonia (1941-44) say nothing on flags.
era-1941.open: The Bulgarian tricolor over the region rests on one line in one FOTW page; no Wikipedia or reference source read mentions it, and 'no regional flag was created' is not covered.

era-1912.says: Neither Wikipedia's Flag of North Macedonia, Vardar Banovina, Vardar Macedonia and Kingdom of Yugoslavia articles nor FOTW's Macedonian pages (mk, mk_hist, mk_wwii, mk_1903, yu_fy-mk) give flags for Vardar Macedonia in 1912-1941.
era-1912.open: Which flags flew in the region (Serbian tricolor 1912-18, Yugoslav flag after) is an inference from the ruling states' flags, not stated for Macedonia; whether the Vardar Banovina had a flag is not covered. Next: FOTW's Kingdom of Serbia and Yugoslavia 1918-41 pages and a source on administration of the region.

era-1392.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Ottoman Empire): pre-modern Ottoman armies used horse-tail standards (tugh) rather than flags; the crescent and star came into use in the second half of the 18th century (1793 decree for naval ships: red with white star and crescent) and a version with a five-pointed star was adopted as the national flag in 1844. FOTW: the 1793 date for the red flag with white crescent and star is reported by one author without evidence.
era-1392.open: Neither source speaks of Macedonia or the vilayets; the red crescent-and-star flag cannot be carried back to 1392, and 'vilayets had none of their own' is not covered.

era-1346.says: Wikipedia (Serbian Empire): Dušan was crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks at Skopje on 16 April 1346 and the empire's capital was Skopje; the article has no flag text. Neither Wikipedia's Flag of North Macedonia nor FOTW's mk.html mentions an eagle banner or a portolan chart.
era-1346.open: The red eagle on gold from a French portolan chart is not found in any source read; only the polity, capital and 1346 date are confirmed. Sought: FOTW's Serbian history pages (not found among rs.html links) and a Bibliothèque nationale catalogue entry.

era-1958.says: Wikipedia: the design was chosen by a technical commission on 15 October 1958 and officially adopted on 21 October 1958, a week after the Malagasy Republic was proclaimed; it describes a white vertical band at the hoist and red over green horizontal bands. FOTW's colonial page says Madagascar adopted a flag on 16 October 1958 similar to the current one, and FOTW's Madagascar page says the coat of arms was adopted on 24 December 1959 and the flag with the arms came later (possibly 1960).
era-1958.open: The sources give 21 October (Wikipedia) and 16 October (FOTW) for the 1958 adoption and FOTW's own Madagascar page has a 1959-60 flag with the arms; the page's account of the colours is contradicted: Wikipedia says the colours originally had no meaning and were explained in 1958 as white purity, red sovereignty, green hope, and FOTW notes that sources disagree on the green (Hova, not coastal peoples).

era-1896.says: FOTW's protectorate page: the French protectorate ended on 29 September 1896 when General Galliéni had the royal eagle on the Queen's palace taken down and replaced by the French national flag, saluted with 21 guns (La Gazette de la Grande Ile, 2005). FOTW's French colonial page says the Tricolore was the rule in French colonies and that Madagascar adopted its own flag only on 16 October 1958.
era-1896.open: Only FOTW (one publisher, in two pages) describes the 1896 hoisting and the colonial flag rule; Wikipedia's flag article does not cover the colonial period. No source read shows a Madagascar badge or governor's flag, so the page's 'colonial badge' is unsupported. A second publisher or a French/Malagasy reference on the 1896 flag-raising was not found. FOTW notes three flag patterns in white, blue and red used in the 1947 revolt.

era-1810.says: Wikipedia: in 1810 Radama adopted a white-and-red bicolour combining his father's two standards, and rulers put their name in red lettering on a white or white-and-red flag. FOTW (citing DK, 1997): the Merina Kingdom's flags were all red and white, with no dates or designs.
era-1810.open: Neither source describes a red disc with a white star or a red border; that emblem is the page's own reconstruction. FOTW gives no dates.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: adopted 6 July 1964 at independence, a black, red and green triband with a red rising sun of 31 rays on the black band; changed in 2010 (white sun, red-black-green) and restored on 28 May 2012. Flags of the World: the Protected Flag, Emblems and Names Act says the flag was 'adopted at independence on 06 July 1964'; the 2010 change and the re-adoption signed 28 May 2012; black for the people of Africa, rising sun for the dawn of hope and freedom, red for the blood of martyrs, green for the nature of Malawi.
era-1964.open: A 1999 article cited by FOTW dates the colours to July 1961 (the party's colours); the flag was off the national scene 2010-2012, so 'unchanged since 1964' is not exact. The page's phrase about the sun echoing Pan-African suns is not in either source.

era-1953.says: Flags of the World (Nyasaland Protectorate page): the Nyasaland Blue Ensign with its own badge 'was used until 23 October 1953, when the territory joined the Federation', and the Governor used a Union Flag with the arms on a roundel during 1953-1963. Its Federation page: the Federal flag was a Blue Ensign with the Federation shield (arms granted 22 July 1954), the Union Flag stayed official beside it, and no territorial flag for Nyasaland is listed. Wikipedia: Nyasaland joined the Federation from 1953 to 1963; the Federation flag is dated 1953-1963 and the Nyasaland flag 1925-1964 in captions.
era-1953.open: Neither publisher says Nyasaland's own Blue Ensign was replaced by the Federal one, only that the badge ensign is dated to 23 October 1953; whether the Federal Blue Ensign served as Nyasaland's flag is not stated.

era-1891.says: Flags of the World: the British Central Africa Protectorate flag was a Blue Ensign with a badge of a branched tree with red fruits; the Nyasaland Protectorate (renamed 6 July 1907) used a Blue Ensign with a badge of a leopard before a rising sun (arms granted 11 May 1914), on a white disc until 1919 and without it afterwards (Admiralty Flag Book 1925), until 23 October 1953; protectorate declared 15 May 1891, renamed British Central Africa in 1893. Wikipedia shows flags and arms for British Central Africa (1893-1907) and Nyasaland (1925-1964) with captions that give dates only and no description.
era-1891.open: Only Flags of the World describes the badges; Wikipedia's articles do not, so the Blue Ensign with a badge is a one-publisher claim. The card's single 'Nyasaland badge' fits 1914-1953 only: the earlier protectorate had a different badge (a tree), and no flag is described for 1891-1893.

era-1957.says: Wikipedia: Federation of Malaya flag, 11 red and white stripes with a blue canton, yellow crescent and 11-point star; approved 19 May 1950, first raised 26 May 1950, raised at Merdeka Square on 31 August 1957, 14 stripes and 14 points from 16 September 1963. Flags of the World (Federation of Malaya 1950-1963): eleven stripes and an 11-pointed star on a blue canton, approved by King George VI on 19 May 1950 and first raised on 26 May 1950, increased to 14 in 1963; FOTW's 1949 proposals page quotes Evans (1953) that the eleven stripes and points indicate the eleven states of the Federation.
era-1957.open: The 31 August 1957 raising is stated by Wikipedia and a FOTW reader comment, not by FOTW's Federation page; FOTW dates the Legislative Council approval to 19 April 1950.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: the Federated Malay States tiger flag (1896-1946) was used by the Malayan Union (1946-1948) and Federation of Malaya (1948-1950), and Crown Colony flags are dated for Singapore, Penang and Malacca. Flags of the World: the Malayan Union was founded in 1946 and renamed the Federation in 1948 with a new flag in 1950; the Straits Settlements colony dissolved in 1946; Penang and Malacca colony flags (Blue Ensign with a badge on a white disc) existed from 1949 and 1951.
era-1946.open: No source read gives a plain Union Jack as the territory's ensign, which is what the card draws; the sources describe the tiger flag and badged Blue Ensigns. The tiger flag is dated 1896-1946 on Wikipedia and 1905-1950 on FOTW.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia (Japanese occupation of Malaya): the infobox captions the Japanese flag as the flag of Japanese-occupied Malaya; the text read does not discuss flags. Flags of the World (Straits Settlements): the pre-war arrangement came to an end with the Japanese occupation. Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Malaysia nor FOTW's Malaysia page covers the occupation.
era-1942.open: The Japanese flag rests on one infobox caption; no second source says what flew over Malaya in 1942-1945 or whether any local flag was permitted.

era-1826.says: Wikipedia: Straits Settlements flag versions dated 1826-1868, 1868-1877, 1874-1904, 1904-1925 and 1925-1946; Federated Malay States tiger flag 1896-1946. Flags of the World (Straits Settlements): the three settlements were administered together after 1826 and became a Crown Colony in 1867; a Blue Ensign with a gold crown c.1868-c.1880, then a Blue Ensign with three crowns on a red lozenge, the white disc removed after 1925; the FMS flag is dated 1905-1950 and the Federated Malay States were headed by the Straits governor as High Commissioner.
era-1826.open: Neither source describes a plain Union flag as the collective ensign, which is what the card draws; the sultanates' own flags are not covered.

era-1826-1.says: Neither Wikipedia (Flag of Malaysia) nor FOTW (Malaysia, Melaka and Straits Settlements pages) covers the Malacca Sultanate or the successor sultanates' banners before the Federated Malay States; FOTW mentions only yellow as the Rulers' royal colour and a golden-yellow Undang of Naning flag.
era-1826-1.open: The plain red banner drawn on the card is not established by any source read; FOTW's yellow royal colour points the other way.

era-1965.says: Wikipedia: independence from the UK in 1965 removed the black-and-white striped hoist, giving the modern design (green rectangle on red with a white crescent), adopted 25 July 1965; Sultan's Standard 1965-1968, Presidential Standard from 1968. FOTW: current flag adopted 25 July 1965, hoist strip withdrawn in 1965, the Sultanate ended about three years after independence.
era-1965.open: FOTW cites Crampton for the current national and presidential flags being introduced officially on 26 July 1968, which conflicts with 1965; the sources read do not reconcile the dates.

era-1954.says: Wikipedia: the Sultanate was restored in 1954 but the flag was not changed back; a Sultan's Standard with a star was used 1954-1965. FOTW's page on the protectorate period quotes Crampton (1990): the Sultan was reinstated in 1954 'and there were no changes to Maldivian flags', which continued until independence in 1965, and shows a Sultan's flag for 1954-1968. Both sources therefore agree on the restoration and on the flags being unchanged.
era-1954.open: The two publishers agree on the dates, but the design drawn here (red field, white-bordered black panel, crescent) is not what they describe: FOTW's sultanate page (Flaggenbuch) gives the state flag as red with a green panel and a crescent, plus a black-and-white hoist band, and Wikipedia's current 1953-1965 flag is the state flag with the crescent facing the hoist. The drawing needs checking before the row can be called attested.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: on becoming a republic in 1953 the national flag was dropped and the crescent on the state flag was reversed to face the hoist. FOTW (Crampton 1990): a republic 1953-1954, 'the crescent was turned to face the fly' and the service flag became the national flag; FOTW's sultanate page shows the earlier state flag with the crescent horns toward the hoist.
era-1953.open: The two publishers disagree on the crescent direction (Wikipedia: now facing the hoist; FOTW: now facing the fly) while agreeing the state/service flag became the national flag in 1953. Neither mentions the 'newly added crescent' or Arabic calligraphy that this page's caption describes.

era-1887.says: FOTW's sultanate page (Crampton 1990, Flaggenbuch): the flag was originally plain red, later given a band of black and white stripes in the hoist; the sultanate's national flag was red with that hoist band and a white crescent pointing to the hoist; the civil ensign had a green panel instead of the crescent, the state ensign a green panel with a star. Wikipedia: plain red flag with a striped hoist (Dhandimathi) to the early twentieth century, then a green rectangle with a crescent between 1926 and 1932; its gallery lists 1796-1903, 1903-1926 and 1926-1953 flags.
era-1887.open: Neither source mentions a black panel bearing the Shahada, a c.1903 date for it, or a sultan named on this page; Wikipedia's 1903-1926 flag image is listed without a description in the text read. The page's caption design is therefore not established by two publishers.

era-1573.says: Wikipedia and both FOTW pages (main, and the sultanate page quoting Crampton 1990) say the flag was originally plain red and was later given black and white stripes at the hoist; undated in both. Wikipedia's gallery dates a plain red flag 1117-1796 and a second flag 1796-1903.
era-1573.open: Two publishers support a plain red historic flag, but neither mentions the Portuguese interlude or a restoration after 1573; Wikipedia's 1796 change and the undated striped hoist mean the claim that plain red was unmodified until the twentieth century is not supported.

era-1558.says: Neither Wikipedia's flag article, nor FOTW's main and sultanate pages, nor Wikipedia's articles on the Maldives and the History of the Maldives (flag search) mention a flag for the Portuguese occupation of Malé.
era-1558.open: No source read gives a flag for the Portuguese occupation; the Cross of the Order of Christ shown is the page's stand-in. A Portuguese vexillological source for Goa-based ensigns of the period was not found in the pages read.

era-1153.says: Wikipedia (gallery caption 1117-1796) and FOTW (main page; sultanate page quoting Crampton 1990) say the earliest Maldivian flag was a plain red field.
era-1153.open: Two publishers support a plain red early flag, but neither gives 1153 (the year of the Islamic conversion on this page) or a specification; Wikipedia's 1117-1796 caption is the only dating and is not explained in the text read.

Wikipedia's Flag of Mali only links the Songhai Empire article; the Wikipedia articles on the Songhai Empire and on Askia Muhammad I, searched for flag, banner and standard, mention none. Flags of the World's Mali pages (main, Bamako, Djenne, Sikasso, Azawad) carry nothing on the empires.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: on 21 September 1964 (independence) the blue canton was replaced by a red fimbriation around the George Cross, which had been added to the flag on 28 December 1943. FOTW: on 21 September 1964 the flag and arms were changed, the blue canton removed and a red fimbriation added; the Republic followed on 13 December 1974.
era-1964.open: Neither source says the George Cross was newly moved to the canton in 1964; it was already on the flag from 1943. Wikipedia and FOTW differ on the Roger I date (1091 vs 1090), not relevant here.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: the George Cross was officially added to the flag on 28 December 1943 (an unofficial flag listed for 1943-1964); its Crown Colony of Malta infobox shows the 1943-1964 flag and a colonial badge for those years. FOTW: the George Cross first appeared on 28 December 1943 on a small blue canton, the red-and-white flag was approved as official on 9 November 1954, and the badge was a white-and-red shield; its Historical Flags page lists State Ensign and Governor's Flag 1943-1964, quoting Barraclough & Crampton (1981).
era-1943.open: The badge was a white-and-red shield with the George Cross in a blue canton, not a blue shield; the drawing's field is a Union Jack with a small square rather than a Blue Ensign. The drawn details need checking against the badge.

era-1814.says: FOTW's Historical Flags page lists State Ensigns 1875-c.1898, c.1898-1923 and 1923-1943, and quotes the Flaggenbuch 1939 as showing red and blue colonial ensigns with a badge of a shield per pale argent and gules (vertically white and red) with a yellow relief border, on a white circle that disappears on the blue ensign; it says various white-and-red badges, with and without the Maltese Cross, were used after the British arrival. Wikipedia lists historical flags for the 19th century, 1875-1898, 1898-1923 and 1923-1943 without designs, and gives the Crown Colony as 1813-1964.
era-1814.open: A colonial Blue Ensign with a white-and-red shield badge is supported for the late 19th and early 20th centuries; the plain white disc drawn here and the 1814 start (Wikipedia has 1813) are not. The drawing shows a Union Jack with a plain disc.

era-1800.says: Wikipedia's Malta Protectorate article (1800-1813) shows the Union Jack as its infobox flag; neither Wikipedia's Flag of Malta nor FOTW's Malta pages describe a flag for 1800-1814 in their text.
era-1800.open: The infobox image is the only evidence; the page's statement that no distinct Maltese symbol existed in this period, and the 1814 end (Wikipedia has 1813), are not covered.

era-1798.says: Wikipedia: a white and red standard was reportedly used by Maltese insurgents in September 1798; its French occupation of Malta (1798-1800) article shows the French flag as its infobox flag and the Order's flag as predecessor. FOTW's Malta pages do not mention the French period.
era-1798.open: No text in the sources read says a French tricolour was flown over Malta; the infobox image is the only support.

era-1530.says: Wikipedia says the Knights' flag, a white cross on a red field, is a more likely source of Malta's colours than the Roger I legend. FOTW's Order of Malta pages give the Order's flag as red with a white (Maltese) cross, seen at buildings in Valletta tied to the Knights, and list the Order's historical ensigns flown in Grand Master Rohan's time (1775-97), citing Strickland's vexillological paper.
era-1530.open: Neither source gives 1530 or 1798 as dates; FOTW's page notes naval and signal variants (a red flamma, pennants and a naval jack) that this drawing does not show.

era-1986.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted at the start of self-government on 1 May 1979 (designer Emlain Kabua): blue field, two diagonal orange and white stripes, a white star in the upper hoist with 24 points for the electoral districts, four long points for Majuro, Jaluit, Wotje and Ebeye; the diagonal represents the equator and the stripes the Ratak (sunrise) and Ralik (sunset) chains. FOTW: adopted 1 May 1979 (DK Pocket Book), Bill 4 of 12 June 1979 approved 22 June 1979 describing blue with two contiguous trapezoidal bars from the lower left, orange above white, and a white 24-point star; the four longer points are Majuro, Ebeye, Jaluit and Wotje; the blue stands for the Pacific.
era-1986.open: The design and its meanings are attested by both. The page begins the flag in 1986, but both sources date it to 1979; 1986 (end of US administration, 21 October 1986 per Wikipedia's Trust Territory article) is the polity's date, not the flag's. Wikipedia reads the 24 points as electoral districts, FOTW as municipal districts; the page's cross-and-Christianity reading of the long rays is FOTW's (star as a cross) but Wikipedia assigns them to four centres.

era-1947.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands): the UN flag was used 1947-1965 and the US flag (50 stars since 1960) throughout; the territory's own flag, light blue with six white stars (one for the Marshalls), was first flown 24 October 1962, approved by the Congress of Micronesia in July 1965 and official 19 August 1965, in use until the 1970s and early 1980s. FOTW (xp-pc): the same six-star flag first hoisted 24 October 1962, official 19 August 1965; before it the US and UN flags were used; it ceased to be used after the trust's dissolution (1980 per FOTW). Wikipedia (Flag of the Marshall Islands) captions: UN flag 1947-1965, TTPI flag 1965-1979. Wikipedia (Trust Territory): 1947-1994; US administration of the Marshalls ended 21 October 1986.
era-1947.open: The sources show the US and UN flags and, from 1965, a territorial flag; the page's single plain US flag drawing is a simplification, and the territorial flag is not drawn. End dates of the TTPI flag differ (1979 caption, 1980, early 1980s); the Marshalls' own flag was adopted 1 May 1979. Wikipedia Trust Territory text read to 100,000 of 160,783 characters.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia's image captions: a Japanese colonial rule flag 1914-1944 and a flag of the Governor of the South Seas Mandate 1920-1944. FOTW's Marshall page does not cover this period. Wikipedia (South Seas Mandate): the mandate is dated 1919-1947 (occupation 1919-1920, Class C League of Nations mandate 1920-1947); its infobox flag is the Flag of Japan and a separate governor's flag is shown without description; the Japanese Navy seized the German Marshall Islands by October 1914.
era-1914.open: Neither source describes the governor's flag, and no FOTW page on the Japanese mandate flags was found; the Hinomaru's use rests on Wikipedia's infobox only. The caption ends 1944 in the Marshall Islands flag article but the mandate runs to 1947 in its own article. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 165,312 characters.

era-1885.says: FOTW (mh-ralik): the Ralik Islands flag (3:5, German influenced) was adopted 20 November 1878 and suppressed in 1885; the Jaluit Company flag (3:5, based on the German national flag) was used from 1885 until the German colony was created on 1 April 1906. FOTW (de_colon): the Jaluit Gesellschaft flag was white with a black-white-red striped disc in the middle; the Imperial German flag was used in colonies other than Kiautschou. Wikipedia (Flag of the Marshall Islands) captions: Ralik flag 1878-1894, Jaluit Company 1885-1906, German New Guinea 1906-1914.
era-1885.open: Wikipedia and FOTW agree on the Jaluit Company flag's years but not on the Ralik end date (1885 vs 1894), and no source describes a 1906-14 German New Guinea flag design. The page's white-field eagle and black-white-red canton pattern matches neither description. The page text was corrected.

era-2017.says: Both sources give 2017, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 25 October 2017; Flags of the World dates it 1361.
era-2017.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1959.says: Wikipedia: the first flag was adopted on 1 April 1959, a green field with a golden star and crescent, unchanged at independence on 28 November 1960 and until the 2017 change; green, crescent and star are symbols of Islam. FOTW (Former Flag): adopted 1 April 1959 (decree cited from Carr 1961; Rabbow gives the constitution of 22 March 1959), an emerald-green flag 2:3 with a gold crescent and five-pointed star in the centre; green and gold are Pan-African colours and the crescent and star Islamic symbols; the yellow stands for the Sahara (Znamierowski).
era-1959.open: Neither source gives a 'no French influence' reasoning. Wikipedia puts the 2017 change at a first raising on 28 November 2017; FOTW describes the 2017 flag as the old one with red stripes added.

era-1904.says: Wikipedia: the French flag flew in Mauritania from the early 20th century until 1 April 1959, when the national flag was adopted; the territory had been an autonomous republic since 28 November 1958. FOTW (French Colonial Empire): in French West Africa, which included Mauritania, the common flag of all possessions was the French Tricolore, local flags being adopted only by some territories shortly before independence; Mauritania's own flag was written into the constitution on 22 March 1959 and adopted officially on 1 April 1959.
era-1904.open: The page's 1904 start (the creation of the territory) is not dated by either source, and both sources show the national flag replacing the Tricolore in 1959, before independence on 28 November 1960 rather than at the end of the era.

era-1040.says: Wikipedia (Almoravid dynasty): the Almoravids adopted the Abbasid black standard (the emissary of 1104 announced the adoption of the black Abbasid banners), the Lamtuna and Massufa tribes used black for their veils and war banners, and the Almohads adopted white against them. FOTW (Morocco historical flags): a contributor writes that the Almoravids (1062-1147) institutionalised white silk banners, one for every unit of 100 soldiers, the leaders' banners inscribed with the shahada, the white flag continuing under the Marinids and Saadians.
era-1040.open: The two sources contradict each other on the colour (black in Wikipedia, white in FOTW's contributor note, which cites no source); neither shows a plain white field as a single dynastic flag. The page's start year 1040 is the dynasty's beginning in Wikipedia's tables, 1062 in FOTW.

era-1968.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives adoption on 12 March 1968. Flags of the World (Mauritius): 'adopted upon independence, on 9 January 1968' (registered that day) and 'first officially hoisted on 12 March 1968, the day of independence' (Southworth 2004); designed by the College of Arms before independence (DK Ultimate Pocket Flags of the World, 1997); when Mauritius became a republic on 12 March 1992 the independence flag did not change (Zrzavy 2002).
era-1968.open: The 1968 start and the unchanged flag since are covered by both publishers; the meanings of the four colours on this page were not checked against either source.

era-1810.says: Flags of the World (pre-independence flags, Prothero citing CO 325/54 and ADM 116/1847B): the Blue Ensign badge, a quartered shield with the motto 'stella clavisque maris indici', was approved 14 December 1869; the arms granted in 1906 (25 August) were placed on a white disc, which was agreed unnecessary on 7 July 1921 and officially removed 14 December 1923, though the disc was used until independence in 1968 (Moss 2005); no defaced Red Ensign existed. Wikipedia's flag table lists British colonial flags for 1810-1869, 1869-1906, 1906-1923 and 1923-1968, and a colonial civil ensign for 1906-1968.
era-1810.open: A Blue Ensign with a Mauritius badge is documented from 1869, not 1810: neither source describes the flag of 1810-1869; the page's single drawing does not distinguish the 1869 badge from the 1906 arms.

era-1715.says: Wikipedia (French Mauritius): the infobox flag is captioned 'Flag (1715-1792)', linked as 'Flag of Isle de France (Mauritius)', and the image file is named for the Royal Standard of the King of France; the article describes no flag in text. Flags of the World (pre-independence flags): the island was Ile de France from 1711 or 1718 to 1810, owned first by the Compagnie des Indes; 'No French-period flag design is described.'
era-1715.open: No source read describes a white ensign with a gold fleur-de-lis or the Revolutionary tricolour; the infobox file name suggests the royal standard but does not say it flew in the colony; the start date varies (1711, 1715, 1718).

era-1598.says: Wikipedia (Dutch Mauritius): the infobox flag is the Dutch East India Company flag for 1638-1710; the island was frequented by Dutch ships from 1598 and named after Prince Maurits, but was only settled in 1638 and abandoned in 1710. Flags of the World (pre-independence flags): 1638-1710 Dutch administration; Sache 'thinks only the normal Dutch flags were used', VOC flags perhaps also (speculation).
era-1598.open: No source read documents a Prince's Flag or any 1598 landfall flag; the only flags named are VOC and 'normal Dutch flags' for 1638-1710, so the page's drawing is unsupported.

era-1917.says: Wikipedia says the current flag was adopted on 16 September 1968 and confirmed by law on 24 February 1984, that a presidential decree of 1916 changed the eagle from front-facing to side-facing, and that a rule on the reverse side's eagle was published on 9 May 1995. FOTW says a decree of 17 August 1968 in the Diario Oficial adopted the flag and arms, that a decree of 8 February 1984 confirmed them, and that the law of 24 February 1984 did not change the design.
era-1917.open: The 1968 dates differ between the sources (16 September, 17 August, and this page's earlier 24 September). The era starts in 1917 and the sources date the current design to 1968. The colours' meanings are disputed and the law gives none.

era-1500bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner in any modern sense from any pre-Aztec Mesoamerican civilization».
era-1500bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1864.says: Wikipedia: the Second Empire flag had a 1:2 ratio with four crowned eagles at the corners; the arms were described in a November 1865 decree. Flags of the World (Second Mexican Empire page): flag and arms adopted by decree of 18 June 1864, confirmed on 1 November 1865 (ratio 1:2), abolished 15 July 1867; the republican government under Juarez kept using the 1823 flag throughout.
era-1864.open: The golden colour of the corner eagles is not stated by either text, and the FOTW text read does not mention corner eagles (only its images do). The 1863 start date on FOTW's page title reflects the empire's proclamation; the flag decree is 1864.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia: in April 1823 the first federal republic adopted a flag with the crown removed from the eagle and a serpent added to its talon; the republic's flag was discontinued in 1864. Flags of the World (1823-1880 page): adopted by decree of 14 April 1823, the crown removed from the eagle and a half circle of oak and laurel added; in use 14 April 1823 to 30 December 1880, with the republican government using it again from 20 September 1863 to 14 July 1867.
era-1823.open: The sources agree on the 1823 decree but differ on the end: Wikipedia says the republic's flag was discontinued in 1864, FOTW says the republican government kept using it through the Second Empire. The page's 'turbulent 19th century' narrative is not itself sourced.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia: Army of the Three Guarantees, 24 February 1821, first use of green, white and red; Iturbide's imperial flag with a crowned eagle decreed November 1821 (or 7 January 1822), first officially used July 1822. Flags of the World (Mexican Empire page, quoting the decrees): decree of 2 November 1821 and confirming decree of 7 January 1822 set vertical green, white and red stripes with a crowned eagle on the white stripe; used from Iturbide's coronation on 21 July 1822; abolished by decree of 14 April 1823. FOTW's main page names Iturbide as creator and mentions a Celaya theory of origin.
era-1821.open: What each colour meant in 1821, and the Mexica eagle-on-cactus symbolism drawn on the page, are not stated in the sources read; the FOTW page says its image of the flag is based on written sources only.

era-1867.says: Wikipedia: a 1916 decree by Carranza made the eagle side-facing; current flag adopted 16 September 1968. Flags of the World: the 1823 decree stayed in effect until 1968 with the flag restored officially on 15 July 1867 and revised in 1880, 1899, 1916 and 1934; its Carranza page gives a decree of 20 September 1916 in effect from 1 October 1916, arms approved 22 August 1918.
era-1867.open: The Porfiriato and Revolution as political periods are not described by the flag sources; the revisions of 1880 and 1899 were found on FOTW only, and the details of those arms changes were not read.

era-1521.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): the saw-toothed red saltire on white flew in the New World viceroyalties, and a viceregal banner lasted as a symbol of New Spain until 24 August 1821. Flags of the World (Mexico history page): the flag and arms of New Spain were those of Spain; its Spain page says the red Burgundy cross, most often on white, was the main symbol of Spanish ships from Charles I (1518) to 1665 and the naval ensign 1506-1701, and a land war flag to 1843.
era-1521.open: The 1521 start and the cross's use over the whole of New Spain are not stated; after 1701 Spain changed royal banners and, in 1785, the sea ensign to red-yellow-red, so 'for most of the period' is as far as the sources go. Cortes's own 1519-1521 standard (red with the Virgin Mary) is a different flag.

era-1325.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Mexico) covers the Mexica eagle-on-prickly-pear legend behind the coat of arms but gives it no date and does not call it a banner. Flags of the World (Mexico history page) says banners carrying the old pre-Hispanic emblem of eagle, snake and prickly pear were widely used on conquest expeditions such as Florida (c.1550), which is after the Mexica period and not an Aztec banner.
era-1325.open: Whether the Mexica had any banner is not established; the reconstruction drawn here has no source. The Mexican native peoples index on FOTW (mx_np) was fetched and had no text for it.

era-1986.says: Wikipedia: adopted 30 November 1978, a light blue field with four white stars for Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae and Yap, derived from the Trust Territory's six-star flag of 1962 (approved 1965); the blue was changed to the UN-flag shade after the Compact of Free Association took effect on 3 November 1986. Flags of the World: 'adopted on 30 November 1978', stars reduced from six to four when Palau and the Marshall Islands went their own way; law describes a circle of four white stars on blue. Wikipedia (Trust Territory): US administration of the Micronesian districts ended 3 November 1986.
era-1986.open: The flag dates from 1978, so this card's 1986 start is the Compact, not the flag; the earlier note that FOTW dates it to 1962 reflected the Trust Territory flag, not the current one. Wikipedia's wording on the 1986 colour change is ambiguous about which blue replaced which.

era-1885-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-contact era, four distinct societies, no single flag».
era-1885-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1947.says: Wikipedia (Trust Territory): UN trusteeship began 18 July 1947 and US administration of the Micronesian districts ended 3 November 1986. Flags of the World: 'Before this flag was adopted the flags of the US and UN were used'; the Trust Territory flag (six stars on blue) was first hoisted 24 October 1962 and made official 19 August 1965, and flew beside the US and UN flags on UN Day. Wikipedia's FSM article: the six-star flag was adopted in 1962 and approved in 1965.
era-1947.open: The trust-territory flag (1962/65-1978/86) is a real flag of this era that the card does not draw; FOTW's fm page and its Trust Territory page give different 1962 days (3 October vs 24 October). The US flag is stated as in use but no source describes how it was flown across 1947-1986.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia (South Seas Mandate): Japan occupied the German islands by October 1914, held a League mandate from 1920 to 18 July 1947, and its infobox shows the flag of Japan (a separate Governor's flag is shown, undescribed). OzOutback (unsigned, no sources cited): the Japanese Navy seized the islands in 1914 flying the Japanese Naval Ensign (red Rising Sun with 16 rays on white) and the 1919 mandate flag showed a stylised emblem in a laurel wreath in black outline on white.
era-1914.open: The two publishers disagree: Wikipedia's infobox uses Japan's flag, OzOutback gives a separate mandate emblem flag and the naval ensign for 1914; the card's plain Hinomaru matches neither description. Neither source gives a decree or contemporary description; FOTW has no mandate page.

era-1899.says: Wikipedia (German New Guinea): the Caroline, Palau and Mariana islands were bought from Spain in 1899 and run from German New Guinea until the Japanese occupation of September-October 1914; drafts for colonial flags and arms were made in 1914 but never put into use. OzOutback (unsigned, no sources): the flag in the protectorate was the black-white-red flag of the German Empire with the coat of arms on a white disk.
era-1899.open: The card's white flag with a black-white-red canton and eagle badge matches the 1914 colonial flag draft, which Wikipedia says was never used; the one source naming the flag in use (OzOutback) describes a different design and is unsigned.

era-1885.says: Wikipedia (Spanish East Indies): the Carolines ('Nuevas Filipinas') were Spanish from 1686 until sold to Germany, effective 12 February 1899; its infobox shows the Spanish flag of 1785-1873 and 1875-1931. OzOutback: the red-yellow-red war ensign (yellow band double width) was adopted in 1785 and became the national flag in 1843 with the arms of Castile and Leon; Flags of the World's Spain page lists the 1843 decree and the 1785 ensign.
era-1885.open: No source describes a separate colonial flag or says how the flag was flown in the Carolines; the Cross of Burgundy ensign of earlier centuries (OzOutback) is not relevant to 1885-1899 but shows the sources' chronology.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Moldova and of the Moldavian SSR): the blue-yellow-red vertical tricolour with the coat of arms (an eagle bearing a shield with an aurochs head, star, rose and crescent) on the yellow stripe was adopted on 6 November 1990 and retained when Moldova declared independence in 1991; 27 April 1990 is the day the tricolour was first adopted by the Supreme Soviet and is Flag Day. FOTW: the flag was established in 1990 and has the arms on the yellow stripe; a national flag of 27 August 1991 bears the arms on a darker yellow rectangle; flag laws of 1994, 2001 and 17 September 2010 define it.
era-1991.open: Both sources date the flag to 1990, not 1991 (27 April tricolour without arms, 6 November 1990 with arms). The page's claim that the colours are a 'more saturated' palette than Romania's is not covered; Wikipedia says the reverse side used a lighter blue before 2010.
