era-1940.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Moldavian SSR): the SSR's first flag, from 1940, was red with the gold hammer and sickle and the Cyrillic initials РССМ above; on 31 January 1952 a decree approved a red cloth with a green stripe in the middle along the whole length (red-green-red, 3:2:3), with a gold hammer and sickle and a red star in the canton, used until 1990. FOTW: the 1941-1952 flag was red with curved yellow initials RSSM and a hammer and sickle (Constitution of 1941, art. 123); the flag of 31 January 1952 had a green bar in the middle, one quarter of the width, with hammer, sickle and star.
era-1940.open: The page's 'plain red until 1952' and a green stripe 'near the bottom' do not match the sources: the early flag carried the initials, and the green stripe was in the middle. The first flag is dated 1940 by Wikipedia and 1941 (constitution) by FOTW; 1990-91 saw the tricolour as the SSR's flag.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Romania): the vertical blue-yellow-red tricolour was Romania's flag from 1867 to 1948, with the Kingdom of Romania from 1881 to 1947. FOTW (Moldova): Bessarabia proclaimed independence in 1917 and joined Romania in 1918, and a 1917-1918 dark blue over red bicolour is reported without sources.
era-1918.open: No source read says that the Romanian tricolour flew in Bessarabia or that Bessarabia had no flag of its own; the link is inferred from the province being part of Romania. The 1940 end date comes from no source read.

era-1812.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Russia): the white-blue-red tricolour was a civil ensign from 1705, the black-yellow-white tricolour was declared the national flag in 1858, and white-blue-red became the national flag in 1896 (1883 for land use). Wikipedia (Principality of Moldavia): its infobox pairs the Bessarabia Governorate with the Russian flag. FOTW (Moldova): Bessarabia became Russian in 1810/1812.
era-1812.open: Russia's flag history is attested, but the white-blue-red tricolour was not the national flag from 1858 to 1896, and no source read describes a flag flown specifically in Bessarabia; the claim that no Bessarabian flag existed is not established.

era-1600.says: Wikipedia (Flag and coat of arms of Moldavia): the arms are an aurochs head with a star between its horns, a rose and a crescent, in sable or gold; Stephen the Great's princely flag of 1485 was red silk with the arms in gold; flag use declined under Ottoman control and, from the early 19th century, red-and-blue standards replaced the red and gold. FOTW (Principality of Moldavia): a 1533 document describes the great flag as red with the arms of Moldavia in gold; a flag of Ieremia Movila captured in 1601 is red with a gold border and the aurochs head, star and crescents in silver; a 1813 document gives a red, yellow and blue standard under Scarlat Calimachi.
era-1600.open: The colour of the aurochs varies in the sources (gold, silver or black) and the 1601 flag shows two crescents instead of a rose; Wikipedia says flag use declined under the Ottomans, and FOTW's 1813 red-yellow-blue standard shows the design changed at the end of the period. The page's 'at least from the 15th century' is supported by the 1485 and 1533 reports.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption of the present flag as 4 April 1881; FOTW gives 4 April 1881, by decree of Prince Charles III, and quotes the Constitution (Article 7): two equal horizontal stripes, red above white. Wikipedia says the earlier flag was similar but with an older coat of arms and was used until 1881.
era-1861.open: The flag dates from 1881, not 1861 (the 1861 Franco-Monegasque Treaty starts the era); the 1861-1881 flag is described only by Wikipedia (an older arms version). The drawing's colours were not compared against a specification.

era-600bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner from Ligurian, Greek, or Roman-era Monoikos survives».
era-600bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia (History of Monaco): the Congress of Vienna made Monaco a protectorate of Sardinia in 1815 after French control ended on 17 May 1814. Wikipedia (flag): the earlier flag with an older coat of arms was used until 1881 (start citation needed) and the red-lozenge banner was unofficial. FOTW's historical page covers only the lozengy banner, used mainly in the 17th century, and no 1815-1860 flag.
era-1815.open: No source states which flag Monaco flew in 1815-1860; Wikipedia's earlier flag with an older coat of arms is undescribed and undated at its start; FOTW dates the restoration to 1814, Wikipedia the protectorate to 1815.

era-1793.says: Wikipedia (History of Monaco): French revolutionary forces seized Monaco in 1793 and French control lasted until 17 May 1814; Wikipedia (flag): the earlier Monaco flag was not used during the annexation; FOTW also dates the annexation to 1793.
era-1793.open: No source read says the French tricolour flew over Monaco, or what flag, if any, was used between 1793 and 1814.

era-1297.says: Wikipedia (History of Monaco): Francesco Grimaldi seized the Rock in 1297 under Genoese sovereignty; Spanish authority from 1524, French recognition in 1641. Wikipedia (flag): red and white have been Grimaldi colours since at least 1339 and a banner of red lozenges on white was used at times, especially in the 17th century, as an unofficial flag. FOTW (historical page): the lozengy banner seems to have been used mainly in the 17th century, with a variable number of lozenges.
era-1297.open: Both sources call the lozengy banner unofficial and mainly 17th-century; no source names a state flag for the lordship in 1297-1793, so using the banner for the whole span is an approximation.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia: the current flag was adopted on 12 February 1992, the communist star above the Soyombo removed, colour standards set on 8 July 2011; the blue stripe is the eternal blue sky and the red stripes are thriving for eternity. Flags of the World: adopted by the new constitution of 13 January 1992, the star surmounting the emblem removed in 1992; Article 12 gives blue as the eternal sky in the middle and red as progress and prosperity on either side.
era-1992.open: The adoption day is 12 February on Wikipedia and 13 January (the constitution) on FOTW; the Soyombo's element meanings differ between the sources.

era-1924.says: WP: first constitution (26 Nov 1924) described a red flag with the state emblem in the centre; 1940 flag had no star; 1945 design with star; star above soyombo for the final 47 years. FOTW: 1924 constitution describes a red flag with the soyombo in the centre; soyombo adopted as state symbol 1924; 1949 gold star over soyombo; star removed 1992.
era-1924.open: The star is not in 1924; exact date of the star differs (1945 per WP, 1949 confirmation per FOTW). Page drawing shows the later layout.

era-1911.says: Wikipedia: after the 1911 declaration of independence the Bogd Khanate adopted a national flag as a symbol of independence. Flags of the World: independence declared 29 December 1911; the 1911 and 1912 flags show the soyombo in the older religious colours, a yellow square with an orange border is reported for 1911-1919, and a 1911 army flag is shown.
era-1911.open: Both sources agree that a flag with the soyombo was adopted, but neither supports a red field, and FOTW points to religious colours and a yellow flag; the card's design is not established.

era-1691.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Mongolia page describes flags under Qing rule, and FOTW's early Mongol flags page covers the Mongol Empire (Chinghiz-khan banners, museum and festival flags, the 1375 Catalan Atlas) but no Qing-era banners.
era-1691.open: Whether the Qing Yellow Dragon Flag flew over Outer Mongolia is not stated by any source read.

era-1368.says: Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Mongolia page describes post-Yuan khanate flags. FOTW's early Mongol flags page describes white and black nine-tailed banners attributed to Chinghiz-khan (Lomantsov, who calls modern reconstructions very doubtful) and Mongol Empire flags, but nothing for the Northern Yuan or later khanates.
era-1368.open: The black Mongol imperial banner for 1368-1691 is not established; the nearest evidence concerns the 13th-century empire, not the later khanates.

era-2006.says: Both sources date the current flag to 2004, before this era begins in 2006, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 13 July 2004; Flags of the World dates it 15 September 2004.
era-2006.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1496.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — direct Ottoman provincial rule, no local banner survives».
era-1496.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-168bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner survives from Illyrian, Roman, or early Duklja/Zeta rule».
era-168bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1992.says: FOTW (cs.html): the blue-white-red federal flag was adopted 27 April 1992 and stayed official after the 2003 renaming as Serbia and Montenegro until the union ended in 2006. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia): the new union removed the red star and kept a plain tricolour. For the republic, Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro) says it adopted its own red, light-blue and white tricolour in 1993; FOTW (cs-cg) gives the law published 29 December 1993, three equal horizontal stripes, red, light blue and white, differing from Serbia's flag in ratio and blue shade.
era-1992.open: Wikipedia's Flag of Yugoslavia contradicts itself on whether the red-star version continued after 1992; FOTW (27 April 1992) is followed here. The page's older statement of a tricolour-and-eagle flag flown alongside is not found in any source read.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro): the Yugoslav republic used a red, blue and white tricolour with a red star, 1945-93, adopted late 1946. FOTW (yu_fy-cg): the Montenegrin flag, a red-blue-white tricolour with a star, was officially adopted 31 December 1946 (arms probably the same time); the republic was a People's Republic until 1963 and Socialist from then until 1991. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia) describes the federal red-star flag as having a gold-yellow border to the star.
era-1943.open: The gold border is documented for the federal flag, not stated for the Montenegrin one; FOTW gives no end date for the flag; neither source says the old royal eagle was deliberately dropped.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia: the Kingdom of Montenegro used a tricolour with an eagle bearing the initials NI in 1910-18. FOTW (me_k): the 1905 Constitution (Art. 39) set the national colours red, bluish and white; Montenegro became a kingdom in 1910 and the court flag's crown changed from princely to royal; the civil ensign 1881-1916 was a plain tricolour with a crown and cypher in the centre.
era-1910.open: The two sources differ on the central device: Wikipedia has an eagle with the NI initials, FOTW a crown with the cypher on the civil ensign (and notes McCandless' claim of a war-ensign version as doubtful). The page's 'peak of territory and diplomacy' wording is not in either source.

era-1852.says: Wikipedia: Danilo I's flag in 1852-60 was red with a white two-headed eagle over a lion; the 1905 constitution set the red, blue and white tricolour. FOTW (me.html): arms of 1851-60 a golden double-headed eagle with a lion on the breast shield. FOTW (me_k): in 1852 Danilo made Montenegro a secular principality and added his golden cypher to the centre of the old cross banner; the eagle-and-lion alaj-banner war flag was designed c.1858; a white-blueish-red tricolour was raised in July 1860 at Prcanj but was not fully established; the tricolour became the national colours by the 1905 Constitution.
era-1852.open: Genuine conflict: Wikipedia dates the eagle-and-lion red flag from 1852, FOTW's historical page dates it c.1858 and says the 1852 change was a cypher on the cross banner. White versus golden eagle is also unresolved. The page's caption 'white double-headed eagle (1852)' is therefore not confirmed.

era-1516.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro): the Prince-Bishopric's flag from 1516 to 1852 was a white cross on a red field, and in 1767-73 under Stephen the Little white with red borders. Wikipedia (Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro) dates the state 1516-1852 and shows a flag image but does not describe it. FOTW (me_k) describes a red cross banner with a yellow border and a cross inside, inherited from the theocratic state, with no start date.
era-1516.open: The sources differ on the cross colour (white on red versus a cross within a yellow-bordered red banner) and no source read dates the flag itself to 1516; only the state is dated 1516. The page's 'some variants reverse the colours' is not covered.

era-1451.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro): medieval Zeta, 1451-96, a red flag with a golden two-headed eagle. Wikipedia (Zeta (state)) describes no flag for the Crnojevic principality and does not mention the eagle. A web search found the golden crowned double-headed eagle on red described as the Crnojevic family arms, not as a documented flag.
era-1451.open: Single source for the flag; no second independent source found. Crnojevic heraldry is described as arms, not as a flag of the principality. The Nemanjic lineage claim is not covered.

era-1918-1.says: FOTW (me.html): in 1918 Montenegro was incorporated into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and the red flag with gold arms was not raised again until 2004; the kingdom became Yugoslavia in 1929. FOTW (yu_shs): late 1918 a new state formed from the united Kingdoms of Serbia and Montenegro and the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs; local laws stayed in use regionally until 1922; its tricolour became the national flag in 1921. Wikipedia (Zeta Banovina) dates the banovina from 3 October 1929 but does not mention the 1918 union.
era-1918-1.open: Both usable pages are FOTW (one publisher); the 'region of Montenegro' stage, the Zeta Banovina boundaries (Herzegovina, Dubrovnik coast) and the '462 years' figure are not covered by any source read.

era-1941.says: FOTW (yu_wwii): in the first days of the war the Montenegrin tricolour was used (design not described); Montenegro was nominally declared an independent kingdom in personal union with Italy. Wikipedia (Italian governorate of Montenegro): the infobox pairs the Italian flag with a local Montenegrin flag whose file name reads 1905-1918, 1941-1944; the 'restored Kingdom of Montenegro' was proclaimed 12 July 1941 and the governorate lasted 3 October 1941 to 12 September 1943. The text describes no flag.
era-1941.open: No source describes the tricolour's design or an eagle for 1941-43; the Wikipedia file name is only an image label. Whether it was a royal-eagle flag is not established. Wikipedia Italian governorate text was read to 100,000 of 141,297 characters.

era-1918.says: FOTW (me.html): incorporation into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918, Yugoslavia 1929, the traditional red flag with gold arms not raised again until 2004. FOTW (yu_shs): the blue-white-red tricolour was formally introduced as the national flag with the 1921 Vidovdan Constitution and made the civil and state ensign by the 1922 law. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia): a horizontal blue-white-red tricolour, first officially adopted 1922. Wikipedia (Zeta Banovina): established 3 October 1929; its infobox shows the Yugoslav state flag under the caption Flag of Zetska Banovina.
era-1918.open: No source states outright that the banovina had no provincial flag of its own; the 'no distinct flag' wording rests on the infobox and FOTW's silence. The banovina's boundaries are not covered by the sources read.

era-1956.says: Wikipedia: the flag adopted by dahir on 17 November 1915 stayed in use; after independence in 1956 it was also allowed as the maritime flag. FOTW: the 1915 decree was confirmed in 1956 and not superseded; Constitution of 1974 (revised 1992) Article 7 describes a red flag with a green five-pointed star.
era-1956.open: Star drawing varies between flag books (FOTW); a 2005 decree set the construction (Wikipedia).

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: 17 November 1915 dahir of Sultan Yusef introduced the green pentagram on red; protectorate-era use limited at sea; merchant flags for the French zone 1919-1956 and Spanish zone 1937-1956. FOTW: Decree of 1915 set the star's size, and the flag was limited as the national flag in the French zone until independence.
era-1912.open: The page's stated reason for the star, and the 1912 start of the protectorate, are not covered by either source.

era-1666.says: Flags of the World (historical flags): the Alawites have ruled 'since 1666'; the flag 'was originally plain red, despite the numerous fanciful designs' European publishers gave it; the Alawites 'were the first to introduce the red flag', raised daily on the fortresses at Rabat and Sale; later sources show red flags with white scissors or triangle borders (Bellin 1756, Diderot 1780, Sinclair 1858), a red flag with a forked pennant (Norie and Hobbs 1848) and a plain red flag on a 1908 card; the French Protectorate began 30 March 1912. Wikipedia: the Alawi flag is dated 1666-1915 and 'was solid red at first' (citation needed); the Sharifs of Makkah also used red; the current flag dates from a dahir of 17 November 1915.
era-1666.open: Both publishers agree on a red Alawite flag, plain at first, but FOTW's later evidence shows decorated red flags in the 18th and 19th centuries, so 'plain red for nearly two and a half centuries' is not supported; the 'red banners at ports and fortresses' point is FOTW's only for Rabat and Sale, and the era end of 1912 versus Wikipedia's 1915 is unresolved.

era-1983.says: Both sources give 1983, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1 May 1983; Flags of the World dates it 01 May 1983.
era-1983.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia: independence 25 June 1975 with a flag defined by Article 68 of the constitution: four diagonal stripes from the upper hoist in green, red, black and yellow with white fimbriations, and a white cogwheel near the upper hoist bearing a red star and an AK-47 crossed by a hoe over an open book; changed in 1983. FOTW (mz_old): the first official flag was adopted 25 June 1975, four irregular triangles of yellow, black, red and green fimbriated white radiating from the upper hoist, with the arms (a black-lined cogwheel, a rifle and a hoe in saltire over an open book, red star) in the canton; replaced in April 1983 (adopted 1 May 1983 on mz.html).
era-1975.open: The sources agree on date, colours and emblem elements; FOTW says 'a rifle' where Wikipedia says AK-47, and the exact stripe order and the wording 'diagonal bands' differ. Article 68 appears only in Wikipedia.

era-1498.says: Wikipedia (Portuguese Mozambique): the Portuguese arrived from 1498 and the colony is dated 1505-1975, an overseas province from 1951; the infobox shows the Portuguese flag dated 1911-1975, the colonial arms 1951-1975 and a governor's flag. Wikipedia (Flag of Mozambique): the Portuguese flag flew beside FRELIMO's in the 1974-75 transition; FOTW (mz_old) agrees that FRELIMO's flag flew beside the Portuguese flag from the truce of 5 September 1974 until independence on 25 June 1975.
era-1498.open: Use of the Portuguese flag in 1911-1975 rests on Wikipedia's infobox; for 1974-75 two publishers agree. No source describes a distinct colonial ensign or flags before 1911, and FOTW's colonial flags page was not read. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 176,229 characters.

era-2011.says: Both: the current yellow-green-red flag with a large white star adopted 21 October 2010 (Wikipedia: Union Flag Law, 2008 Constitution, 2:3; FOTW: State Flag Law 8/2010, 2:3, raised 3 p.m.).
era-2011.open: The 2011 civilian-led government is not covered by either flag page.

era-1974.says: Wikipedia: adopted 3 January 1974, designed by Mya Thaung, 5:9, a blue canton on red with 14 stars round a cogwheel and paddy ear, used to 2010. FOTW: flag adopted 27 December 1973 (the constitution is dated 3 January 1974); a red flag with a blue canton and a white emblem of a cog wheel and a paddy ear surrounded by 14 five-pointed stars; ratio usually 5:9.
era-1974.open: The two sources differ by a week on the adoption date (27 December 1973 vs 3 January 1974); neither mentions ruling-party ideology.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: used 4 January 1948 to 3 January 1974, designed by Maung Win, no stripes, one large star and five small stars in a blue canton on red. FOTW: the 1948 flag is red with a blue canton holding one large white star and five small white stars; adopted with the constitution of 24 September 1947 and hoisted first at 4:25 a.m. on 4 January 1948; a contributor says the big star stood for the Union and the five small ones for five states (another recalls the Anti-Fascist League flag as the source of the large star).
era-1948.open: What the five small stars stand for is a contributor's statement in FOTW, not a document; Wikipedia does not explain them.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia: the peacock flag was the State of Burma's national flag 1943-45 (state flag from 1 August 1943), with a gold peacock for the State of Burma and a red peacock for the Burma Defence Army; a provisional Japanese Military Administration flag 1942-43. FOTW: the Japanese created a puppet state on 1 August 1943 with a flag 'probably' horizontally yellow, green and red with a peacock on a disc (a Japanese newspaper shows yellow-green-red with a peacock on a white disc), abolished 1 August 1945; in 1942 the pro-Japanese provisional government used the Synyethe-Wunthann party flag unofficially.
era-1942.open: The sources disagree on design (Wikipedia: peacock flag; FOTW: yellow-green-red triband with peacock), so the single 'green field' drawn on the page is not confirmed; the 1942 provisional flag is described differently by the two (Japanese Military Administration vs party flag).

era-1886.says: Wikipedia: the UK Union Flag was the colonial flag 1886-1942 and again 1945-48, with a separate British Burma colonial flag 6 February 1939 to 30 March 1941 and 1945-1948 and a provisional one in 1941-42. FOTW: from 1886 to 1939 Burma was part of India and the British (or Indian) flag flew; from 6 (adopted 9) February 1939 the Blue Ensign with a Burmese badge (a golden disc with a peacock) until 1941 and again in 1945-1948.
era-1886.open: The page's 'colony' wording: Burma was part of British India until 1937 (FOTW notes 1886-1939 as part of India); the designs of the 1941-42 provisional flags are not described.

era-1044.says: Wikipedia lists a Hanthawaddy kingdom flag about 1287-1552 and a Konbaung national flag about 1752-1885 and links the peacock to the Konbaung dynasty. FOTW (historical flags): a golden hintha on green flag of the early Mon c.1300-1500; the Thu Ye Gyee 'hero's' military flag c.1300-1885 (yellow circle with seven animals on red); the Konbaung flag 1700-1885 (white with a peacock on a red disc); and dark red three-pointed flags with a black cross at Mandalay in the 1850s, described as a royal artillery standard.
era-1044.open: Both sources date the peacock flag only to the Konbaung dynasty (1700/1752 onwards), so the page's use of it 'for the whole pre-colonial span' is contradicted; nothing is said about Bagan (1044) or Toungoo, and FOTW's dates come from a web source and a private list.

era-1990.says: Wikipedia's infobox: adopted 21 March 1990. FOTW (Namibian flag 1990 - ): on 21 March 1990 South West Africa gained independence as the Republic of Namibia and adopted a new flag chosen by a committee; the symbolism given by the chairman of the National Symbols Sub-committee on 2 February 1990 (citing F. G. Brownell, Archives News 1990) is red for the people and their heroism, white for peace and unity, green for vegetation and agriculture, blue for the sky, the Atlantic Ocean and rain, and the gold sun for life and energy; one source says the colours came from the SWAPO flag adopted in 1971.
era-1990.open: Neither source says the design 'deliberately breaks' from the German and South African flags; FOTW's note that the colours came from the SWAPO flag (adopted 1971) is a single attribution to a 1990 flag book.

era-1915.says: Wikipedia's captions: a South West Africa flag for 1915-1919 (identification uncertain), a merchant flag 1915-1928, South African-derived flags for South West Africa 1928-1990, bantustan flags and the SWAPO flag at the UN 1976-1990. FOTW (Flag History of Namibia): South African troops took German South West Africa on 9 July 1915; under the mandate the South African Red Ensign was flown in the territory until 31 May 1928, when the South African national flag (orange, white and blue stripes with flaglets in the centre) was adopted; FOTW also lists the bantustan flags.
era-1915.open: FOTW's account stops at the 1928 adoption; the flag shown on the page is the plain orange-white-blue without the flaglets, a simplification, and the SA Red Ensign (1915-28) is not what the page shows for the whole span.

era-1884.says: Wikipedia: the Reich Colonial Office flag was used in German South-West Africa from 24 April 1884 to 9 July 1915, with an undated proposed colonial flag shown. FOTW (Flag History of Namibia): German colonies had no distinctive flags or arms of their own; the Imperial German arms and flags were used throughout the empire, including German South West Africa; colonial flags designed in 1912-14 (the German tricolour with a blue shield bearing a silver ox's head and a diamond for South West Africa) were never taken into use because of the war; German forces surrendered on 9 July 1915.
era-1884.open: The exact imperial flag flown (the black-white-red civil ensign drawn on the page vs. the Reich Colonial Office flag Wikipedia names) is not described by either source.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Nauru): a Blue Ensign with a seven-pointed Commonwealth Star and five Southern Cross stars was used in the Australian occupation (1914-1920) and the League of Nations mandate, and again from 1945 to 1968 under the UN trust territory; New Zealand and the UK were co-mandatories but their flags were not used; a white flag with a red disc for 1942-1945; the history rows cite a Flagmakers PDF. Flags of the World (Nauru historical flags): in 1924 the Chiefs proposed a national flag and the Australian Administrator objected and proposed a 'distinguishing' flag, which Melbourne said (2 June 1925) could not be recognised even as a distinguishing flag; London (27 August 1925) suggested a Nauru badge for use on British-pattern ensigns and the Union Jack for the Administrator; it also lists a Customs Flag for 1921-1968 without detail.
era-1920.open: Flags of the World describes no flag flown by the mandate administration, so the Blue Ensign rests on Wikipedia alone (itself sourced to a commercial PDF); the page's 'Britain, Australia, New Zealand jointly' wording is contradicted by Wikipedia's note that only Australia's flag was used; the Customs Flag page was not read.

era-1888.says: Wikipedia (German Marshall Islands): Nauru was incorporated into the Marshall Islands protectorate on 16 April 1888; the Jaluit Company began administering the colony in January 1888 and on 31 March 1906 the German government took direct control, placing the Marshall Islands and Nauru within German New Guinea; it does not name the German New Guinea Company. Flags of the World (German colonies): the German New Guinea Company flag (1885-1899) was white with a black-white-red canton and a black lion holding a red fleur-de-lys, the Jaluit Gesellschaft flag was white with a black-white-red striped disc, and Nauru has no flag entry; the imperial colonial flag is not mentioned. Wikipedia (Flag of Nauru) still lists the New Guinea Company flag for 1888-1899 and the Imperial Colonial Office flag for 1899-1914, citing a Flagmakers PDF.
era-1888.open: The sources contradict each other on who administered Nauru (the Jaluit Company, not the German New Guinea Company, per Wikipedia's Marshall Islands article), so the flag listed for Nauru in 1888-1899 is doubtful; no source mentions the eagle ensign on this page's drawing; the 1914-1920 span is Australian occupation.

era-1990.says: Wikipedia: the 9 November 1990 constitution (Article 5, Schedule 1) gave a geometric description of the flag; in 2008 a proposal to change the design was rejected. FOTW's page on the flag's legal basis quotes the constitution's Article 5, that the flag 'as handed down by tradition' has two juxtaposed triangular figures with crimson base and deep blue borders, a white moon with eight visible rays and a twelve-rayed sun, with Schedule 1 construction steps; a contributor note dates that constitution 9 November 1991 (a probable slip) and FOTW's main page says the double pennant was adopted officially on 16 December 1962.
era-1990.open: FOTW labels its extract '1999' and gives 1991 for the adoption in a contributor note, so the year of the text it quotes is not firm in FOTW; the 2008 rejected proposal is only in Wikipedia. Neither source says the design changed in 1990.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: flag adopted 16 Dec 1962 with the new constitutional government, standardised by Rimal at King Mahendra's request; human faces removed to modernise. FOTW: adopted 12 Dec 1962, sun and moon stylised 16 Dec 1962; a contributor believes the faces were removed in 1962.
era-1960.open: Adoption date differs (12 vs 16 Dec 1962); FOTW's face-removal statement is a contributor's belief; the 1960 start of the period is not covered.

era-1951.says: Wikipedia: sun and moon carried human faces until 1962. FOTW: flags with faces in 1939 and 1958 reproductions and in a 1928 book.
era-1951.open: Origin of the faces is only in Wikipedia (some historians credit Jung Bahadur); 'older informal proportions' not covered.

era-1846.says: FOTW's main page: the flag is based on two pennants of rival branches of the Rana dynasty, joined in the 19th century, official from 1962; contributors say the double pennant has been used since the 19th century and Rana family members were prime ministers until 1961. FOTW's page on Landon's 1928 book shows a 1928 national flag of two red triangles with a green border and white faces on the crescent and sun, and royal and army flags with the same emblems. Wikipedia gives no dates for the Rana period and says some historians credit the Rana ruler Jung Bahadur with changing the sun and moon into faces.
era-1846.open: Neither source mentions the 1846 Kot Massacre or says the flag stayed unchanged through Rana rule; Wikipedia's attribution of the faces to Jung Bahadur suggests a change within it, and the double pennant's date of origin differs between sources (see the 1768 row).

era-1768.says: Wikipedia: the Gorkha kingdom's flag began as a single red triangular Shah banner and many accounts date the double pennant to Prithvi Narayan Shah, without dates. FOTW: an unverified contributor comment credits Prithvi Narayan Shah with the flag's shape, while other contributor notes say the individual pennants were used for about two centuries and the double pennant only 'since the 19th century'; the earliest depiction it cites is Landon's 1928 book.
era-1768.open: The sources conflict on when the double pennant began (Prithvi Narayan Shah's unification, 1768, versus the 19th century); no dated source for the unification-era flag was found and the drawing remains a reconstruction. The faces are unsupported for this period.

era-1902.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 24 March 1902; Flags of the World dates it 12 June 1902. Flags of the World's history pages (David Prothero, from Admiralty and Gazette sources) reconcile the two: the New Zealand Ensign Act 1901 received royal assent on 24 March 1902 and the proclamation was published in the New Zealand Gazette on 12 June 1902, making the Blue Ensign with four red white-bordered stars the national flag.
era-1902.open: The design and colours were not checked against a specification. The page's wording on the Union Jack and the Southern Cross meaning is its own and was not tested.

era-1840.says: Wikipedia: Union Jack used after 1840 with the United Tribes flag still on some ships; 'NZ' blue ensign decreed 15 Jan 1867; Southern Cross design approved 23 Oct 1869 for government ships. Flags of the World (historical flags, Prothero): Treaty of Waitangi 1840, the Union Jack becomes the national flag and remains the land flag until 1902; 1867 first New Zealand Blue Ensign with red letters NZ; 23 October 1869 gazette of the Blue Ensign with four red stars, a Union Jack with white stars and a pennant; 1874 governor's flag replaces the Jack.
era-1840.open: Both sources agree and contradict this page's drawing and caption: the flag of the colony was the Union Jack, with a plain blue ensign never listed; the 1867 and 1869 ensigns were for government vessels. Left unreviewed until the drawing is checked against these.

era-1834.says: Wikipedia: adopted at Waitangi in March 1834, designed by Henry Williams; an 1835 New South Wales gazette notice describes a red St George's cross on white with a canton of a red cross on blue and four white stars. Flags of the World (historical flags pages): Busby's despatch of 26 March 1834 reports that 25 chiefs chose, on 20 March, among three flags (3, 10 and 12 votes), the one the missionaries had adopted; it was gazetted in 1835, the canton blue with a red St George's cross fimbriated white and four stars, and replaced by the Union Jack on 6 February 1840.
era-1834.open: The star points differ among accounts (eight-pointed in Busby's 1834 drawing, five- or six-pointed in the gazetted version) and the canton cross's fimbriation changed from black to white. FOTW's own caption notes the original had eight-pointed stars, so the page's eight-pointed stars fit the 1834 drawing, not the gazette.

era-1908.says: Wikipedia: September 1908 (11 or 5 September); official 27 August 1971; 30 January 2025 FSLN flag recognised. FOTW: 4 September 1908 decree; 5 September arms; Decree 1,908 of 25 August 1971 published 27 August; 2002 Law 432.

The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1838.says: Wikipedia: after the republic collapsed Nicaragua continued to use the federation flag until 1854; 1854-1856 a yellow-white and scarlet tricolour; William Walker's flag 1855-1857; further flags 1858-1889, 1889-1893, 1893-1896, 1896-1908; 1908 adoption (11 or 5 September 1908). FOTW: a blue-white-blue flag was reportedly first hoisted on 4 July 1818 (Louis Aury's squadron); current flag form adopted 4 September 1908 by decree. FOTW (ni-hist): the national flag adopted 21 April 1854 (bottom stripe 'nacar') ran with interruptions to 1889; a Walker flag of about July 1856 to May 1857 was not a national flag (Walker used blue-white-blue); the 1858 constitution under Tomas Martinez readopted blue-white-blue; further flags c.1869-73, 1889, 1893 and 1896; the 1908 flag adopted 4 September 1908. FOTW (cam-us): Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Honduras left the Federation in 1838; flags of the four states are based on the Federation's blue-white-blue; the Diet at Leon decreed a blue-white-blue flag on 2 April 1851.
era-1838.open: Two publishers confirm that blue-white-blue flags were in use at several points, but they give no sequence agreeing across 1838-1908 and neither describes an early volcano emblem; FOTW's list is full of disputed or unverified entries.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Central America) lists a flag for the Captaincy General of Guatemala (Mexico) used 5 January 1822 to 1 July 1823 without describing it; Wikipedia (Flag of Nicaragua) has no 1821-1823 entry. FOTW (cam-us): independence from Spain 15 September 1821, incorporation into Mexico 5 January 1822 and independence restored 1 July 1823, with no flag described for the period.
era-1821.open: The dates are attested by two publishers, but neither describes the flag or says a green-white-red Mexican tricolour was flown over Nicaragua; the era start 1821 precedes the 5 January 1822 incorporation.

era-1524.says: Wikipedia (Nicaragua): a Burgundy-cross flag listed for New Spain until 1785 and a Spanish flag for the Captaincy General of Guatemala 1785-1821. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): saw-toothed red saltire on white, flown in the New World viceroyalties; Nicaragua not mentioned. FOTW does not cover the colonial period. Wikipedia (Captaincy General of Guatemala): colonisation began in 1524, the captaincy general was established in 1609 and disestablished 15 September 1821, and it included present-day Nicaragua; the infobox flag file is the Cross of Burgundy though the text does not discuss a flag.
era-1524.open: A Burgundy-cross flag over Nicaragua is shown only by Wikipedia infobox and list entries; the date range for which it applied is not established, and FOTW does not cover the colonial period.

Neither source reports any later change to the green-white-green design.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia ('Flag of Nigeria (1914-1960)'): adopted 1952, in use 1914, relinquished 1960; a Blue Ensign with the Union Jack and a badge (red disc with green hexagram, crown, 'Nigeria'). Flags of the World (Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria): the colony 'flew a British Blue Ensign with the Colonial badge in the fly', the badge a red field with two interlocked triangles forming a six-pointed star and a crown, with the Tudor Crown before 1953 and St Edward's Crown from 1953 to 1960; a Red Ensign was used at sea; a governor's flag was the Union Flag with the badge in a laurel wreath.
era-1914.open: The two descriptions of the badge differ in detail (Wikipedia: red disc and green hexagram with 'Nigeria'; FOTW: red field with interlaced triangles and a crown), and the page's drawing is schematic; the Tudor-to-St Edward's Crown change in 1953 is not shown.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: in 1959 Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi won the flag competition; the green-white-green flag was officially adopted at midnight on 1 October 1960 and hoisted by Lt David Ejoor; green stands for agriculture, white for unity and peace. FOTW: the flag was chosen in 1959 from 2,870 suggestions, first officially hoisted on 1 October 1960; green is agriculture, white is peace and unity.
era-1960.open: Neither source mentions forests or a deliberate absence of regional symbols.

era-1861.says: Flags of the World: Lagos Colony (annexed 6 August 1861) flew a Blue Ensign with the colony's badge from 1886 to 1906 (Prothero 2001); Southern Nigeria (1900) and Northern Nigeria (1900) each 'flew a blue ensign defaced with the badge of the protectorate in the fly', badges added to the 1889 Admiralty Flag Book by amendment in March 1901 (Prothero 2002); Lagos was merged into Southern Nigeria in 1906 and the two protectorates amalgamated in 1914. Wikipedia: infobox ensigns for the Colony of Lagos (file dated 1888-1906) and for the Northern and Southern Nigeria Protectorates (1900-1914).
era-1861.open: Neither publisher describes the badges' designs, and no ensign is documented for Lagos in 1861-1886; the page's unbadged Blue Ensign is a generic stand-in.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 8 September 1948. FOTW quotes Crampton (1985) that the flag was created in 1948 (blue-red-blue stripes) and its 1946-1948 page ends the provisional People's Committee flag on 8 September 1948.
era-1948.open: Only the date was compared; the design symbolism (star, disc, stripe meanings) and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification. FOTW's 'North Korea 1948 (dubious)' page describes a different, probably fictional, flag and gives no adoption date.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: the taegukgi was widely used in both occupation zones in 1945-1947; the Soviets began proposing a new flag only in 1947; the design was written into the provisional constitution on 20 February 1948. FOTW: a taeguk-type flag with trigram and colour differences from today's South Korean flag was used from February 1946 to 8 September 1948 by the Korean Provisional People's Committee; Wikipedia's Flag of Korea lists a People's Committee flag for 1945-1946.
era-1945.open: The north's 1946-48 flag was a variant of the taegukgi, not identical to the page's drawing; no source read describes a flag of a Soviet administration itself.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia: from 1910 the Japanese flag replaced the taegukgi on the peninsula and the taegukgi became a symbol of resistance. FOTW: under Japanese rule (1910-1945) the Korean taeguk flag was prohibited; the Hinomaru was used in Korea until 15 August 1945; the exile government enacted a law on making the national flag on 29 June 1942.
era-1910.open: Wikipedia's Flag of Korea lists a Provisional Government flag for 1919-1945; the exile government is not otherwise covered here.

era-1897.says: Wikipedia: the taegukgi was used by the Korean Empire until annexation in 1910. Wikipedia's Flag of Korea lists taegukgi versions for 1882-1910 and an imperial banner for 1897-1907. FOTW's history page says only that its 1899 flag 'might be' the national flag of the Korean Empire (1897-1910).
era-1897.open: FOTW is explicitly uncertain about which flag was the Empire's; the 1897 founding date as a flag event and the claim that the flag was unchanged are not stated by a second source.

era-1883.says: Wikipedia: the taegukgi ('Flag of Great Extremes') was adopted in 1883 as Korea's first national flag. FOTW: Bak Yeong-hyo used it from September 1882 and it was formally proclaimed on 6 March 1883 (another contributor gives 27 January 1883).
era-1883.open: FOTW contributors disagree on the exact 1883 date and on the first hoisting in 1882; symbolism of the design is not covered.

era-1392.says: Wikipedia gives 1883 as the adoption of Korea's first national flag. FOTW's history page cites an 1856 Japanese flag chart titling a flag 'Korean National flag' and an 1876 blue flag with a yellow dragon titled 'Korean King Standard', but no dynastic banner for the 1392-1882 span itself.
era-1392.open: The 'royal blue' dynastic colour is not documented by a source read; the FOTW items are single-publisher and late (1856, 1876) and a Japanese flag book shows a yellow square flag with a red border as a king's standard.

era-918.says: Wikipedia's North Korea flag article describes no Goryeo flag. Wikipedia's Flag of Korea list names three Goryeo royal flags (Bong-gi 'phoenix', Haema-gi 'seahorse', Sang-gi 'elephant'), each marked 'Extant 1392'.
era-918.open: Single publisher, and the list does not date them to the dynasty as state flags; FOTW's Korean history page does not mention Goryeo banners. No reference source read.

era-676.says: Wikipedia's North Korea flag article describes no Silla flag. Wikipedia's Flag of Korea list shows a Silla military banner, a blue field with a white crescent moon, noted there as a reconstruction based on past observations.
era-676.open: Single publisher, explicitly a reconstruction; FOTW's Korean history page does not mention Silla banners. No reference source read.

era-1972.says: Wikipedia: the Union Flag is the only official flag for Northern Ireland; the government and parliament were abolished in 1972 (elsewhere attributed to the Constitution Act 1973); a 2021 commission recommended a Civic Flag. FOTW: Flags Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2000 restrict flags on government buildings to the Union Flag; College of Arms advised in November 1973 that use of the arms was improper after the 1973 Act.
era-1972.open: 1972 versus 1973 for the end of the Ulster Banner's official status; the March 1972 prorogation is not in either source.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: Royal Warrant of 1924 for the government's arms; the banner was first flown over Parliament Buildings for the 1953 coronation and officially used with Tudor Crown (1924-1953) and St Edward's Crown (1953-1972). FOTW: 2 August 1924 Royal Warrant, 29 May 1953 Royal Assent for widespread use, arms redrawn with St Edward's crown on 6 January 1971, abolished 1973.
era-1953.open: The crown on the 1950s-60s flag is disputed between the two sources; the design (star and red hand) is not specified in the Wikipedia text read.

era-1921.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Northern Ireland): there is no official flag for Northern Ireland except the Union Flag; on 1 July 1953 the Minister for Home Affairs said the Union Flag was the only officially recognised flag. FOTW: 'The official flag of Northern Ireland is the Union Flag' (Prothero 2002), made official for all purposes after the Stormont government went in 1973.
era-1921.open: Both sources also describe the Ulster Banner, which Wikipedia dates to a 1924 royal warrant for the Government of Northern Ireland (official use 1924-1953 with the Tudor Crown) and FOTW treats as introduced and widely used from 1953; neither describes a flag specific to 1921.

era-1801.says: FOTW (United Kingdom): the Union Flag was adopted 1 January 1801 with St Patrick's saltire added after the Union with Ireland Act 1800. Wikipedia (Union Jack): design in force from 1 January 1801; after the 1921 Treaty, Northern Ireland's Prime Minister Craig welcomed that the flag would not need changing ('mutilating the Union Jack') and in December 1922 the flag was not changed.
era-1801.open: Neither source describes use of the flag in Ulster specifically before 1921 beyond Ireland being part of the United Kingdom; the 1801-1921 span is inferred from the Union Flag's continuous use.

era-1177.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Ireland): the Lordship of Ireland was founded in 1177 and the Kingdom of Ireland (1542-1800) 'had no official flag or arms'; a Royal Standard of Ireland is captioned 1542-1801 and the arms are blazoned azure a harp Or. FOTW (Lordship of Ireland): the Lordship banner of arms is a modern historical banner, not a documented flag; three crowns on blue arms are attributed from the 1380s. Wikipedia (Flag of Northern Ireland): the Red Hand origin is disputed; the Royal Standard of Ireland is listed 1541-1800.
era-1177.open: No source documents a gold harp on blue flag, or a flag with an Ulster red hand, for this span; the first source calls the Kingdom flagless and the second calls the Lordship banner non-historical.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia's chronology of the flag marks a break in 1940-45 and the cross flag as the flag again from 1945. Store norske leksikon (L. Roede): the national flag was drawn by Frederik Meltzer, adopted by royal resolution of 13 July 1821 and is Norway's flag today (navy-blue Nordic cross with white borders on red); 8 May is flag day for the liberation of 1945.
era-1945.open: The page's statement that the exiled government and the resistance kept the flag flying throughout is not covered by either source.

era-1905.says: Store norske leksikon: the pure flag (without union mark) was made the merchant flag by law of 10 December 1898, with a swallow-tailed state flag without the mark; the naval ensign had to stay a union flag under the constitution until the dissolution of the union in 1905, when the mark was taken out of it (naval ensign without mark from 9 June 1905). Wikipedia: Storting abolished the mark 1898-99, pure flag first flown 1899, royal standard 15 November 1905.
era-1905.open: SNL's own captions and text differ on the state flag date (15 vs 10 December 1898); the royal standard date rests on Wikipedia alone.

era-1814.says: Store norske leksikon: Dannebrog with the Norwegian lion in the upper hoist field was proclaimed Norway's flag on 27 February 1814 by the regent Christian Frederik; Swedish-pattern union naval flag from 1815; Meltzer's flag laid before the Odelsting on 4 May 1821 and adopted by royal resolution of 13 July 1821; on 20 June 1844 both countries' merchant and naval flags received the common union mark (the 'herring salad') in the canton, until 1905. Wikipedia agrees on 1814, 1821 (13 July approval for civilian use) and 1844.
era-1814.open: The 1821 flag's Storting approval is dated May 1821 by Wikipedia (11 and 16 May) and 4 May presentation by SNL; the page's earlier statement that the plain civil flag never carried the union mark is contradicted by both sources.

era-1523.says: Store norske leksikon: in the 17th and 18th centuries the Danish Dannebrog gradually became the usual flag, also on Norwegian warships and fortresses, and from 1748 it was the only recognised Danish-Norwegian merchant flag; the lion banner was occasionally used as a ship and fortress flag. Wikipedia: Norway used Denmark's flag from 1537 to 1814 (citation needed), the Norwegian lion banner flew over Akershus at least until 1698, was in regimental colours from 1641, and the 1748 decree made Dannebrog the only legal merchant flag.
era-1523.open: Neither source says Dannebrog was the flag from 1523; Wikipedia gives 1537 and SNL describes a gradual change in the 1600s and 1700s. 'No flag of its own for the entire span' is too strong: the lion banner survived on ships and fortresses (page text corrected).

era-995.says: Store norske leksikon: the oldest known form of Norwegian flag is the lion of the realm's arms on a banner, shown on Duchess Ingebjorg's seal of 1318 - a royal flag with the golden lion and silver axe on red, later sometimes used on ships and fortresses. Wikipedia: Eirik II used a golden lion with axe and crown on red, which from 1280 became the royal standard; the earliest certain depiction is the 1318 seal; earlier rulers used other banners (raven, serpent, red lion on gold under Inge I in the 1130s, Sverre's eagle).
era-995.open: Before about 1280 the sources describe other banners, not the lion on red, so the c.995-1280 stretch of this era is not covered; 'St. Olav's axe' is not stated by either source.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia's chronology table shows a break at 1940 with a Nazi Germany flag icon until the national flag returned in 1945. The Storting's own history page reproduces a wartime photograph of the occupied Storting building with a German propaganda poster and a swastika in the flagpole; the building was taken over by the occupiers and later by Reichskommissar Terboven. FOTW covers no historical Norwegian flags.
era-1940.open: Only the Storting building is documented; Reich flags over other Norwegian institutions, the Nasjonal Samling emblem, any domestic ban on the Norwegian flag and its use abroad are not covered by sources read.

era-1397.says: FOTW and Wikipedia (Emblems of the Kalmar Union) both cite two letters of 1430 in which King Eric orders the priests of Vadstena and Kalmar to wear the 'banner of the realms' on their robes, described as a red cross in a yellow field. FOTW adds that there is no pictorial evidence and no surviving flag, and that a red-on-yellow flag in a museum is a recreation; Wikipedia's Flag of Norway lists a contested 'Union' flag with a Nordic cross without design details. Wikipedia's emblems article puts the Three Crowns in the union arms, not on the banner.
era-1397.open: The red cross on yellow rests on two 1430 letters only, read by FOTW's contributors and Wikipedia without a primary-source edition; no source puts three crowns on the banner, so the drawing on this page is not confirmed. Sought: Bartholdy (1996, 1997), cited by FOTW, not read.

era-1526.says: Wikipedia's Flags of the Mughal Empire says the principal imperial standard, the alam, was primarily moss green with a lion and sun facing the hoist, and describes scarlet pennons with green borders in an Akbar-era manuscript; neither Wikipedia's Flag of Pakistan nor FOTW's Pakistan page mentions Mughal flags.

era-1899.says: Wikipedia lists the German colonial flag and the German Emperor's standard for 1899-1914. FOTW's German colonies page says the Caroline Islands, like some other German colonies, used the Foreign Office service flag or the Imperial ensign rather than any special colonial flag.
era-1899.open: The white field with a black-white-red canton and colonial badge drawn here is not described by either source and FOTW says no special Carolines flag existed; the drawing needs redrawing against the flag actually used (service flag or ensign).

era-1885.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Palau lists the Spanish flag (1785-1899) and its Spanish East Indies article says Palau was ruled from Manila until the remaining islands were sold to Germany under the 1899 treaty, showing the 1785 Spanish flag as the colony's flag. FOTW's Spain page gives the flag as red-yellow-red in the ratio 1:2:1 (the yellow stripe twice the width of each red), originating as the 1785 war ensign and made the state and war flag by Royal Decree of 13 October 1843.
era-1885.open: Neither source states where the flag was actually raised in Palau; Wikipedia also lists the German New Guinea Company flag for 1885-1899, which did not govern Palau.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia: the flag of the United States of Colombia (also the current Colombian flag) was in use from 26 November 1861 to 3 November 1903, a provisional New Granada flag from 1830 to 1834, the New Granada and Grenadine Confederation flag from 1834 to 1861, and Panama had its own Federal State flag (1855-1863) and Sovereign State flag (1863-1886); Wikipedia (Flag of Colombia): New Granada's colours adopted 9 May 1834, Colombia's flag adopted by law 26 November 1861. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy Flag): it remained in use in Spain's overseas empire and as a jack until 1785. FOTW (Spain 1506-1700): the red Burgundy cross was the main Spanish symbol from 1518 to 1665, a military banner possibly carried by the conquistadors, with separate ensigns for American waters.
era-1519.open: Neither publisher mentions Panama, Peru or New Granada; the Burgundy cross is described as a military banner and was superseded for naval use in 1785 and by the Spanish national flag by 1821, so it cannot be shown as the colony's banner for the whole 1519-1821 span.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia lists a Territory of Papua flag for 1906-1971, a Territory of New Guinea flag for 1921-1971, the Flag of Australia in the Territory of Papua and New Guinea 1949-1971, and a 1962 local flag, without designs. Flags of the World (historical flags): Papua's flag from 1908 was the Australian Blue Ensign with PAPUA on a white disc, the Mandated Territory of New Guinea (1921-1942) used a defaced Blue Ensign with a crown above T.N.G. on a white disc, customs flags with initials on the Australian Blue Ensign, and from 1951 an Australian national flag customs flag with T.P. & N.G.C.; the undefaced Australian Blue Ensign was reportedly flown for customs after the war.
era-1920.open: Both sources show defaced territorial ensigns on an Australian Blue Ensign base, so the card's undefaced Australian ensign and the page's 'no distinct flag' are only partly right; the date range 1920-1975 is not matched by either source.

era-1884.says: Wikipedia dates a German Imperial Colonial Office flag to 1884-1914, a proposed German New Guinea flag of 1914 never implemented, and a Territory of Papua flag from 1906. Flags of the World (historical flags): British New Guinea used a Blue Ensign with a crown above NG on a white disc in 1885-1888 and BNG in 1888-1906, then Papua's Blue Ensign with PAPUA from 1906; the page links German New Guinea flag pages but gives no design for them.
era-1884.open: Neither source describes a split flag or a German eagle motif; the card's split design is the page's own device, and the FOTW German New Guinea pages were not read.

era-1870.says: Wikipedia: on 25 November 1842 Congress unified the flags as a red, white and blue tricolour, 'officially adopted in 1842', the obverse with arms and the reverse with the treasury seal (a lion below a Phrygian cap, 'Paz y Justicia'), last modified by decree of 15 July 2013. Flags of the World: the flag was introduced by the General Congress on 25 November 1842 and its history lists 'flag with the national coat of arms on the obverse and a Treasury Seal on the reverse' for 1842 to 1954(?), with later versions to 2013 (decree of 15 July 2013, proportions 11:20).
era-1870.open: Both publishers date the flag to 1842, so 1870 is only the start of the post-war era, not of the flag; the emblems were simplified in 1988-90 and altered by the 15 July 2013 decree, so the plain triband drawn is a simplification.

era-1864.says: Wikipedia: on 25 November 1842 Congress unified the flags as a red-white-blue tricolour with arms on the obverse and treasury seal on the reverse. Flags of the World: its history lists this version (arms obverse, treasury seal reverse) for 1842 to 1954(?) with the question mark in the source, and its 1842 page says the flag was modelled on the 1812 flag; it says nothing about the Paraguayan War (1864-1870).
era-1864.open: No source read mentions the war or states how the flag was used, worn or flown in 1864-1870; FOTW's 1842-1954(?) version span is indirect and queried, and the question of captured or variant war flags is not covered.

era-1811.says: Wikipedia: a blue flag with a six-pointed star was raised 15 May 1811; blue-yellow-red stripes were used from 17 June 1811; a red-white-blue tricolour was adopted 15 August 1812; Francia restored the blue design in 1826; Congress unified the flag as the red-white-blue tricolour on 25 November 1842. FOTW: the earliest mention of a red-white-blue tricolour in Paraguay is 15 August 1812, and the design was regularised in 1842.
era-1811.open: The page's 'same general colours' for the Francia period is wrong; Wikipedia lists blue and other flags. FOTW does not name Carlos Antonio Lopez, and Wikipedia names him only for 1842.

era-1537.says: Wikipedia: the last formally used Spanish flag was the red and yellow flag set by Charles III in 1785 for naval and military use. Flags of the World: Paraguayan troops carried white, blue and red flags in 1806 at Buenos Aires; its history lists a blue flag before the 1811 tricolours, tags a provisional blue flag as used 15 May-6 June 1811, and describes the 1812-1826 simple tricolour as bearing the arms of Asuncion on the obverse and of the King of Spain on the reverse.
era-1537.open: No source read places the Cross of Burgundy in colonial Paraguay; the sources read give no flag for 1537-1785.

era-1825.says: Wikipedia: 25 February 1825 Congress adopted the flag with the new arms; 31 March 1950 Odría removed the arms from the civil flag. FOTW: flag and arms adopted by law 25 February 1825; Decree 1323 of 31 March 1950 confirmed the plain triband as the pabellón nacional; flag without arms is civil, with arms state and war.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia: San Martín's flag decreed 21 October 1820, diagonally quartered white and red with a laurel crown and sun; replaced in March 1822 by a horizontal white band between two red ones with a golden sun, and on 31 May 1822 by a vertical triband with a golden sun; Congress adopted the red-white-red design with the new arms on 25 February 1825. FOTW: the decree of 21 October 1820 text (a quartered flag, white above and below and a second colour at the sides, with a wreath and sun); a flag of 1822; and a flag 'modified to horizontal form in 1823' because it was confused with the Spanish flag, the decree being of 25 February 1825.
era-1821.open: The sources agree on the October 1820 quartered flag but differ on the 1822-23 flags: Wikipedia has a vertical triband from 31 May 1822, FOTW a horizontal one from 1823. The page's drawing, a vertical red-white-red with a sun, matches only Wikipedia's flag of May 1822, not the 'early' quartered banner named in its caption, and neither source mentions a flag specific to 1821.

era-1542.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Peru): during the Viceroyalty of Peru the colonial-era Spanish flag flew over Peru; citing the historian Jorge Fernández Stoll, the old viceroyalty flag was the red and white cross of Burgundy. FOTW (Burgundy Cross Flag): the cross was Spain's ensign from 1506 and military flag to 1843. U.S. National Park Service: Spanish ships and fortresses in the New World flew the white flag with the red Burgundian saltire until 1785.
era-1542.open: These sources support Spanish flags, chiefly the Cross of Burgundy, over the viceroyalty, but they give no viceroyalty dates and do not describe the page's schematic drawing (a red band over a white field with three gold squares), which matches no flag read. Whether a Peruvian-specific flag existed is not addressed.

era-1532.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Peru): the colonial-era Spanish flag flew over Peru in the viceroyalty period; Wikipedia's article does not cover the conquest decade. FOTW (Spain 1506-1700 and Burgundy Cross Flag): the Burgundy cross was Spain's ensign from 1506 and 'the flag, if any was' carried by the conquistadors.
era-1532.open: No source read gives Pizarro's banner, dates for the conquest decade or a flag for it; the page's schematic Spanish banner is not described by any source.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: 1936 E.O. 23 standardised specifications; 4 July 1946 hoisted at independence; RA 8491 of 1998 codified colours; eight-rayed sun for the provinces that rebelled. FOTW: E.O. 23 (25 March 1936); E.O. 321 of 12 June 1950; RA 8491 of 12 February 1998; white triangle for the Katipunan.
era-1946.open: The blue shade changed several times (1955, 1985, 1998).

era-1565-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia: flag banned during the occupation, then used by the Second Republic. FOTW: Second Republic revived it 14 October 1943; upside-down from 8 December 1941; wartime position in 1944.
era-1942.open: The two sources describe the occupation differently.

era-1935.says: Wikipedia: ban repealed 30 October 1919; legally adopted 26 March 1920; E.O. 23 standardised specifications in 1936. FOTW: 1919 Flag Day order; E.O. 23 of 25 March 1936.
era-1935.open: The Commonwealth's start date (1935) is not covered.

era-1898.says: Wikipedia: the Flag Act of 1907 made display of the Philippine flag and Katipunan emblems illegal; it was repealed (24 October 1919 per Wikipedia, 30 October 1919 per FOTW's history), and Act No. 2928 of 26 March 1920 legally adopted the flag as the official flag of the Philippine Islands. FOTW (Quezon's history): the Civil Commission declared the Filipino flag illegal in the Sedition Act of 23 August 1907 after a nationalist election celebration; Governor General Harrison signed the repeal on 30 October 1919. FOTW's 1956 article (Quirino) puts the proscription at 6 September 1907 and says it lasted twelve years.
era-1898.open: The sources agree on the 1907-1919 ban (with differing day dates) but none describes a 'US insular ensign' or says which flag the administration flew; the American flag over the islands is implied rather than stated. Next: a source on US flag use in the Philippines (e.g. US Navy or War Department flag orders).

era-1898-1.says: Wikipedia: unfurled at Kawit on 12 June 1898, first displayed in battle on 28 May 1898. FOTW: conceived by Aguinaldo in Hong Kong in 1897, sewn there; adopted 19 May 1898; Battle of Alapan 28 May 1898; proclaimed 12 June 1898 at Kawit.
era-1898-1.open: The era title says Malolos; the proclamation was at Kawit.

era-1945.says: FOTW (explanation of the flag): the 1936 flag, with the navy blue, was restored upon the return of American forces in 1944 and was hoisted at the recognition of Philippine independence on 4 July 1946; FOTW (flag history) says the Commonwealth flew it upside down from 8 December 1941 to Japan's surrender. Wikipedia: the flag is flown red-side up in wartime and was the national flag of the Commonwealth; its Flag of the Philippines article says the flag was legally adopted in 1920 (Act 2928).
era-1945.open: The orientation flown in 1945-46 is not stated; the page's 'peacetime blue-over-red' is an inference from the 4 July 1946 hoisting.

era-1565.says: Wikipedia (Spanish East Indies; Captaincy General of the Philippines): the colony ran from 1565 to 1898/1901, governed from Manila, under New Spain until 1821 and then Madrid; neither article read has flag text. FOTW (Quezon): the triangle and stripes of the Philippine flag may trace to Spanish colonial navigational flags for the Philippines.
era-1565.open: No source read describes the flag flown in the Spanish period, and the Cross of Burgundy is not mentioned by any of them; FOTW says it has no detailed Spanish-era flags. Next: a Spanish naval-history source (e.g. Museo Naval) on ensigns in Manila.

era-1989.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1919, before this era begins in 1989, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1 August 1919; Flags of the World dates it 1 Aug 1919.
era-1989.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1947.says: FOTW (Kedzierski) says the flag was unchanged except for the eagle, and that the communists took the crown off it, without a date. Wikipedia has the crown removed in 1944–1990, the crownless emblem used from 1944 and legalised in 1952, a resolution approving the crownless design in 1955, and a decree of 7 December 1955 upholding the 1927 shade of red.
era-1947.open: This page used to say the crown was removed in 1955; the sources put it in practice from 1944. The 1980 Act (31 January 1980) is the flag law in force through the end of this era.

era-1945.says: FOTW says the flag stayed the white-red bicolour under the communists. Wikipedia's coat-of-arms article has the communist-era emblem in use from 1944.
era-1945.open: This page used to say the crowned eagle continued through 1945–47; the source has it crownless from 1944. Nothing was found specific to the Provisional Government.

era-1939.says: Wikipedia says Home Army and Peasants' Battalion insurgents wore white-red armbands in 1939-1945, that Polish soldiers raised a flag at Monte Cassino on 18 May 1944 and that a white-red flag was hoisted in Warsaw on 1 August 1944. Flags of the World (General Government page, contributor text) says German swastika flags flew in the major cities of the occupied territory and the Polish flag was forbidden on pain of death; its underground-state page says the legal symbols of the government in exile and its Delegation were those of the Second Republic; its 20th-century page says the government in exile and its troops in WWII kept using the crowned eagle.
era-1939.open: All the FOTW statements are contributor posts without a cited basis. Neither source describes a civil flag of the government in exile in detail (the page's 'white-red civil flag with the crowned eagle' is not itself described), nor the move of the government from Paris to London.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Kedzierski, citing the Encyclopaedia of Poland, 1996) says the question was resolved on 1 August 1919 with white above red; Pierre Gay explains the order heraldically. Wikipedia says the Sejm adopted the white-red bicolour on 1 August 1919, with a coat-of-arms variant for civil ensign use and diplomats abroad, and that a presidential decree of 13 December 1927 set the red as vermilion from 29 March 1928.
era-1918.open: The placement of the eagle at the hoist, as this page describes the state flag, is not confirmed: the 1980 law places the arms in the white stripe.

era-1815.says: FOTW says the Sejm formally introduced the national colours on 7 February 1831 during the November Uprising. Wikipedia says the white-red cockade was adopted that day and was worn by insurgents in 1830, 1846, 1848 and 1863-1864. FOTW's 19th-century page (contributor posts) describes an official flag of the autonomous Kingdom of Poland in 1815-1831, a white flag with a blue St Andrew's saltire and a red canton bearing a crowned eagle, says the Sejm replaced it with the white-red bicolour in 1831, and says only Russian flags were legal afterwards until the First World War.
era-1815.open: The caption's 'no official Polish flag' is contradicted for 1815-1831 by the FOTW contributors (one of whom gives 12 April 1833 for the saltire flag's abolition in Russia, a date no source confirms). Whether each partitioning power banned the white-red colours is stated only in an unsourced FOTW post about Russia; Prussian and Austrian practice is not described.

era-1807.says: Wikipedia says the Duchy of Warsaw's military wore the white cockade, and its coat-of-arms article gives the Duchy's arms as the House of Wettin combined with the Polish eagle. FOTW's 19th-century page has contributor posts that disagree: a horizontal white-amaranth flag in one, a red flag with the white eagle in another, a guess in a third. The Wikipedia article on the Duchy of Warsaw carries a hidden note in its infobox saying the Duchy did not use a national flag (see its talk page).
era-1807.open: Not established: the sources give no flag of the Duchy of Warsaw, only a cockade and arms. The FOTW posts name no basis and conflict, and the Wikipedia remark is an editors' note, not a cited statement.

era-1025.says: Wikipedia says the eagle first appeared on coins under Boleslaw I (reign 992-1025), about the year 1000, as the Piast dynasty's arms, and in the 12th century on shields, ensigns, coins and seals of the Piast dukes. A contributor on FOTW's 20th-century page says some very early Polish arms and banners had the eagle without a crown.
era-1025.open: This page says the earliest royal seals; Wikipedia says coins. Whether a white eagle on a red field was flown as a banner in 1025-1138 is not established; the uncrowned eagle rests on one unsourced contributor post.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia: Commonwealth ends in 1795; Duchy of Warsaw military wore the white cockade from 1807. Flags of the World's royal banners page ends with the banner of Stanislaw August Poniatowski (1764-1795), and its 19th-century page starts with the Duchy of Warsaw (1807); neither has anything for 1795-1807.
era-1795.open: Nothing is stated for 1795-1807 itself in Wikipedia, in FOTW's main page, 19th-century page or royal banners page. The Polish Legions of 1797-1807 were not looked up. The silence is not evidence that no banner was held.

era-1569.says: Wikipedia: Commonwealth banner first plain white with Poland's White Eagle and Lithuania's Pursuer, red and white later dominating, 17th century banners in two to four stripes. Flags of the World: Zygmunt III banner red-white-red; Wladyslaw IV and Jan Kazimierz four red and white stripes with the state crest; its royal banners page also shows banners of Zygmunt II August (the 1553 court banner, kept at Wawel, bearing many provincial arms including the Pillars of Gediminas), Zygmunt III, Wladyslaw IV and Stanislaw August, with little text.
era-1569.open: The drawing's eagle beside the Pogon on red alone is not described by any source read; the royal banners page gives pictures and brief reign notes, not a description of the design.

era-1320.says: Wikipedia says that under Ladislaus the Short (r. 1320-1333) a red cloth with the White Eagle became the Kingdom's banner, used at coronations and battles. Flags of the World gives a banner of Wladyslaw Lokietek (1320-1333) among its Polish royal banners and a red banner with a white eagle beside Jagiello at Grunwald in 1410; a contributor on its 20th-century page says the eagle gained a crown in 1295 or slightly earlier.
era-1320.open: The crown rests only on that FOTW contributor post, which gives no basis; Wikipedia does not say the eagle was crowned. A Lokietek coronation link is not stated by either source.

era-1138.says: Wikipedia: royal banner of arms dates to Boleslaus the Generous (r. 1076-1079); early vexilloids (stanice) appear by the 10th century. Flags of the World (20th-century page, a contributor) says some very early Polish arms and banners had the eagle without a crown.
era-1138.open: Piast eagle origins and duchy-by-duchy variants are not covered by Wikipedia, Flags of the World's main, historical, royal-banner or 20th-century pages. Nothing read ties any banner to the individual duchies of 1138-1320.

era-1974.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia says the republican revolution of 5 October 1910 was followed by a flag commission on 15 October 1910, the flag's first presentation on 1 December 1910, a decree published in the Diário do Governo on 19 June 1911 after approval by the Constituent Assembly, and official adoption by regulations published on 30 June 1911. FOTW says the flag and arms were adopted on 30 June 1911 and that the Assembly described two vertical bands of dark green and scarlet, green at the hoist. Wikipedia gives green as the nation's hope and red as the blood of those who died; FOTW's contributors give Hope and Sacrifice (Marques) and say the symbolism was added later (Candeias).
era-1910.open: The meanings of the colours are disputed. Neither source covers the Estado Novo era.

era-1640.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): royal flags had a white field until 1830, when the liberal government decreed blue and white, and the victorious standard became the national flag in 1834. Flags of the World: the national arms on a white rectangular field were the national flag from 1495 to 1830/34, a green Aviz-cross flag was popular but unofficial in 1640, and 'the liberal flag, a vertical bicolor of blue and white charged with the coat of arms' was used for about 80 years (1830-1910). Wikipedia's list: white arms flag 1640-1667, national flag vertical blue-white 1834-1910.
era-1640.open: The card shows only the 1830/34-1910 flag, while the era runs from 1640 and the flag was white with the arms until 1830/34; the sources differ on 1830 (FOTW, decree) versus 1834 (Wikipedia list, national flag), and neither describes a crown on the arms.

era-1580.says: Flags of the World: between 1580 and 1640 Portugal, as a separate realm under the same king, was allowed to use its own flags, and the arms-on-white flag was also used. Wikipedia's list: a Portuguese royal flag for 1578-1640 and a white sea flag with the arms on branches for 1616-1640, used at sea during the Iberian Union; Wikipedia's Flag of Portugal says Portugal kept its own flag under the personal union.
era-1580.open: The card's Cross of Burgundy 'with no separate Portuguese design' is contradicted by both publishers, which show Portuguese arms flags in use; no source read says the Cross of Burgundy flew in Portugal.

era-1139.says: Wikipedia's list of Portuguese flags: royal banner of five blue escutcheons on white from 1185, with a red border bearing yellow castles from 1248 (1248-1385), and a green Aviz cross added 1385; earlier banners (blue cross, 1095/1143) are hypothetical. Flags of the World's history page: 1185 white with five blue escutcheons (11 bezants each), 1248 red with yellow castles (number not fixed), 1385 with the Aviz cross; Wikipedia's Flag of Portugal: the Ourique legend of 1139 is myth, five-shield quinas date from Sancho I (1185, verification needed), the red bordure with castles is linked to the 1249 Algarve conquest by a weak argument, and seven castles were fixed in 1578.
era-1139.open: The card's 1139 start is not supported (the sources date the quinas to 1185 and earlier banners are hypothetical); the flag shown fits only 1248-1385, since the Aviz cross follows in 1385 and white arms flags replace banners from 1495.

era-1926.says: Wikipedia's list of Portuguese flags shows the national flag as one entry, '30 June 1911 - present', and lists other flags (navy minister 1911-1974, Prime Minister 1952-1972) that have dates in 1926-1974. Flags of the World dates the flag to 30 June 1911 and its history page describes 'the modern, republican flag' without mentioning the Estado Novo.
era-1926.open: Both sources say the current flag dates from 1911 but neither says anything about 1926-1974; a continuous '1911-present' entry is not a statement that the Estado Novo kept it unchanged, so that claim and the comparison with Spain remain unconfirmed.

era-1971.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1949, before this era begins in 1971, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 9 July 1971; Flags of the World dates it 09 Jul 1971.
era-1971.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.
