era-1916.says: Wikipedia: 1916 treaty with Britain (the nine points stand for the ninth reconciled emirate); in 1932 the British Navy suggested an official flag and Qatar added the nine-pointed serrated edge, diamonds and the word 'Qatar'; maroon was standardised in 1936; the wording and diamonds were removed in the 1960s; adopted 9 July 1971. FOTW: the distinctive flag emerged in the 1930s and in about 1949 the plain flag came into use with the colour altered from red to maroon.
era-1916.open: The sources disagree on the date maroon was fixed (Wikipedia 1936, FOTW c.1949); neither uses the word 'protectorate' and neither describes the page's intermediate plain white hoist band.

era-1868.says: Wikipedia: Qatar's historic flag, 18th century to 1860, was plain red (linked to Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a), and in the 19th century a white vertical hoist stripe was added to suit a British directive. FOTW's historical page: the first flag was plain red until about 1860, when a narrow serrated white stripe was added at the hoist (some sources say it was not originally serrated), and the flag stayed in that form to 1916.
era-1868.open: Both sources put the plain red flag before about 1860, so a plain red flag for 1868-1871 is contradicted by FOTW (red with a white hoist stripe from about 1860) and left undated by Wikipedia; neither covers the 1868 treaty or a red flag 'shared across the coast'.

era-1783.says: Wikipedia and FOTW's historical page both say Qatar's first flag was plain red, Wikipedia from the 18th century and FOTW until about 1860 (when a serrated white hoist stripe was added in FOTW); FOTW does not link it to Bahrain.
era-1783.open: Two publishers support a plain red Qatari flag to about 1860, but neither covers 1783 or Bahrain's Al Khalifa orbit, and the caption's 'Bahrain's own shared maritime color' is not supported; the 1860-1868 part of this row falls in the white-stripe period in FOTW.

era-1871.says: Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW covers the Ottoman garrison. FOTW's historical page gives the flag for 1860-1916 as red with a narrow serrated white hoist stripe, then a short-lived white flag with a red square and crescent around 1916; a contributor summary of 1930s British letters in the Qatar Digital Library says Qatar's flag was in 1929 'exactly like Bahrain's flag but dark red'. Wikipedia says a white hoist stripe was added in the 19th century to suit a British directive.
era-1871.open: No source read describes Ottoman garrison banners at Doha or an Al Thani local flag in 1871-1916 other than the white-striped red flag, whose date rests on FOTW's 'about 1860' and a contributor's 1929 description; the placeholder drawing remains unverified.

era-1989.says: Wikipedia says protesters in Timișoara on 20 December 1989 waved flags with the Communist arms cut out, and that on 27 December 1989 the National Salvation Front restored the simple tricolour of 1867. FOTW (Heimer) gives 27 December 1989 for the re-establishment of the plain tricolour without naming the instrument, says the flag with a hole became a symbol of the revolution, and gives Article 12 of the Constitution (21 November 1991) and Flag Law 75/1994.
era-1989.open: The instrument of 27 December 1989 is not named by either source.

era-1947.says: FOTW (Neumann) says that after the communist takeover in 1948 the tricolour was charged with a new coat of arms of Soviet inspiration. Wikipedia says Romania became a people's republic on 30 December 1947 and royal symbols were outlawed (citation needed), that a 1948 emblem showed a rising sun, tractor, oil drill and wheat, that a red star was added in 1952 and that the arms changed in 1965 (all citation needed).
era-1947.open: FOTW does not cover 1965. This page used to say the coat of arms formally replaced the royal one in 1965; neither source says so.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia's coat-of-arms article says that after Transylvania joined Romania its arms went in the fourth quarter and Banat's in the third, and that the lesser arms appeared in the Official Gazette no. 92 of 29 July 1921. FOTW says the tricolour was codified in 1872 as a plain tricolour with the arms on military and naval ensigns.
era-1918.open: This page used to date the new arms to 1922; the source gives 1921. Whether the flag was unchanged at the union is not described by either source.

era-1859.says: Wikipedia says the United Principalities used a red-yellow-blue horizontal tricolour in 1859–1866 and that the vertical order, blue at the hoist, yellow, red at the fly, was set on 26 March 1867. FOTW says the tricolour became the national flag in 1859 under Cuza, horizontal with blue on top until 1862 and red on top from 1862 to 1867, and that sources differ on the switch to vertical (Heimer 1866, Neumann 1867).
era-1859.open: The sources disagree on which colour was on top in 1859–62, so the drawing follows Wikipedia. This page used to say a vertical tricolour was adopted in 1861–62, and that it fused Wallachia's blue and yellow with Moldavia's red; neither source says that.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Romania): on 30 December 1947 Romania was proclaimed a people's republic and the royal coat of arms and tricolors showing it were outlawed. Wikipedia (Kingdom of Romania): the infobox shows the Flag of Romania for 1881-1947 and the text covers King Michael's 1944 coup without mentioning a flag. FOTW (ro-wr22): an army flag from 1940 carries King Michael's monogram in the corners; the tricolour with arms as a 1936-47 war flag is called doubtful by its author, who has seen no law or photograph of it. FOTW (ro-1922): royal standards of 1922-47 were used until the monarchy ended.
era-1944.open: No source describes the national flag of 1944-47 as such; the continuity of the plain tricolour rests on Wikipedia's infobox image only. Wikipedia Kingdom text read to 100,000 of 183,749 characters.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Romania): Antonescu was declared Conducator on 6 September 1940 and the state was renamed 'Legionary Romania'; the infobox still shows the Flag of Romania and the text describes no flag change. FOTW (ro-1922): the only 1940 flag item is Marshal Antonescu's personal standard, a blue-yellow-red tricolour with the lesser arms' eagle, said (Alex Danes, 2008) to have been used in Berlin on 23 November 1940; it is not a national flag change. FOTW (ro-wr22): army flags made under Michael I (crowned 1940) carry his monogram.
era-1940.open: No source states the national flag used in 1940-44 or that the Iron Guard emblem never replaced it; the tricolour's continuity rests on Wikipedia's infobox image. Wikipedia Kingdom text read to 100,000 of 183,749 characters.

era-1881.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Romania): the vertical blue-yellow-red tricolour (blue at the hoist) was set on 26 March 1867, the coat of arms placed only on army and princely flags, the civilian flag carrying none. FOTW (ro.html): the flag was codified in 1872 as a plain tricolour, military and naval ensigns carrying the arms. Wikipedia (Kingdom of Romania): the kingdom ran 1881-1947 and the Flag of Romania is its infobox flag; its arms are shown for 1881-1921. FOTW (ro-1922): the 1872 arms were used until 1921.
era-1881.open: The sources date the tricolour differently (Wikipedia 1867, FOTW 1872). Neither describes an 1881 flag change, a crown on a state version or a personal Hohenzollern flag, so the caption's 'first king's own arms' is not confirmed; FOTW says only that military ensigns carried the arms.

era-1600.says: Wikipedia: Michael the Brave's flag, black eagle on a green juniper branch with a cross in its beak, damask yellow-white faded to white (undated). Flags of the World: c. 1593-1601 white banner with raven, juniper and double cross; 1532-35 red banner with bird on peak; 1688-1714 Brancoveanu personal flag; 1834 Ghika tricolor with eagle on the yellow band. Wikipedia (Wallachia): the infobox flag is dated c.1593-1611 and its flags section lists dated images (Michael the Brave 1593-1611, Mihnea III 1658, the 1821 uprising, an 1834 war ensign, 1848, an 1858 naval ensign) but does not describe their colours.
era-1600.open: No source describes a gold field or a 17th-18th century princely flag of a black eagle on gold; Wikipedia's Wallachia captions give dates but no descriptions. The 1859 fusion of devices is not covered.

era-1600-1.says: Flags of the World: 1457-1504 Stephen III red great banner with aurochs head, star, sun and moon; c. 1600 Jeremiah Movila red banner with aurochs head and two crescent moons; 1834 Sturdza blue militia standards; 1842-48 Bibesco red flag. Wikipedia: Moldavian arms and flags in blue, yellow, red, no dates. Wikipedia (Moldavia): the 14th-15th century flag in the infobox is a modern reconstruction of a princely standard, and the attested versions of symbols other than the aurochs vary considerably; the 1829 Treaty of Adrianople assigned red-over-blue pennants; a flag 'according to the Organic Regulation' is dated 1831-1862.
era-1600-1.open: A black aurochs head and the rose are not stated in any source; Wikipedia's Moldavia text points to a separate flag article that was not read. Wikipedia text read in two parts (first 100,000 plus the remainder).

era-82bce.says: Wikipedia (Dacian Draco): the Dacian standard has the form of a dragon with open wolf-like jaws containing metal tongues, carried by Dacian soldiers in about 20 scenes of Trajan's Column (wars of 101-102 and 105-106); it is thought to have been filled by the wind and to have whistled; Rome probably adopted it after conquering Dacia, and the first Roman cavalry depiction dates to Marcus Aurelius (161-180). FOTW (ro.html and ro_legnd.html): the standard on Trajan's Column was a metal wolf's head with coloured cloth bands, Dan Dima agreeing the wolf-head standard existed but saying its colours cannot be reconstructed from marble.
era-82bce.open: Attested only as a Dacian military standard shown on Trajan's Column (101-106), not as a national flag of a kingdom from c.82 BCE; the draco's origin is disputed and its colours are not reconstructable. The page's 82 BCE start and Roman Dacia end (271) are not covered by these sources.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia says the RSFSR Supreme Soviet declared the imperial tricolour the national flag on 22 August 1991, that Decree No. 2126 of 11 December 1993 defined it as three horizontal bands with a 2:3 ratio, and that a federal constitutional law of 25 December 2000 legalised it. FOTW says the flag was raised over the Supreme Soviet building on 21 August 1991 and officially acknowledged on 22 August, that it was used alongside the Soviet flag until a December 1991 decree, that decree No. 2126 changed the ratio from 1:2 to 2:3, and that Flag Day was introduced on 22 August 1994.
era-1991.open: FOTW's contributors place the 1991 adoption steps differently (21 or 22 August). This page used to say the tricolour was the national flag from 1883 to 1917; the sources say it was authorised on land in 1883 and made the sole national flag in 1896.

era-1922.says: Wikipedia says the USSR flag was established on 18 April 1924, that rules of 23 March 1925 required the RSFSR flag on local soviet buildings, and that in January 1954 the RSFSR flag gained a light blue strip near the pole, approved by the law of 2 June 1954. Flags of the World's Soviet Union page (a contributor) says the flag with hammer, sickle and star was adopted in 1923, with a red star bordered yellow; its RSFSR pages say the RSFSR flag was revised in 1954 to add a hoist bar of one eighth of the flag's length, light blue by the 1978 constitution, and that the 1918 RSFSR flag with initials in the canton stayed in use to 1937, with another flag in 1937-1954.
era-1922.open: The sources differ on the year the USSR flag was set (1923 FOTW, 1924 Wikipedia). The page's RSFSR details (the blue stripe from 1954) belong to the republic's own flag, not the all-Union banner drawn, and the 1937-1954 RSFSR flag is not described here.

era-1917.says: Wikipedia says that on 13 April 1918 the All-Russian Central Executive Committee set a red RSFSR banner, the decree not specifying colour, size or proportions, and that the initials appear in the sample of 17 June 1918. Flags of the World (early Soviet Russia page, contributors citing orders and the 1918 constitution): a red flag with the Cyrillic initials in the canton was recommended by Order No 320 of April 1918, and a flag approved on 20 May 1918 had yellow ancient-script initials in the canton with a gold border; the flag of that pattern was readopted as war flag in 1920 and continued to 1954.
era-1917.open: The dates differ among sources for the first lettered flag (April, May and 17 June 1918). Whether plain red improvised flags were official before then is not settled, and the page's 'gold initials' is FOTW's 'yellow'.

era-1917-1.says: Wikipedia says the Provisional Government kept the white-blue-red tricolour until the October Revolution (citation needed). FOTW (Bottasini) says it was used until the fall of Kerensky's government in November 1917.
era-1917-1.open: Neither source says it was flown without a crown or eagle, as this page does.

era-1721.says: Wikipedia says the tricolour was first raised on 6 August 1693 on the yacht Saint Peter, became the commercial maritime flag by decree on 31 January 1705, that the black-yellow-white tricolour was decreed the official heraldic state flag on 23 June 1858, that white-blue-red was authorised on land on 28 April 1883, and made the sole national flag by an imperial order of 29 April 1896. FOTW says it was used as a naval ensign in 1693 without formal adoption, adopted as the merchant flag on 20 January 1705, became the civil ensign in 1799, and was recognised for use on land in 1883 as an alternate civil flag, Russia having two civil flags until 1914.
era-1721.open: FOTW and Wikipedia differ on 1693 (raised vs not formally adopted) and on 1883 (7 May or 28 April). This page used to say the tricolour became the official national flag by decree in 1883.

era-1547.says: Wikipedia: 1552 Kazan banner of the Saviour (white or red per sources); 1612 Pozharsky's crimson banner; 1669 a white banner with red border and a gold two-headed eagle for Kolomenskoye; 6 August 1693 a white-blue-red tricolour with a golden double-headed eagle on a yacht; 1696 a red taffeta banner with white border and golden eagle; the tricolour became the merchant flag on 20 January 1705. FOTW (main page, and its Tsar's personal flags page): Allard's 1695 flagbook shows a white-blue-red triband with a golden double-headed eagle; the Tsar's standard in Moscow in 1693-1699 was the tricolour with a golden eagle; a vessel standard of 1699-1917 was gold with black arms and an eagle; a flag of Ivan IV at Kazan is a dark trapezoid with an icon, stars and crosses.
era-1547.open: The gold flag with a black double-headed eagle drawn here fits FOTW's vessel standard from 1699 (inside this era only for 1699-1721), not 1547-1699, where the sources show golden eagles on white, red or tricolour grounds; the 1497 seal and 'the Tsar's own standard' wording are not covered. FOTW's Ivan IV flag is disputed by its contributors.

era-1882.says: Wikipedia lists the British Leeward Islands flag for 1871-1952 and 1952-1958 (images, no description), the West Indies Federation flag for 1958-1962, and a flag of Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla for 1958-1967 and 1967-1983, the latter described as a vertical green, yellow and blue tricolour with a palm tree at the centre. FOTW gives only the 16 February 1967 coat of arms and describes no flag for 1967-1983 or any Blue Ensign. Wikipedia (Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla): the colony was established 16 June 1882, the associated state ran 27 February 1967 to 19 September 1983, and the infobox shows flags for 1958-1967 and 1967-1983 without describing them. FOTW (kn-ai): the vertical blue-yellow-green tricolour with a black palm tree (three branches for the islands) was adopted on 27 February 1967, and the three islands were joined into one colony in 1882; it documents no Blue Ensign for the entity and asks about Leeward Islands flags 'until 1958?'.
era-1882.open: Associated state 1967-83: a palm tricolour is described by both publishers (the Blue Ensign on the page is contradicted). Colony 1882-1967: no source describes a flag or badge, so the row stays unreviewed. The page text was corrected.

era-1713.says: Wikipedia lists the British Leeward Islands flag for 1871-1952 as an image without a written description; neither page mentions the Treaty of Utrecht, any 1713 event, or a Blue Ensign. Wikipedia (Saint Kitts) also describes alternating English/British and French control through the 17th and 18th centuries but its text read does not mention the Treaty of Utrecht.
era-1713.open: No flag is described for 1713-1882/1967 by any source read; Utrecht (1713) is not in the Wikipedia text read (first 100,000 of 116,060 characters). The Blue Ensign with a Saint Kitts-Nevis badge is unconfirmed.

era-1623.says: Wikipedia (Saint Kitts): the first English colony was established in 1623, followed by a French colony in 1625; the colonists divided the island with the English in the middle and the French at both ends; a Spanish force seized the island in 1629 and the English settlement was rebuilt after the 1630 peace. Neither the Wikipedia flag page nor FOTW covers any English ensign for this span.
era-1623.open: The settlement history is sourced but no flag is described; the English ensign as 'flag of record' is the page's own choice. Nevis's 1623/1625 English status is not covered by the text read. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 116,060 characters.

era-1979.says: Wikipedia: the Pitons flag was adopted on 1 March 1967 (Associated State) and kept at independence in 1979, when 'the blue colour's shade and the triangles' sizes were modified marginally' (1979-2002: yellow triangle enlarged, arrowhead narrower); designed by Dunstan St Omer. Flags of the World (Saint Lucia): the 1967 flag (1 March 1967 - 1979) had a lower golden triangle and a lighter blue; the current flag was adopted 22 February 1979 and designed by Dunstan St Omer.
era-1979.open: The caption 'adopted 1967, unchanged since' is contradicted by both sources, which report a marginal redesign at independence in 1979; the page's description of the meaning of the colours was not checked against either source.

era-1814.says: Flags of the World (colonial flags, Prothero 2000): a Blue Ensign with the colony seal badge on a white disc, showing the island from the west with the Pitons and Soufriere, motto 'Statio Haud Malefida Carinis', c. 1875-1937 (Smith 1975: end of the 19th century; Znamierowski: to 1938), replaced by a badge approved 26 October 1937; the arms granted by royal warrant 16 August 1939 on a Blue Ensign until 1967; the first British ensign 'could date at least to' 1814. Wikipedia: Union Jack with St Patrick's saltire 1801-1875; Union Jack defaced with the 1875 arms 1875-1939 (the governor's with the same arms); Blue Ensign with the arms 1939-1967; Pitons flag 1967.
era-1814.open: The two publishers disagree on the 1875-1939 flag (Flags of the World: Blue Ensign with a seal badge; Wikipedia: a Union Jack-based flag), and no source describes a flag for 1814-1875 beyond Wikipedia's Union Jack; the Pitons appear in the 1875 seal badge but not on a Blue Ensign across 1814-1979.

era-1660.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Saint Lucia): France colonised the island in 1635 and signed a treaty with the indigenous people in 1660; the 'drapeau aux serpents' was adopted by French colonial officials in 1766 as a civil ensign (listed 1766-1796) and the King's Colours became the colony's flag after the British annexation (1796-1801). Flags of the World (colonial flags, Heimer 1997): France first settled in 1650 and during French rule the island used the same flag as Martinique; it became British in 1814.
era-1660.open: Neither source mentions a white ensign with fleur-de-lis, the count of fourteen changes of hands or the share of years each power held the island; the French settlement date differs (1635 versus 1650); Martinique's flag is not described on the page read.

era-1979.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption of the current flag as 12 October 1985; FOTW says it was introduced on 21 October 1985 when the new government rejected the 1979 independence flag, keeping the colours (blue, larger yellow, green) without white fimbriations and adding three green diamonds in the centre.
era-1979.open: The sources differ on the day (12 or 21 October 1985) but agree on 1985; the era begins at the 27 October 1979 independence, when a different flag (vertical blue-white-yellow-white-green with the arms on a breadfruit leaf) was adopted, so the 1979-1985 flag is not the one drawn. The colour meanings were not compared.

era-1763.says: Wikipedia says sovereignty switched between the French and British through the 18th century until the Peace of Paris of 1783 gave Saint Vincent to Britain. era-1997.says: Wikipedia: a red field with a blue canton bearing five white stars forming the Southern Cross, designed with four stars in 1948 and the fifth star added; infobox adopted 24 February 1949; the Official Flag and National Anthem of Samoa Act 1994 regulates it. FOTW: the flag has a red field and blue canton with five stars (construction from the official government site and the 1994 Act); the four-star flag was adopted 26 May 1948 and the five-star flag on 24 February 1949.
era-1997.open: Both sources date the design to 1948-49, not 1997; the page's statement about the fa'amatai system is not covered. FOTW notes that the country was called Western Samoa until 1997, and the name change did not alter the flag.

era-1962.says: Wikipedia: New Zealand approved the flag on 26 May 1948 (four stars), a fifth star was added on 24 February 1949, and the flag was kept at independence on 1 January 1962. FOTW (historical flags): Samoa adopted the flag on 26 May 1948 with four stars like New Zealand's, the fifth star was added on 24 February 1949, and Samoa gained independence in 1962; a Colonial Office letter says the four-star flag was approved on 9 September 1948 and the five-star version was published in the New Zealand Gazette on 24 February 1949.
era-1962.open: The exact 1948 approval date varies (26 May or 9 September 1948 in FOTW); 'adopted 1949' on the page is the date of the five-star flag. Neither source covers the 1997 change of name.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia: New Zealand occupied German Samoa on 29 August 1914; only the New Zealand flag was flown until 1920, when under the League mandate a Blue Ensign with three palms was adopted; on 26 May 1948 New Zealand approved a new flag. FOTW (historical flags): from the mandate, defaced Blue (land) and Red (sea) Ensigns with three palm trees, warrant for the Red Ensign issued 16 January 1925; the High Commissioner kept a defaced Union Jack; the 1948 four-star flag replaced the ensigns and was used ashore alongside the New Zealand Ensign.
era-1914.open: The sources show Samoa with its own defaced ensigns from 1920 and its own flag from 1948, so a plain New Zealand ensign is documented only for 1914-1920 and as the flag flown with the Samoan flag after 1948; the page's drawing is not confirmed for the span.

era-1900.says: Wikipedia (German Samoa): the protectorate lasted 1900-1914 and the imperial flag was raised at Mulinuu on 1 March 1900; its infobox shows the colonial office's service flag. FOTW (German colonies): colonies without their own arms flew the Reichsdienstflagge, and a photograph shows a normal national flag at a pavilion in Apia; FOTW (1914 colonial flags): Solf's 1914 proposal for Samoa was the black-white-red flag with a shield of three palms, which was never introduced because of the war.
era-1900.open: The sources show the imperial flags, not a Samoa-specific flag; the page's drawing, a tricolour with a shield, resembles the 1914 proposal that FOTW says was never introduced, so it is not a flag that flew in 1900-1914.

era-1862.says: The Government of San Marino (Conoscere San Marino): the flag is white over blue with the national arms at the centre, adopted on 6 April 1862 and slightly modified in 2011, and the arms took their final form on 6 April 1862 after the treaties with the Kingdom of Italy, the colours being drawn from the 14th-century arms of the three peaks of Titano. Flags of the World: flag adopted 6 April 1862 by decree of the Supreme Council (Southworth), arms in present form from that date (Pedersen). Wikipedia: the decree of 6 April 1862 standardised the coat of arms but did not mention the flag; a white-azure bicolour is first recorded in 1829.
era-1862.open: Wikipedia's infobox gives the flag as early 1800s, and says the 1862 decree concerned the arms; the page's snow and sky meanings are not in the sources, which give peace for white and liberty for light blue (Wikipedia).

era-1600.says: The Government of San Marino: the first flag, adopted in 1465, was a horizontal orange, white and violet tricolour with the arms, and the white and blue cockade of 1797 started the change that led to the colours of 1862. Wikipedia: first record of a white-azure bicolour in 1829, a white and blue cockade in 1797, unstandardised white-blue flags until 2011. Flags of the World (historical flags): the old republic flag attested in 1465 was used until about 1797, a flag like the modern one from 1797.
era-1600.open: None of the sources mentions the 1600 Statutes, and they date the white-over-blue bicolour from 1797, not 1600, so the card's bicolour before 1797 is contradicted by the 1465 tricolour.

era-301.says: Wikipedia: the oldest attested standard is dated 4 September 1465, commissioned in Florence, a tricolour of gold, white and alessandrino. The Government of San Marino describes the 1465 flag as an orange, white and violet tricolour; Flags of the World (historical flags) dates the attested old republic flag to 1465. The Government page says the present colours are drawn from the 14th-century arms of the three peaks of Titano.
era-301.open: No source covers the founding legend of c.301 or any flag before 1465, and none dates white-over-blue colours to this era.

era-1926.says: Wikipedia says the Nejd state flag followed today's Saudi pattern very closely and the Hejaz flag followed pan-Arab patterns. FOTW (evolution of the flag, citing the Flag Bulletin): the next design stage 'may have been introduced' at the unification as the Kingdom of the Hijaz and of Nejd and its Dependencies in February 1927, with the shahada in thuluth script filling nearly the whole field; in 1925 Abdulaziz became King of Nejd and Hejaz 'with unknown flag alterations' and Hussein had used the Arab Revolt flag. Saudipedia: the sword was placed below the shahada under Abdulaziz and the form approved in 1937.
era-1926.open: The union's flag in 1926-32 is not established: FOTW says unknown/may have been, Saudipedia gives no 1926 flag; the page's 'sword carried over' is unconfirmed.

era-1902.says: Wikipedia says a different Arabic inscription was used in 1902-1921 and that the sword was added in 1921 by Abdulaziz. FOTW (evolution of the flag): the sword was added in 1902 when Abdulaziz established himself as Sultan of Nejd (one contributor, 1996); FOTW (Nejd and Hasa): rbvex.it reports a green flag with a white hoist and white inscriptions, with or without, used 1902-1921, while the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa's flag is a Wikipedia reconstruction without proof. Saudipedia (Saudi encyclopedia): King Abdulaziz adopted the First Saudi State flag with a sword beneath the shahada, without a date.
era-1902.open: The sources conflict on when the sword was added (1902 per FOTW's contributor, 1921 per Wikipedia; Saudipedia gives no date), and none links a flag to the retaking of Riyadh.

era-1818.says: Saudipedia says the First Saudi State's flag continued to be used through the Second Saudi State; Wikipedia says followers of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab used the shahada on flags from the 18th century and that the Al Rashid emirate of Jabal Shammar opposed the Saudis until 1921. FOTW (Ha'il): the Rashidi emirate (1835-1920) is shown in Wikipedia with an Ottoman-like flag with a thin golden crescent and an eight-pointed star, from an Arabic Wikipedia and a dead website.
era-1818.open: Nothing read describes flags for the Ottoman-Egyptian occupation (1818-1840) or the Najd under Rashidi rule from a primary or reference source; the Second Saudi State's green flag rests on Saudipedia's one sentence; the page's drawing remains a placeholder.

era-1744.says: Saudipedia (citing the Saudi Press Agency): the First Saudi State, founded 1727 by Imam Muhammad bin Saud at Diriyah, flew a green flag of silk and wool with a white part by the pole and the shahada in the centre (no sword; the sword was added under King Abdulaziz). Wikipedia: followers of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab used the shahada on their flags from the 18th century. FOTW: shahada on solid green was an old flag of the Wahhabi reformist movement of the late 18th century.
era-1744.open: Saudipedia dates the state's foundation to 1727, not 1744 as on the page; FOTW notes that the flag's exact age is unclear and that 19th-century accounts (Baxter, 1934) give it as about a century old.

era-1999.says: FOTW's Scotland page says the saltire became much more prominent from the 1970s and that on 1 July 1999, the day the Scottish Parliament opened, the Union Flag and the Saltire were both used but normally only the Saltire is flown (the Union Flag flew at Edinburgh Castle; the General Assembly building, the Parliament's temporary home, flew both). Wikipedia says the Saltire is the correct flag for private individuals and bodies and is flown, where possible, from Scottish Government buildings every day.
era-1999.open: Neither source says the Saltire was flown over a new Parliament building in 1999 as such (the Parliament sat in the General Assembly building); Wikipedia gives no date for the government-buildings practice. FOTW's note that the Union Flag is also used is a 1999 observation. The 1801 date in FOTW's UK page is the Union Flag, not the saltire.

era-1707.says: Wikipedia: James VI's proclamation on the Union flag of 12 April 1606, a design presented to Queen Anne in 1707 with the English cross uppermost, and St Patrick's cross added in 1801. FOTW: James VI/I combined the Scottish and English flags in 1606, Queen Anne continued that design in 1707 (a Scottish version put the saltire over St George's cross), and the modern Union flag was introduced in 1801.
era-1707.open: Neither source says the Union Flag was used 'mainly at sea' after 1707; FOTW says only that the saltire became much more prominent in the 1970s.

era-1603.says: Wikipedia dates the Union of the Crowns to 1603, the Union flag proclamation to 12 April 1606, the Scottish Privy Council's protest to 7 August 1606 and an unofficial Scottish Union Flag variant used at sea in the 17th century. FOTW's chronology: the saltire on blue 1542, a Scottish ship illustrated with three saltires in 1588, the Union flag in 1606, and Queen Anne continuing it in 1707 with a Scottish version having the saltire over St George's cross.
era-1603.open: Neither source states that the Saltire was flown domestically as Scotland's own flag throughout 1603-1707 (the dated saltire items fall before 1603 or concern the Union flag), and no reference source on Scottish flag use in the 17th century was found in the pages read.

era-1249.says: Wikipedia's Royal Banner article: the earliest recorded use of the lion rampant as a royal emblem was by Alexander II in 1222, the double border set with lilies came under Alexander III (1249-1286), and a royal banner displaying the arms was used by the King of Scots until the Union, now restricted by statute. FOTW's royal banner page: 1222 seal of Alexander II as the first known lion coat, and the double tressure first definitely on a seal of Alexander III (d. 1286); the lion on yellow also appears on the Great Michael's flag. On the Saltire both Wikipedia and FOTW give the 1286 seal of the guardians, the 1385 ordinance, 1503/1507 and 1542.
era-1249.open: The lion rampant is dated to 1222, before this row's 1249 start, and the red-on-gold standard's colours are given only by FOTW's blazon (or, a lion rampant gules within a double tressure flory counter-flory); the 'personal banner' wording is the page's own. The Saltire on blue is first certain in 1542 (FOTW) or 1507 (Wikipedia).

era-843.says: Wikipedia's flag article reports as legend that the Saltire's use as Scotland's flag began on the eve of the Battle of Athelstaneford in 832, and its village article tells the story of Saint Andrew's vision to the Pictish King Oengus II and the white cross in the sky. FOTW's legend page gives the same story from the chronicles of Fordun, Boece, Leslie, Spottiswoode and Bower (the king is 'Hungus', the enemy Athelstan's Angles), notes Nick Groom's report that the tale rests on a lost source of c.1165, and FOTW's main page says the earliest record of the flag (1165) refers to a 9th-century battle with no surviving original.
era-843.open: Both treat it as a legend, not as a documented banner; the date varies (832 in Wikipedia and Groom, 'about the 8th century' in FOTW's account, and about 800 in Spottiswoode), and FOTW dates the oldest surviving record to 1180 (a seal) where the cross is a religious emblem. Neither source mentions the Kingdom of Alba or the 843 start used for this row.

era-20.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1959.says: Wikipedia: on 4 April 1959 Senegal merged with French Sudan to form the Mali Federation, whose new green, yellow and red vertical tricolour bore a stylised kanaga figure on the centre band; on 20 August 1960 Senegal left, kept the colours and replaced the kanaga with a green star. FOTW: Mali Federation formed 4 April 1959, independence 20 June 1960, Senegal seceded 22 August 1960 (also given as 20 August) and replaced the 'kanaga (black man figure)' with a green star.
era-1959.open: Bambara and Dogon origin of the kanaga, and Mali's later retention of it, are not covered; FOTW and Wikipedia differ on the day (20 or 22 August 1960).

era-1659.says: Wikipedia (Saint-Louis): the French moved their fort to the island of Ndar in 1659, and nine chartered companies succeeded one another in administering Saint-Louis between 1659 and 1779; Wikipedia's Flag of Senegal says French authorities barred Senegal from using its own distinctive colonial flag (undated) and that a yellow star on green was used by the Republic of Senegal in 1958-59. FOTW (Senegal) points to French flags of the governor-general of French West Africa and governor of Senegal on its France pages and shows only the 1958-59 pre-independence flag among its colonial pages.
era-1659.open: No page read states which flag flew over Saint-Louis or French West Africa (the tricolour is the page's assertion; the chartered companies' own flags are not described), and the 1659 start is for the French settlement, not any flag.

era-2006.says: Wikipedia says an Assembly recommendation of 2004 reintroduced the state and civil flags, the new constitution of 2006 sanctioned them, the Law on National Symbols was enacted in 2009 and the flags were standardised, with colour values, in 2010. FOTW says the Assembly declared Serbia the successor of Yugoslavia on 5 June 2006 and raised the state flag, that a 2009 law fixed 3:2 proportions with the lesser arms toward the hoist, and that the Government fixed the official designs on 11 November 2010.
era-2006.open: The flag's first return was 2004; 2006 is the constitution and independence.

era-279bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no state flag from Illyrian tribes, Roman Moesia, or the early medieval Serbian principality».
era-279bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Serbia and Montenegro gives adoption in 1992 and relinquishment in 2006. FOTW's page on the union says the flag was adopted 27 April 1992, a horizontal blue-white-red, and describes the UN-building flag as the old Yugoslav flag without the red star; the page runs to the end of the union in 2006.
era-1992.open: Colour shades were not checked against a specification. FOTW's separate Serbia page (1992-2004) shows Serbia's own red-blue-white flag in the same years; this era concerns the federal flag.

era-1882.says: Wikipedia says the Kingdom adopted a state flag with arms and a civil flag without in 1882. FOTW says the kingdom kept the principality's tricolour as its national flag, with a civil ensign and a state flag carrying the royal arms (a crowned double-headed eagle bearing the cross-and-firesteels shield) in the centre, used until 1918.
era-1882.open: The page text and drawing put a plain shield with cross and four letters on the blue band; neither source describes the arms that way. The civil flag's exact form differs between the two sources.

era-1878.says: Wikipedia says the four six-pointed stars were removed after the Congress of Berlin in 1878; FOTW's Principality page agrees (stars removed from the canton in 1878; flag unchanged until the kingdom's new arms in 1882) and says the plain tricolour was the civil flag while the state flag carried the arms.
era-1878.open: The page said the arms were not added until 1882; FOTW says the state flag kept the principality's arms through 1878-82 (only the stars went), so the plain tricolour drawn here is the civil flag.

era-1804.says: Wikipedia: Sretenje Constitution flag 15 Feb 1835 (abolished April 1835), a firman of December 1835 allowing a red-blue-white merchant tricolour, and a firman of January 1839 setting arms on the blue band and four six-pointed stars on the red band. FOTW's Principality page: the Takovo flag of 1815 was white with a large red Greek cross (per Paja Jovanovic's painting), the 1835 constitution flag, a Sultan's decree of autumn 1835 granting the tricolour, and a compromise of December 1838 adding arms and stars, used to 1878. FOTW's uprising page says 1804 banners had no fixed colours.
era-1804.open: Takovo flag: FOTW only; Wikipedia's Flag of Serbia does not mention it (its painting article describes a red cross on white as painted, not as a documented flag). The sources date the arms-and-stars flag differently (December 1838 against January 1839).

era-1944.says: FOTW says Serbia in Socialist Yugoslavia used a red-blue-white flag with a star, officially adopted 17 January 1947 (the coat of arms carried a red star). Wikipedia says the Socialist Republic kept the tricolour with a red star from 1947 to 1991, preceded by a Serbian Partisan flag in 1945-47, and that the star was removed in 1992.
era-1944.open: 1944-47 was a Partisan-flag interlude, not the tricolour with star. Neither source describes the star's gold border.

era-1918.says: FOTW describes the Kingdom's flag as blue-white-red, in use before the law and formally introduced with the 1921 constitution and prescribed by Article 2 of the 1922 law; Wikipedia's «Flag of Yugoslavia» gives the 1922 law. Wikipedia's «Flag of Serbia» says Serbia's tricolour use ended with the creation of the Kingdom in 1918.
era-1918.open: This page's statement that the blue-white-red was «presented as a neutral flag for the whole kingdom» was not found in either source.

era-1166.says: FOTW says the oldest described Serbian flag is a red-and-blue silk flag in a 1281 Dubrovnik inventory, and cautions that the usual red-blue bicolour reconstruction has no evidence behind it; Wikipedia gives the same 1281 item (colour order unknown), the 1339 Dulcert chart (red double-headed eagle, white field per Wikipedia, yellow per FOTW) and says medieval flags were dynastic, not state flags.
era-1166.open: Nothing read dates a Nemanjic eagle flag before 1339; the 1166-1281 span has no flag evidence and the field colour of the eagle flag is disputed between the two sources.

era-1941.says: FOTW's page on Serbia in the Second World War says its author found no reference to a flag for the Nedic regime and guessed the Serbian colours continued to fly; it says the Serbian Volunteer Corps flag was the regular Serbian flag with the corps emblem, and that Chetniks used black flags with texts such as 'Freedom or Death'. Wikipedia's Flag of Serbia has nothing on 1941-44.
era-1941.open: FOTW's remarks are the author's inference and uncited; no source read establishes a state flag for 1941-44. Wikipedia's Government of National Salvation article shows a flag image in its infobox but its text was not found to describe one. Not looked for: Serbian archives or Samardzic.

era-1459.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Serbia starts the Ottoman-era tricolour story in 1835; FOTW's uprising page says banners in 1804 were borrowed from churches or haiduk bands and had no fixed colours. Neither describes a flag of the Pashalik of Belgrade.
era-1459.open: Sanjak of Smederevo on Wikipedia shows infobox flags for 1459-1817 (Habsburg 1686-91 and 1718-39 entries) without text sources; not accepted as evidence. No flag for 1459-1804 is established.

era-1402.says: Wikipedia mentions a 1439 portolan chart (Gabriel de Vallseca) showing a flag of Emperor Dusan; FOTW's medieval page covers the 13th-14th centuries only (1281 inventory, Dulcert 1339, Hilandar flags attributed to Dusan). Neither covers Lazarevic's arms or a Hungarian-vassal shield.
era-1402.open: The Despotate's own flag is not described by any source read; Wikipedia's Serbian Despotate infobox has no flag image.

era-1371.says: Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Serbia nor FOTW's Serbia pages (main, medieval, uprisings) mention Prince Lazar or Moravian Serbia flags; Wikipedia's Moravian Serbia infobox carries a flag image with no supporting text.
era-1371.open: The claims that no banner survives and that a red cross 'Lazarica' banner comes only from later legend are not covered; not found in any page read.

era-1346.says: Wikipedia says Dusan was crowned emperor in 1346 and adopted the fire-steel motif, and that the 1339 Dulcert chart shows a white flag with a red double-headed eagle; it also says the later kings' flag was a red double-headed eagle on yellow (occasionally white). FOTW describes the same chart as a red two-headed eagle on a yellow field above Skopje and describes two triangular flags kept at Hilandar that tradition attributes to Dusan.
era-1346.open: The sources agree on a red double-headed eagle but differ on the field (white, or yellow) and neither shows an imperial cross-and-firesteel shield; the page's drawing of that shield is unconfirmed.

era-1996.says: Both sources give 1996, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 8 January 1996; Flags of the World dates it 18 June 1996.
era-1996.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1977.says: WP: after Mancham was overthrown by France-Albert René in 1977 a red, white and green flag with a wavy white stripe, based on the SPUP flag, was used for 19 years until 1996. FOTW: a green, white and red wavy flag replaced the 1976 flag after a year following the coup.
era-1977.open: Neither source mentions a palm tree or star or the page's colour meanings. WP is inconsistent on the colours' attribution (SPUP vs United Seychelles).

era-1976.says: WP: independence flag (29 June 1976) with alternating blue and red triangles, used 1976-77. FOTW: white saltire dividing blue (hoist/fly) and red (top/bottom) fields.
era-1976.open: The page's green-white-red banded flag with shield is not supported by either source; meanings of colours not given.

era-1810.says: Flags of the World (colonial flags page): the Blue Ensign with a badge approved in April 1961 (Mrs McEwen, Toronto; a giant tortoise, coco-de-mer tree, boat and fish, based on an earlier design attributed to General Charles Gordon) was used 1961-1976, and the earlier flag with Gordon's badge from 1903 to 1961; before 1903 Seychelles was administered as a dependency of Mauritius; the United Kingdom proclaimed sovereignty in 1814. Wikipedia: colonial flags 1903-1961 (badge by Gordon) and 1961-1976 (badge by McEwen), with Governor's flags, and Seychelles a dependency of Mauritius before 1903.
era-1810.open: Both publishers support a badged Blue Ensign only for 1903-1976 (FOTW names the Blue Ensign for 1961 on); nothing read gives a flag for 1810-1903, and FOTW dates British sovereignty to 1814 rather than 1810.

era-1756.says: Flags of the World (colonial flags page): Captain Nicolas Morphey took possession for Louis XV on 1 November 1756; the colonies founded in 1770 and 1772 failed; on 30 July 1791 a corvette brought the Tricolor; Governor Quinssy surrendered to the British in 1794, hoisting the Union Jack, and later returned to the Tricolore; the UK proclaimed sovereignty in 1814. Wikipedia's Flag of Seychelles page does not cover the French period.
era-1756.open: The Tricolor in 1791 is FOTW's alone, and no source read describes the royal ensign at the 1756 taking of possession; the card's end of French rule in 1810 differs from FOTW's 1814.

era-1961.says: Both sources give 1961, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 27 April 1961; Flags of the World dates it 1961.
era-1961.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1896.says: Wikipedia: the colony and protectorate's flag of 1889-1916 was a Blue Ensign defaced with a circle (elephant, oil palm, mountains, initials S.L.), and from 1916 to 1961 with a badge showing an oil palm and an African person watching a ship arrive; arms were granted in 1914. FOTW's colonial flags page gives the same: the 1889-1914 Blue Ensign with an S.L. badge and the 1916-1961 blue ensign whose badge (after Barraclough, 1965) shows a liberated slave, a ship and a palm tree with the motto 'Auspice Britannia Liber'.
era-1896.open: The sources date the first flag to 1889, not 1896, and neither uses the name 'Lion Mountains' for the badge; the drawn badge is schematic.

era-1808.says: Wikipedia: crown colony from 1808 using the Blue Ensign defaced with the territory's arms, no specific flag given for 1808-1889; its colony article gives 1808-1961. FOTW's colonial flags page starts with the 1889 Blue Ensign and badge and describes nothing earlier.
era-1808.open: A plain undefaced Blue Ensign for 1808-1889, as drawn, is not supported by either source; neither describes a flag for those 80 years.

era-1787.says: Wikipedia: land near Bunce Island was acquired in 1787 by philanthropists and abolitionists for freed slaves; FOTW's colonial flags page notes the 1916 badge showed the Union Flag as it was before 1801. Neither mentions the Province of Freedom, the Sierra Leone Company or a flag for the settlement.
era-1787.open: Whether the settlement flew the Union Jack is not covered; the drawing also shows the post-1801 Union Jack with St Patrick's cross, which did not exist before 1801.

era-1963.says: Wikipedia: Malaysian flag hoisted over Singapore 16 September 1963; Singapore flag reconfirmed 9 August 1965; no statement on flying both. FOTW: the question whether Singapore kept its 1959 flag in Malaysia is raised and unanswered.
era-1963.open: Whether the 1959 flag flew inside Malaysia, and alongside the federal flag, is not stated by either source.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: Singapore adopted its own Crown Colony flag after the war, modified from the Straits Settlements flag with one crown instead of three (captions 1946-1952 and 1952-1959); the 1959 flag was adopted on 3 December 1959. Flags of the World's page on the Crown Colony of Singapore 1946-1959 shows a Blue Ensign with a Tudor crown badge for the colony; its main page says the Union Jack flew over Singapore 1819-1959 and that the 1959 flag was adopted on 3 December 1959.
era-1946.open: FOTW's main page conflicts with its own sub-page and with Wikipedia (Union Jack only); its sub-page is a short contributor note without a cited basis, asking itself about the crown change in 1953. The colony flag is established for 1946-1959; for 1959-1963 the 1959 self-government flag applies, as the page says.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Singapore): the Japanese national flag was used on land by the military and at public events. Wikipedia's Syonan-to article shows the Japanese merchant flag of 1870 in its infobox as the flag of the occupied territory. FOTW does not cover the occupation (no Singapore or Japan page found for it).
era-1942.open: A separate Syonan-to flag, the page's 'military administration ensign' wording, and whether any Singaporean flag flew are not covered; the two Wikipedia articles both point to a Japanese national or merchant flag, one publisher.

era-1819.says: Wikipedia: Singapore was part of the Straits Settlements, whose flag was a Blue Ensign with a red diamond holding three gold crowns; the city had no separate flag. Flags of the World's Straits Settlements page, citing National Archives files: Singapore (bought 1819 and 1824) was administered with Penang and Malacca as the Straits Settlements from 1826, made a Crown Colony in 1867, with a Blue Ensign and a gold crown badge c.1868-c.1880, then the three-crown lozenge badge; the flag was adopted in 1874 and discontinued in 1942. FOTW's main page says the Union Jack flew over Singapore 1819-1959.
era-1819.open: The ensign is established for about 1868-1942 only; the flag over the 1819-1826 trading post and under the East India Company before 1867 is not described, and FOTW's 'Union Jack 1819-1959' conflicts with its own Straits Settlements page.

era-1993.says: Wikipedia says the flag was adopted on 1 March 1990 as the flag of the Slovak Republic within Czechoslovakia, initially without the arms, that the constitution of 3 September 1992 added the coat of arms on the hoist side, and that a law of February 1993 described the details. FOTW says Slovak legislation of 1 March 1990 laid down the plain tricolour, that the constitution was enacted on 1 September 1992 with the flag in article 9, paragraph 2, that the flag was first hoisted on 3 September 1992 in front of Bratislava Castle, that the arms were added because the plain flag could be mistaken for Russia's, and that a law of 18 February 1993 set the shield's proportions.
era-1993.open: The sources differ on 1 or 3 September 1992 and on the article number. This page used to say the arms were first codified in 1939.

era-1990.says: Both sources say a Slovak flag, the plain white-blue-red tricolour, was adopted on 1 March 1990 within Czechoslovakia (Wikipedia: the interior ministry tasked Čisárik and Vrtel with the design). FOTW (Heimer) adds that the state flag was unchanged by that legislation.
era-1990.open: This page shows the Czechoslovak flag for 1990–93 and does not mention the Slovak flag of 1 March 1990. The «hyphen war» was not covered by either source.

era-1939.says: FOTW (Kravcik) says a law of 23 June 1939 enacted the white-blue-red tricolour as the Slovak State's flag. Wikipedia says the Slovak Republic used the flag during the war and that a war flag existed for its military.
era-1939.open: This page used to say the arms were added to the flag in 1939; neither source says so, and FOTW says they were added by the 1992 constitution. The 1939 constitution was not covered.

era-1938.says: Wikipedia (List of Slovak flags): the white-blue-red flag was the official flag of the autonomous Slovak land in 1938-1939; Wikipedia (Flag of Slovakia) lists the flag of the autonomous land in a caption and says the tricolour's current form dates back to 1848. Flags of the World (Slovakia 1848): the first Slovak white-red bicolour dates to 23 April 1848 at Brezova, blue was added in August 1848, and the tricolour was in use since then, mostly unofficially; it does not describe 1938-39.
era-1938.open: Wikipedia's wording that the tricolour was official in the autonomous land conflicts with the page's 'informal' use alongside the state flag; neither the Wikipedia article on the land nor FOTW describes the flag in that period, so it is left unreviewed.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sache) says the white-red flag was first officially hoisted in Washington on 18 October 1918, and Wikipedia says the National Assembly approved the flag with a blue hoist triangle on 30 March 1920 to distinguish it from Poland's.
era-1918.open: These sources are about the Czechoslovak flag, not Slovakia specifically; neither says the blue was chosen to include Slovakia (FOTW: the third Slavic colour from 1848; a Slovak-mountains reading is «late mythology»).

era-1699.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Hungary): the red-white-green colours were visible at a coronation in 1790, formally described in 1806 and mandated by Act XXI of 1848. Flags of the World (Hungary): the official colours of the flag of the Kingdom of Hungary were stated in 1806; contributors say the tricolour was first used in 1801 by Palatine Joseph or from the 1830s, and a quoted book gives 1608; for 1867-1918 the tricolour was flown with or without the arms, which changed by period.
era-1699.open: None of the sources read supports a single red-white-green flag with the Holy Crown arms flown from 1699, nor says anything on the Slovak counties; the first dates are 1608, 1790, 1801 or 1806 depending on the source.

era-1000.says: Wikipedia (Arpad stripes): barry of eight gules and argent, four red and four silver stripes, depicted from 1202 on the seal of King Emeric, on a Zurich armorial of about 1340 and in a Chronicon Pictum banner of about 1360; a claim that Stephen I used a striped banner is marked as needing a citation. Wikipedia (Flag of Hungary) adds a dynasty standard in the 13th century. Flags of the World (Kingdom of Hungary): Revnivtsev says the Arpad stripes flag was used by Arpad kings 1000-1301; the stripes appear on royal seals from the early 13th century.
era-1000.open: The 1000 start date rests on one FOTW contributor; Wikipedia's earliest evidence is 1202. Neither source says the banner flew in Slovak-inhabited counties, which the page asserts.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Slovakia): Czechoslovakia used its own flag in 1920-1939 and 1945-1992; Wikipedia (List of Slovak flags): the Czechoslovak flag was used 1920-1992. Flags of the World (Czechoslovakia): Sensen writes that through these periods the state used the same flag, and Heimer that the flag of the state was unchanged by the 1990 laws; the 1960 and 1963 arms, not the flag, added a red shield with a star that Kriżan says represented Communism.
era-1948.open: FOTW's Slovakia page is silent on 1948-90; whether any Communist emblem was ever put on the flag itself is answered only by the contributors' statement that it stayed unchanged.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: Czechoslovakia used its own flag in 1945-1992 and the 1939-45 government in exile used it too. Flags of the World (Czechoslovakia): Sensen writes the state used the same flag at all these times, and the Czech Republic adopted it; its Slovakia pages say a 1939 law gave the Slovak State its own white-blue-red flag.
era-1945.open: The 1945-48 restoration is not described as a separate event by either source; the page's 'deliberate break' wording is its own comment.

era-1526.says: Wikipedia (Arpad stripes): rulers who used the stripes include Janos Szapolyai (1526-1540) and Gabor Bethlen in the 17th century, but the stripes fell out of use as a flag after the Middle Ages and were revived by Rakoczi's cavalry in 1703-1711. Flags of the World (Kingdom of Hungary) does not cover Habsburg-era royal banners for 1526-1699 systematically and lists only scattered items such as a 1664 Zrinski flag and coronation flags from 1618.
era-1526.open: Neither source describes the flag of Royal Hungary or says the pre-Mohacs flag 'continued unbroken'; Wikipedia says the opposite for the stripes as a flag. Slovakia's own place in it is not covered.

era-1991.says: Both sources give 1991, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 25 June 1991; Flags of the World dates it 27 June 1991.
era-1991.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-200bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — Celtic Noricum, Roman province, and Slavic migration, no flag survives».
era-200bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1945.says: FOTW (Heimer, 1996) describes a white-blue-red flag with a star, officially adopted on 18 January 1947. Wikipedia says a red star was officially placed on the republic's flag in 1945.
era-1945.open: The dates differ: 1945 (Wikipedia) and 1947 (FOTW) for the start; FOTW gives the flag's abandonment as 27 June 1990, Wikipedia the removal of the star and adoption of the new flag as 27 June 1991. This page says 1945–1991. Neither source mentions the gold border on the star that this page describes.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia says the Partisans and the Slovene Home Guard both used Slovene national colours and that the Partisan flag, with a red star, was adopted on 26 September 1941. FOTW says the Home Guard, created by the German occupiers, used a Slovenian tricolour with the Carniola-derived arms, describes Partisan flags that are only vaguely like the postwar Yugoslav flag, and says it is not quite clear whether the Ljubljana Province arms were used as a flag before 1943. Wikipedia (Province of Ljubljana): Italy annexed the Ljubljana province in 1941 (formed 3 May 1941, abolished 9 May 1945); Germany and Hungary occupied and annexed the north, Germany also a strip along the Sava and Sentvid; the article describes no flag. FOTW (si^wwii) covers German- and Italian-linked formations but not Hungarian occupation flags.
era-1941.open: No source read says which national flags flew in each zone, and none supports the caption's 'Slovenia had none of its own' (FOTW and Wikipedia describe Slovene tricolours used by the Home Guard and the Partisans). Hungarian-zone flags are not covered by FOTW.

era-1918.says: FOTW describes the flag as blue-white-red, formally introduced with the 1921 constitution and prescribed by Article 2 of the 1922 law. Wikipedia's «Flag of Slovenia» says the whole kingdom officially used a blue-white-red flag while the Slovene tricolour stayed associated with Slovenia, and «Flag of Yugoslavia» gives the 1922 law.
era-1918.open: Wikipedia's infobox gives 1918 and its text 1922 for the flag's adoption. FOTW says the Slovene tricolour was soon banned or rarely tolerated under the kingdom.

era-29.says: Wikipedia gives the proclamation of the State as 29 October 1918 and its union with the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes as 1 December 1918 (Boban, 1993), and shows a flag image it does not describe. FOTW's Slovenia page says Slovenes adopted the tricolour when they joined the State in 1918 but that the State was too short-lived for the flag to be made official, and gives no colour order. For the successor Kingdom, Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia) and FOTW (yu_shs) both give a horizontal blue-white-red tricolour (blue on top), based on the 1848 Pan-Slavic flag; FOTW says it was used before the law and formally introduced in 1921, Wikipedia that the first flag was officially adopted in 1922.
era-29.open: Neither source says what flag the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs itself flew or in what order. The page's red-white-blue order is the reverse of the Kingdom's documented blue-white-red and remains unconfirmed.

era-1816.says: Wikipedia dates the Kingdom of Illyria from the patent of 3 August 1816 to 8 December 1849 and shows a flag image without describing it. Kamra (text credited to Slovenian Wikipedia): the Congress of Vienna recognised Austrian control, the territory was re-established in 1816 as the Illyrian Kingdom without Dalmatia, and it was abolished officially in 1849. FOTW (ah-land) does not mention the Kingdom of Illyria and says the Empire allowed colours only, not national or state flags.
era-1816.open: No source describes the flag; the white-over-red flag with an eagle on this page is unconfirmed. Kamra repeats Wikipedia, so is not independent. A FOTW search found only the Gorizia page listing the Litorale as an Illyrian province, not a flag.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia (Illyrian Provinces): 1809-1814/1815, the infobox flag links to the Flag of France; Treaty of Schonbrunn 14 October 1809; official languages initially French, Italian and German, with Croatian and Slovenian added in 1811, and a plan for Slovene-language elementary and secondary schooling in Slovene areas; the ecoles centrales had French as official language; Austria recovered the area in 1813-1814. Kamra (text credited to Slovenian Wikipedia): founded 14 October 1809; official notices in French and German, a Slavic edition only planned; Austrian forces entered in 1813.
era-1809.open: The French tricolour rests on Wikipedia's infobox link only; no second source or FOTW page describing it was found. The Slovene-schooling point is a plan in Wikipedia and Kamra does not state the language of instruction. Wikipedia text read to 100,000 of 106,207 characters.

era-973.says: FOTW says the white-blue-red tricolour was hoisted in Ljubljana on 7 April 1848, now Slovenia's flag day, and was used in 1848–1918 as the landesfarben of Carniola, which the Austrian rulers hardly recognised; it says Ferdinand I restored the Carniolan arms in 1836. Wikipedia says the tricolour was raised on 7 April 1848 by Lovro Toman and students and later recognised by Austria as Carniola's official flag.
era-973.open: The sources name different designers (Toman and students; Peter Kozler and Anton Globočnik). Wikipedia marks the 1836 date citation-needed, and FOTW's 1836 entry concerns the arms rather than the colours. Nothing was found for a Carniolan flag before 1848.

era-1849.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Slovenia): after 1848 the Austrian government recognised the white-blue-red tricolour as Carniola's official flag. Wikipedia (Duchy of Carniola): Ferdinand I recognised white-blue-red as Carniolan colours in 1836, confirmed in 1848 as the crownland's official flag colours; Carniola a separate crown land from 1849 to 29 October 1918. FOTW (si.html): 1848-1918 the tricolour was Carniola's landesfarben, hardly recognised by Austrian rulers. FOTW (ah-land, Rosenfeld list c.1883-85): Carniola white-blue-red, Carinthia red-white, Styria green-white; the Empire permitted colours only, not national or state flags.
era-1849.open: The sources disagree on how far Austria recognised the tricolour. None describes a shared black-and-gold Habsburg banner for the crownlands, so the page's caption and drawing are unconfirmed; the crownland colours given by FOTW are different from black and gold.

era-1813.says: Wikipedia (Illyrian Provinces): the Austrian Empire recovered the area in 1813-1814 and formal annexation followed at the Congress of Vienna on 9 June 1815. Kamra: Austria declared war in August 1813, Dubrovnik was occupied 20 September 1813 and Zadar fell 6 December 1813; the Illyrian Kingdom was re-established in 1816. Neither Wikipedia (Flag of Slovenia) nor FOTW (si.html) covers a flag for the interval.
era-1813.open: No source read describes a flag for 1813-1816; this is not a finding that none existed.

era-828.says: Wikipedia (March of Carniola): Friulian dukes held jurisdiction 788-828, governors of Bavaria from 828, the lands in East Francia from 843, the march probably dating from the late ninth century, first explicit mention in an imperial charter of 973, and separated from Bavaria in 976 as part of the new Duchy of Carinthia; the article's infobox shows an image captioned Flag of Carniola whose file name refers to the March of Verona and Aquileia, with no description in the text. FOTW dates Carniolan arms (Andechs red eagle) to the early 13th century, after this span.
era-828.open: No flag for 828-973 is described in any source read; the infobox image is not evidence of a period flag. The dates are now sourced; the absence of a flag is not a finding.

era-658.says: Wikipedia (Carantania): principality 658-828, no flag or arms described. Wikipedia (Black panther (symbol)): the current form was first reconstructed by Jozko Savli in the 1980s; there is no direct evidence of the symbol from Carantania; the panther appears on arms of Carinthian and Styrian lords (Sponheim, Duke Herman II, Margrave Ottokar III). 24ur.com (2 May 2021): historians Miha Kosi and Andrej Pleterski say heraldry did not exist in 8th-century Carantania and call the panther a modern construct or invention of Savli.
era-658.open: These sources support reclassifying the row as a modern reconstruction (not an attested flag); left unreviewed under the upgrade brief. The page's earlier claim of 19th-century nationalist adoption was not found and has been removed from the text; the panther's use in Carinthian and Styrian arms is undated in Wikipedia.

era-1978.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1977, before this era begins in 1978, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 18 November 1977; Flags of the World dates it November 1977.
era-1978.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1893-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-contact and early-contact era, no single flag».
era-1893-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1893.says: Wikipedia's table: Union Jack 1893-1906; Blue Ensign with the protectorate's name and the Tudor Crown 1906-1947; Blue Ensign with a turtle shield 1947-1956; Blue Ensign with a quarterly shield on a white disk 1956-1966 and without the disk 1966-1977; the present flag ratified 18 November 1977. FOTW's historical pages: Blue Ensign badge 'BRITISH SOLOMON ISLANDS' around a crown c.1906-1947, replaced in 1947 when arms were granted by a red shield with a turtle on a white circle (Gresham Carr 1953), replaced again in 1956, with a 1956-1966 Blue Ensign; the official title was British Solomon Islands Protectorate until 1975.
era-1893.open: The page's single Blue Ensign with a badge disc stands for several different badges across the span, and Wikipedia's Union Jack for 1893-1906 is not in FOTW (which starts c.1906 and a Resident Commissioner's ensign c.1902); the description of the turtle badge is internally inconsistent in Wikipedia (shield vs disc) and the 1966-1977 variant is Wikipedia-only.

era-1969.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1954, before this era begins in 1969, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 12 October 1954; Flags of the World dates it 12 Oct 1954.
era-1969.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted 12 Oct 1954 by the Trust Territory council (designer Mohammed Awale Liban), used as co-official flag of the Trust Territory 1954-1960, used by the independent State of Somaliland 26 June-1 July 1960 and later adopted by the Somali Republic. FOTW: adopted 12 Oct 1954; Somalia was created 1 July 1960 and united with British Somaliland to form the Somali Republic; Flag Day is 26 June.
era-1960.open: Neither source gives an adoption date for the Republic's use of the flag; FOTW's text gives both 26 June and 1 July for the first republican hoisting.

era-1884.says: Wikipedia's image captions: British Somaliland used the UK flag 1884-1903 and local flags 1903-1960; Italian Somaliland the Italian flag 1889-1941, a British occupation flag 1941-1950, then the Italian and UN flags 1950-1960.
era-1884.open: FOTW's Somalia page links to separate colonial pages that were not read; no designs are described, so the Blue Ensign and badged tricolor shown are not confirmed.

era-1285.says: Wikipedia's image captions list flags for the Sultanate of Mogadishu (10th-16th century), Ajuran Empire (13th-17th), Adal Sultanate (1415-1577), Hiraab Imamate, Majeerteen Sultanate (1648-1927) and Isaaq Sultanate (1700s-1884).
era-1285.open: Wikipedia gives no design or evidence for these flags (they may be modern depictions); the page's statement that no flag survives is not confirmed either way. FOTW does not mention the sultanates.

era-1994.says: Both sources give 1994, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 27 April 1994; Flags of the World dates it 27 Apr 1994.
era-1994.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1652-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — Khoikhoi and San societies, no flag survives».
era-1652-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1928.says: Wikipedia says the 1928 flag was first hoisted on 31 May 1928, based on the Prinsenvlag, with the Union Flag, the Orange Free State flag and the Transvaal Vierkleur in the white band; that the arrangement means each miniature flag enjoys equal precedence; that a brighter version was adopted in 1982; and that the flag was relinquished on 20 April 1994. FOTW says the old national flag was in use in 1928–1994, in blue, white, red and green.
era-1928.open: This page says the three small flags symbolise the union of Britain's and the two defeated Boer republics' domains; Wikipedia describes the arrangement as one of equal precedence. FOTW does not give the 1928 date.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia (Red Ensign article): a Red Ensign with the coat of arms of South Africa on a white disc, authorised by Admiralty warrants of December 1910, the civil ensign 1910-1951 and used on land as a de facto national flag until 1928; Wikipedia's Flag of South Africa article says the same of the Red Ensign from 31 May 1910. Flags of the World: Admiralty warrant of 28 December 1910, amended 25 March 1912 to put the shield on a white roundel; the Union Jack was officially the national flag, the Red Ensign often regarded as the national flag, merchant ensign to 1951.
era-1910.open: The Union Jack was officially the national flag; the Red Ensign's 'de facto' status was popular practice (FOTW calls the perception erroneous). The badge is the Union's arms (FOTW says its quartered shield reportedly carries emblems of the four provinces), not a separate 'Union badge'.

era-1652.says: Wikipedia: the VOC used a version of the Prinsenvlag at the Cape from 1652 to 1795; its list dates the VOC flag 1652-1795 and 1803-1806. Flags of the World: the Dutch and VOC tricolours flew until the first British occupation on 17 September 1795; the flags generally used by Dutch vessels were the Prinzenvlag, an orange-white-blue tricolour (the orange later changed to red), and the Cape flag was either the Netherlands' or the Company's, the Dutch flag bearing the Company's cipher, though the author says no evidence of a Cape cipher on flags exists.
era-1652.open: The card's end date of 1806 spans the British occupation (Union flag 1795-1803) and the Batavian Republic (Dutch tricolour 1803-1806). The VOC monogram flag is FOTW's, not Wikipedia's, and FOTW doubts the Cape cipher.

era-1806.says: Flags of the World: the Cape Colony flew the undefaced British Union flag from 1805/06 until a Blue Ensign with the colony's arms (Royal Warrant 29 May 1876) was introduced, used until 31 May 1910; Natal adopted Red and Blue ensigns in 1870 with the Blue later given a simpler badge; the Orange Free State flag had seven white and orange stripes with the Dutch flag in the canton (delivered 12 January 1856, in use to 31 May 1902). Wikipedia's list of South African flags: Cape Blue Ensign 1876-1910, Natal 1875-1910, Natalia 1839-1843, Transvaal Vierkleur 1857-1902 and Orange Free State 1857-1902.
era-1806.open: The card's Blue Ensign over the Cape and Natal fits only 1875/76-1910: both publishers date the badge to the 1870s and FOTW says the Cape flew the plain Union flag before that; the Vierkleur's design is not described in the pages read.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: 12 July 1948 adopted; 15 October 1949 geometry standardised; 21 February 1984 dimensions codified; 1997 decree fixed colours. FOTW: 25 October 1997 presidential ordinance on standard specification; July 2007 National Flag Law.
era-1948.open: FOTW is silent before 1997; the 1883 and 1948 dates rest on Wikipedia.
