era-814bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1831.says: Wikipedia: government dates the flag to 1831 (1835 also cited), created as a fleet flag after Navarino (1827) under Hussein II. FOTW: adopted 1831 per Sache (Hassine I), 1835 per other books, modelled on the Ottoman flag of the time.
era-1831.open: Sources split on 1831/1835 and on which bey; the page's autonomy-from-Istanbul framing is not in either.

era-1881.says: Wikipedia: the flag was not changed during the protectorate and captions the flag of the Beylik (1827-1881) and Tunisia (1881-1959). Flags of the World (page on Tunisia under French administration, quoting Smith in Flag Bulletin no. 195, 2000): Tunisia, a French protectorate, retained its national flag on land and at sea; an unofficial version with a tricolour canton was used for a time, and a formal proposal in 1925 to adopt it was not acted on. Its historical page quotes the same article on the bey's separate state standard of green and red stripes with the sword of Ali.
era-1881.open: The French tricolour was not flown 'alongside' the flag as a rule in these sources, only in an unofficial canton variant. The start (1881 Treaty of Bardo) and end dates, and the bey's status, are not covered.

era-1574.says: Wikipedia: caption for an Eyalet of Tunis flag 1574-1705 and a Husainid flag 1705-1827, with no text description. Flags of the World (historical flags page, citing Franciae Vexilla 1999 and Flag Bulletin no. 195): Tunisia was nominally Ottoman from 1574 to 1881; ensigns with six white and red or green and red horizontal stripes were reported from 1756; the bey's state standard, said by one author to be three centuries old, was a many-striped flag with the sword of Ali; 14th-century portolans show crescent flags for Tunis.
era-1574.open: The sources do not show the plain Ottoman red flag with crescent and star for 1574-1831; they show striped Husainid ensigns and standards from 1756, so the page's claim is not supported. What flew from 1574 to 1705 is not described.

era-1923.says: Wikipedia says the Republic kept the last Ottoman flag in 1923, that Turkish Flag Law No. 2994 of 29 May 1936 set the flag's measures, proportions and red tone, and that Law No. 2893 of 22 September 1983 replaced it. FOTW says no design change occurred when the Empire became the Republic, that the 1936 law adopted the 1844 design without alteration, that the law was enacted on 29 May 1936 and published on 5 June 1936 (as No. 2,995), that Law No. 2,893 superseded it in 1983, and that the law gives no colour specification.
era-1923.open: The sources give the 1936 law's number as 2994 or 2,995. FOTW does not describe the 1919–23 war.

era-7500bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no flag concept existed anywhere in this span».
era-7500bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1793.says: Wikipedia says the star and crescent on red was introduced as the Ottoman flag in 1844, a late 18th-century design. FOTW, quoting Smith, says the form was set under Selim III in 1793 and the five-pointed star dates from about 1844.
era-1793.open: The firman of 1844 that this page named was not found in either source; the sources differ on 1793 or 1844.

era-1918.says: FOTW (tr.html): except for the issuance of design specifications, no change was made when the Ottoman Empire became the Republic of Turkey. Wikipedia (Flag of Turkey): after the republic was declared in 1923 the new regime maintained the last flag of the Ottoman Empire, standardised by the Flag Law of 29 May 1936; the War of Independence and the Ankara government appear only as sidebar links. Wikipedia (Flag of the Ottoman Empire): the Ottoman army used regimental standards bearing the Shahada after the 1914 jihad declaration, continued for a while after 1922, and the Caliphate standard of Abdulmejid II (19 November 1922 to 3 March 1924) was a green flag with a white star and crescent on a red oval.
era-1918.open: Two publishers confirm the flag was kept in 1923, but neither says what flag the Ankara nationalist government flew in 1919-1923 or that both governments used the same design; the claim for the wartime period is not established.

era-1453.says: FOTW says the basic form was apparently established in 1793 under Selim III, when navy flags changed from green to red and a white crescent and multipointed star were added, and that the five-pointed star dates from about 1844; it says the new rulers after 1453 'may have adopted the existing emblem' (speculation). Wikipedia says the star and crescent appear on Ottoman flags from the late 18th or early 19th century and gives 1844 for the red flag with white star and crescent; it does not cover 1453-1793. Wikipedia (Flag of the Ottoman Empire): a simple crescent flag appeared from the foundation in 1453 and was still reported at the 1780 Battle of Kagul; a 1574 illustration shows plain red banners for the Sultan's retinue; two 1613 naval flags in the Spanish Navy Museum include a green flag with a white crescent near the hoist; a 1793 decree required ships to use a red flag with a white star and crescent, the eight-pointed star flag being official 1793-1844 and the five-pointed star adopted in 1844.
era-1453.open: Wikipedia supports a crescent without a star before 1793 but also shows green and plain red banners, and FOTW has green naval flags before 1793; a plain red field with white crescent as the most widely attested flag is not established. Page text corrected.

era-330.says: FOTW presents as tradition, not documented flags, that Diana's moon was Byzantium's symbol and that in 330 a star over the crescent was linked to the Virgin Mary; it describes no Byzantine flag design. Wikipedia does not cover Byzantine banners. FOTW (gr_byz): the peacetime imperial flag was yellow with a black crowned double-headed eagle and the war banner porphyr red with a golden eagle; Neubecker (1977) describes the 14th-century flag as the St George cross combined with the Palaiologos arms (1258-1453), the corner charges read as firesteels or the Greek letter Beta, though one contributor argues the cross with firesteels is an old Orthodox symbol not specific to the Palaiologos; the 1350 Book of All Kingdoms shows red flags with a yellow cross and four chain links.
era-330.open: Only FOTW describes Byzantine flags and its sources disagree on the firesteel cross; no second publisher confirmed a gold cross with firesteels on imperial red, and the labarum and imperial purple are not covered. A web search did not surface a Wikipedia article on Byzantine flags.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia: the current flag was adopted 19 February 1992; Wikipedia's Turkmen SSR infobox labels the Turkmenistan flag 1991-1992 and gives independence declared 27 October 1991. Flags of the World (Turkmenistan): in 1992 (a year after independence) Turkmenistan adopted a new flag with a green field, white crescent and stars, five carpet guls at the hoist and a dark red hoist stripe (Notholt, 1995); olive branches were added on 29 January 1997; current version dated 24 January 2001; the five guls are reportedly named after five tribes.
era-1991.open: The page's 'adopted in 1992' is supported, but the era starts in 1991 and neither source says what flag flew between October 1991 and 1992; the 1997 and 2001 changes (olive branches, redrawn guls) show the flag was not unchanged after 1992.

era-1040-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — ancient Turkmen lands and early Merv».
era-1040-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1924.says: Wikipedia: the 1926 constitution set a red flag with a gold hammer and sickle and star in the canton; 1937 gold letters; 1940 Cyrillic letters; 1 August 1953 two horizontal blue bars across the middle; 23 September 1974 emblems moved to the hoist. Flags of the World agrees on the main points: 1 August 1953 adoption of the two-blue-bar flag (Heimer 1996; stripe proportions by Sensen), a 1924-1929 commemorative flag with TSSC lettering, 1930s star with hammer and sickle, 1937 Latin initials, 1940s Cyrillic initials. Wikipedia's SSR infobox dates the 1974 flag to 1991.
era-1924.open: Two publishers now agree on the chronology, but this page's drawing (a turquoise stripe near the base with a star in the canton) matches neither the 1953 nor the 1974 flag, so the row stays unreviewed until the drawing is replaced; the 1974 change is not covered by Flags of the World pages read.

era-1917.says: Flags of the World (Central Asian khanates) says local Bolsheviks created the Soviet Republic of Turkestan on 30 April 1918, a federated soviet republic from 11 April 1921, dissolved on 27 October 1924; it describes no flag for it, only an anti-Soviet all-Turkestani insurgent flag used 1921-January 1924 and the Basmachi flag. Wikipedia (Turkmen SSR) lists the Turkmen Oblast of the Turkestan ASSR from 7 August 1921 and says the Soviet Politburo divided Central Asia in October 1924.
era-1917.open: The administrative entity is confirmed, but no source read describes any flag of the Turkestan ASSR, and the page's Soviet red flag with hammer and sickle for it is unconfirmed; the Turkmen SSR proclamation date (Wikipedia: 13 May 1925) differs from this page's 1924.

era-1881.says: Flags of the World (Turkmenistan): the Khanate of Merv, annexed in 1884, flew a plain red flag. Wikipedia (Transcaspian Oblast): established 1881, abolished 1921 (the lead says it existed until 1924), with a coat of arms but no flag in the infobox. Flags of the World (Central Asian khanates) does not mention Transcaspia or Russian imperial flags.
era-1881.open: The Russian imperial tricolour over the Transcaspian Oblast is not stated in any source read; Wikipedia's end date (1921 or 1924) differs from this page's 1917.

era-1500.says: Wikipedia says the five guls on the modern flag are named for five tribes; Flags of the World (Turkmenistan) says they are reportedly named after five tribes (Notholt 1995) and quotes a 2003 coat-of-arms law naming them akhalteke, salyr, aersary, chovdur and yomut. Neither that page nor the Central Asian khanates page describes tribal banners, tamgas or a flag before 1884, apart from the plain red flag of the Khanate of Merv.
era-1500.open: No source calls the tribal-emblem motif a reconstruction or documents tribal banners or tamgas for 1500-1881; the page already labels the drawing an informed reconstruction.

era-1040.says: Neither Wikipedia nor Flags of the World covers Seljuk, Mongol or Timurid-era flags for the region; additionally read this session without result: Flags of the World's Turkmenistan page, its Central Asian khanates page (Khiva, Bukhara, Turkestan 1921-24 only) and its early Soviet Turkmen page.
era-1040.open: The sources read are silent on flags for c. 1040 to the 1500s; this is not a finding that no flag existed. Flags of the World's 14th-century Book of All Kingdoms pages (linked from other country indexes) were not searched for Turkestan or Merv.

era-1978.says: Wikipedia: the flag, a light blue field with the Union Jack in the canton and nine yellow stars on the fly half, was originally adopted on 1 October 1978, the day of independence; the 1995 government introduced a different flag and the 1997 government reverted on 11 April 1997. Flags of the World (last modified 2026): the 1978-95 flag, the 1995-1997 flag, and the reversion on 11 April 1997 to the 1978 flag; the British Blue Ensign became obsolete on 1 October 1978 when the new flag was adopted on independence.
era-1978.open: The flag was different from 1995 to 1997 (Wikipedia: October 1995 under Prime Minister Latasi, reversed by the next government), so the page's 'present' span has a two-year gap. FOTW's own date of 1975 on the main page refers to the separation of the Ellice Islands, not this flag.

era-1892-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-contact era, no single flag».
era-1892-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia: Colony of Tuvalu from 1 Oct 1975; own arms 3 Dec 1976; own Blue Ensign with the new arms 3 Dec 1976 to 1 Oct 1978. FOTW: new blue ensign with arms adopted 3 Dec 1976, obsolete 1 Oct 1978.
era-1975.open: Page dated the ensign from 1975 and spoke of a badge disc; the sources date the ensign from Dec 1976; 1975-76 flag not covered.

era-1892.says: Wikipedia: Gilbert and Ellice Islands arms granted 1937, Blue Ensign with arms unofficial then official 1969, used to 1975/76. Flags of the World (Gilbert and Ellice Islands page, quoting Whitney Smith and Admiralty files): the Gilbert and Ellice Islands became a protectorate in 1892 and a colony in 1915; government vessels flew the Blue Ensign defaced with the shield of the arms from 1937 to 1979 (without the white disc until 1976), legal sanction as civil flag on 28 August 1969.
era-1892.open: The two sources agree on the Blue Ensign with the arms, but only from 1937; neither describes a flag of the protectorate (1892-1915) or colony (1915-1937) before the arms. The page's 'shared with the Gilbert Islands' is true of the joint colony, but the 1892 start is not supported.

era-1962.says: Both sources give 1962, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 9 October 1962; Flags of the World dates it 09 Oct 1962.
era-1962.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1700-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — early Buganda and neighboring kingdoms, no flag survives».
era-1700-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1894.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Uganda): the British protectorate flew a Blue Ensign with its colonial badge featuring a crested crane from 1914 to March 1962, the Governor having a standard with the Union Jack and the badge; Wikipedia (Uganda Protectorate): the protectorate ran 18 June 1894 to 9 October 1962 and its infobox flag is dated 1914-1962. FOTW (ug.html): the crested crane was the flag badge of Uganda under British colonial rule and the former flag-badge; FOTW's British East Africa page lists the date of the Blue Ensign badge as unknown.
era-1894.open: Attested for the Blue Ensign with the crested crane badge; both Wikipedia pages date the flag from 1914, so 1894-1914 is not covered, and FOTW gives no dates. Whether the badge is the 'grey' crowned crane is not stated.

era-1700.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Uganda): the Kingdom of Buganda had a national flag prior to colonisation, with no design or dates. FOTW (ug-bugan): flags of 1861-81, c.1881-89, 1884-86/1889 and 1891-92 are undescribed images by Jaume Olle; Pakenham's account has Lugard in 1892 finding the Kabaka flying 'an enormous home-made flag, two lances and a shield on a red ground'; the current flag is blue-white-blue with the kingdom's logo.
era-1700.open: No source describes a Buganda flag before 1861 or the sun-and-star emblem, and the red-ground 1892 flag contradicts the white field drawn. The page text was corrected.

era-1922.says: Wikipedia says that on 7 December 1922, asked whether the Garter King of Arms would issue new regulations after the Irish Free State was established, the Home Secretary said no, and that the flag has never been changed; it says no law has made it the national flag, its status resting on precedent and a 1908 ministerial statement. FOTW quotes Graham Bartram on that 1908 statement and Christopher Southworth that there is no UK Flag Act.
era-1922.open: The flag's status is by custom, not statute; both sources say so.

era-927.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-800bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1707.says: Wikipedia (Union Flag): after the Acts of Union the flag gained regularised status as 'the ensign armorial of the Kingdom of Great Britain' and on 17 April 1707 Sir Henry St George presented designs to Queen Anne, who approved the design numbered one. Flags of the World (history of the Union Flag, Prothero 1998): the flag became 'the ensign armorial of the United Kingdom of Great Britain' as a provision of the 1707 Act of Union; the 1606 flag (proclamation of 12 April 1606, St George's and St Andrew's crosses joined, for ships at sea) lacked St Patrick's cross, which came in 1801. Wikipedia (Kingdom of Great Britain): infobox flag file dated 1707-1800; the Acts took effect on 1 May 1707.
era-1707.open: Flags of the World gives no 1707 proclamation or royal warrant and does not describe a separate 'flag of Great Britain'; the Wikipedia design approval (17 April 1707) rests on that article alone.

era-1801.says: Wikipedia says George III's proclamation of 1 January 1801 set the blazon, adding St Patrick's saltire counterchanged with St Andrew's. FOTW quotes the proclamation's «quarterly per saltire, counterchanged argent and gules», and Southworth that the original saltires were of even width, the narrower St Patrick saltire an Admiralty variant soon after.
era-1801.open: The narrow St Patrick saltire seen on the flag today came after the 1801 proclamation, which this page does not mention.

era-1603.says: Wikipedia says a royal decree of 12 April 1606 joined the English and Scottish crosses for use at sea and that subjects of both kingdoms were to fly it. FOTW says it was introduced as a maritime flag, that the 1606 flag placed the red cross of St George over the blue St Andrew's flag with a white X, and, quoting Procter, that a 1634 proclamation reserved it for warships.

era-1200.says: Flags of the World (England): the earliest reference to the cross of St George as an English emblem (not flag) is a 1277 Welsh war account roll (Perrin, 1922); the St George banner flew at Caerlaverock in 1300; the cross became a national flag in the 16th century after the Reformation removed other saints' banners, with the earliest sea record in 1545. Wikipedia (Flag of England): red crosses marked English soldiers from the 1270s, 1277 banners 'of the arms of Saint George', a St George banner beside the royal banner by 1300, Edward III's Order of the Garter in 1348, and the Genoa/1190 origin 'cannot be substantiated'; the 1367 Book of All Kingdoms shows England's flag as solid red. Wikipedia (Kingdom of England): infobox 'Flag (from the 16th century)' and 'Royal Banner (1406-1603)'.
era-1200.open: Both publishers place the St George's cross as an English emblem from the 1270s and as the national flag only from the 16th century, not from c. 1200 or the Crusades; the claim that the design 'has never once been altered' was not checked.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia says the flag was de facto restored on 24 August 1991 and officially adopted again by parliament on 28 January 1992, and that the sky-blue version of 1917–1921 was reintroduced in 1992 and remains in use alongside a darker blue standard (DSTU 4512:2006). FOTW (Grechylo) gives the State Flag decree of 28 January 1992 (No 2067-XII), a Presidium decree of 18 September 1991 allowing ceremonial use, and says the blue-yellow flag first flew at the Supreme Council on 4 September 1991.
era-1991.open: FOTW's own sources disagree: Gutterman gives 21 January 1992 for making it the only flag. The page's remark that the colours were read as sky over wheat was not found in either source.

era-900.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1949.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Ukrainian SSR): the UN demanded changes to the republic flags in 1949; the lettering was dropped and an azure horizontal stripe (one third of the width) added; decree of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of 21 November 1949, de jure adoption 5 July 1950; the decree says the blue symbolises the might and beauty of the people and the blue banner of Bohdan Khmelnytsky. FOTW (Ukraine in the Soviet Union 1949-1991): adopted 21 November 1949, light blue bar in base covering a third of the height; FOTW's flag-history page (citing the Encyclopedia of Ukraine) agrees on 21 November 1949, red upper two thirds, azure lower third, gold hammer, sickle and star above.
era-1949.open: Neither source calls the blue stripe a coded echo of the banned blue-yellow flag; the page's wording about that is unsourced and has been hedged.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Ukrainian SSR): a flag adopted in 1937 (caption 1937-1950) carried a small gold hammer and sickle above the gold Cyrillic letters УРСР on red, and the republic's flag was changed only in 1949. FOTW (early flags): the 1940s flag was red with yellow Cyrillic initials URSR in the upper hoist and a yellow hammer and sickle below, replaced on 21 November 1949; the 1937 flag had the hammer and sickle above the initials.
era-1944.open: The two sources differ on whether the emblem sat above or below the lettering and neither mentions a star; the drawing and caption on the page still show a plain red field with hammer, sickle and star and need redrawing from these descriptions.

era-1921.says: Wikipedia: the first UkrSSR flag (10 March 1919) was red with gold Cyrillic У.С.С.Р.; a decade later У.С.Р.Р.; a gold border was added in the 1930s; in 1937 a small gold hammer and sickle was added above gold serif УРСР. FOTW (early flags): 1919 red with yellow initials in the upper hoist; 1923 yellow initials with no hammer and sickle; 1927 initials U.S.R.R.; 1930s yellow border round the canton; 1937 little yellow hammer and sickle above URSR.
era-1921.open: The page's gold 'hammer-and-sickle-and-star' is not what either source describes (lettering with, from 1937, a small hammer and sickle); the drawing and caption still need redrawing. The 1921 start date is the page's own: the sources date the first flag to 1919.

era-1917.says: FOTW (Historical Flags 1917-1918, citing the Encyclopedia of Ukraine): the Ukrainian National Republic was proclaimed 20 November 1917, independence declared 22 January 1918, national flag of yellow over light blue adopted 22 March 1918; under the Hetmanate (from 29 April 1918) light blue over yellow; the restored UNR kept light blue over yellow from December 1919. Wikipedia (Flag of Ukraine): blue-yellow flags in Petrograd on 25 March 1917 and Kyiv on 29 March 1917, 22 March 1918 as official adoption in its infobox; the Hetmanate's and Directorate's flag light blue-yellow; Wikipedia's UNR article records blue-and-yellow flags at the Kyiv demonstration of 13 April 1917.
era-1917.open: The sources agree on a blue-and-yellow bicolour but the stripe order changed (yellow over blue in 1918 per FOTW, blue over yellow afterwards); the page's 'blue-over-gold' drawing fits 1918-21 only in part. Neither source says the Central Rada adopted it.

era-1654.says: FOTW (Hetmanate Flags, 18th century): the Cossack Hetmanate existed 1648-1734; the Hetman's flag c.1706 was red and triangular, and a Hetman used a red flag with Archangel Michael already in 1655; the 'famous blue flag' with a Cossack figure was a regimental flag of the 18th century, not a Hetmanate flag; the Zaporozhian Sich flag showed a star, sun and moon greeting a cross. FOTW (Cossack Flags): a dark red banner with a white Maltese cross near the hoist dates to a Black Sea Cossack flag of 1792. Wikipedia: blue-yellow Cossack banners were widely used in the 16th-18th centuries alongside red-black, crimson-olive and raspberry ones.
era-1654.open: A crimson banner with a white cross is attested only in FOTW (the Sich's great banner and the Black Sea Cossack flag of 1792), both Zaporozhian rather than Hetmanate; Wikipedia's Cossack Hetmanate and Zaporozhian Sich articles contain no flag text. No second publisher or reference source was found for the Hetmanate's own flag in 1654-1795.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia's Ukraine flag article does not cover the 1941-44 occupation; its Reichskommissariat Ukraine article (read in full text) mentions no flag or symbol. FOTW's history page dates use of a yellow-over-azure flag by the Ukrainian Liberation Army and Division Galizien to 1943-45 and quotes one unverified reader recalling a flag with a white trident.
era-1941.open: Which flag was flown over the Reichskommissariat administration is stated by none of the pages read (Wikipedia Flag of Ukraine and Reichskommissariat articles, FOTW ua.html, ua-flhis.html); the page's drawing of Nazi Germany's flag is therefore unconfirmed. A source on Reichskommissariat Ukraine administration or German occupation flag orders is needed.

era-1795.says: FOTW's history page (quoting the Encyclopedia of Ukraine): in Russian-ruled Ukraine only the white-blue-red imperial flag and official flags based on it were used, with no territorial flags. Wikipedia: the blue-yellow flag was flown in Lviv in 1848 (Austrian Galicia), in Dnieper Ukraine in 1905, and first in the Russian Empire at a 25 March 1917 Petrograd demonstration.
era-1795.open: The imperial flag's exclusive use rests on FOTW alone; Wikipedia's Ukraine article does not say what official flag flew, and its 1905 and 1917 displays show the page's 'none permitted' is too absolute. No Wikipedia or reference page read dates a 1795 start. Sought: Flag of Russia (imperial period) coverage of civil use in Ukraine - not read.

era-1569.says: FOTW's history page (citing the Encyclopedia of Ukraine): within the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Polish kingdom each Ukrainian principality, voivodeship, land and county had its own banner, usually matching its coat of arms; Peremyshl land had a golden two-headed eagle on azure. FOTW's 1410 page (after the Ukrainian vexillologist A. Grechilo) shows Lviv Land and Peremysl Land banners at Grunwald.
era-1569.open: All from one publisher (FOTW); Wikipedia's Ukraine, Cossack Hetmanate and Grand Duchy of Lithuania articles contain no Polish Crown flag over Ukraine. The page's white eagle on red over Ukraine is not found in any source read.

era-1349.says: FOTW: the 15th-century Grand Duchy of Lithuania flag was red with a golden Gediminas emblem; a later Lithuanian flag was red with a white knight on a horse (also claimed by Belarusians); FOTW's 1410 page shows Lviv and Peremysl banners at Grunwald. Wikipedia's Grand Duchy of Lithuania article says the historical Lithuanian flag (horseback knight on red) dates in its initial design to the reign of Vytautas the Great.
era-1349.open: Wikipedia's Lithuania article dates the knight design to Vytautas (1392-1430), not to 1349, and neither source says it was the flag across the Rus' lands from 1349; the page's start date and its use over Ukraine are unsupported.

era-1240.says: FOTW's history page (citing the Encyclopedia of Ukraine): the Rus' kingdom's Galician-Volhynian standard showed a golden lion on azure (undated), and in Oct 1848 the Supreme Ruthenian Council in Lviv adopted a golden lion on blue as the Ukrainian arms. Wikipedia has only an undated caption calling a lion-on-blue flag the Kingdom of Ruthenia flag; its Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia and Kingdom of Ruthenia articles contain no flag text.
era-1240.open: Only FOTW states the lion standard and gives no date; no reference source naming a medieval primary basis was found, so 1240-1349 is not sourced.

era-1971.says: Both sources give 1971, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 2 December 1971; Flags of the World dates it December 1971.
era-1971.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1853.says: Wikipedia (Trucial States): the Perpetual Maritime Truce was signed on 4 May 1853 (infobox) and the Trucial States Council flag is dated 1968-1971. Wikipedia (Flag of the UAE): white segment imposed on six emirates' flags - Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah red with white border (No. 2), Ajman and Dubai red with white hoist bar (No. 1), Abu Dhabi red with white rectangle at upper hoist - and only Fujairah plain red. Flags of the World (1820 treaty page, Carr 1956): No. 2 flown by Sharjah, Ras al-Khaimah and Kalba; No. 1 (white hoist stripe, later than 1833 or 1864 per Stelter) by Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Dubai and Umm al-Qaiwain; Fujairah added white lettering to red in 1952 and returned to plain red in 1961; Abu Dhabi's sea flag was red with a white strip 1905-1930. Flags of the World (emirates flags): Sharjah, Ras al-Khaimah and Kalba used red bordered white; Fujairah kept plain red (Ollé).
era-1853.open: Two publishers agree that most Trucial sheikhdoms flew red flags with white elements and only Fujairah plain red, so this page's 'plain red (most sheikhdoms)' is contradicted; 1853 appears only as the date of the truce, not of any flag; the Perpetual Maritime Truce is covered by Wikipedia alone.

era-1820.says: Flags of the World (1820 treaty page, quoting Article 3 from C. R. Low's History of the Indian Navy via Prothero 1998): the treaty of 8 January 1820 required the friendly Arabs to carry 'a red flag, with or without letters in it, at their option', in practice a red flag in a white border of equal width ('White pierced Red', the centre one ninth of the flag), as a sign of peace with Britain. Wikipedia (Qawasim) quotes the same: 'a red rectangle contained within a white border of equal width to the contained rectangle'; Wikipedia (Trucial States) dates the treaty 8 January 1820.
era-1820.open: Both publishers describe the treaty flag as red within a white border, so this page's plain red field for 1820-1853 is contradicted; whether every signatory flew the white border in practice (Abu Dhabi readopted plain red in 1833/34 per Flags of the World) is not settled.

era-1727.says: Wikipedia (Qawasim): the infobox founds the Al Qasimi line in 1722; image captions show a 'Flag of the Al Qawasim prior to 1820', 'flown after 1820 during war time only', bearing the motto 'A victory from Allah and an imminent conquest' (no date more precise than 'prior to 1820'). Flags of the World (1820 treaty page): the Qawasim, the leading tribe, were closely tied to the treaty flag, and other tribes saw it as the Qawasim flag.
era-1727.open: No source gives the design or colour of the pre-1820 Qawasim flag in text, and the caption's motto implies lettering rather than plain red; c. 1727 is not dated by Wikipedia (1722 founding).

era-1960.says: Both sources give 1960, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 3 December 1775; Flags of the World dates it 4 July 1960.
era-1960.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1959.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the United States): Executive Order 10798 of 3 January 1959 set the 49-star design after Alaska's admission, and the flag became official on 4 July 1959. Flags of the World (49 stars): the flag flew from 4 July 1959 to 3 July 1960, the proclamation was signed on 2 January 1959, Alaska's admission added the 49th star, and the stars were in staggered rows.
era-1959.open: The signing date is 3 January on Wikipedia and 2 January on FOTW; FOTW calls the document a proclamation and does not number an executive order; FOTW's own pages mention Executive Order 10834 for the 50-star flag.

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: the 48-star flag was adopted in 1912, the first flag act to specify an arrangement, six rows of eight stars. Flags of the World (48 stars): the flag flew from 4 July 1912 and followed Arizona and New Mexico joining; the Army Quartermaster describes the 48 stars in six rows of eight; its star-arrangement page says no law specified the arrangement until 1912.
era-1912.open: The order is not agreed: FOTW says Taft approved the arrangement on 14 February 1912 and attributes Executive Order 1556 of 24 June 1912 to flag sizes and proportions, not the star layout; the end date is 1959 on the page title but 3 July 1949 in one FOTW contributor note.

era-1865.says: Wikipedia's table gives 36 stars in 1865-1867, 37 in 1867-1877, 38 in 1877-1890, 43 in 1890-1891, 44 in 1891-1896 and 45 in 1896-1908. Flags of the World's index lists the same counts and years (36 stars 1865-1867, 37 1867-1877, 38 1877-1890, 43 1890-1891, 44 1891-1896, 45 1896-1908, 46 1908-1912) and its 36-star page says one star was added for Nevada in 1865.
era-1865.open: The page stops at 45 stars and 1912, but both sources add a 46-star flag for 1908-1912; FOTW says the Army and Navy had approved patterns from 1865 but no star arrangement was legally fixed.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia gives 34 stars in 1861-1863 (Kansas) and 35 in 1863-1865 (West Virginia). Flags of the World: the 34-star flag added Kansas (admitted 29 January 1861) and flew from 4 July 1861 to 3 July 1863; the 35-star flag added West Virginia in 1863 and flew from 4 July 1863 to 3 July 1865.
era-1861.open: Neither source says that the Union deliberately kept the seceded states' stars; the page's remark that the refusal to remove a star was a political statement is a comment, not a sourced fact.

era-1818.says: Wikipedia: Congress passed a plan on 4 April 1818, suggested by Samuel C. Reid, returning the stripes to 13 and setting 20 stars, with a star added for each new state on the following 4 July, and gives 33 stars in 1859-1861. Flags of the World quotes the act, approved 4 April 1818, requiring thirteen horizontal stripes, alternate red and white, and a star added on the 4 July after each admission, taking effect 4 July 1818; its index lists 20 stars in 1818 through 33 stars in 1859-1861.
era-1818.open: FOTW does not name Reid; the page's claim that period flags show real variation in star layout is supported by FOTW's note that military patterns existed from 1818 but were not binding on the public.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia: the stars and stripes went from 13 to 15 on 1 May 1795 for Vermont and Kentucky. Flags of the World (15 stars): in 1795 two stars were added for Kentucky and Vermont, the only US flag with fifteen stripes, which flew from 4 July 1795 to 4 July 1818 and over Fort McHenry in the War of 1812.
era-1795.open: The start is 1 May 1795 on Wikipedia and 4 July 1795 on FOTW; neither source read mentions the Flag Act of 1794.

era-1777.says: Wikipedia says Congress resolved on 14 June 1777 that the flag be thirteen alternate red and white stripes with thirteen stars on a blue field, that the designer is unknown, and that William Canby first publicly told the Betsy Ross story in 1870 with no evidence in Washington's diaries or Congressional records. FOTW says Canby said he heard it from his grandmother and found nothing to support it in US records, that no record of a 1776 congressional committee on a flag exists, and that Francis Hopkinson was the only person at the time to claim credit.
era-1777.open: FOTW does not cover the 1777 resolution. The star arrangement is not specified by Congress, and the circular arrangement drawn is traditional, not documented.

era-1607.says: Wikipedia: the Continental Union Flag first appeared on 3 December 1775 aboard Alfred, and whether the flag raised at Prospect Hill on 1 January 1776 was the Continental or the British Union Flag is disputed. Flags of the World (Grand Union Flag): first raised in early December 1775 aboard the Continental Navy's flagship; Ansoff holds the Prospect Hill flag was a British Union flag in the canton; used after the Declaration of Independence, with a latest reference in March 1777; a Philadelphia chandler charged for a 'Union Flagg, Green and Red, 13 stripes' on 20 December 1775.
era-1607.open: The British colonial flags of 1607 to 1775 on this card's long span are not covered by Wikipedia or FOTW's pages read; stripe colours of the Continental Colors are questioned by McMillan.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia: statute of 11 July 1830 reduced the stripes from nineteen to nine; 1952 decree formalised the sun's design with sixteen rays. FOTW: nine equal blue and white stripes, white canton over the top five, yellow sun with sixteen alternating straight and wavy rays.
era-1830.open: The departments claim is in neither source; the 1828 date is inconsistent inside Wikipedia (nineteen or nine stripes).

era-1825.says: Wikipedia: in 1825 the Thirty-Three Orientals planted a tricolour marked 'Libertad o Muerte' at Agraciada Beach, and the flag law that followed specified light blue, white and crimson. FOTW: Lavalleja's flag had three horizontal bands of sky-blue, white and deep scarlet with 'Libertad o Muerte' on the middle band, and a contributor notes the flag was defined as celeste by an 1825 law; the Flag Law of 18 December 1828 later replaced it with the striped sun-canton flag.
era-1825.open: FOTW's page for the 33 Orientales flag does not mention the Agraciada landing or the 1825 law (only the uy_hist contributor note does); how the flag was worn is not described.

era-1816.says: Wikipedia: during Brazilian control a provincial flag of white between two green stripes was used. FOTW (historical page): Uruguay joined the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves in July 1821 and was a Brazilian province from February 1824 to October 1828; the Portuguese invasion defeated Artigas in July 1816; it links a separate Cisplatine page but gives no flag.
era-1816.open: Neither publisher describes the Portuguese flag of 1816-22 or a Brazilian Empire banner as drawn here; the Wikipedia green-striped provincial flag differs, and the dates of Brazilian control differ from this page's 1822-25 (FOTW 1821/1824-1828).

era-1680.says: Wikipedia: the earliest flag described is Artigas's 1814 flag (white stripe between two blue, with red). FOTW (historical page): Artigas used red, blue and white for the Eastern Province's flag, in use 1814-1817; no Spanish colonial or Banda Oriental flag is described.
era-1680.open: The Cross of Burgundy over the Banda Oriental is not mentioned by either publisher (for Spanish use of the Cross of Burgundy generally see the Argentina entries); the 1680 start is not a flag event.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 18 November 1991. FOTW's Uzbekistan page says the flag was adopted 18 November 1991 under the Law on the state flag (Official Gazette no. 141 of 28 November 1991), with the state emblem following in July 1992, and gives the construction sheet.
era-1991.open: Design and swatch colours were not checked against the construction sheet.

era-1924.says: Wikipedia says the Uzbek SSR flag was approved in 1952 with a blue stripe one-fifth of the width, white-edged. FOTW says the striped flag was adopted by decree on 29 August 1952: red, with a blue bar fimbriated white across the middle (stripes 20+1+8+1+20), a hammer and sickle and a star in the upper hoist. Earlier flags (1925, 1926, 1931, 1937, 1941) were plain red with yellow initials or the republic's name in the upper hoist.
era-1924.open: The drawing puts the blue stripe near the base with no white edging and shows a hammer-and-sickle-like emblem in the canton in gold; both sources put the stripe across the middle with white edging, and FOTW gives no colour for the emblem. The drawing needs redrawing and the 1924-52 flags are not the one drawn.

era-1917.says: FOTW (after Sokolov and Ivanov) gives the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic a red flag with crescent and star in 1920, a green-over-red flag with a yellow crescent and star bearing a red hammer and sickle in 1921, and a plain red flag from October 1923; the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic flew a red flag with a green canton holding a yellow crescent and star (1920-23). Wikipedia's article on the Bukharan republic says its flag combined the hammer and sickle with the crescent.
era-1917.open: The Turkestan ASSR flag is not described by any source read (Wikipedia's infobox shows only an image). The page's general statement of Soviet red flags with a hammer and sickle fits Bukhara in 1921 only; Khorezm used a crescent and star without a hammer and sickle.

era-1865.says: Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Uzbekistan nor FOTW's Uzbekistan pages describe the Russian tricolour over Turkestan; FOTW says the emir's flag of Bukhara is known from the early 20th century (a museum flag, green with a red border and white hand, crescent and stars), and that the Khiva flag displayed in its museum dates from 1917-22 with earlier flags unknown.
era-1865.open: Wikipedia's Russian Turkestan article has no flag in its infobox or text. Wikipedia's Turkestan ASSR infobox lists the Russian flag of 1896-1918 as the predecessor image, which is not text evidence. Which Russian flag flew over the governorate-general is not established; nor is a khanate flag before 1900.

era-1500.says: FOTW says the Bukhara emirate's national flag 'remains elusive' and shows only the emir's flag of the early 20th century and a museum flag (green, red border, white hand of Fatima, crescent and three stars); for Khiva it knows only a 1917-22 flag. Wikipedia's Khanate of Bukhara article gives no flag image, and its Emirate article shows an exile-published 1929 flag.
era-1500.open: A green field with a white crescent as the flag of the 1500-1865 khanates is not stated by any source read; the nearest evidence is early 20th century. Kokand has an infobox image only.

era-1370.says: FOTW says, citing Znamierowski and undated, that blue was Tamerlane's colour. Wikipedia's Timurid Empire has a Flag section: little certainty about the empire's flag; Timur's armies are thought to have used red banners with a crescent, and a flag with three circles in the Catalan Atlas may relate to Timurid lands (per Yuka Kadoi), though Kadoi calls the evidence scant and ambiguous.
era-1370.open: The sources disagree on the colour (blue against red or brown/silver); the three-circle motif is tentative. The blue field with three rings drawn here is a reconstruction not stated by either source.

era-1220.says: Wikipedia's Black Standard article says the Abbasid Revolution adopted black banners, which became associated with the Abbasid Caliphate. Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Uzbekistan nor FOTW's Uzbekistan page mentions the Samanids or any flag before the Timurid note.
era-1220.open: That the Samanids flew plain black as Abbasid-suzerain governors is not stated by any source read; Wikipedia's Samanid Empire article has no flag text.

era-1980.says: Both sources give 1980, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 18 February 1980; Flags of the World dates it February 1980.
era-1980.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1906-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-contact era, no single flag».
era-1906-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1906.says: Wikipedia's flag table lists a British New Hebrides Blue Ensign with the territory emblem (Tudor Crown 1906-1953, St Edward's Crown 1953-1980), a British resident commissioner's flag, a French vertical tricolour (1906-1940, 1944-1980), a Free French version with the Cross of Lorraine (1940-1944), and the 1963 and 1966/1971 Games flags; Wikipedia (New Hebrides) describes the 1906 Protocol as joint sovereignty with two parallel administrations, one British and one French, and no condominium flag. Flags of the World (New Hebrides flags): the British Blue Ensign had a white disc lettered NEW HEBRIDES around a crown (Tudor to 1953, St Edward's after), the Resident Commissioner flew a Union Flag with the same disc; the French-side flag was probably the tricolour (Stilling, unconfirmed); the Free French used a tricolour with the Cross of Lorraine (1940-1945); 'no official joint condominium flag is documented' after the 1889-1906 Commission flag.
era-1906.open: The French-side flag is confirmed only by Wikipedia's table (Flags of the World calls it a probable tricolour); the absence of an official joint flag is Flags of the World's finding for the documents it knows, not proof; the page's single drawing does not show both flags.

era-1929.says: Holy See Press Office (vatican.va): the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929 led to the flag's present form, and the modern flag was first raised on 8 June 1929, yellow and white with the crossed keys surmounted by the tiara at the centre. Flags of the World: flag adopted 8 June 1929 (introduced 1825) and arms adopted 7 June 1929; the modern flag first officially hoisted on 8 June 1929. Wikipedia's infobox gives 7 June 1929.
era-1929.open: The adoption day is 7 June on Wikipedia and 8 June on the Holy See and FOTW pages; the page's remark that the 1929 flag is almost unchanged from the last Papal States flag is not stated by the sources, which date the yellow-white colours to 1808.

era-1870.says: Wikipedia: the Papal States were conquered by Italy on 20 September 1870; 1870-1929 appears only in navigation boxes. Flags of the World (historical flags): the Papal States were annexed in 1870 and the Papal Navy flew a white ensign with a tiara-keys emblem between Saints Peter and Paul (Becker, 2004). The Holy See page says only that Pius IX added the papal arms after returning from Gaeta.
era-1870.open: Papal ceremonial use of the yellow-white flag in 1870-1929 is not described by any source read; the navy ensign is a different flag.

era-1825.says: Wikipedia: 17 September 1825 yellow-and-white bicolor replaces the earlier flag, colours from the metals of the keys. Flags of the World: yellow-and-white flag recorded as introduced 1825 (Smith: gold and silver accepted 1825); 1808 as origin of the colours.
era-1825.open: Wikipedia and Flags of the World disagree on 1808 versus 1825 origin; neither dates the keys and tiara on the flag; 'unbroken' from 1825 not stated.

era-756.says: Holy See Press Office: before 1808 the flag was red and amaranth ('giallorossa'), from the Holy See's arms and the colours of the Senate and People of Rome; the oldest surviving yellow-white papal flag dates from 1824. Wikipedia: before 1808 a yellow-red bicolour; a white merchant flag with the papal arms in 1803, official 7 June 1815. Flags of the World (historical flags): the earliest attested papal flag was red with a white cross, probably about 1195, and a red flag with white keys in 1204; yellow-red mostly as cockades in the 1700s; a yellow-white merchant flag by Cardinal Chamberlain in 1825.
era-756.open: Sources support yellow-red colours only for the last centuries before 1808 and earlier red flags; none documents a gold and red gonfalone from 756, or calls it a gonfalone.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia: 20 November 1817 eighth star decreed; 1930–54 seven-star flag; 17 February 1954 coat of arms on the state flag; 2006 current flag. FOTW: eight stars adopted March 2006; seven-star flag used before 2006.
era-1830.open: The sources give no dates for the 1836, 1859 and 1863 star changes.

era-1500.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1810.says: Wikipedia: Miranda's flag first flown 12 March 1806 (Jacmel) and 3 August 1806 (La Vela de Coro); Congress adopted it in 1811. FOTW: Congress recognised it in July 1811.

era-1819.says: FOTW (Great Colombia): the yellow-blue-red tricolour designed by Miranda was provisionally adopted on 17 December 1819 and prescribed by the law of 4 October 1821, with the arms of Cundinamarca; FOTW (Colombia history) gives yellow-blue-red horizontal stripes at 3:2:1. Wikipedia (Flag of Colombia): Miranda created the yellow, blue and red flag, adopted by the Gran Colombia congresses on 17 December 1819; Wikipedia and FOTW on Venezuela say Miranda's tricolour inspired the flags of Colombia and Ecuador.
era-1819.open: A central star is not established: FOTW says Bolivar's variant with an added blue star for Angostura is disputed and that arms sat in the canton or centre in 1820-21; neither source describes a fixed central emblem on the 1819 flag.

era-1777.says: Neither Venezuela flag page covers Spanish colonial flags. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy Flag): the Burgundy flag remained in use in Spain's overseas empire and as a jack until Charles III's red-yellow-red naval ensign of 1785. FOTW (Burgundy Cross Flag): the saltire was an ensign 1506-1670s and a jack until 1785, and Spain's military flag on land to 1843.
era-1777.open: Neither publisher mentions Venezuela or the captaincy's seal; the Burgundy cross is plausible for land forces but the naval ensign changed in 1785, so its use as the banner of the Captaincy General is not documented.

era-1976.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1955, before this era begins in 1976, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 23 November 1940; Flags of the World dates it Adopted 1955.
era-1976.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-938.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1954.says: Wikipedia: gold-star flag first seen 23 November 1940; modified 30 November 1955 (smaller star, straighter rays); State of Vietnam yellow flag by ordinance 2 June 1948, Bảo Đại 1949; NLF flag 20 December 1960; unified 2 July 1976. FOTW: current design modified from a 1945 flag in 1955 (30 September or 30 November); 2 July 1976 unified hoisting.
era-1954.open: FOTW does not cover the South's flag.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: Viet Minh proclaimed the gold-star-on-red flag at Tan Trao on 17 August 1945, the Democratic Republic was proclaimed 2 September 1945, a decree of 5 September adopted the flag, the Assembly voted for it on 2 March 1946, and the State of Vietnam's yellow flag with three red bands followed by ordinance on 2 June 1948. FOTW: the Democratic Republic (2 September 1945) flag was set by the Presidential Decree of 5 September 1945 with a construction annex; the Tran Trong Kim government under Japanese rule used a yellow flag with three red stripes; the State of Vietnam was recognised by France on 8 March 1949.
era-1945.open: FOTW's State of Vietnam page has no flag description and copies Wikipedia. The drawing's three red stripes touch each other; the sources describe stripes on yellow. The date of the State of Vietnam's flag differs (June 1948 against the March 1949 recognition).

era-1802.says: Wikipedia's Long tinh flag article says the yellow flag with a vertical red stripe was designed by Emperor Khai Dinh (reigned 1916-25) from the ribbon of the Order of the Dragon of Annam, was designated the first national flag in the 1940s, and ran to mid-1945; Wikipedia's Flag of Vietnam calls it arguably the first national flag, adopted in the final years of the Nguyen dynasty. FOTW's Indochina page, quoting an unsourced Worldstatesmen chronology, dates a yellow Long Tinh Ky flag with a red circle to 1802-1885, and other yellow flags (Dai Nam) to 1885-1920.
era-1802.open: The two sources conflict on design (stripe against circle) and date (1920s against 1802); neither supports a yellow field with a red bar for the Nguyen dynasty from 1802. The drawing, which shows a red bar, needs checking.

era-1887.says: Wikipedia: the French flag, a yellow protectorate flag with the tricolour in the canton, and the Long tinh banner all flew in Annam and Tonkin; its Indochinese Union article shows the French flag for 1887-1954. FOTW: the French flag was the rule in French colonies and local flags the exception; it dates a French protectorate flag of Annam 1923-1945 and the Union Indochinoise to 1887.
era-1887.open: The sources support the French tricolour across the Union, but the drawing is a horizontal red-white-blue flag (the Dutch pattern), not the French vertical blue-white-red; it needs redrawing. Local protectorate flags (1920s-45) are not shown.

era-938-1.says: Wikipedia says traditional images show the Trung sisters in yellow turbans in their AD 40 revolt, which it calls royal standards, not national flags. FOTW's Military History Museum page shows Vietnamese battle flags (938 Bach Dang, 1077 Ly army) and Song, Yuan and Ming flags but no Chinese flag for the commanderies.
era-938-1.open: No source read mentions a Chinese imperial dragon standard over the 111 BCE-938 commanderies; the page's drawing is a placeholder.

era-1959.says: Flags of the World: 'The Welsh flag was granted official status in 1959'; in February 1959 the Queen directed that only the red dragon on a green and white field be flown on government buildings in Wales and London; the white-and-green field is 'in the livery colours of the Tudors'. Wikipedia: officially recognised as the national flag in 1959 (cited to a 1959 Hansard written answer by Henry Brooke), government use of the earlier badge-based flag dropped that year at the Gorsedd of Bards' urging; the Tudor livery was added to the flag later.
era-1959.open: The page's 'in informal use for generations' is not stated by either source for this exact green-and-white design: Wikipedia says the Tudor colours came after Henry VII's standard and a badge-based white flag (1953) was used until 1959. Flags of the World's 1 January 1801 date for this row's earlier reading was the Union Flag, not the Welsh flag.

era-400.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1536.says: Flags of the World: Wales was united with England under the Statute of 1284 and entrenched by Acts of 1535 and 1543; after Henry VII's dragon standard no other such flag was recorded until 1840; the history page records Henry VII's red dragon standard blessed at St Paul's on 27 August 1485 and a 1807 declaration that a red dragon on a mound should be the King's badge for Wales; in 1953 the augmented badge was set on a white flag. Wikipedia: red dragon on a green mount became the Royal Badge of Wales in 1807 and a badge flag followed in 1953.
era-1536.open: Nothing read describes the 1801 Union Flag or its use in Wales; the claim that Wales used England's, then Great Britain's, then the UK's flag is an assumption, supported only by FOTW's statement that Wales had no portion of the Union Flag. Not read: a source on English flags used in Wales.

era-1283.says: Flags of the World: the Statute of Wales was passed on 19 February 1284 and Wales treated as a principality within England; the dragon appeared in the royal arms in the 15th century; the history page records that Llywelyn the Last (proclaimed Prince of Wales 1258) likely fought under the Lions of Gwynedd and that Glyndwr displayed a golden dragon on white at Caernarfon on 2 November 1401. The history page and the main page do not mention St George's cross over Wales.
era-1283.open: No source read says that St George's cross flew over Wales in 1283-1536; the card's caption is unsupported.

era-850.says: Flags of the World's history page: the Historia Brittonum (c. 800, attributed to Nennius) gives the red dragon as the British symbol, 'there is no clear evidence of a Welsh dragon banner before 1401', Matthew Paris's sketch of Gruffudd ap Llywelyn's arms shows lions, and Llywelyn probably fought under the Lions of Gwynedd; its Glyndwr page has contributors attributing a four-lions banner (Powys and Deheubarth arms) to him. Wikipedia (Kingdom of Gwynedd): c. 500-1283, infobox flag is the arms of Gruffudd, Dafydd and Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, and no dragon is Gwynedd's emblem; Wikipedia (Flag of Wales): Historia Brittonum c. 828, Glyndwr's dragon 1400-1401.
era-850.open: The two publishers support a lions banner for 13th-century Gwynedd, not a lions-and-dragon combination, and give no banner at all for c. 850-1200; the card's four lions are not what the Gwynedd arms show (the Glyndwr four-lions arms are a contributor's claim for a later date).

era-1990.says: Wikipedia's infobox and FOTW's main page both give 22 May 1990 for the flag, the date Yemen was formed by the union of North and South; FOTW's North Yemen page adds that the new flag removed the star of the Yemen Arab Republic's flag. Both describe a red-white-black tricolour without an emblem.
era-1990.open: Only the adoption date and the removal of the star were compared; whether the flag was neutral 'deliberately', as this page says, and the swatch colours are not stated by these sources.

era-1967.says: Wikipedia: Yemen Arab Republic flag adopted 1 November 1962 (red-white-black tricolour with one green star), relinquished 22 May 1990; PDRY flag adopted 30 November 1967 with a light blue triangle and red star near the hoist. FOTW's North Yemen page: the same tricolour with a green five-pointed star in the white stripe, hoisted 1 November 1962 (the UAR flag with one star removed); FOTW's South Yemen page: red-white-black tricolour with a light blue hoist triangle containing a red five-pointed star, introduced about 30 November 1967.
era-1967.open: The two publishers agree on design and dates; FOTW's date for the southern flag is 'about 30 November 1967'. Wikipedia's wording on the symbolism (triangle for the people, star for the NLF) is not in FOTW.

era-1918.says: FOTW's Kingdom of Yemen page: the kingdom was nominally Ottoman until 1918 and independent after; its flag 'adopted in 1927' was red with a white sabre and five stars (National Geographic 1951), in use until 1962 and by the royalists to 1970; the imam's own flag was red with the shahada. Wikipedia repeats FOTW's wording about the kingdom and adds caption dates 1918-23, 1923-27 and 1927-70. For the south, FOTW and Wikipedia give the Aden Colony Blue Ensign with a dhow badge from 1937 (the flag in use until 18 January 1963) and Wikipedia says the Protectorate of South Arabia used the Union Jack.
era-1918.open: Wikipedia's text on the kingdom is copied from FOTW, so the two are not independent there. Designs for 1918-1927 are not described, and the page's British Aden 'colonial ensigns throughout' is not supported before 1937 (FOTW: Aden was part of British India until then). A Yemeni or museum source for the Mutawakkilite flag was not found.

era-1839.says: Wikipedia and FOTW's Kingdom of Yemen page say Yemen was nominally Ottoman until 1918. FOTW's British-rule pages say Aden was a dependency, then a Chief Commissioner's province, of British India until 1 April 1937, when it became a Crown colony and its Governor needed a new Union Jack and Blue Ensign badge (the Chief Commissioner had flown the 'Viceroy's Union').
era-1839.open: No source read gives a flag for Aden in 1839-1937 beyond the Viceroy's Union of the Chief Commissioner, nor Ottoman provincial banners for the north; the plain red field is the page's own placeholder.

era-897.says: Neither Wikipedia's flag article nor FOTW's Yemen, North Yemen, South Yemen and Kingdom of Yemen pages mention the Zaidi Imamate before the 20th century or any flag for 897-1839; FOTW notes only the imam's flag of the twentieth century (red with the shahada).
era-897.open: Green as a Zaidi colour and any Ayyubid, Rasulid or Ottoman interlude flags are not covered by any source read.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: green field with an orange fish eagle in flight over red, black and orange stripes in the fly, adopted 24 October 1964 and modified in 1996 (lighter green, adjusted eagle); green for vegetation and natural resources, red for the freedom struggle, black for the people, orange for copper. Flags of the World: same colour meanings and 24 October 1964, modified in 1996; Whitney Smith is cited that the flag is based on the flag of the United National Independence Party.
era-1964.open: The 1996 modification is a design change within the era; the sources do not say the design was a deliberate break from the Blue Ensign tradition, and the green's meaning is given slightly differently by the two (agriculture or vegetation).

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: a blue ensign with the Federation emblem for the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland (1953-1964), and separately a Blue Ensign with the territory's emblem for Northern Rhodesia (1939-1964). FOTW (Northern Rhodesia): Northern Rhodesia joined the Federation on 3 September 1953; the Federation flew a blue ensign with the shield of the Federal Arms in the fly, with the palets wavy taken from the Northern Rhodesia arms; the Federation was dissolved on 31 December 1963; the Governor's flag, a Union Jack with the arms on a white roundel in a green laurel garland, continued through the Federation.
era-1953.open: The Federation's ensign is the flag of the union, and the sources do not say whether the territory's own Blue Ensign (Wikipedia, 1939-1964) was flown alongside it. The Federation ended on 31 December 1963, ten months before independence, so the page's end date of 1964 is approximate.

era-1924.says: Wikipedia: the Union Flag for the United Kingdom in 1924-1964 and a Blue Ensign with the territory's emblem for Northern Rhodesia from 1939; the territory's arms date to 1927. FOTW (Northern Rhodesia): the Governor's office was created in 1924 when it became a protectorate; the badge granted in 1928 was told to the Colonial Office in 1938 to have never been used on any flag, only on the Public Seal; the arms were formally granted by Royal Warrant on 16 August 1939; 'presumably' the badge was used on a flag after 1943 when governors flew their defaced Union Jack on land; unofficial red ensign versions are also reported.
era-1924.open: Both sources contradict a Northern Rhodesia Blue Ensign with its own badge between 1924 and 1939; FOTW's account of 1939-1953 and the red ensign variants are not in the page's drawing, which also shows a badge on a white disc.

era-1891.says: Wikipedia: for the British South Africa Company (1891-1924) a Union Jack with the company emblem in the centre; Barotseland flags for 1864-1891. FOTW (British South Africa Company): the company's flag, raised at Bulawayo on 4 November 1893, was a Union Jack with the company badge (a yellow lion with an elephant's tusk) on a white roundel, with or without a red ring; the company Blue and Red Ensigns with the crest 'in all probability were never used'. FOTW (Northern Rhodesia): a contributor's scant visual evidence suggests the shield on a blue ensign for 1910-1924, the badge being the company crest.
era-1891.open: The two sources agree that the company's flag was a Union Jack with a badge in the centre, so the page's drawing, a Blue Ensign with the badge on a disc in the fly, matches the ensign that FOTW says probably never flew. The dates 1891-1924 are Wikipedia's; FOTW gives the company's rule as 1890 to September 1923, and the Northern Rhodesia territory as separated in 1910.

era-1980.says: Both sources give 1980, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as April 18th, 1980; Flags of the World dates it 18 April 1980.
era-1980.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1979.says: Wikipedia: the Zimbabwe Rhodesia flag was adopted 4 Sept 1979; in Dec 1979 Britain took interim control and the Union Jack became the official flag, though the Zimbabwe Rhodesia flag continued to be flown de facto. FOTW Rhodesia: Dec 1979-Apr 1980 the Union Flag was used de facto while the Zimbabwe-Rhodesia flag was in common use. FOTW Zimbabwe: the country returned to British colony status in this period; no new flag described.
era-1979.open: FOTW's Rhodesia page dates the Zimbabwe-Rhodesia flag 1 Sept 1979 / June-Dec 1979, Wikipedia 4 Sept 1979; the Lancaster House stage is not covered.

era-1965.says: Wikipedia: green-white-green vertical triband charged with the coat of arms adopted 11 Nov 1968, the first national flag to contain the Zimbabwe Bird; the 1964 light blue ensign continued three years after UDI. FOTW Rhodesia: UDI 11 Nov 1965; Flag of Rhodesia Act 1968, flag adopted and first raised 11 Nov 1968, three equal vertical stripes with the arms on the white stripe; republic declared 2 March 1970 with the flag unchanged; replaced in 1979.
era-1965.open: The page's claim that the flag was adopted as Rhodesia moved to become a republic is not covered (republic came in 1970); 'plain shield rather than gold relief' is not covered.

era-1923.says: Wikipedia: from 1923 Southern Rhodesia's flag was a Blue Ensign with the shield from its coat of arms (arms granted 11 Aug 1924); Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland flag 1953-63; a light blue ensign introduced April 1964. FOTW Rhodesia: dark blue ensign 1923-1953 in two variants (with and without a white disc), Federation ensign 1953-63, Southern Rhodesian light blue ensign 1964-68 flown alongside the Union Flag.
era-1923.open: Both sources have the ensign changing to light blue in 1964 and in use to 1968, not 'until 1965'; they differ on the badge (arms shield vs white disc).

era-1890.says: FOTW (BSAC page): the Company flag was a Union Jack with the Company badge (a yellow lion holding an elephant's tusk on a wreath, 'B.S.A.C.' beneath) at the centre, with several variants; the first flag of sovereignty was a plain Union Jack raised at Fort Salisbury on 13 September 1890; the first Company flag reached Fort Salisbury in 1892 and was raised at Bulawayo on 4 November 1893; Blue and Red Ensigns were designed but 'in all probability' never used. Wikipedia (BSAC): the Company administered Southern Rhodesia until 1923 and shows a 'Flag of the British South Africa Company' image without describing it.
era-1890.open: FOTW describes a Union Jack with a badge, not the Blue Ensign with a Company badge drawn on this page, and says the ensigns were probably never used; only one publisher describes the design, and the Wikipedia image was not seen.

era-1583-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1949.says: FOTW (coflg): sixty-five colonial badges were in use in 1949, declining as colonies became independent, with the badge-size restrictions lifted in 1999; FOTW (colonial flags): colonial flags date from 1869 and many colonies took arms before independence. Wikipedia's list shows remaining territories with flags of their own (British Virgin Islands 1960, British Antarctic Territory 1963, British Indian Ocean Territory 1990) and Akrotiri and Dhekelia using the Union Jack.
era-1949.open: Neither source says how the Union Flag is used by the Commonwealth of Nations (the page's 'via the Commonwealth' claim) or gives the 1949/1997 dates; the Commonwealth flag itself is not covered. Next: the Commonwealth Secretariat's page on the Commonwealth flag (not read).

era-1947.says: FOTW coflg: 1865 Blue Ensign with colony badge in the fly; 1869 governors' Union Jack with badge; 1882-1927 defaced Red Ensigns; 1941 governor's flag in all circumstances; 65 badges in 1949; badges declined as colonies became independent. WP: colonies adopted own badges from the early 19th century, Colonial Naval Defence Act 1865 required emblems.
era-1947.open: Page said 'badge in the canton'; FOTW says in the fly for ensigns. Dates 1947-1980s as a wave are not stated by either source.

era-1919.says: FOTW (colonial flags): a plain Red Ensign was the proper ensign of any vessel registered in a British colony, and the Admiralty authorised defaced Red Ensigns for overseas territories by warrant between 1882 and 1927 (North Borneo 1882, Kenya 1890, Canada 1892, Palestine 1927). Wikipedia (Red Ensign): the flag flown by British merchant ships since 1707, plain or defaced with a badge, allocated to merchantmen by an order in council of 1864.
era-1919.open: Neither source treats 1919 or the post-war mandates as a turning point (Palestine's 1927 warrant is the only mandate named); the 'informal' territorial use stated on the page is not in them.

era-1783.says: FOTW (colonial flags): in 1865 the Admiralty ruled that vessels maintained by a colony under the Colonial Naval Defence Act should fly a Blue Ensign with the colony's seal or badge in the fly; colonial flags were introduced in 1869 with governors' flags. Wikipedia (Colonial Naval Defence Act 1865): in 1866 the Admiralty advised colonies that vessels under the Act must fly the Royal Navy Blue Ensign with the colony's seal or badge; Wikipedia's historical-flags list says colonies began adopting their own badges in the first half of the 19th century.
era-1783.open: The Blue Ensign with a colonial badge is documented only from 1865-69, so the first eight decades of this era (1783-1865) are not covered and the 'standard from 1783' start is not stated; it was the government/naval vessel flag, not a flag for every colony or territory.

era-1583.says: Wikipedia (historical flags list): early colonial flags, including the Thirteen Colonies, were variations of the Red and Blue Ensigns without badges, and British America used a Red Ensign with the first Union Jack in the canton until 1776 (de facto) / 1783 (de jure). Wikipedia (Red Ensign): an English red ensign with the Cross of St George in the canton from the 1620s, used by Massachusetts from its founding (until the cross was removed after 1636), and a 1674 proclamation of Charles II confirmed it for English merchant ships. FOTW (United Kingdom): first Union Flag 1606 (St George over St Andrew), St Patrick's cross added 1 January 1801.
era-1583.open: Both colonial-flag statements are Wikipedia only; FOTW's pages read (gb, gb-ensig, gb-colon, gb-hist) give nothing on colonial use before 1865. 'King's Colours / Grand Union pattern' is not in any source, and the c.1583 start is the page's own.

era-1795-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1959.says: Wikipedia: the eight-stripe design was kept after statehood in 1959, and Hawaii Revised Statutes 5-19 (2024) define its specifications. Flags of the World: the Hawaii Revised Statutes describe the flag as eight horizontal stripes, alternately white, red, blue; its historical page's chronology (summarising Quaife et al., 1961) has the State of Hawaii using the Hawaiian flag, confirmed in 1959.
era-1959.open: Neither source gives the year the flag was first codified in state law (the FOTW chronology says 'confirmed 1959'), nor the meaning of the eight stripes beyond the contributor's 'eight principal islands'.

era-1898.says: Wikipedia: the design was kept after US annexation in 1898; the governor's flag in territorial years carried 'TH'. Flags of the World's historical page: the Territory of Hawaii used the Hawaiian flag, confirmed in 1903, and it shows a territorial governor's flag, a blue-over-red bicolour with eight white stars. Wikipedia's Republic of Hawaii article records that at the transfer of 12 August 1898 the Flag of Hawaii was lowered over Iolani Palace and the US flag raised.
era-1898.open: The use of the Hawaiian flag as a flag of the Territory rests on one FOTW chronology (summarising a 1961 book) and Wikipedia's 'kept'; whether a separate territorial banner was designed beyond the governor's flag is not covered. The territory's incorporation date is not given in the sources used.

era-1894.says: Wikipedia: the design was kept after the 1893 overthrow of the monarchy. Flags of the World: on 8 April 1896 the Republic's government issued a diagram with flag regulations (a fimbriated Cross of St George one stripe wide, 1/6 border); its historical page's chronology says the Republic of Hawaii readopted the Hawaiian flag in 1894.
era-1894.open: Neither source describes why the flag was kept or its effect on the Republic's legitimacy, which the page's caption asserts.

era-1893.says: Wikipedia's lead says the design was kept after the 1893 overthrow of the monarchy. Flags of the World's historical page has a chronology saying the US flag was flown in Hawaii from 1 February to 1 April 1893 and the Republic readopted the Hawaiian flag in 1894; it says nothing of a flag of the Provisional Government between.
era-1893.open: A flag specific to the Provisional Government (January 1893 to July 1894) is not described, and the chronology suggests a gap in which the US flag flew. Sources do not support or refute the caption.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia: the British Red Ensign was the unofficial flag c.1793-1816; a distinct Hawaiian flag first reached a foreign port in March 1817; early versions (1816-1845) varied in stripe count (nine stripes, 1:2 canton; Golovnin in 1818 saw seven); the eight-stripe design was specified in 1843 and first unfurled on 25 May 1845. Flags of the World's historical page: Hawaii flew the Union Jack from 1794 to 1816 and an early version of the present flag from 1816 to 1843; a quoted Polynesian newspaper of 31 May 1845 says the new national banner with eight stripes was unfurled on 25 May 1845, differing little from the former, which had seven; a contributor adds that the stripe count varied and was set at eight after 1843.
era-1795.open: The attribution to Kamehameha I is traditional and disputed (Wikipedia; a FOTW poster credits Captain Hunt for the 1845 design and others Captains Adams or Beckley). FOTW's chronology gives 20 May 1845, its newspaper quote 25 May. The meaning of eight stripes as eight islands appears only in FOTW's quoted newspaper and a contributor.
